items.title: Aquaporin channels in cytotoxic brain edema following severe head trauma: Systematic review of molecular mechanisms and therapy.
items.abstract: Cytotoxic brain edema significantly worsens outcomes in severe traumatic brain injury (TBI), but the molecular pathways involved aren't fully characterized. This review draws on studies published since 2015 to assess how aquaporin-4 (AQP4), the only AQP isoform evaluated across the included studies, contributes to edema formation and resolution, and interventions targeting it. PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL were searched for studies published between January 2015 and December 2025 examining AQPs in post-TBI cytotoxic edema in preclinical or human observational studies. Study design, TBI model, edema metrics, and intervention effects were extracted. Risk of bias was appraised narratively (SYRCLE for animal studies; Newcastle-Ottawa for the single human study). Forty-two studies described post-TBI changes in AQP4 expression and polarity across controlled cortical impact, cryogenic, and diffuse injury models. Loss of perivascular AQP4 polarity accompanied impaired water clearance and worsening swelling, whereas restored polarization accompanied edema resolution. Because the measures used could not cleanly separate cytotoxic from ionic and vasogenic edema, outcomes are reported as total or mixed edema except where a method isolated intracellular swelling. Direct strategies (siRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, knockout) reduced brain water but faced delivery and timing barriers; pharmacologic agents such as fingolimod and minocycline modulated AQP4 and improved edema and function. Translational readiness varied across models and metrics. These predominantly preclinical findings identify AQP4 modulation as a mechanistically compelling strategy for cytotoxic edema after severe TBI; however, direct clinical evidence remains minimal, and translational claims should be interpreted with caution. Standardized preclinical frameworks and early-phase safety evaluation are needed.

items.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.
items.abstract: To investigate long-term trends in treated dry eye disease (DED) prevalence and medication prescribing patterns in Korea using a nationwide mandatory insurance claims database. Retrospective nationwide clinical cohort study. Patients identified from the Korean NHIS mandatory claims database (2014-2023). DED was defined by at least one relevant ICD-10 diagnosis code together with at least one prescription for a DED-related topical medication within the same calendar year. Annual overall, sex-specific, and age-specific prevalence was calculated using the corresponding mid-year resident population. Medication classes and single-use versus multi-use formulations were evaluated. Medication use in Sjögren syndrome-associated versus non-Sjögren DED was compared using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. Annual treated DED prevalence, medication prescribing proportions, formulation-specific prescribing trends, and differences between Sjögren syndrome-associated and non-Sjögren syndrome DED. Approximately 61.8 million patient-years were analyzed, representing 9.87 million unique patients. Annual treated DED prevalence ranged from 4.84% to 5.61% and was consistently higher in women and older individuals. Hyaluronic acid (HA) remained the most prescribed medication, although its proportional share declined from 85.03% in 2014 to 76.89% in 2023 (P < .001). Diquafosol prescriptions increased from 4.61% to 10.77%, and cyclosporine prescriptions increased from 2.39% to 5.77% (both P < .001). Single-use HA prescriptions increased from 39.73% to 73.76% (P < .001), and single-use diquafosol accounted for 61.8% of diquafosol prescriptions by 2023. Cyclosporine was prescribed to 26.00% of patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED and 7.51% of those with non-Sjögren DED; the adjusted OR was 4.06 (95% CI, 3.99-4.12). Over the past decade, DED management in Korea shifted toward the anti-inflammatory cyclosporine, the mucin and water secretagogue diquafosol, and preservative-free single-use formulations. Patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED demonstrated distinct prescribing patterns, including substantially greater cyclosporine use after adjustment for age and sex.

items.title: Defining the optimal duration of remote home tonometry for accurate characterization of intraocular pressure fluctuation.
items.abstract: To determine the minimal duration of remote intraocular pressure (IOP) monitoring needed to yield accurate IOP fluctuation metrics in patients. Secondary modeling analysis of retrospective data, validated with a large national database. 397 patients from the Moran Eye Center and/or Wilmer Eye Institute and 1,579 patients from a MyEyes CorporationTM database who utilized an iCare HOME/HOME2 tonometer and recorded ≥3 measurements throughout each day over several consecutive days. Bootstrapped progressive day-censorship analyses and exponential decay modeling were used to estimate the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error for IOP metrics, including mean, maximum, range, and standard deviation (SD). Ground truth for each metric was defined using all available measurements within each eye-specific monitoring period. Sensitivity analyses assessing the effects of diagnosis, treatment, and three daily IOP measurements were also completed. Mean absolute error (MAE) and mean relative error (MRE) for IOP mean, maximum, range, and SD; the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error. Across both datasets, approximately 6-7 monitoring days were required to achieve 95% of the modeled reduction in error for daily mean, maximum, range, and SD of IOP in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated longer monitoring requirements in primary open-angle glaucoma (9.1-10.0 days) compared with glaucoma suspects (5.5-6.7 days), secondary open-angle glaucoma (6.4-8.0 days), and primary angle-closure glaucoma (7.8-8.3 days). Monitoring durations remained relatively consistent before and after selective laser trabeculoplasty (8.4-9.0 days) and Hydrus microstent implantation (6.0-6.8 days). Restricting measurements to only three daily IOP recordings throughout the day extended monitoring duration to approximately 10 days in the Moran/Wilmer dataset and longer in the MyEyes dataset. Additionally, 74.1% of peak IOP measurements occurred outside typical clinic hours. Remote tonometry provides clinically meaningful characterization of IOP metrics beyond traditional office-based measurements. Depending on the clinical context, seven to ten consecutive monitoring days consisting of measurements across each day are needed to represent a patient's true IOP pattern.

items.title: Validation of senescence as a therapeutic target in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) through navitoclax delivery.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a chronic liver disease characterized by steatosis, inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. Increasing evidence suggests that cellular senescence contributes to MASH progression by promoting lipid accumulation, inflammatory signaling, and fibrogenic responses, highlighting hepatic senescent cells as a potential therapeutic target. Senolytics selectively eliminate senescent cells, but their application in MASH remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we developed in vitro models integrating hepatic lipid accumulation and hepatocyte-macrophage inflammatory crosstalk to facilitate investigation of the contribution of cellular senescence to MASH pathology and to evaluate senescence-targeted interventions. Senescent hepatic cells showed enhanced lipid accumulation and amplified inflammatory signaling with macrophages. Natural Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) derived from adipocytes reduced senescence-associated phenotypes but exhibited context-dependent biological effects, highlighting the limited control over their intrinsic bioactivity. Navitoclax, a senolytic targeting anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family proteins, reduced senescence-associated phenotypes, but its clinical use is limited by its dose-dependent toxicity. Hence, we conceived nano-Cell Vesicle Technology Systems (nCVTs), a biohybrid-based platform combining cell-derived membranes with synthetic lipids for controlled delivery of navitoclax. Navitoclax-loaded nCVTs retained senolytic activity and reduced inflammatory signaling and fibrotic activation in vitro. Importantly, in a Western diet- and fructose-induced (WDF) MASH mouse model, navitoclax-loaded AML-12-derived nCVTs alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation while reducing histopathological activity score and fibrotic profiles. Neither navitoclax formulation reduced platelet counts or hemoglobin concentrations at the tested dose. Collectively, these findings support cellular senescence as a therapeutically relevant target for MASH and identify nCVTs as a promising engineered platform for controlled senolytic delivery.

items.title: Impaired formation and updating of internal predictive models in a rat model of fragile X syndrome.
items.abstract: Predictive coding frameworks propose that perception emerges from a continuous comparison of incoming sensory signals with internally generated predictions, with mismatches between the two computed as prediction errors. Disruptions to the balance between these top-down predictions and bottom-up sensory signals are theorized to contribute to sensory abnormalities in neuropsychiatric conditions like autism spectrum disorders. However, disambiguating bottom-up from top-down contributions to sensory processing remains a difficult challenge, particularly in animal models. Here we develop a probabilistic oddball detection task in which rats must track local statistics within a trial to detect a deviant stimulus, as well as global statistics across trials to anticipate when a deviant will occur. This design enables formation of experimentally specified internal models of deviant expectation that can be quantitatively derived from behavior and manipulated independently of local stimulus statistics. We used this task to characterize sensory predictive behavior in a Fmr1 KO rat model of Fragile X Syndrome, the most common monogenic cause of autism. Male Fmr1 KO rats detected deviant stimuli at wildtype levels but exhibited reduced anticipation of deviant occurrence based on cross-trial statistics and failed to adapt their behavior when these statistics changed. Computational modeling revealed that these behavioral deficits reflected an overweighting of immediate sensory evidence and temporal response pressure at the expense of learned predictive expectations, consistent with imprecise internal models skewed towards sensory immediacy. These findings provide evidence for disrupted predictive processing in Fragile X Syndrome, consistent with active inference accounts of autism, and highlight the utility of this probabilistic oddball task design for interrogating predictive coding and perceptual impairments in neuropsychiatric conditions.

items.title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: Building Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Electroencephalography.
items.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) remains important in clinical neuroscience because it records brain activity as a time-resolved physiological process. It offers millisecond temporal resolution, can be used at the bedside and supports prolonged monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded EEG analysis through automated pattern recognition, representation learning, large-scale screening and decision support in epilepsy, sleep medicine, cognitive disorders, psychiatric conditions, intensive care, disorders of consciousness and anaesthesia monitoring. High classification accuracy in a research dataset, however, is not clinical readiness. EEG signals are shaped by physiological state, artefacts, acquisition systems, preprocessing choices and clinical context. Labels may come from expert annotations, diagnostic categories, behavioural scales, treatment responses or long-term outcomes, and these sources do not always define the same biological target. This review argues that EEG-AI translation should be judged by the strength of its evidence, not by technical performance alone. We examine why EEG is valuable yet hard to standardize, how EEG features can serve as candidate biomarkers, and why translational maturity differs across clinical scenarios. We then discuss the evidence gaps behind high-performing models, focusing on target validity, data leakage, confounding, external validation and clinically aligned metrics. Finally, we argue for clinical understandability rather than model interpretability alone, and for human-machine workflows rather than isolated classifiers. Future EEG-AI systems should be assessed by whether their outputs are biologically plausible, externally generalizable, understandable to clinicians and safe in real-world care.

items.title: State-Dependent EEG Markers of Excitation/Inhibition and Hemodynamic State Are Associated with Random Noise Stimulation Effects.
items.abstract: Non-invasive brain stimulation effects vary substantially across individuals, yet the physiological factors associated with this variability remain unclear. We tested whether baseline and task-related EEG markers of excitation/inhibition (E/I) and hemodynamic state are associated with the effects of transcranial random noise stimulation (tRNS) on learning. Participants completed a mathematical learning task during active or sham tRNS. We indexed E/I-related population dynamics using the EEG aperiodic exponent, for which lower values have been linked to relatively greater excitation than inhibition, and assessed hemodynamic state using fNIRS-derived oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO). Behavioral learning was modeled using generalized linear mixed-effects models. tRNS accelerated learning relative to sham stimulation but did not reliably induce pre-post changes in resting-state aperiodic exponent or HbO. Instead, stimulation effects were state-dependent. Higher resting-state aperiodic exponent and lower resting-state HbO were associated with greater behavioral gains under tRNS, while task-related aperiodic exponent was associated with stimulation-related differences in learning. Task-evoked HbO was associated with learning rate but did not significantly differentiate stimulation effects. Across modalities, the findings identify complementary electrophysiological and hemodynamic correlates of variability in learning under stimulation. However, statistical support for the EEG moderation effects was attenuated in models including participant-specific learning slopes, indicating sensitivity to random-effects specification and the need for replication. The findings argue against a simple tonic-shift account of tRNS and support a state-dependent framework in which stimulation effects depend on ongoing electrophysiological and hemodynamic context. EEG and fNIRS provided complementary information about variability in learning and stimulation response, supporting multimodal approaches to understanding and individualizing neuromodulation.

items.title: Same Networks, Different Dynamics: Parsimony in Auditory Cognitive Task Processing.
items.abstract: Distinct cognitive states might be supported either by dedicated, task-specific brain networks or by flexible modulation within shared ones, a distinction central to understanding how the brain allocates neural resources. Guided by the principle of parsimony, we hypothesized that both language and numerical cognition, when matched for sensory modality and attentional demand, would engage a common network architecture differentiated primarily through targeted modulation of connectivity strength and temporal dynamics rather than wholesale reconfiguration. We applied a jackknife-based dynamic functional connectivity approach to examine time-varying network engagement during auditory language comprehension and auditory math problem-solving in 172 age- and sex-matched participants from the Human Connectome Project-Young Adult cohort, using the Desikan-Killiany atlas and an 85% participation threshold. Of the significant connections identified, many were retained across both tasks, with 87 connections common to story and math, compared with 26 story-associated and 11 math-associated connections. Rather than indicating a novel shared-core architecture, this overlap is consistent with prior evidence that task functional connectivity is strongly constrained by a common intrinsic connectivity backbone. We therefore used the shared edge set as a common network framework for testing how two modality-matched, but cognitively distinct auditory tasks differ in connectivity strength and temporal variability. Among the 87 shared connections, 84 showed significant task-related differences in mean connectivity strength, indicating that story-math differentiation was expressed primarily through quantitative modulation of shared connections rather than wholesale changes in edge membership. Exploratory rolling-correlation analyses further suggested that some edges may show temporal variability in math-story connectivity correspondence even when mean connectivity strength is similar, highlighting a potential dynamic feature not captured by static connectivity estimates alone. Together, these findings suggest that story and math processing rely on a broadly shared connectivity backbone, while task differentiation emerges through graded modulation of connection strength and, in some cases, temporal variability.

items.title: Objective assessment of depressive symptoms using eye-tracking features: An exploratory pilot study.
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) exhibits significant symptom heterogeneity, challenging precise clinical assessment. Current evaluations rely on subjective patient and clinician reports, limiting objective monitoring. Eye-tracking technology offers a non-invasive approach to assessing and characterizing clinical features in depressive patients, enabling personalized assessment and management. This cross-sectional pilot study included 74 patients with MDD and 80 healthy controls. Participants completed a free-viewing task and a visual search task. Depressive, anxiety (including tension), anhedonia and sleep symptoms were assessed using the HAMD-17, HAMA, DARS, and PSQI scales. Correlations between symptom scores and eye-tracking variables were analyzed in an exploratory, hypothesis-generating framework, followed by regression models to identify associated eye-tracking variables. Multiple eye-tracking features showed exploratory associations with specific symptoms, although none of these associations survived correction for multiple comparisons. Suicidal ideation was associated with longer average fixation duration for threatening pictures during the free-viewing task (AUC 0.753); anhedonia severity with first fixation latency/duration for angry faces in the visual search task; sleep disturbance with longer fixation durations and first fixation latency for positive faces; and tension with longer first fixation duration for negative faces (AUC 0.743). Specific eye-tracking features, particularly those related to processing threatening pictures and emotional faces, were associated with severity of depressive symptoms such as suicidal ideation, anhedonia, sleep disturbance, and tension in this exploratory pilot study. These preliminary findings require replication in independent samples before clinical application but support the potential utility of eye-tracking as an objective tool for assessing symptom domains in MDD.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of pharmacological interventions for panic disorder with or without agoraphobia: A systematic review and network meta-analysis, accounting for dose.
items.abstract: Panic disorder (PD) features recurrent and unpredictable panic episodes accompanied by a variety of somatic symptoms. This is the first network meta-analysis (NMA) accounting for dose that explores direct and indirect comparisons focusing on pharmacotherapy for PD, with and without agoraphobia. We conducted a NMA searching for RCTs comparing pharmacological interventions against each other/or placebo in patients with PD, indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE,Embase,Web-of-Science/Scopus(from inception up to 2026, April 3). Co-primary outcomes were the change in anxiety symptoms/response and the change in weekly frequency of panic attacks. Tolerability/remission/acceptability, as well as the risk of specific adverse events, were secondary outcomes. Confidence-In-Network-Meta-Analysis was appraised. Overall, 92 RCTs, encompassing 36 different treatment combinations, involved 14,510 participants. Sensitivity analysis, including non-sponsored studies only and excluding outliers for major effect modifiers, indicated that brofaromine (SMD = -2.47; 95%CI = -3.57;-1.47), alprazolam (SMD = -0.66; 95%C.I. = -1.11;-0.22), alprazolam sublingual (SMD = -0.61; 95%C.I. = -1.14;-0.06); fluvoxamine (SMD = -0.53; 95%C.I. = -0.79;-0.26), fluoxetine (SMD = -0.52; 95%C.I. = -0.81;-0.22), alprazolam substained-release (SMD = -0.41; 95%C.I. = -0.70;-0.13) outperformed placebo for anxious symptoms reduction. Imipramine, alprazolam, and brofaromine outperformed placebo for response. Fluvoxamine (SMD = -0.33; 95%C.I. = -0.61;-0.04) and alprazolam sustained-release (SMD = -0.30; 95%C.I = -0.58;-0.01) outperformed placebo in the change in weekly frequency of panic attacks. However, a meta-regression of efficacy effect sizes against the adapted AMSTAR-Plus score showed that larger SMDs (i.e., brofaromine) were associated with lower AMSTAR scores, reflecting lower study quality. Our findings align with previous NMAs and current guidelines, updating and expanding knowledge by concurrently appraising different drugs/doses through refined transitivity/sensitivity analyses.

items.title: Individualized Transcranial Temporal Interference Stimulation (TIS): Research Advancements and Clinical Translation Pathways.
items.abstract: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation (TIS) is a promising tool for non-invasive deep brain modulation, yet inter-individual anatomical differences cause substantial electric field (E-field) variability under identical parameters, hindering clinical translation. We review recent progress (2017-2026) in individualized TIS, focusing on why inter-individual variability occurs and how to address it for clinical applications. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, preprint repositories (bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv), and clinical trial registries from June 2017 through August 2026, synthesizing studies across quantitative E-field variability, biophysical mediation mechanisms, computational optimization frameworks, and human trials. Even with individualized optimization, the focal spot can shift by up to 1.2cm between subjects. Target modulation depth varies with age and sex, largely due to variations in skull thickness and cerebrospinal fluid volume. For E-field optimization, individualized finite element method (FEM) modeling remains the most accurate approach, whereas faster population-based optimization (17% error margin) is viable only for superficial brain areas. In human translational studies, a clear distinction must be maintained across levels of evidence: while individualized montages targeting the striatum and subthalamic nucleus demonstrate physiological target engagement, behavioral modulation in healthy cohorts, and preliminary acute symptom relief in pilot patient trials, definitive clinical efficacy in large-scale randomized trials (e.g., ongoing nucleus accumbens protocols) and effective active sham protocols remain ongoing challenges. Individualized planning is essential for deep TIS. Future studies should focus on multi-center trials and standardized in vivo closed-loop validation using functional neuroimaging and electrophysiology.

items.title: A novel behavioral paradigm to model hypermemory-like features in rats.
items.abstract: Episodic memory is essential to everyday life and personal identity, but its dysfunction can affect mental health. Translational animal models for investigating these dysfunctions remain limited, particularly for abnormally enhanced memories. We developed a paradigm to induce hypermemory-like features in adult male and female rats using object recognition (OR) and object location (OL) tasks mimicking the rumination-like component of hypermemory. During odor-context association training, rats explored two identical objects with a cinnamon scent. Over the following 6h, they received 12 brief re-exposures to cinnamon odor, an odor-free stimulus, or a novel neutral odor to control for nonspecific effects. Re-exposure to the learning-associated odor was designed to promote iterative consolidation of spatial memory. After 24h, memory was assessed under odor-free conditions. Odor re-exposure selectively enhanced OL memory in both sexes, whereas OR memory remained unaffected. Neither total object exploration nor locomotion was altered. Enhanced spatial memory was accompanied by increased ventral hippocampal c-Fos expression in both sexes. Unlike conventional memory paradigms, which primarily assess memory impairment or enhancement, our approach models the persistence of otherwise short-term memories through repeated exposure to a learning-associated cue. Our protocol is designed to model key features theoretically associated with hyperfunctional episodic memory, using repeated olfactory reactivation to mimic rumination and memory replay hypothesized to contribute to enhanced autobiographical memory in HSAM. This simple paradigm provides a novel translational tool for investigating the behavioral and neurobiological mechanisms underlying enhanced memory consolidation and memory persistence.

items.title: Disentangling Reproductive History and Parenthood in Late-Life Cognitive and Vascular Brain Health.
items.abstract: Women bear a greater burden of Alzheimer's disease (AD), prompting interest in whether reproductive history contributes to late-life brain health. Yet parity, a count of live births, compresses biologically and socially distinct reproductive trajectories into a single measure. Current human biomarker studies provide little evidence that parity tracks amyloid-β or tau pathology. The clearest human evidence links adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs), particularly hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), to later vascular brain injury and vascular dementia, supporting a life-course vascular framework that separates preconception susceptibility, pregnancy complications, and postpartum recovery. Mother-father comparisons further indicate that parenthood-related social exposures contribute to the observed associations. Obstetric history therefore has direct relevance to vascular risk assessment, whereas AD biomarker testing should follow established clinical and biomarker indications rather than parity. Future studies should pair exposure-resolved reproductive histories with serial postpartum phenotyping, vascular neuroimaging, and longitudinal AD biomarkers.

items.title: From maternal womb to parents' arms: the influence of postnatal caregiving in the association between prenatal stress exposure and infant development.
items.abstract: Maternal psychological distress during pregnancy has been associated with an increased risk of altered neurodevelopmental outcomes in the offspring, yet the mechanisms linking prenatal exposures to later physiological, behavioral, and socio-emotional outcomes remain incompletely understood. This narrative review examines the potential role of postnatal caregiving in mediating or moderating some of these associations. Evidence suggests that prenatal distress often persists into the postpartum period and may impair the quality of early maternal caregiving, thereby providing a potential postnatal pathway through which risk is transmitted. A limited number of human studies support mediation by caregiving quality, although findings are inconsistent. Evidence for moderation is similarly mixed, but several studies indicate that sensitive caregiving can attenuate associations between prenatal distress and poorer cognitive, behavioral, temperamental, and stress-related outcomes, whereas low-quality caregiving may amplify vulnerability. Biological pathways that may underlie these effects are discussed, including caregiver-dependent calibration of the infant stress response systems, oxytocin-related stress regulation, epigenetic modification of stress-related genes, and experience-dependent development of neural circuits involved in emotion regulation. Overall, the available evidence challenges deterministic models of fetal programming and supports a broader developmental perspective in which prenatal and postnatal influences jointly shape neurodevelopment. Future research in humans adopting longitudinal, multi-method, and biologically integrated approaches may clarify when, how, and for whom caregiving is protective. Clinically, integrating antenatal mental health care with postnatal interventions that support caregiver-infant relationships may contribute to reduce risk for psychopathology and promote children's resilience.

items.title: A multilevel circuit gating framework for transforming sexual motivation into sexual action: Insights from mouse models.
items.abstract: Sexual behaviour consists of a appetitive phase and a consummatory phase. Based primarily on research evidence from rodents (particularly male mice), this paper presents a multi-level gate model that explains how the transition between these two phases occurs. In this model, the processing of cues associated with a potential mate is initiated in the main olfactory bulb (MOB) and the accessory olfactory bulb (AOB) systems. These cues are then transmitted through limbic circuits, such as the medial amygdala (MeA) and the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), where they are encoded as valuable mating information. Subsequently, these cues are integrated with internal motivational states, including social cues, hormonal status, Sexual reward experience, and sexual satiety, within cell-type-specific circuits centred on the preoptic area (POA). This integration process results in the generation of a motivational gain. When intrinsic motivational states are integrated with somatosensory inputs related to the partner, a state-dependent sensory contact gating mechanism facilitates the transition from exploratory contact to mating behaviours (e.g. mounting). In the downstream process, theperiaqueductal gray (PAG), brainstem, spinal cord, and mesolimbic reward circuits coordinate the sequence of intromission and ejaculation behaviours. During the process of mating, feedback mechanisms such as reward reinforcement and sexual reward modulate future motivational states and action thresholds. Finally, we discuss sex differences in the neural mechanisms underlying the transition from appetitive to consummatory. This conceptual model provides a testable hypothesis regarding the neural mechanisms underlying sexual dysfunction caused by insufficient sexual motivation or disrupted action gating thresholds.

items.title: IGF Signaling in Autism and Related Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Biomarkers and Therapeutic Targets.
items.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD), including both idiopathic and syndromic forms, is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social communication, restricted and repetitive behaviors, and diverse molecular etiologies. Increasing evidence implicates dysregulation of insulin-like growth factor (IGF) signaling in ASD and related neurodevelopmental disorders, including Rett syndrome, Angelman syndrome, Fragile X syndrome, Phelan-McDermid syndrome, and schizophrenia. However, the diagnostic and therapeutic significance of IGF1 and IGF2 across these disorders remains incompletely understood. This review synthesizes recent evidence on the roles of IGF1 and IGF2 as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in syndromic and idiopathic ASD and related neurodevelopmental disorders. Preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that dysregulated IGF signaling contributes to disease pathogenesis by altering the PI3K/AKT/mTOR and MAPK/ERK pathways, which regulate neuronal survival, neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity and cognitive function. IGF1 exhibits the strongest clinical evidence, particularly in Rett syndrome and Phelan-McDermid syndrome, whereas IGF2 shows promising therapeutic potential for improving learning, memory, and synaptic function in Angelman syndrome, Fragile X syndrome, and schizophrenia. Metformin studies also demonstrate effects on metabolic and behavioral outcomes through pathways overlapping with IGF signaling, although direct IGF1 or IGF2 mediation remains unestablished. Clinical translation remains limited by small study populations, methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent biomarker findings, and insufficient long-term safety data. This review highlights IGF signaling disorders and emphasizes its potential for biomarker development, targeted therapeutics, and precision medicine. Future multicenter clinical trials integrating multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence, and standardized biomarker validation will be essential to translate IGF-based interventions into clinical practice.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of exon skipping therapies for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked recessive disorder characterized by progressive muscle weakness and muscle wasting. Exon skipping therapies have been approved as part of the therapeutic arsenal for DMD, however, there is contrasting evidence regarding their clinical benefits. The aim of this study was to determine the efficacy and safety of exon skipping therapies for DMD. ology: A systematic review was conducted in three databases including PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Cochrane-Ovid, based on the following question using PICO strategy: What is the efficacy of exon skipping therapies for DMD? Search was limited to randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and Open Label RCTs with reported results, published between January 2016 and December 2024, involving patients with DMD treated with any of the existing exon-skipping therapies, reporting efficacy measured by primary clinical and secondary molecular outcomes. Secondary safety outcomes were also registered. Eligible studies were assessed for risk of bias. A descriptive analysis was performed in subgroups according to variants amenable to exon 45, 51, or 53 skipping. A total of nine studies were left after the final filters were applied. Studies were conducted across centers in seven different countries. Four studies used viltolarsen (exon 53), three eteplirsen (exon 51), and two golodirsen (exon 53). Trial length was heterogeneous with an average length of 119.6 weeks (±78.5). Overall, studies with exon skipping medications reported improvement in the clinical outcomes including the 6-minute walking test, time to stand and the North Star Ambulatory Assessment. Biological measurements showed an increase in dystrophin expression and exon skipping percentage. Long term follow up evidenced stabilization of both clinical and molecular outcomes in DMD patients, compared to age and treatment-matched controls. Exon skipping therapies have evidenced improved clinical and molecular outcomes. Longer follow-up extension studies are needed to further elucidate their effect in comparison to age-matched controls.

items.title: Integrating neuroplasticity into whole-brain modeling: From synapses to neural populations.
items.abstract: The brain's ability to learn, adapt, and recover hinges on synaptic plasticity, yet most large-scale neural models overlook this core feature. In this review, we argue that embedding plasticity is essential for the simulation of realistic population-level brain activity. To this end, we explore specific computational attempts at scaling microscopic single-neuron plasticity rules to mesoscopic populations, drawing from mechanistic insights into short-term synaptic dynamics, long-term potentiation, and homeostatic regulation. We also discuss how plasticity mechanisms in neural field and neural mass models can potentially help us understand recovery trajectories, and how dysfunctional plasticity can play a role in them. Finally, we review state-of-the-art multiscale co-simulations methods that bridge spiking neuron networks with neural field and mass models and discuss their ability to link microscopic synaptic mechanisms with macroscopic brain dynamics. By embedding plasticity as a core feature, we can develop mean-field models that are more realistic and powerful tools for understanding brain function and recovery.

items.title: Persistent Circulating Proteomic Signatures Distinguish Magnetic Resonance Angiography-Defined Carotid Plaque Vulnerability.
items.abstract: Carotid artery luminal stenosis alone may not predict the risk of future neurovascular events. Plaque vulnerability is emerging as an independent predictor of higher risk for a neurovascular event. We evaluated blood proteomics, paired with high-resolution cross-sectional imaging preoperatively. From preoperative and postoperative blood samples, our objective was to identify blood proteins that distinguish patients with vulnerable and non-vulnerable carotid artery plaques. We conducted an exploratory, single-center proteomic study of 27 consecutive patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with preoperative 3.0T magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging. Plaques were classified as vulnerable when magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging identified at least one high-risk feature: thin fibrous cap, lipid-rich necrotic core, ulceration, intraplaque hemorrhage, or inflammation. Serum samples were analyzed preoperatively and postoperatively using a high-throughput, untargeted proteomics technology (Olink). Differential protein abundance between vulnerable and non-vulnerable groups was assessed separately at each time point. For both time points, the vulnerable group demonstrated a blood proteomic signature involving diacylglycerol signaling and oxidative stress proteins, including diacylglycerol kinase iota and peroxiredoxin-like 2B, with postoperative vulnerability additionally associated with platelet activation (Ras guanyl releasing protein 2), cytoskeletal remodeling (metastasis suppressor 1), and ribonucleic acid/ribosome-related proteins (Shwachman-Bodian-Diamond syndrome protein, RNA-binding protein with multiple splicing 2, zinc ribbon domain-containing protein 2). Non-vulnerable plaques showed a higher abundance of proteins involved in cellular maintenance and deoxyribonucleic acid repair. Furthermore, the persistence of higher diacylglycerol kinase iota and peroxiredoxin-like 2B in the vulnerable group and X-ray repair cross-complementing protein 2 in the non-vulnerable group at both time points suggests stable, patient-level systemic differences detectable in blood, despite plaque removal. Serum proteomics identified distinct systemic pathways associated with cross-sectional imaging carotid plaque vulnerability, highlighting diacylglycerol signaling, oxidative stress, and platelet activation as candidate mechanisms and new biomarker candidates for risk stratification, symptom surveillance, and targeted medical interventions.

items.title: Modeling exhaled aerosol deposition in an impaction filter across clinically measured breath flowrates.
items.abstract: Exhaled breath offers a non-invasive matrix for detecting recent drug use, but high intra and inter-study variability in collected drug mass currently hinders its transition into reliable quantitative clinical and forensic tools. To enable standardized, reproducible sampling protocols, we evaluated flowrate-dependent aerosol capture in an impaction filter device (Breath Explor). We expanded a computational fluid and particle dynamics (CFPD) model across a flowrate spectrum informed by clinical data from 38 participants (N=12,295 exhalations; mean flowrate 0.15 ± 0.04 L · s-1). We also enhanced the near-wall transport model to resolve turbulent aerosol dispersion at high resolution. CFPD simulations showed that turbulent forces account for up to 20% of mass deposition for submicrometer-size aerosols within this operational range. Crucially, capture efficiency varied more than two-fold-ranging from 42% at 0.05 L·s-1 to 90% at 0.3 L·s-1-at a constant exhaled volume. These findings demonstrate that breath flowrate directly impacts aerosol recovery, suggesting that participant flowrate guidance or mathematical recovery normalization could improve the reproducibility of drug quantification. Ultimately, this work demonstrates how combining real-world clinical data with CFPD modeling can inform standardized, quantitative breath diagnostics.

items.title: A high-resolution wireless sensing platform for the characterization of urodynamic events in murine models.
items.abstract: Cystometry in murine models is fundamental for understanding lower urinary tract dysfunctions. However, the high cost of commercial equipment and the mechanical limitations of wired systems, which can introduce electronic noise and restrict mobility, often hinder implementation and can compromise animal welfare. This work presents CISTREC, a low-cost, high-signal-integrity wireless pressure monitoring platform designed for preclinical research. The system integrates a digital sensor with on-chip signal conditioning and a 24-bit digital output, enabling direct digitization at the sensor and minimizing susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. Data transmission was performed via Bluetooth Low Energy 5.0 (BLE), providing galvanic isolation and portability. Validation included in vitro characterization from 0 to 160 cmH2O, and in vivo evaluation in an overactive bladder (OAB) model induced by acetic acid in Wistar rats. In vitro tests demonstrated a coefficient of determination of 0.999946, a root-mean-square error of 0.3454 cmH2O, an effective experimental resolution of 0.0742 cmH2O, and a full-scale signal-to-noise ratio (SNRFS) of 76.23 dB. In the in vivo experiment, the high resolution enabled accurate capture of biomarkers, including high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) and non-voiding contractions (NVCs). Significant changes were observed in the pathological model, including a reduction in the inter-contraction interval and a decrease in bladder compliance. The CISTREC system achieves metrological performance in line with reported specifications of high-end commercial systems, at a low cost. Its wireless architecture and high sensitivity facilitate access to advanced urodynamics, promoting the principle of refinement in animal experimentation without compromising rigorous scientific standards.

items.title: Using a Living Lab to Refine an Electronic Prescribing Workflow: Insights From the eRIKA Project.
items.abstract: The integration of eHealth solutions into routine health care remains challenging despite their potential to improve care quality and efficiency. Living labs (LLs) have emerged as an approach to addressing these challenges by enabling co-design and iterative testing of eHealth tools. LLs promote collaboration among patients, health care professionals, developers, and policy makers. However, systematic insights into their practical implementation remain limited. This study explores the use of an LL approach to dynamically create and adapt project workflows, as well as its potential as a methodological framework for developing an implementation plan for a digital prescribing workflow (eRIKA [eRezept als Element Interprofessioneller Versorgungspfade für Kontinuierliche Arzneimitteltherapiesicherheit]). The analysis focuses on intervention-level insights identified throughout the LL process. The study also reflects on the limitations of the approach. The co-design process was structured into 4 thematic sprints conducted across 3 regions in Germany (Saarland, Berlin, and Westphalia-Lippe) between November 2022 and September 2024. Workshops were held with general practitioners (GPs), pharmacists (PHs), medical assistants, and pharmacy technicians recruited from 6 GP practices, 6 pharmacies, and 1 hospital (n=17). Audio-recorded workshop data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Three themes were identified: (1) Workflow Efficiency, encompassing demands for filtering and prioritization mechanisms to manage information volume, direct digital communication channels, and concerns about workload; (2) Technical Implementation, addressing the need for seamless system integration, data integrity of the medication history, and interoperability with existing practice management systems; and (3) A New Way of Working, reflecting interprofessional negotiations around roles and responsibilities and regulatory requirements, including data privacy. Notably, strongly divergent views emerged between GPs and PHs regarding what data PHs require to conduct effective medication safety reviews. Consistent with previous research, the results highlight concerns about workload, system interoperability, roles and responsibilities, and regulatory barriers to implementation. Beyond these established challenges, the results also reveal interprofessional tensions between GPs and PHs regarding the extent of data sharing required for effective pharmaceutical counseling. These findings inform the subsequent phase 1 and phase 2 evaluation studies and contribute to the growing evidence base on LL methodology in digital health implementation. RR2-10.2196/87277.

items.title: Late rupture of a myelomeningocele sac devoid of neural placode associated with good functional outcome 2 years after postnatal repair: illustrative case.
items.abstract: Neurological deficits in myelomeningocele are driven by a three-hit paradigm: primary myelodysplasia, intrauterine chemotoxic amniotic fluid exposure, and mechanical traction on the neural placode. How sac integrity and rupture timing influence these progressive pathophysiological hits remains poorly understood. A neonate presented with a prominent S1 myelomeningocele sac that remained intact until approximately 35 weeks' gestation. Rather than a distinct neural placode, postnatal repair at 36+3 weeks revealed a hairpin loop of functional nerve roots within the myelomeningocele sac that entered and exited via the dorsal defect. A mild Chiari type II malformation was identified only on postnatal imaging. Following postnatal repair, the child demonstrated not only excellent lower extremity motor function as expected, but also excellent urinary sphincter function with no hindbrain herniation or ventriculomegaly 2 years postrepair. This case illustrates a possible "best of both worlds" clinical scenario in which the persistent hydrostatic pressure of the intact sac protected against early hindbrain herniation and direct toxicity, while the structural absence of a neural placode within the sac reduced mechanical stretch injury. Finally, rupture of the myelomeningocele sac only in late gestation minimized chemical toxicity to neural elements. Overall, this case highlights the multifaceted and varied nature of myelomeningocele pathophysiology. https://thejns.org/doi/abs/10.3171/CASE26739.

items.title: Developing a core outcome set for Meniere's disease trials, the COSMED study: results from two separate, two-round Delphi surveys on outcome domains and outcomes.
items.abstract: BackgroundInconsistencies in outcome measures used in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in Menière's Disease (MD) make it challenging to compare trial results. A Core Outcome Set (COS) standardizes outcome measures across studies, improving comparability and enhancing data synthesis for stronger evidence in clinical trials.ObjectiveTo develop a consensus-based COS for MD trials by identifying the most clinically relevant outcome domains and outcomes, using a Delphi procedure.MethodsTwo two-round Delphi surveys were conducted among international experts, including ENT specialists, neurologists, audiologists, and clinical researchers, to identify outcome domains and outcomes for inclusion in the COS. Participants assessed the importance of MD-related outcome domains in the first Delphi survey, and outcomes in the second Delphi survey using a 9-point Likert scale, with predefined consensus thresholds determining inclusion.ResultsA total of 112 experts from 35 countries participated in this study, each completing at least one Delphi round. In the first Delphi, consensus was reached on inclusion of six out of twelve predefined outcome domains: body function and structures, hearing, dizziness, tinnitus, aural fullness, and quality of life. In the second Delphi, consensus was reached on the inclusion of the following additional outcomes: dizziness severity, number of vertigo attacks, duration of vertigo attack, hearing loss, pure tone average, tinnitus severity, aural fullness severity, quality of life related to dizziness, quality of life related to hearing, quality of life related to social activity or work, drop attacks and vestibular function.ConclusionThis study represents a key phase of the COSMED-study through two structured, two-round Delphi procedures on outcome domains and outcomes to be considered in the COS for MD.

items.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex modulates single-neuron activity in humans.
items.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) is an established treatment for depression, yet the fundamental question of how cortical stimulation influences single neurons in deep brain circuits critical for mood regulation remains unanswered. Using a rare opportunity to record from intracranial microelectrodes while TMS was delivered in four neurosurgical patients, we evaluated the responses of 185 single neurons. Artifact cleaning enabled single-neuron spikes to be resolved as early as 8 ms after stimulation. We found that single-pulse TMS to the left dlPFC elicited time-locked firing responses in 46% of neurons (26% facilitated only, 19% suppressed only, 1% both). These responses occurred within deep bilateral cortical and subcortical structures, including the putamen and thalamus. Single-pulse TMS tended to facilitate spiking in striato-thalamic putative inhibitory neurons from ~8 ms, peaking at ~80 to 100 ms, and decaying until ~600 ms. In contrast, putative excitatory neurons and limbic areas were suppressed with a slower time course lasting to ~1,000 ms. TMS-evoked potentials recorded from intracranial depth macroelectrodes to quantify network activity revealed that the modulation of responsive neurons was positively correlated with cortico-striato-thalamic network activity and anticorrelated with limbic network activity in one participant with sufficient network and unit sampling. These results suggest that dlPFC TMS recruits a high percentage of neurons spanning cortical and subcortical brain regions bilaterally. The recruitment pattern selectively involves increasing the firing rate of inhibitory neurons in executive control networks while suppressing limbic excitatory drive, providing a candidate cellular mechanism for how cortical stimulation modulates distributed brain networks.

items.title: Sickness Absence in Primary Aldosteronism and References: a Longitudinal Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is a common cause of hypertension and is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity. However, its impact on work capacity remains unknown. We investigated sickness absence and disability pension among patients with PA and in matched reference groups with and without hypertension. A nationwide eight-year longitudinal cohort study based on linked register data, including 838 individuals with PA aged 18-67 in 2019 and two matched reference cohorts with and without hypertension. Outcomes included annual proportions of individuals with sickness absence (in spells >14 days) or disability pension, mean annual net days, and trajectories of absence days. Patients with PA had a higher mean annual proportion with sickness absence than individuals with hypertension (21% (range: 18-23%) vs 17% (range: 17-19%) and those without hypertension (10% (range: 9-12%)). Mean annual sickness absence days were 27, 20, and 9, respectively. The combined mean annual number of sickness absence and disability pension days was similar in PA and hypertension (54 (range: 40-66) vs 53 (range: 50-57), and higher than in those without hypertension (25 (range: 22-29)). Trajectory analysis identified four patterns of absence days; 12% of patients with PA had persistently high absence, significantly associated with female sex, higher age, lower education, unmarried status, rural residence, cardiovascular disease, and treatment with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. PA is associated with substantial and sustained sickness absence and disability pension, comparable to that observed in hypertension and higher than in individuals without hypertension. These findings extend the clinical impact of PA beyond cardiovascular morbidity and highlight the importance of considering work capacity in clinical management. items.title: Global Epidemiology of Neonatal and Infantile-Onset Epilepsies and Epilepsy Syndromes (GENIE): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Despite the profound impact of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies on neurodevelopmental outcomes and mortality, consolidated global epidemiological evidence remains lacking. To estimate the global incidence and prevalence of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies and epilepsy syndromes and to characterize their associated etiological profiles. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception through December 18, 2025. Population-based observational studies reporting the incidence or prevalence of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies or epilepsy syndromes were eligible for inclusion. Two authors independently and in duplicate performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment of included studies using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal checklist for prevalence studies. Generalized linear mixed-model random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool the estimates of incidence, prevalence, and etiology. Subgroup meta-analyses were conducted by country, World Health Organization (WHO) region, World Bank income, and diagnostic criteria. Metaregression was used to investigate the association between study-level covariates and pooled incidence estimates of infantile-onset epilepsy syndromes. Cumulative incidence and prevalence of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies and epilepsy syndromes. A total of 86 population-based studies from 30 countries across 4 WHO regions were included. The pooled cumulative incidence of infantile-onset epilepsies within the first 2 years of life was 236.0 cases (95% CI, 164.7-338.2; 95% prediction interval [PI], 53.0-1044.3) per 100 000 live births. Among epilepsy syndrome subgroups, developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) had the highest incidence at 67.7 cases (95% CI, 42.1-108.9; 95% PI, 7.1-636.1) per 100 000 live births. Infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) was the most incident DEE, with 31.6 cases (95% CI, 27.5-36.2; 95% PI, 13.7-72.6) per 100 000 live births. Among self-limited epilepsies, self-limited infantile epilepsy had the highest incidence at 13.0 cases (95% CI, 9.2-18.2; 95% PI, 6.4-26.4) per 100 000 live births. Subgroup analyses revealed limited geographical representativeness, with the majority of studies from high-income countries in the European Region. The findings underscore a significant global burden of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies, primarily driven by DEEs, specifically IESS. Given substantial between-study heterogeneity, the pooled estimates should be interpreted as broad indicators rather than precise, generalizable rates. Geographic disparities, with a lack of data from the African and Eastern Mediterranean Regions, underscore the need for population-based studies in underrepresented regions and longitudinal research on survival, remission, and functional outcomes.

items.title: Delirium and Long-Term Cognitive Trajectories in Cognitively Unimpaired Adults.
items.abstract: Delirium is a state of acute confusion characterized by deficits in attention that occurs commonly during hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes; however, the association of delirium with longitudinal cognitive trajectories is not fully understood. To evaluate the association of delirium during hospitalization with subsequent development of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), dementia, and longitudinal cognitive trajectories. This cohort study used data from participants with hospitalizations in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) from October 2004 to December 2023. The MCSA is a prospective, population-based longitudinal study of cognitive aging among residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota. Of participants enrolled in the MCSA between 2004 and 2023, individuals who experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter were included in this study. Participants with dementia at MCSA enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. Follow-up continued until development of MCI or dementia, last MCSA visit, or the end of the study. Delirium was identified using a validated natural language processing algorithm applied to clinical notes from hospitalizations, associated emergency department visits, and follow-up within 30 days after hospitalization. Delirium status was modeled as a time-dependent exposure. Incident MCI and dementia were assigned through MCSA expert consensus evaluations, including neuropsychological testing performed every 15 months. Association between delirium and development of MCI or dementia was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for patient age, sex, level of education, and apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 allele carrier status; cognitive trajectories were assessed with linear mixed-effects models. Of 7030 participants enrolled in the MCSA, 3542 individuals experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter and were included, and 41 participants with dementia at enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. The cohort included 3501 participants with at least 1 hospitalization. Median (IQR) age was 74.1 (66.6-80.9) years, 1676 participants (47.9%) were female, median (IQR) level of education was 14 (12-16) years, and 910 participants (26.0%) were APOE ε4 carriers. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 7.2 (4.1-10.4) years, 75 participants (2.1%) had delirium documented within 30 days of hospitalization. Delirium was associated with increased risk of MCI (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 3.67; 95% CI, 2.19-6.15) and dementia (aHR, 5.39; 95% CI, 2.94-9.85) and with accelerated decline in longitudinal cognitive testing. In this cohort study among adults in the MCSA, including those with unimpaired cognition at baseline, delirium during hospitalization was strongly associated with increased risk of MCI and dementia and accelerated cognitive decline in subsequent years.

items.title: Long-Term Anatomical Response to Navigated Micropulse Laser in Chronic Central Serous Chorioretinopathy: A 24-Month Longitudinal Study.
items.abstract: Chronic central serous chorioretinopathy (cCSC) is characterized by persistent subretinal fluid (SRF), and long-term anatomical response to navigated subthreshold micropulse laser (NSML) varies among patients. This study evaluated 24-month anatomical and functional outcomes after NSML and investigated baseline optical coherence tomography (OCT) parameters associated with treatment response. This retrospective longitudinal study included 61 eyes with treatment-naïve cCSC treated with NSML and followed for 24 months. Eyes were classified as responders or nonresponders according to complete resolution or persistence of subretinal fluid (SRF) at month 24. Baseline and 24-month OCT parameters, including SRF height, subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM) height and width, choroidal thickness, Haller layer thickness, and Sattler/choriocapillaris complex thickness, were compared within and between groups. Pearson correlation analysis assessed associations between longitudinal OCT changes and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent baseline predictors of anatomical response. At 24 months, 33 eyes (54.1%) achieved complete SRF resolution, whereas 28 eyes (45.9%) showed persistent SRF. Baseline SRF height was significantly greater in responders than in nonresponders (205.2 ± 143.3 μm versus 129.9 ± 80.1 μm; p = 0.0127), while other baseline OCT parameters and BCVA were comparable between groups. Responders showed significant reductions in SRF height and SHRM width and a significant improvement in BCVA, whereas nonresponders showed no significant structural improvement and significant BCVA worsening. In multivariable analysis, baseline SRF height was the only independent predictor of complete anatomical response at 24 months (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 2.46; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.13-5.35; p = 0.023). Long-term anatomical response to NSML in cCSC is heterogeneous. Greater baseline SRF height was independently associated with complete SRF resolution at 24 months, suggesting that more active but potentially reversible disease may be more likely to benefit from treatment.

items.title: Attention in model-based cognitive neuroscience: Mechanisms for optimization under constraint
items.abstract: Two major criticisms of attention research are: 1) verbal theories lack the specificity to make falsifiable predictions about how the various mechanisms of attention operate; and 2) the term ``attention’’ is frequently ascribed to conceptually similar phenomena despite dissociable neural underpinnings. The field of model-based cognitive neuroscience is well-positioned to address (1) through mathematical formalization of hypothesized processes, but may perpetuate (2) insofar as similar algorithms and parameters may recur across modeling traditions without necessarily drawing upon a shared neuro-mechanistic basis. This review provides a function-first organization of the algorithms that have been hypothesized to implement or give rise to ``attention'' at various levels of processing: perception, decision-making, and learning. We ground mathematically-formalized processes in the performance-relevant objectives they serve and the processing constraints that limit them. In doing so, we provide a road map of the broader computational-level solutions that ``attention'' mechanisms have been invoked to provide.

items.title: A partial least squares approach for within-subject correlations in neuroscience
items.abstract: Partial least squares correlation (PLSC) is a multivariate technique used in neuroscience to capture patterns of relationships between neural data and covariates of interest. Conventionally, PLSC captures between-subjects correlations (e.g., between average neural activation and average task performance). However, within-subject correlations (e.g., trial-by-trial relationships between neural activation and subjective ratings or stimulus attributes) are often of interest as well. Thus, we introduce an extension of PLSC to capture within-subject correlations. We validate this approach against related parametric methods and demonstrate that it detects known effects in simulated data and reproduces published findings in open fMRI and EEG datasets. This method is freely available as part of the pyplsc and mne-plsc Python packages.

items.title: Beyond individual features: Identifying computational principles in perceiving visual beauty
items.abstract: Prior research in empirical aesthetics has related beauty to visual features like curvature, color, or shape. Although these feature-based accounts have identified reliable visual correlates of beauty, the literature on feature preferences is highly fragmented, with individual features studied for individual stimulus domains. Here, we argue that making further progress hinges on complementing feature-based approaches with approaches aimed at distilling computational principles that underlie the perception of beauty. Recent advances in computational neuroscience can drive this new line of research by linking visual beauty to the coding of visual information in artificial neural networks and the biological brain. We highlight two examples of how this approach has identified overarching computational principles. First, metabolic processing costs, both in artificial and biological vision, are inversely related to perceived beauty, suggesting that beauty may reflect energy-efficient, fluent visual coding. Second, integrative processing in artificial and biological vision captures the efficient spatial representation of image elements across space and predicts beauty ratings. Synthesizing these findings, we derive a neuro-computational framework for assessing computational principles in the perception of beauty, which uses artificial neural networks for exploration at scale and then validates candidate principles using human behavior and brain data. We discuss candidate principles that could be explored using this approach, like spatiotemporal predictability, and delineate how the new insights could be reconciled with feature-based approaches. In conclusion, complementing feature-based studies with studies targeting computational principles promises a comprehensive and mechanistic understanding of why certain visual stimuli are perceived as beautiful, and others are not.

items.title: Cell IO: a database linking single-cell transcriptomes to literature-derived knowledge of cell functions and perturbations
items.abstract: Abstract Single-cell transcriptome databases tell us which genes a cell type expresses, but what a cell type does, and what happens to it when a gene is perturbed, remains scattered across the literature. Cell IO (https://cell-io.riken.jp/) links these two kinds of knowledge through Cell Ontology identifiers. Its transcriptome layer re-processes 10x Chromium single- cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq experiments of human, mouse, and rat from the Sequence Read Archive with a uniform pipeline, annotates clusters with Cell Ontology terms restricted by the tissue of origin, and stores the cell type composition and UMAP embedding of every experiment (currently 14,931 experiments and 82.9 million cells). Its literature layer holds 895,258 claims extracted with a large language model and verified in a second pass from open-access abstracts, review articles, and gene perturbation studies in immunology and neuroscience, each with the verbatim sentence, highlighted entity spans, evidence strength, and ontology-normalized cell, gene, and context. The web interface lets users search cell types by name, synonym, or identifier, find the experiments in which a cell type is most abundant, inspect the composition and embedding of each experiment, read and filter the claims about a cell type by knowledge base, direction, evidence strength, and organism, and identify cell types whose functional characterization is missing from part of the literature. Cell IO is freely available without registration.

items.title: The relevance of sleep and chronopsychology in understanding maladaptive behaviors in eating disorders: A narrative review.
items.abstract: Background and aims Circadian disruption and sleep-wake dysregulation have been increasingly linked to psychiatric conditions, yet their role in eating disorders and addiction-like maladaptive behaviors remains insufficiently examined in an integrative framework. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on chronotype, circadian misalignment, sleep features, and behavioral addictions across anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, orthorexic tendencies, and night eating syndrome. Methods Literature published between 1970 and 2025 was identified through PubMed, Google Scholar, and reference screening, focusing on chronobiological, sleep-related, neuroendocrine, and behavioral aspects of eating disorders. Results Delayed sleep timing, eveningness preference, and insomnia symptoms commonly co-occur with disordered eating. Findings suggest overlapping mechanisms linking circadian dysregulation, sleep-related and compulsive, reward-driven behaviors, including binge eating and compensatory practices. Objective measures indicate alterations in sleep continuity, slow-wave sleep, and REM parameters. Neuroendocrine evidence further supports links among biological rhythms, appetite regulation, and sleep regulation. Preliminary chronotherapeutic interventions, such as light exposure and sleep phase modification, show promise but remain insufficiently tested. Overall, subclinical, clinical and emerging eating disorders remain underrepresented in chronobiological research. Discussion and conclusions Circadian misalignment may represent a clinically relevant and modifiable dimension underlying maladaptive eating behaviors. However, fragmented evidence and methodological limitations restrict firm conclusions. A structured research agenda is proposed to guide future integrative research.

items.title: Teaching Physiology Through Comparative Framing: Effects on Physiological Reasoning in Undergraduate and Graduate Exercise Physiology Students.
items.abstract: Background : Developing students' ability to transfer physiological principles across contexts remains challenging in physiology education. Comparative framing (CF), in which physiological principles are presented through nonhuman examples, may facilitate transfer by organizing reasoning around variation in environmental challenges and physiological function. However, whether benefits arises from CF itself or engagement with physiologically rich examples remains unclear. Methods : A between-semester controlled design was conducted across undergraduate (n = 99) and graduate (n = 43) exercise physiology courses. Semesters were randomly assigned to CF or human-centered framing (HF), with instructional content and structure held constant. Primary outcomes were parallel, non-identical transfer assessments administered before instruction, immediately afterward, and at delayed follow-up. Secondary outcomes included a content equivalence assessment, a two-tier conceptual reasoning measure, and mental effort ratings. Reflective writing was analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Results : Both conditions demonstrated comparable content acquisition. Significant Framing x Time interactions were observed for Systems and Adaptive Integration and Translational Application, but not Mechanistic Reasoning. The benefits of CF were concentrated in reasoning tasks requiring context-dependent interpretation and integration of physiological principles and became more pronounced at delayed follow-up. Reflective writing analyses converged with the quantitative findings, with the largest thematic differences observed in adaptive versus pathological reasoning. Conclusion : CF produced more durable physiological reasoning despite comparable content learning, suggesting that its educational value extends beyond engaging students with physiologically rich examples alone. Organizing physiology around context, function, and physiological trade-offs may provide a framework for promoting transfer and context-dependent physiological reasoning.

items.title: Simplifying CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 Maintains Diagnostic Performance: An Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Background The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) diagnostic algorithm assesses hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) probability of liver observations in high-risk individuals, but complexity may limit its adoption. Purpose To evaluate whether LI-RADS v2018 can be simplified without impairing diagnostic performance by removing threshold growth (TG) and reducing size cut-offs. Study type Retrospective meta-analysis. Population Eight thousand five hundred eighty-two patients (mean age: 59 ± 11 years; 6610 male) at risk for HCC with CT/MRI (986 CT, 6554 MRI, and 1042 CT/MRI). Field strength/sequence Field strength: 1.5T and 3.0T; sequences varied by institution per LI-RADS technical requirements. Assessment LI-RADS v2018 using major features only was compared with seven simplifications removing TG and/or applying single size cut-offs (≥ 10, ≥ 15, and ≥ 20 mm) in individual participant data (IPD) of 64 studies (29 institutions, 11 countries) from the LI-RADS Living Systematic Review and IPD Meta-analysis Project. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2. Statistical tests Summary receiver operating characteristic curves estimated area under the curve (AUC) across LR-3 to LR-5; LR-5 sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value (PPV) were estimated using a one-step bivariate mixed-effects model. Differences were assessed by cluster bootstrap. p Results Nine thousand four hundred six observations were included. Excluding TG with a 10-mm cut-off showed AUC similar to LI-RADS v2018 (0.80 vs. 0.81, p = 0.44) and significantly higher LR-5 sensitivity (73.8% vs. 71.8%) with similar specificity (72.5% vs. 73.7%, p = 0.13) and PPV (97.8% vs. 97.8%, p = 0.73). Removing TG with 15-mm and 20-mm cut-offs had significantly lower AUC than v2018 (-0.03 [95% CI: -0.041, -0.019]; -0.043 [-0.054, -0.032], respectively) and sensitivity (-13.2% [95% CI: -14.5%, -12.0%]; -30.1% [-31.7%, -28.5%], respectively). Of the 64 studies, 17 had low-risk of bias, and 56 had low applicability concerns. Conclusion Simplifying LI-RADS v2018 by removing TG and using a 10-mm size cut-off preserved diagnostic table AUC while improving LR-5 sensitivity without loss of specificity or PPV. Protocol registration Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/cjwgp). Evidence level 3. Technical efficiency Stage 2.

items.title: Troponin Thresholds for Risk Stratification of Chest Pain Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department: Alternatives to the 99th Percentile.
items.abstract: Background Two methods are used to determine cardiac troponin (cTn) thresholds for high-risk stratification for myocardial infarction (MI), namely the assay's healthy population 99th percentiles and a threshold that has a positive predictive value (PPV) of about 70%. We hypothesized that these methods may produce inconsistent prediction of MI risk. Methods We compared the positive likelihood ratio (LR+), sensitivity, and specificity at 99th percentiles and published high-risk thresholds for a high-sensitivity (hs) cTnI (Abbott) and cTnT (Roche) assay. We simulated the high-risk threshold derivation methodology that derives thresholds with 70% PPV as a function of prevalence and sample size. We derived and validated thresholds based on LR+ = 20 and specificity = 95%. Results In 2584 patients there was an almost 2-fold difference in LR+ between males and females at the sex-specific 99th percentiles, and a 2- to 3-fold difference between assays. Thresholds giving 70% PPV were much higher in lower-prevalence cohorts for both assays, being 3- to 10-fold lower at 5% than 20% prevalence. Thresholds derived using a LR+ or specificity had similar performance in a validation cohort between sexes but had a 2-fold difference in LR+ in a validation cohort between assays. Conclusions In patients presenting to the emergency department with possible MI, sex-specific 99th percentile thresholds convey lower risk of MI for females than males. Risks also differed between assays. Risk thresholds derived using the PPV vary considerably with the prevalence and size of cohort. Thresholds derived with specificity or positive likelihood ratio had more consistent risk-prediction.

items.title: The Contour Neurovascular System Versus Woven Endobridge for Endovascular Embolization of Cerebral Aneurysms: A Propensity Score-matched Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background and objectives The Woven Endobridge (WEB) and the Contour Neurovascular System (Contour) are both intrasaccular devices used to treat cerebral aneurysms. We compared outcomes of these 2 devices using data from 2 large registries. Methods Data were sourced from the WorldWideWEB Consortium, which included 1363 cases treated with WEB from 2017, and a registry of 277 Contour cases from 10 European centers starting the same year. Patient demographics, aneurysm characteristics, procedural specifics, and outcomes were analyzed. Propensity score matching was applied for comparison. Results Before matching, the Contour group had more men (37.9% vs 30.8%), more asymptomatic cases (83.4% vs 70.3%), and fewer acute subarachnoid hemorrhage cases (10.8% vs 26.2%). After matching, no significant differences were found in demographics or aneurysm characteristics between groups. The median age was 60 years, and median aneurysm dimensions were comparable. Logistic regression showed no significant differences between WEB and Contour in achieving complete occlusion (odds ratio [OR] = 1.01, 95% CI, 0.67-1.52, P = .971), adequate occlusion (OR = 0.85, 95% CI, 0.41-1.76, P = .665), or achieving modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2 at last follow-up (OR = 0.48, 95% CI, 0.21-1.02, P = .064). Retreatment (OR = 2.23, P = .086), thromboembolic complications (OR = 0.75, P = .452), and adjunctive treatment use (OR = 1.93, P = .141) were also similar. Conclusion The WEB and Contour demonstrated comparable clinical and angiographic outcomes in this large multicenter study comprised majority small, asymptomatic cerebral aneurysms.

items.title: Beyond social facilitation and inhibition: Experimenter presence regulates executive function engagement in children.
items.abstract: Executive function (EF) performance, which is often treated as an index of children's endogenous self-regulatory capacity, is assumed to be independent of immediate context. However, EF is typically assessed in the presence of an experimenter, and little is known about how this presence shapes performance. We examined the developmental trajectory of experimenter presence effects on children's EF and their modulation by working memory demands. French children aged 4-8 years (N = 54, 17 boys, 37 girls, majority White and upper-middle SES) completed a Go/no-Go task in which working memory load was orthogonally manipulated, both in the presence and absence of the experimenter. Children were slower and made fewer errors when the experimenter was present. Exploratory order analyses showed that these effects were stronger when the experimenter presence condition was completed first, particularly among younger children. Subsequent drift diffusion modeling indicated that the order-dependent effects of experimenter presence were associated with increased nondecision time, with modest evidence and little evidence for changes in evidence accumulation and response caution, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate that children's EF performance in a canonical task is shaped by their immediate social context.
