items.title: Spatiotemporal variations and influencing factors of highly pathogenic avian influenza risk in the Pan-Tibetan Plateau region.
items.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is a major infectious disease threatening the poultry industry and public health severely. The spatiotemporal patterns and driving forces, however, remain elusive in the Tibetan Plateau and its vicinity, an ecologically critical corridor for migratory birds. This study aims to identify the factors driving these variations and to assess the HPAI risk in wild birds and domestic poultry across this region. Based on HPAI records from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the Official Veterinary Bulletin and 34 potential drivers in the Pan-Tibetan Plateau (PTP), comprising Xizang Autonomous Region (XZ), Qinghai Province (QH), Gansu Province (GS), Sichuan Province (SC), Yunnan Province (YN) and Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region (XJ), this study utilized the MaxEnt models to simulate spatial patterns of HPAI risk of wild birds, domestic poultry, and the integration of both, and identify key risk factors. Performances of models for wild birds and domestic poultry models were robust (both Test AUC values > 0.9). Although the mixed model performed acceptably overall, it significantly underestimated the infection risk in wild birds. High-risk areas of wild birds HPAI were concentrated in XZ, QH, GS and XJ (> 93%), showing a close relationship with natural factors like slope and distance to water sources. Conversely, those for domestic poultry were mainly distributed in YN, SC, GS (about 70%) and the peripheries of provincial capitals, dominated by socioeconomic variables such as gross domestic product and road networks. Moreover, overlapping HPAI risk areas were found in GS, XJ, XZ, and QH, which may be associated with increasing poultry production and fragmented wetland landscape. Additionally, it's recommended that HPAI risk modeling be stratified by host types, particularly in areas with sparse surveillance data. HPAI risks in wild birds and domestic poultry are dominated by natural factors and socioeconomic conditions respectively, and overlapping high-risk areas require focused attention. This study contributes to the understanding of HPAI transmission mechanisms in different hosts, providing a scientific basis for differentiated surveillance in the PTP.

items.title: Retention of graphene-reinforced polymethyl methacrylate crowns bonded to titanium-base abutments: an exploratory in vitro study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the effects of resin cement type, chemical surface pretreatment, and their interaction on maximum pull-out force and residual-cement distribution in graphene-reinforced polymethyl methacrylate crowns bonded to titanium-base abutments. Twenty-four CAD-CAM crowns were distributed among four protocols (n = 6): Multilink Hybrid Abutment or RelyX Unicem 2, each with or without chemical pretreatment. Pretreatment comprised Monobond Plus on titanium and SR Connect on the crown intaglio surface. After cementation, specimens were stored dry for 1 week at 20 °C and underwent axial pull-out testing at 1 mm/min. Maximum pull-out force was reported in N. A 2 × 2 factorial analysis assessed cement, pretreatment, and their interaction; heteroscedasticity-robust HC3 inference was used as a sensitivity analysis. Welch analysis of variance and Games-Howell comparisons were retained as exploratory protocol-level analyses. Residual-cement scores were analysed using Fisher's exact test (α = 0.05). Mean maximum pull-out force was 452.9 ± 74.0 N for Multilink Hybrid Abutment with pretreatment (Group A), 688.7 ± 185.1 N for RelyX Unicem 2 with pretreatment (Group B), 400.7 ± 94.7 N for Multilink Hybrid Abutment without pretreatment (Group C), and 366.8 ± 82.4 N for RelyX Unicem 2 without pretreatment (Group D). The cement × pretreatment interaction was significant (F = 7.86; P = 0.011; partial η² = 0.282) and remained significant with HC3 robust inference (interaction coefficient, 269.7 N; 95% CI, 49.9 to 489.5 N; P = 0.019). Residual-cement distributions differed among protocols (Fisher exact P < 0.001). The significant cement × pretreatment interaction indicates that the effect of chemical pretreatment depended on the resin cement. The estimated increase associated with pretreatment was 52.2 N for Multilink Hybrid Abutment and 321.9 N for RelyX Unicem 2; these exploratory estimates should be interpreted in light of the small sample size and wide confidence intervals. Within the limitations of this exploratory in vitro study, chemical pretreatment showed a cement-dependent association with maximum pull-out force. The largest increase was observed with RelyX Unicem 2. Pretreatment was also associated with a shift in residual-cement distribution toward mixed failure patterns.

items.title: Impact of improved access to medications for opioid use disorder in residential treatment.
items.abstract: Health officials in the United States (USA) are seeking strategies to mitigate overdose mortality. Medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) are effective but underused in residential treatment centers. We used a simulation model to investigate population-level health and health economic impacts of requiring residential treatment centers to offer MOUD to patients with opioid use disorder (OUD). We used a cohort state-transition model in Massachusetts, USA, simulating 4 strategies: (1) status quo - a small fraction of residential centers offers MOUD; (2) 'Improved MOUD' - all residential centers routinely offer MOUD to admitted patients; (3) 'Improved MOUD with linkage' - adding linkage to outpatient MOUD for those discharged on MOUD; and (4) 'Improved MOUD with extended linkage' - adding linkage for all patients being discharged. We used two complementary simulation approaches: a closed cohort estimating per-person outcomes for residential treatment patients and an open cohort estimating state-level impacts across the Massachusetts OUD population. Outcomes included person-time on MOUD, overdose fatalities, costs (2024 US dollars), cost-effectiveness and budgetary impact. In the closed cohort, compared with the status quo, the 'Improved MOUD' strategy increased person-time in MOUD by 36% and prevented 5 [95% uncertainty interval (UI) = 1-6] overdose deaths per 10 000 individuals at one year. Over a lifetime horizon, this strategy extended life expectancy by 0.0041 life-years (LY) and discounted quality-adjusted life expectancy by 0.0034 quality-adjusted life-years (QALY) at an incremental lifetime cost per person of $309. 'Improved MOUD with extended linkage' was the preferred strategy, providing more LY (0.0096) and QALY (0.0080) at lower incremental cost ($198). The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio compared with the status quo was $40 195/QALY gained. At the state level, this strategy prevented 2.64 (95% UI = 0.49-4.76) overdose deaths per 10 000 individuals over 10 years (a 0.40% reduction). The 5-year budgetary impact to the Massachusetts health care system of providing MOUD in residential treatment was $9.65 million. Findings were robust in sensitivity analyses; however, there is some risk of unintended consequences should facilities choose to close rather than offer MOUD. In a scenario in which 21% of sites closed (reflecting centers that discourage MOUD) outcomes were worse than under the status quo. Residential treatment programs for opioid use disorder appear to be an effective and cost-effective venue for expanding the use of medications for opioid use disorder, with the greatest value achieved when care navigation links patients to community-based treatment upon discharge.

items.title: Pharmaceutical Industry Pay-Per-Click Advertising Strategies to Influence Public Opinions on Drug Pricing.
items.abstract: This analysis characterizes the magnitude, timing, and keyword targeting strategies of the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America's (PhRMA) pay-per-click advertising expenditures and their relation to major drug pricing policy developments (2019-2025). Pay-per-click advertising allows advertisers to purchase prominent placement in search engine results, allowing their content to appear above organic results when users search for specific terms. We extracted pay-per-click advertising data from Semrush, a commercial digital marketing intelligence platform, for the domain www.phrma.org from February 2019 through December 2025. We classified keywords into mutually exclusive categories using a specificity-based pattern-matching algorithm and categorized landing-page URLs by content theme using URL string matching. We analyzed monthly spending against a timeline of major legislative and regulatory events. PhRMA spent an estimated $58.8 million across 283,517 keyword instances, generating 17.1 million paid visits to phrma.org and its subdomains. Insurance and health plan keywords dominated spending ($32.4 million; 55.1%), including general and non-health insurance terms. Nearly half of total expenditures (47.5%; $27.9 million) drove traffic to pages classified as criticizing pharmacy benefit managers. Monthly spending showed little linear association with the selected Google Trends index (r = -0.05), but spending surged around well-publicized US legislative and regulatory actions, peaking at $4.8 million in May 2023; March-September 2023 accounted for 36.5% of total spending. Overall, PhRMA pay-per-click spending surges coincided with major US drug pricing policy developments.

items.title: A retrospective cohort analysis of risk of drug overdose deaths among US Vietnam War-era veterans, 1979-2021.
items.abstract: Drug use among United States military veterans has clinical and public health implications. This study determined the risk of post-military service drug overdose mortality (1979-2021) among all veterans who served in the military during the 1961-1975 Vietnam War-era. This retrospective cohort study compared the risk of drug overdose mortality among all United States military veterans that served in Vietnam during the Vietnam War (theater veterans) to that of all veterans who served during the Vietnam War but not in Vietnam (non-theater). This comprehensive population assessment included veterans born between 1900 and 1958, alive as of 1979 and with military service between 1961 and 1975. Participants included 9 496 285 Vietnam War-era veterans (2 443 567 theater; 7 052 718 non-theater). Mortality outcomes included all, accidental and intentional drug overdoses (1979-2021) and drug overdoses involving opioids and/or stimulants (1999-2021). Drug overdose mortality risks were assessed using Cox Proportional Hazards models that generated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) adjusted for covariates. Trends of overdose mortality rates over time for theater vs. non-theater veterans were assessed by calculating average annual percent change (AAPC) in crude rates/100 000 persons (CRs). Average age at baseline approximately 33 years. Most veterans were male (~97%), Caucasian (>75%) and Army (~50%). There were 9148 theater veteran drug overdose deaths (CR = 10.01) and 33 322 among non-theater veterans (CR = 12.87). Compared with non-theater veterans, theater veterans had increased risks of all drug overdose mortality (HR = 1.03, P < 0.0001; 95% CI = 1.01-1.06) and accidental drug overdose mortality (6427; 23 347, respectively) (HR = 1.08, P < 0.0001; 95% CI = 1.05-1.12); risk of intentional drug overdose mortality was lower (1683; 6435, respectively) (HR = 0.90, P < 0.001; 95% CI = 0.85-0.95). Theater veterans had increased risk of accidental drug overdose deaths involving opioids without stimulants (HR = 1.10, P = 0.0005; 95% CI = 1.04-1.17), stimulants without opioids (HR = 1.20, P < 0.0001; 95% CI = 1.12-1.29) and opioids and/or stimulants (HR = 1.13, P < 0.0001; 95% CI = 1.08-1.17). CRs for all drug overdose mortality (1979-2021) increased for theater veterans (CR = 4.06, 1979; CR = 15.48, 2021; AAPC = 2.70, P < 0.001) and non-theater veterans (CR = 4.32, 1979; CR = 24.05, 2021; AAPC = 3.94, P < 0.001). Theater and non-theater veterans had increased CRs of overdose deaths (1999-2021) involving stimulants without opioids (AAPC = 5.30, P < 0.013 and AAPC = 6.28, P < 0.006, respectively). United States military veterans who served in Vietnam during the Vietnam War have a small increased risk of drug overdose mortality compared with veterans who did not serve in Vietnam.

items.title: Influence of different sagittal split osteotomy techniques on bone contact in mandibular advancement: a double-blind randomized clinical trial.
items.abstract: This randomized, double-blind, single-center controlled clinical trial compared sagittal split osteotomy (SSO, Dal Pont modification as refined by Epker) and anterior oblique osteotomy (AOO) in terms of lingual split patterns and bone contact area (BCA) following mandibular advancement. The study included 52 patients (104 osteotomies) with skeletal class II facial and occlusal patterns who underwent orthognathic surgery. Fracture patterns were classified according to Plooij (2009) into four types using Lingual Split Scale (LSS). The magnitude of point B advancement and BCA between proximal and distal segments were measured using Dolphin Imaging software. The SSO group demonstrated a significantly greater BCA compared to the AOO group (P < 0.001). The magnitude of mandibular advancement (P = 0.14) and execution time (P = 0.081) were similar between groups. However, the distribution of lingual cortical split patterns differed significantly (P < 0.001). In the SSO group, LSS3 fractures predominated, followed by LSS1, whereas the AOO group showed a higher prevalence of LSS1 fractures, followed by LSS2 and LSS3. Although no absolute superiority of either technique was observed, SSO resulted in greater BCA and may therefore be considered the preferred technique for large mandibular advancements.

items.title: A positive maternal anti-red blood cell antibody test: A critical alert for neonatal bilirubin neurotoxicity.
items.abstract: A positive maternal anti-red blood cell (RBC) antibody test is a critical indicator of postnatal isoimmune hemolytic disease and risk of neonatal bilirubin neurotoxicity. Though rare, it remains consequential. Rh negativity and a positive anti-RBC test reveal a high-risk pregnancy that can lead to hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN), requiring supervised skilled perinatal and neonatal expertise. Thus, public health systems have mandated policies to minimize severe postnatal adverse outcomes such as symptomatic postnatal anemia and hemolytic hyperbilirubinemia -a neurotoxic risk factor. Review of interviews with families of alloimmunized mothers have revealed concerns of inconsistent prenatal education of potential postnatal sequelae. Many felt inadequate to cope with a premature infant and needs for intensive care, repeated blood testing, prolonged phototherapy, breastfeeding disruption, and blood transfusions or possible exchange transfusions. Therefore, expert and skilled counseling throughout the pregnancy and at birthing are especially needed with interpreting test results. Specific "hand-off" at birthing of the pivotal test result of anti-RBC antibody is essential. Partnering of both perinatal-neonatal teams with families should increase parental education so that they can monitor their own baby's well-being to ensure a healthy childhood and school age outcomes.

items.title: Visual, hearing, and dual sensory impairment and risk of dementia: The role of social isolation, depressive symptoms, and cognitive function.
items.abstract: Sensory impairment (SI), including visual impairment (VI), hearing impairment (HI), and dual sensory impairment (DSI), is common in aging adults and associated with increased dementia risk. Older adults with SI often have poorer cognition, a predictor of dementia. We investigated associations of VI, HI, and DSI with incident dementia while accounting for baseline cognition, and assessed indirect pathways through cognition, social isolation, and depressive symptoms. 51,584 UK biobank participants aged 60-70 years with objectively measured visual and hearing function were followed for incident dementia for a mean of 12.1 years. VI was defined as visual acuity worse than 0.30 LogMAR in better-seeing eye; HI as speech-reception threshold in noise greater than -5.5 dB; DSI as both VI and HI. Cognition was assessed using pairs matching and reaction time tests. Dementia was ascertained through linked medical records and death registries RESULTS: After adjustment for cognition and covariates, VI, HI, and DSI remained associated with increased incident dementia risk. Direct-effect HRs were 1.33 for VI, 1.37 for HI, and 2.21 for DSI (all p < 0.05). VI, HI and DSI were also indirectly associated with dementia through depressive symptoms, social isolation, and cognition. The total indirect effect of DSI through all mediators increased dementia risk by 10.5%. VI, HI, and DSI were associated with dementia risk through direct and indirect pathways. Findings support prevention and treatment of VI and HI as potentially modifiable dementia risk factors, and highlight integrated sensory, cognitive, and psychosocial approaches for dementia prevention and healthy aging.

items.title: The independent and joint impact of social and internet isolation on depression and loneliness among older adults: evidence from cross-cultural cohort studies.
items.abstract: This study examined independent and joint associations of social and internet isolation with incident depression and loneliness among older adults in two culturally distinct cohorts. This study utilized data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA, N = 3536) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, N = 3120). Cox proportional hazards regression models were applied to assess the independent and joint effects of social and internet isolation on depression and loneliness. Additionally, a random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to examine heterogeneity across different cultural contexts. In both ELSA and CHARLS cohorts, social isolation was more strongly associated with loneliness (ELSA: HR = 2.36, 95% CI: 1.81-3.09; CHARLS: HR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.21-2.05), whereas internet isolation showed a stronger association with depression (ELSA: HR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.05-1.58; CHARLS: HR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.11-2.23). Both forms of isolation independently contributed to elevated risks of depression and loneliness. Participants experiencing both forms of isolation had the highest risks of depression and loneliness, particularly in the ELSA cohort. The results were consistent with social support theory and extended the understanding of the association between social and internet isolation and mental health outcomes.

items.title: Validation of the SPiRO Score for the Prediction of ICU Admission in Patients Presenting With Leptospirosis in Tropical Australia.
items.abstract: In some resource-limited settings the case-fatality rate of severe leptospirosis can exceed 50%. Early recognition of severe disease can expedite transfer to referral centres for advanced supportive care. The entirely clinical, 3-point SPiRO score can be calculated rapidly at presentation to predict a patient's subsequent clinical course. In its derivation study, a SPiRO score of 0 had a negative predictive value (NPV) for intensive care unit (ICU) admission of 98% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 96-99). In this validation cohort we sought to confirm the SPiRO score's prognostic utility and to compare its performance to other leptospirosis-specific and general disease severity scores. We examined consecutive adults presenting to four high-caseload hospitals in tropical Australia with laboratory-confirmed leptospirosis between June 2016 and April 2026. The SPiRO score's ability to predict ICU admission before hospital discharge was compared with that of the leptospirosis-specific QuickLepto score and commonly used disease severity scores, namely the SOFA, qSOFA, qSOFA-lactate, NEWS-2, qNEWS, UVA and the SIRS scores. There were no deaths in 309 episodes of leptospirosis, but in 62 (20%) there was an ICU admission. The SPiRO score performed as well as, or better than, all the other scores in predicting ICU admission. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the SPiRO score was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.77-0.89); only the SOFA score had a higher value: 0.84 (0.79-0.90), although the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.08). The SPiRO score had the highest NPV for ICU admission of any of the scores: 95 (95% CI: 91-97)%. The SPiRO score can be calculated easily at the bedside at presentation to expedite the recognition of patients with leptospirosis who are most likely to deteriorate. In resource-limited settings this entirely clinical score can also help reduce unnecessary escalation of care, optimising the use of finite health resources.

items.title: Understanding barriers to HIV testing during pregnancy among women who attended ANC in Soweto, Johannesburg: a socio-ecological perspective.
items.abstract: Vertical transmission of HIV remains a significant challenge to maternal and child health in high burden settings. Early identification of maternal HIV status enables timely antiretroviral therapy initiation and helps prevent transmission during pregnancy, childbirth, and breastfeeding. This study explored barriers to HIV testing uptake among pregnant and postpartum women attending antenatal care (ANC) services in Soweto, Johannesburg. A qualitative research design was employed, involving in-depth interviews with ten adult women who accessed ANC services. Data were analysed thematically using Atlas.ti 23 software. Findings revealed multilevel barriers across the socio-ecological spectrum. At the individual level, fear of HIV testing and its potential outcomes discouraged uptake. Interpersonal factors, particularly partner and family influences, shaped women's testing decisions. Institutional barriers included negative healthcare providers attitudes, inadequate privacy, and insufficient counselling. At the community level, stigma amd discrimination discouraged HIV testing, while systematic barriers included gaps in implementing and enforcing HIV testing policies. These findings highlight the need for intergrated interventions addressing individual, interpersonal, community, institutional and systemic barriers. Strengthening confidentiality, improving healthcare provider communications, reducing stigma and enhancing policy implementation may improve HIV testing uptake among pregnant and postpartum women and streghthen maternal HIV prevention services.

items.title: Characteristics, Implementation and Effects of Nurse-Driven Sepsis Protocols in Hospital Settings: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: To synthesize evidence on the characteristics, implementation and effects of nurse-driven sepsis protocols on process-of-care indicators and clinical outcomes. Systematic review without meta-analysis. Studies were included if they described and evaluated nurse-driven sepsis protocols in hospitals. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts and full texts for eligibility. The Johns Hopkins Nursing Evidence-Based Practice model was used to appraise included studies. Data were extracted and narratively synthesized. Eight databases were searched from database inception to 30 June 2025. Fifteen studies were included, most using before-and-after designs and conducted in the emergency departments (n = 7) and hospital-wide settings (n = 4). Protocols commonly used systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria for screening (n = 12) and incorporated key Surviving Sepsis Campaign recommendations (n = 14). Most studies reported improved or comparable outcomes to baseline in overall sepsis bundle compliance and key process-of-care indicators, including timely antibiotic administration, blood culture collection, lactate measurement and fluid administration. All 11 studies evaluating mortality reported reductions, although only four were statistically significant. Findings for hospital length of stay were inconsistent. Common implementation strategies included nurse education and training, coupled with audit and feedback. Nurse-driven sepsis protocols may improve adherence to and timeliness of key sepsis care processes. Effects on clinical outcomes are less certain, given the predominance of before-and-after designs and inconsistent findings for hospital length of stay. The review identifies implementation strategies that can guide future sepsis quality improvement initiatives. Nurse-driven protocols may support nurses in initiating timely sepsis care and strengthening adherence to recommended care processes. Further high-quality studies are needed to establish effects on clinical outcomes and broader impacts, including healthcare costs, intensive care resource utilization, patient and nurse satisfaction, and safety outcomes. No patient or public contribution.

items.title: Survey-Weighted Explainable Gradient Boosting for Regional Disparities in PHQ-9-Defined Depression in Korea: 2024 Korea Community Health Survey.
items.abstract: To analyze regional disparities in depression defined by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) among Korean adults using spatial statistics and survey-weighted prediction models based on the 2024 Korea Community Health Survey (KCHS), and to visualize region-specific contributing factors using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) METHODS: This cross-sectional secondary analysis evaluated 231,469 respondents. Survey weights were applied to logistic regression, XGBoost, and LightGBM models to classify concurrent depression status, operationally defined as a PHQ-9 score of 10 or higher. Spatial autocorrelation was assessed using global Moran's I and Local Indicators of Spatial Association. SHAP values quantified global feature importance and the spatial heterogeneity of dominant positive mean contributors across 250 harmonized municipal units RESULTS: The national weighted prevalence of PHQ-9-defined depression was 4.1 percent, with weak positive global spatial autocorrelation and regional variation ranging from 0.9 percent to 8.2 percent. In the independent test set, LightGBM achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.92, an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.43, and a Brier score of 0.03. No local association remained significant after false discovery rate correction. SHAP analysis identified perceived stress, subjective happiness, and subjective health status as the most influential global predictors. Mapping revealed spatial heterogeneity: perceived stress was the most frequent dominant positive mean contributor, whereas other municipal units showed subjective health status, subjective happiness, smoking status, sleep duration, income, and other contributors. Regional contributor rank retention varied across bootstrap samples (median, 72.5%). Psychosocial and structural characteristics contributed to concurrent classification of PHQ-9-defined depression, with exploratory geographic variation in aggregated SHAP contributions. Combining explainable machine learning with spatial statistics may inform further local assessment. This study was exempted from review by the Institutional Review Board of Kangbuk Samsung Hospital (KBSMC IRB No. 2026-02-008).

items.title: Perceptions of living with drug-resistant epilepsy and the potential role of neuropalliative care.
items.abstract: To assess quality of life factors in persons with drug-resistant epilepsy (PWDRE) and determine if PWDRE would be interested in palliative/neuropalliative care involvement. For this qualitative study, adults living with DRE (n=20) participated in semi-structured interviews regarding personal identity, relationships, medical care, and needs related to living with epilepsy. Participants were introduced to the term "palliative care" (PC) and queried on its potential usefulness within their regular medical care. Responses were coded thematically. Clinical data were extracted from medical records. Most participants felt DRE had significantly affected their perception of self, family, and social life. Ongoing concerns included loss of independence and uncertainty related to their epilepsy. The main sources of strength were close relationships and faith. Most (90%) expressed a desire for more information and education from their medical providers about epilepsy, the diagnostic process, medical and surgical therapies, and psychosocial issues. Most (80%) had not established advance directives. Prior to this study, few (20%) could accurately define PC. After being educated about PC, about half thought it could be useful in their care, especially in times of worsening seizures, before surgery, or when confronting major life decisions. Many PWDRE expressed an interest in the potential benefit of palliative care involvement in addition to their routine medical care. Gaps in communication, complex symptom management, and advance directives could be addressed with inclusion of PC approaches and collaboration with a PC team, though further research is needed to demonstrate benefit.

items.title: Serum urate and the risk of incident osteoarthritis: A prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Serum urate has been implicated in joint inflammation and may contribute to osteoarthritis (OA) development. This study aimed to examine the associations between serum urate and the incidence of knee, hip, and hand OA in a large population-based cohort. This prospective cohort study included 43,1530 UK Biobank participants (mean age 56 years, 55% women) who were free of knee, hip, and hand OA at baseline with available serum urate measurements. Both linear and non-linear associations between serum urate levels and incident OA were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Potential mediation by biomarker of inflammation (IL-β, IL6, CRP, and TNF) and cartilage metabolism (CILP, COMP, CRATC1, and MMP1) was evaluated. Over a median follow-up of 14 years, 29,686 (6.88%), 19,040 (4.41%), and 11,696 (2.76%) participants developed knee, hip, and hand OA, respectively. Per 1 standard deviation increase serum urate was associated with a higher risk of incident OA (knee: hazard ratio [HR]=1.08, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.06-1.10; hip: HR=1.05, 95% CI: 1.03-1.07; hand: HR=1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.07). Non-linear associations were not observed for hip or hand OA, whereas a non-linear association was identified for knee OA. The relationships between serum urate and the risk of OA were partially mediated by inflammatory (proportion of mediation: 4.21%-15.14%) and cartilage metabolism biomarkers (proportion of mediation: 3.86%-16.33%). Higher serum urate was associated with an increased risk of OA across knee, hip, and hand joints. Inflammatory and cartilage metabolic pathways may partly mediate this relationship.

items.title: Inarigivir Exhibits RIG-I-Independent Antiviral Activity Against HBV DNA Replication in vitro by Inhibiting Viral Polymerase Activity.
items.abstract: Inarigivir (SB 9200) is a linear dinucleotide antiviral drug designed to act as a RIG-I agonist, activating cellular innate immune responses. Clinical trials in hepatitis C virus (HCV) patients have confirmed the innate immune-activating antiviral activity of Inarigivir. In hepatitis B virus (HBV) patients, clinical trials using Inarigivir have demonstrated significant reductions in HBV DNA and RNA levels, although heterogeneous drug-induced liver injury has been observed at higher doses. To further explore Inarigivir's mechanism of action against HBV, we characterized its antiviral effect in various hepatocyte-derived cell lines, including transiently transfected HepG2 and Huh7 cells, inducible HBV stable cell lines HepAD38 and HepDES19, and HBV-infected human hepatocytes. Our results show that Inarigivir inhibits HBV DNA replication in a dose-dependent manner without affecting HBV RNA levels or pgRNA encapsidation. HBV RNA immunoprecipitation assays revealed that Inarigivir does not affect viral polymerase binding to pgRNA, while the in vitro endogenous polymerase reaction (EPR) assays demonstrated that Inarigivir inhibits HBV DNA synthesis catalyzed by polymerase within the capsid. Additionally, we provided several lines of evidence indicating that Inarigivir's antiviral effect is independent of the RIG-I signalling pathway in hepatocyte-derived cells. Taken together, our study demonstrates a RIG-I-independent antiviral mechanism of Inarigivir by inhibiting HBV DNA replication as a dinucleosidic non-chain-terminating reverse transcriptase inhibitor.

items.title: An updated systematic review finds variable uptake of core outcome sets across different areas of health.
items.abstract: Research waste occurs when researchers do not measure relevant outcomes or when similar studies on a healthcare condition report inconsistent outcomes. A core outcome set (COS) is developed for a particular health condition to ensure that outcomes meaningful to decision-makers, including patients, are measured consistently across similar studies, which can improve comparison and facilitate easier translation of research to practice. Failure to use COS however means COS development itself will contribute to research waste. The aim of this systematic review update is to identify studies evaluating COS uptake and explore the level of uptake across different areas of health. The original review, published in 2021, identified 26 studies covering COS uptake in randomized controlled trials (RCTs; n=24) and systematic reviews (n=2) for COS published upto 2018. We searched the COMET database for studies reporting the uptake of any published COS irrespective of the study design, context or setting. Two authors independently screened the articles to identify relevant studies and discussed with another author in case of disagreements. Data extraction was performed by one reviewer and verified by another reviewer. We developed a new tool to assess the risk of bias in COS uptake studies. We identified 30 new studies in this update reporting the uptake of 42 COS in: RCTs (n=25, 83%), systematic reviews (n=3, 10%) and other studies (n=2, 7%). In this updated review comprising 56 studies, the full uptake of COS ranged from 0% to 82%, median 9% (38 out of the eligible 53 studies of COS developed for research). In relation to the risk of bias, 91% (n=48) used an appropriate time since COS publication for evaluating uptake, and 81% (n= 43) had a low risk of bias for scope matching between the COS and the studies which should have used the COS. The number of health conditions where COS uptake has been studied has increased but the level of uptake remains relatively low. Researchers performing COS uptake studies should be aware of the potential risk of bias that can occur; there is room for improvement in matching the scope of the COS to the studies assessed.

items.title: Urine drug testing practices at Opioid Treatment Programs in a large health system, 2018-2025.
items.abstract: The COVID-19 public health emergency prompted substantial changes in opioid treatment program (OTP) practices, including expanded methadone take-home dosing and telehealth use. While many of these changes persisted after the emergency period, less is known about how urine drug testing practices were altered and whether any changes were sustained over time. We examined monthly trends in urine drug testing among patients receiving methadone for opioid use disorder at 112 OTP clinics operated by a large national treatment organization. Administrative electronic medical record data from January 2018 through June 2025 were used to construct patient-level testing measures. A testing event was defined as any day in which a patient received at least one urine drug test. Interrupted time series analyses assessed changes in the level and trend of average monthly testing at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020. In January 2018, patients were tested 1.13 days a month on average. Testing frequencies increased by 0.003 days per month on average until February 2020 (p = 0.016). In the first two months of the COVID-19 pandemic testing frequency decreased to 1.00-1.02 days per month (about an 11% decline (p = 0.006)). Testing levels returned to pre-pandemic levels by May 2020. They trended slightly downward through the end of the study period and were at 1.14 days on average in June 2025 (p = 0.033). Urine drug testing frequency modestly decreased during the first months of the COVID-19 pandemic but quickly returned to pre-pandemic levels. This may reflect the fact that urine drug testing regulations for OTPs were not changed as part of broader post-pandemic federal regulatory reforms. Future research should focus on how to best tailor urine drug testing practices to improve patient engagement, safety, and recovery.

items.title: Heart Failure Care in Greece: A Call for Action.
items.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major public health challenge in Greece, affecting an estimated 300,000 individuals and imposing a substantial burden through high mortality, recurrent hospitalizations, impaired quality of life, and escalating healthcare costs. Although significant advances in pharmacological therapies, device-based interventions, and multidisciplinary care have improved outcomes in recent years, important gaps persist in the implementation of evidence-based HF care across the country. This viewpoint from the Heart Failure Working Group of the Hellenic Society of Cardiology (HCS) highlights five strategic priorities for the development of a comprehensive national HF strategy. First, improving the recognition and diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), an increasingly prevalent and frequently underdiagnosed condition, through greater awareness, structured diagnostic pathways, and the adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. Second, strengthening the national advanced HF network by establishing coordinated referral pathways and equitable access to advanced therapies such as heart transplantation and durable left ventricular assist devices. Third, integrating palliative care into routine HF management to address symptom burden, psychosocial needs, and advance care planning throughout the disease trajectory. Fourth, expanding access to cardiac rehabilitation through hospital-based, community-based, and home-based programs capable of overcoming geographical disparities and improving functional outcomes. Fifth, developing a specialized HF nursing workforce through structured education and certification programs aligned with European standards. Collectively, these interconnected priorities provide a framework for advancing and modernizing HF care in Greece. A national HF registry is proposed as the foundational infrastructure supporting all five priorities.

items.title: Microplastic exposure and obesity-related metabolic dysfunction: A proposed gut microbiota-metabolite framework.
items.abstract: Microplastics (MPs), as emerging global contaminants, have infiltrated aquatic systems, soil, and food chains, raising concerns about their health risks, particularly their potential link to metabolic disorders like obesity. This review evaluates evidence that MP exposure may influence host energy metabolism and adipogenesis and examines the potential involvement of the gut microbiota and its metabolites. Dietary MP exposure can alter microbial communities and associated metabolic pathways. Such dysbiosis may impair intestinal barrier integrity, trigger chronic inflammation, and promote adipose dysfunction, thereby potentially contributing to obesity-related metabolic disturbances. We synthesize findings from animal studies, in vitro models, and multi-omics approaches, highlighting the roles of MP physicochemical properties, exposure dose, and duration in obesity-related metabolic effects. Current limitations include insufficient long-term assessments at environmentally relevant concentrations, uncertainties in cross-species extrapolation, and unclear interactions with co-pollutants. Future studies could combine organ-on-a-chip (OoC) models with microbial and host single-cell or spatial approaches to test microbiota-host crosstalk. Overall, this review synthesizes emerging evidence on the potential links between MP exposure and adipogenesis dysregulation and identifies priorities for future mechanistic research and risk assessment.

items.title: Culturally adapted exercise training intervention for Hispanics/Latinos with multiple sclerosis: Study protocol for a hybrid type 1 implementation randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Hispanics with multiple sclerosis (MS) have worse walking mobility and health-related quality of life (QOL) than non-Hispanic white counterparts. Hispanics further receive less specialty care and have low physical activity rates. Exercise training can improve MS symptoms, including mobility and QOL, but there are few RCTs of exercise training programs in Hispanics with MS. The moVement for Advancing Mobility and Strength in MS (VAMOS-MS) study is a hybrid type 1 implementation randomized control trial that culturally adapts the Guidelines for Exercise in MS (GEMS) intervention for Hispanics with MS. The primary outcome is walking dysfunction, measured using the MSWS-12; the secondary outcome is Health-Related QOL (HRQOL), measured by the MSIS-29. Implementation outcomes include measures of Acceptability, Appropriateness, Feasibility, Adoption, and Sustainability. Exercise behavior will be measured using the Godin Leisure Time Exercise Questionnaire (GLTEQ). Following the baseline assessment, participants will be randomized to the 16-week GEMS exercise training condition or the 16-week waitlist control. Participants will receive materials, equipment, and coaching calls with a trained Community Health worker (CHW). Outcomes will be measured at baseline, 16 weeks, and 32 weeks. The data analysis will be conducted using the intent-to-treat principle, with linear mixed models including an interaction term between condition and time. Implementation outcomes will be analyzed using descriptive and qualitative methods. VAMOS-MS is a culturally adapted, home-based exercise training program for Hispanics with MS. It incorporates community feedback to inform the adaptation and implementation of an evidence-based exercise training program for scalability among Hispanics with MS.

items.title: A coaching and feedback intervention to improve responsive feeding and child dietary intake in rural family child care homes: Protocol for a cluster randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Rural family childcare homes (FCCHs) are important settings for improving young children's dietary intake, yet rural providers face structural and training barriers to implementing responsive feeding practices. This cluster randomized controlled trial will enroll 120 rural FCCH providers and approximately 240 children aged 3-5 years in Nebraska and Kansas. Providers will be randomized to EAT Family Style intervention, a 16-week package of seven online responsive-feeding modules and individualized Cooperative Extension coaching with video-based feedback, or Better Kid Care standard-practice online professional development. Assessments will occur at baseline, post-intervention (16 weeks), and early maintenance follow-up (24 weeks). The primary child outcome is observed combined fruit and vegetable intake during childcare. Secondary and exploratory child outcomes include overall diet quality assessed using the Healthy Eating Index; intake of five food groups-whole grains, protein foods, vegetables, fruits, and dairy; skin carotenoid scores; and BMI-for-age z-scores. Provider outcomes include observed and self-reported feeding practices and mealtime emotional climate. RE-AIM-informed process measures will guide evaluation of reach, adoption, implementation dose and fidelity, and maintenance. Linear mixed-effects models will estimate condition-by-time effects while accounting for repeated measures and clustering. Multilevel mediation analyses will examine whether provider motivational capacity, responsive feeding practices, and mealtime emotional climate help explain effects on child dietary outcomes. The study evaluates the effectiveness of a theory-informed, workforce-embedded responsive-feeding package relative to standard online professional development and will inform future dissemination in rural early care and education settings.

items.title: Col23a1 acts as an ECM-resident signal to drive DDR1-p38/ERK-dependent EMT in antimony-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
items.abstract: Antimony (Sb) exposure causes pulmonary fibrosis, but the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Using a chronic Sb exposure mouse model combined with single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified Col23a1 as a highly and specifically expressed collagen in alveolar epithelial type II (AEC II) cells, with its expression correlating with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Further analysis demonstrated that Col23a1 was enriched in the extracellular matrix (ECM), where it engaged discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) to activate p38 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation, thereby driving EMT in AECs. Protein-protein interaction screening identified P4HA1 as a Col23a1-interacting candidate and that molecular docking supported a potential interaction. Functionally, P4HA1 stabilized Col23a1 and promoted its ECM deposition, while DDR1-p38/ERK signaling reciprocally sustained P4HA1 expression, forming a self-amplifying positive feedback loop. Pharmacological inhibition of DDR1 or p38/ERK and P4HA1 knockdown each attenuated Sb-induced EMT in AECs. Importantly, AEC-specific Col23a1 knockdown via AAV6-SPC-shCol23a1 in mice substantially reduced fibrotic remodeling and EMT in vivo, and ECM from Col23a1-knockdown lungs failed to induce EMT in naïve epithelial cells, confirming that ECM-resident Col23a1 is the functional component driving this fibrotic signal. Collectively, these findings establish a Col23a1-DDR1-p38/ERK self-amplifying axis as a driver of Sb-induced pulmonary fibrosis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding the pulmonary toxicity of Sb and identifying this axis as a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Access to pharmacological management for osteoporosis in older people with hip fractures in long-term care: A nationwide cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: To examine whether individuals who had a hip fracture while accessing long-term care (LTC) in a facility or at home, or were waiting for LTC, received recommended pharmacological management for osteoporosis before and in the year after fracture. A population-based cross-sectional study using the National Historical Cohort of the Registry of Senior Australians (ROSA). Older people hospitalised with a hip fracture while accessing or waiting for facility or home-based LTC in Australia between 01/01/2012 and 31/12/2018. Utilisation of pharmacological management for osteoporosis (i.e., bisphosphonates, denosumab, teriparatide, strontium) before and one year after hip fracture was examined using linked pharmaceutical, hospital, and aged care data. Logistic regression models examined the associations between individual and LTC setting characteristics and accessing pharmacological management in the year after fracture. Of the 52,233 (71.3% female, 87.7 median age) hip fractures that occurred during the study period, 58.3% (n = 30,441) in were in individuals receiving facility-based LTC, 14.6% (n = 7603) were receiving home-based LTC, and 27.2% (n = 14,189) were waiting for LTC. Forty three percent (N = 22,622 of 52,233) had received pharmacological management for osteoporosis at any time prior to hip fracture and 21% received it in the previous year. One-year post fracture, 39% of the 30,768 individuals who were still alive had received pharmacological management for osteoporosis. Older age, male gender, having dementia, receiving facility-based LTC, and not receiving pharmacological management prior to fracture were associated with lower receipt of pharmacological management after fracture. These results highlight that the use of pharmacological management for osteoporosis for older people experiencing a hip fracture while in or waiting for LTC remains low, despite clinical guideline recommendations. Of the 52,233 older Australians who had a hip fracture while receiving or waiting for long-term care between 2012 and 2018, 43% had received osteoporosis medication at any time prior to fracture. In the year after fracture, 39% of the 30,768 individuals who were still alive received osteoporosis medication. These national estimates highlight that access to pharmacolocical management for osteoporosis in long-term care recipients following hip fracture remains low, despite clinical guideline recommendations.

items.title: Saturated and Trans Fatty Acids Were Not Associated with All-Cause or Cause-Specific Mortality in a Japanese Population with Relatively Low Intakes: The Japan Public Health Center-Based Prospective Study.
items.abstract: World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines recommend that saturated fatty acids (SFAs) and trans fatty acids (TFAs) should comprise ≤10% and ≤1% of total energy intake, respectively. However, evidence of the mortality risk associated with increased TFA and SFA intake in populations with a relatively low fat intake is limited. To examine the association between total fat, SFA, TFA, monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA), and polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) intake and all-cause and cause-specific mortality in a Japanese population. We included 90,807 participants aged 45-74 years with no history of cancer or cardiovascular disease (CVD). Dietary assessment was performed using a validated food frequency questionnaire. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models for each quintile of dietary fat intake: total fat, SFA, MUFA, PUFA, TFA, industrially-derived TFA (i-TFAs), and ruminant-derived TFA (r-TFA). During a mean follow-up of 18.9 years, 22,618 deaths occurred. None of the analyses of fat intakes in quintiles showed a positive association with all-cause mortality for higher intakes of all fats, even for i-TF. In females, a nominally significant association was observed for all-cause mortality with PUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.92 [0.84-0.997]) and cancer mortality with MUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.84 [0.73-0.97]).In females, higher intakes of total fat and MUFA were nominally associated with higher respiratory disease mortality, whereas a higher SFA intake showed a suggestive association (P for trend <0.05). In this study, neither SFA nor TFA intake was positively associated with all-cause mortality, and higher PUFA intake was inversely associated with all-cause mortality in females.

items.title: Eicosapentaenoic acid in adipose tissue is associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke: A Danish case-cohort study.
items.abstract: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have been linked to a lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, however, their association with hemorrhagic stroke remains uncertain. We investigated associations between adipose tissue content of individual omega-3 PUFAs (α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosapentaenoic acid (DPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), the sum of EPA+DHA), and the risk of hemorrhagic stroke and its subtypes intracranial and subarachnoid hemorrhage. This case-cohort study based on the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health Cohort included 54,546 men and women aged 50 to 65 years at baseline (1993-1997). Adipose tissue composition of omega-3 PUFAs was determined by gas chromatography for all hemorrhagic stroke cases and within a randomly drawn subcohort of 4,615 participants. Cases were identified by linkage to the Danish National Patient Register. Hazard ratios (HR) were obtained by weighted Cox regression. During a median of 21 years follow-up, we identified 729 hemorrhagic stroke cases. In multivariable analyses, a significant inverse association between the content of EPA in adipose tissue and the risk of total hemorrhagic stroke was found. Thus, the HR for hemorrhagic stroke was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.50-0.82) when comparing the highest quintile of EPA content in adipose tissue with the lowest. Associations were similar when stratified according to sex and when investigating subtypes of hemorrhagic stroke, although findings were not statistically significant for subarachnoid hemorrhages. No statistically significant associations were observed between adipose tissue content of DHA, DPA and EPA+DHA and hemorrhagic strokes. A high content of ALA in adipose tissue was associated with a higher risk of hemorrhagic stroke (HR for quintile 5 vs. 1: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.01-1.72). A high content of EPA in adipose tissue was associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke, while a high content of ALA was associated with a higher risk in this cohort.

items.title: Metabolomic biomarkers of ultraprocessed food intake and their associations with all-cause mortality in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC).
items.abstract: Higher ultraprocessed food (UPF) intake is associated with higher mortality risk in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The mechanisms underlying this association are not fully understood. Plasma metabolites reflect endogenous metabolism and exogenous exposures and may provide insights into the biological effects of diet. We aimed to identify metabolites associated with UPF intake and examine their prospective associations with mortality. Among adults with CKD in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study (n=1226; 48% women, mean age 59 years), we assessed cross-sectional associations between UPF intake (servings/day) and 486 plasma metabolites using multivariable linear regression. UPF intake was classified according to the Nova system. Metabolites were measured using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (Broad Institute). We examined prospective associations between significant UPF-related metabolites and the risk of death using Cox proportional hazards regression models. At FDR-adjusted P<0.05, 26 metabolites were significantly associated with UPF intake. Three metabolites (C4-OH carnitine, myristoleate, and aconitate) were positively associated with UPF intake. The remaining 23 were inversely associated with UPF consumption, including several highly unsaturated (≥5 double bonds) ≥34-carbon glycerophospholipids. Over a median follow-up of 15 years (25th-75th percentile: 8-17), 539 deaths occurred. Nine UPF-related metabolites were associated with mortality (FDR-adjusted P<0.05). Highly unsaturated (≥6 double bonds) 38- and 40-carbon glycerophospholipids were among the metabolites most strongly associated with UPF intake (inversely) and with a lower risk of death. Metabolite markers of a dietary pattern rich in ultraprocessed foods may participate in metabolic pathways contributing to mortality risk in CKD.

items.title: Pandemic electronic benefit transfer benefit disbursement amounts in relation to food security and food spending among low-income U.S. households with children.
items.abstract: Pandemic Electronic Benefits Transfer (P-EBT) program benefits, which provided food money to U.S. low-income households with children, increased food spending and reduced food hardship when initially implemented. We now leverage variation in P-EBT disbursement amounts across states and over time to examine these associations across the program duration. Per capita annual P-EBT benefit amount disbursements were estimated for income-eligible children. Among low-income U.S. households with children aged 0-17 in the national Current Population Survey Food Security Supplement (2020-2023), we examined 12-month household food insecurity, child food insecurity and usual weekly food spending. Logistic and negative binomial models adjusted for household and state characteristics, accounted for state clustering, and applied survey weights to account for the complex survey design and nonresponse. Each $500 in per capita annual P-EBT benefits ($9.62 per week) was associated with a 3% more weekly food spending (IRR = 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.05) and a lower odds of household food insecurity (OR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.88, 0.99) but not child food insecurity (OR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.85, 1.02) in the following year. Findings demonstrate associations across the P-EBT program duration and have implications in support of similar programs like the recently implemented SUN Bucks program.

items.title: An Albuminuria Guided Approach to Risk Stratification and Therapeutic Decision-Making in CKD.
items.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a global public health challenge, yet therapeutic evaluation and regulatory acceptance are constrained by reliance on late clinical endpoints such as kidney failure. Albuminuria, assessed as urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) reflects glomerular and systemic vascular injury and responds rapidly to treatment. Epidemiologic evidence demonstrates a continuous, graded association between both baseline and changes in UACR and subsequent risk for kidney failure, cardiovascular events, and mortality. Trial level analyses demonstrate that treatment effects on change in UACR is also associated with long-term treatment benefit on CKD progression across drug classes and disease populations. Meta-analysis indicates that a treatment benefit of ≥30% decline in UACR is associated with approximately a 20% treatment benefit on CKD progression, supporting its use as a clinically meaningful surrogate endpoint. Residual albuminuria during treatment identifies patients at persistently high risk and provides a rationale for therapy intensification. Recent studies demonstrate that combination therapies can achieve substantial additional reductions in UACR, in selected settings exceeding 50%. This review synthesizes biological, epidemiologic, and clinical trial evidence supporting albuminuria-guided risk stratification and a treat-to-target approach using serial UACR monitoring to personalize CKD care, while improving clinician understanding of albuminuria changes as markers of therapeutic response.

items.title: [Emergencies during heat-related extreme weather events].
items.abstract: Climate change is placing an increasing burden on emergency medical care. In addition to heat-related illnesses, exacerbations of common chronic diseases and a higher incidence of injuries are major contributors to the growing number of emergency department presentations. At the same time, vector-borne diseases and other climate-related health risks are becoming increasingly relevant. Against the backdrop of demographic change, strengthening societal resilience, improving public health literacy, and implementing effective heat protection measures are of particular importance. In addition to prevention and public education, regular review of heat-sensitive medications should be considered an essential component of patient care. Overall, the health consequences of climate change are emerging as a major challenge for both prehospital and hospital emergency care, underscoring the need for timely adaptation of healthcare systems and emergency care strategies.

items.title: Effect of ethnicity on response to treatment escalation in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR): a longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Ethnic disparities in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) outcomes are well documented, but data on treatment response across ethnic groups remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate the effect of ethnicity on clinical outcomes following treatment escalation in a diverse UK cohort. In this longitudinal cohort study, we analysed data from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR), including patients recruited from 64 UK secondary and tertiary rheumatology and nephrology centres. Eligible patients were aged 16 years and older, with active moderate-to-severe SLE, defined as having at least one BILAG A score, at least two BILAG B scores, or a SLEDAI-2K score of at least 6, who had initiated rituximab or belimumab within the past 12 months, or standard immunosuppressive therapy within the past 1 month. Ethnicity was categorised as White, South Asian, Black, East Asian, or mixed or other ethnicities. The primary outcome was major clinical response (MCR) at 6 months and 12 months, measured using mixed-effects logistic regression. Individuals with lived experience of SLE were involved in the study design. Between July 1, 2010, and Nov 10, 2021, 1688 patients were recruited to the BILAG-BR. Of these, 1266 were excluded because they did not meet the study eligibility criteria, and 422 patients were included in the study. 383 (91%) patients were female, 39 (9%) were male, and the median age was 40·5 years (IQR 31·3-50·8). 245 (58%) of 422 patients were White, 77 (18%) were South Asian, 70 (17%) were Black, 19 (5%) were East Asian, and 11 (3%) were of mixed or other ethnicities. At baseline, Black patients had higher baseline disease activity, greater organ damage, and more comorbidities. At 12 months, 99 (23%) of 422 patients had met MCR criteria, including eight (42%) of 19 East Asian patients, 23 (30%) of 77 South Asian patients, 60 (24%) of 245 White patients, seven (10%) of 70 Black patients, and one (9%) of 11 patients with mixed or other ethnicities. In the adjusted five-group model, patients of Black ethnicity had lower odds (OR 0·13 [95% CI 0·02-0·88]) of meeting MCR criteria compared with White patients. MCR criteria were met by fewer than a quarter of patients after treatment escalation. Patients of Black ethnicity had higher baseline disease burden and lower observed response than White patients. These results support the need for more personalised, equitable approaches to SLE management and reinforce the importance of ensuring diversity in clinical research. The British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register who received funding support from Roche, GSK, Otsuka, and Lupus UK.

items.title: Trends in the burden of diseases and their associations with multidimensional development among children and adolescents in China from 2000 to 2019: a retrospective analysis of a nationwide, repeated, cross-sectional survey.
items.abstract: Rapid social progress has transformed the health profile of Chinese children and adolescents, with declining diseases associated with poverty and rising diseases associated with wealth. This study aims to describe national trends in disease transitions and examine their associations with multidimensional provincial development. In this retrospective study, we analysed data from the 2000, 2005, 2010, 2014, and 2019 waves of the nationwide, repeated, cross-sectional Chinese National Surveys on Students' Constitution and Health in Han Chinese children and adolescents aged 7-18 years from 30 provinces in mainland China. The survey used a multistage, stratified, cluster-sampling design with balanced distributions by age, sex, and residence (urban vs rural). Collected data were prevalences of diseases associated with wealth and development (overweight and obesity, dental caries, and visual impairment) and their coexistence (multimorbidity associated with wealth) in addition to diseases associated with poverty (undernutrition, anaemia, and Ascaris infestation), and their coexistence (multimorbidity associated with poverty). We integrated 13 provincial indicators reflecting economic, social, environmental, infrastructure, and innovation development to construct a Multidimensional Equality Development Index (MEDI) using an entropy method. To examine national trends in disease transitions and their associations with multidimensional development we used mixed-effects logistic regression and restricted cubic splines. Population-attributable fractions were estimated to describe how development domains related to disease patterns. The study included 1 085 072 participants across five survey waves. Between 2000 and 2019, nationally, the prevalence of diseases associated with wealth increased and that of diseases associated with poverty declined substantially. In 2019, prevalence of visual impairment was highest (67·8%), followed by overweight and obesity (24·3%), dental caries (21·9%), multimorbidity associated with wealth (20·1%), anaemia (10·1%), undernutrition (4·7%), Ascaris infestation (0·8%), and multimorbidity associated with poverty (0·5%). The overall median MEDI score increased from 0·11 (IQR 0·09-0·16) in 2000 to 0·20 (0·15-0·28) in 2019. When data were pooled over 20 years, restricted cubic-spline analyses showed a non-linear association between MEDI score and odds of the disease outcome; higher MEDI scores were generally associated with lower odds of diseases associated with poverty, and higher odds of diseases associated with wealth (excluding visual impairment). Multidimensional development was associated with simultaneous reductions in prevalence of diseases associated with poverty and increases in prevalence of diseases associated with wealth. Disparities in most diseases associated with wealth between higher and lower MEDI areas have largely narrowed, suggesting a potential dual burden in lower MEDI areas and the need for targeted strategies. These findings highlight the need to enhance cross-sector investments to promote balanced, sustainable improvements in child and adolescent health. The National Key Research and Development Programme of China and the National Natural Science Foundation of China.

items.title: Estimated global treatment costs for 31 cancer types by stage, year, and follow-up period: a systematic review and modelling study.
items.abstract: Cancer is a growing health and economic burden worldwide, yet comprehensive global estimates of cancer treatment costs are sparse. Such data are crucial for economic evaluations to inform policy making and practice to improve cancer control and outcomes. We aimed to synthesise available estimates of direct cancer treatment costs by stage, year, and follow-up period and predict global cancer treatment costs. In this systematic review and modelling study, we extracted estimates of cancer treatment costs (ie, direct treatment costs only) from the medical literature, screening 25 896 studies, of which 196 were included in our final dataset, covering 31 cancer types across 44 countries. Costs were standardised as a ratio of country GDP per capita and adjusted for follow-up period. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to synthesise the estimates as a function of GDP per capita, accounting for cancer type, stage (I-IV), year of diagnosis, and follow-up period. We then estimated global and regional treatment costs (overall and by cancer type) in US$ 2022 based on the latest available incidence data from GLOBOCAN. This study is registered on PROSPERO (#CRD420251138446). Globally, total 10-year treatment costs for newly diagnosed cancers in 2022 were estimated to be $771·48 billion (95% UI 719·99-823·81), with breast cancer being the largest driver of costs ($96·07 billion [80·78-109·43]), followed by leukaemia ($86·11 billion [80·36-94·87]) and lung cancer ($84·36 billion [73·18-95·28]). North America and Europe accounted for 64% of total costs, but only 36% of diagnosed cancer cases. Mean costs per diagnosed patient were $38 650 (95% UI 36 070-41 280) globally, ranging from $3380 (95% UI 2960-3820) in eastern Africa to $93 600 (95% UI 87 170-100 150) in North America. As a ratio of GDP per capita, treatment costs declined with increasing GDP per capita (from 3·16 [95% UI 2·61-3·81] at $500 GDP per capita to 1·36 [1·07-1·70] at $100 000 GDP per capita), especially for stage IV cancers, which declined from 8·06 (6·57-9·61) at $500 GDP per capita to 4·53 (3·48-5·83) at $100 000 GDP per capita. Cancer types with the highest mean cost ratios were bone cancer (6·27 [95% UI 2·45-11·73]), leukaemia (6·16 [5·59-7·01]), and multiple myeloma (5·74 [3·78-6·74]). Treatment costs remained stable over time by year of diagnosis for stage I-II cancers, but steadily increased for stage III cancers, and rose substantially for stage IV cancers. These cost estimates provide new important data for economic evaluations, which can support expenditure planning, priority setting, and policy making to help guide strategic investment and resource allocations to improve cancer care and outcomes across different settings. items.title: Gene library deep sequencing for protein superfamily profiling.
items.abstract: Unraveling protein function at scale remains challenging. Gain-of-function (GOF) screens harnessing open reading frame (ORF) libraries enable systematic annotation of proteins that drive cell behavior and drug action. However, non-uniform gene coverage and undesired coding sequence variations compromise ORF library integrity and constrain the obtainable biological insight. In contrast, sequencing methods for characterizing current and next-generation ORF libraries remain limited. Here, we developed the scalable library deep sequencing workflow PPLseq (pooled plasmid library sequencing) for cost-effective, barcode-free ORF sequencing with single-nucleotide resolution. In a prototypical superfamily library of >300 human G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), PPLseq validated ORF identities and revealed sequence and coverage variation. Integration of PPLseq into high-throughput gene engineering facilitated assembly of a new GPCR fusion library. Systematic imaging-based phenotyping identified robustly expressed yet understudied receptors. Collectively, these results demonstrate broadly applicable, accessible, and accurate genetic library sequencing in library-to-phenotype profiling toward deeper insights into proteome function.

items.title: Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis.
items.abstract: When subject to damage or stress, cells develop responses in order to maintain tissue homeostasis. Two such responses are ferroptosis and cellular senescence, but how cells decide between these outcomes remains unclear. Here, we show that senescent cells increase import and membrane levels of multiple polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), but a specific intermediate PUFA, dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA, 20:3ω-6), is reduced. Exogenous repletion of DGLA instead results in cell death by ferroptosis. Senescent cells manifest additional features associated with ferroptosis, including labile iron and expression of lipoxygenases as well as low-level membrane peroxidation. Oral DGLA supplementation lowers markers of senescence in aged mice and improves age-related functional outcomes. Finally, obese humans with lowered DGLA desaturation rates have lower markers of adipose tissue senescence. Together, our data implicate shifts in PUFA metabolism as a driver of decisions between senescence and ferroptosis.

items.title: Association Between District-level Aggregate Carcinogen Emissions and Thyroid Cancer Incidence in Korea: An Ecological Study Using Bayesian Spatial Models.
items.abstract: We examined the association between district-level aggregate carcinogen emissions and diagnosed thyroid cancer incidence in Korea, accounting for co-occurring environmental exposures (air pollutants, indoor radon, and proximity to nuclear power plants [NPPs]) and area-level sociodemographic factors. This ecological study analyzed thyroid cancer incidence (2014-2018) across 229 Korean districts (si-gun-gu) using Bayesian hierarchical Poisson models. The primary exposure was a district-level aggregate carcinogen emission indicator (area-weighted releases of International Agency for Research on Cancer Group 1/2A/2B carcinogens). Models mutually adjusted for CO, NO₂, PM₁₀, SO₂, indoor radon, and NPP proximity, together with sociodemographic, behavioral, urbanicity, and healthcare-access covariates. Relative risks (RRs) per 1-SD increase and 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated overall, by sex, and by cancer-screening stratum. The emission indicator was associated with higher incidence overall (RR, 1.04; 95% CrI: 1.01-1.06) and in women (1.04; 1.02-1.06), but not in men (1.02; 0.99-1.06). CO was inversely associated with incidence (0.96; 0.93-0.99), whereas population density was positively associated (1.13; 1.06-1.21). NO₂, PM₁₀, SO₂, indoor radon, and NPP proximity showed no association after adjustment for the urban-rural context. The emission association remained robust with alternative zero handling and exclusion of the highest-emitting districts. It did not differ between screening strata. District-level aggregate carcinogen emissions, predominantly organic solvents by mass, were associated with diagnosed thyroid cancer incidence, most clearly in women. These hypothesis-generating findings may indicate either that as-yet-unidentified chemicals increase thyroid cancer risk or that the models incompletely captured the variables underlying the reported urbanicity-thyroid cancer association.

items.title: Barriers and Facilitators of Hypertension and Diabetes Screening in Primary Healthcare Facilities in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A Mixed-Methods Study.
items.abstract: Introduction/ObjectivesTo identify health-system and provider-level barriers and facilitators influencing hypertension and diabetes screening in public primary health care (PHC) facilities in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.MethodsWe conducted a qualitatively dominant convergent mixed-methods study from May to December 2025 in 10 public PHC facilities. Facility readiness was assessed using a checklist adapted from the WHO Service Availability and Readiness Assessment and analyzed descriptively. Semi structured interviews with 21 clinical staff were analyzed thematically using the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model and Theoretical Domains Framework.ResultsOverall readiness was 82.3%, but only 4.6% of clinical staff had received NCD-related training and 4.2% of the workforce was dedicated to NCD care. Stock-outs of glucose test strips and HbA1c reagents, limited HbA1c availability, inadequate equipment maintenance, and duplicate documentation constrained screening. Providers described limited refresher training, selective age- or symptom-based diabetes screening, heavy workload, and burnout as barriers. Peer learning, supportive supervision, NGO assistance, community-based health insurance, teamwork, and professional commitment were facilitators.ConclusionsScreening was constrained by interacting capability, opportunity, and motivation barriers rather than by the absence of guidelines alone. Priorities include competency-based in-service training, reliable diagnostic supplies and equipment maintenance, reduced documentation burden, and protected provider motivation. Transfer to similar settings requires contextual adaptation.

items.title: Racial Disparities in Outcomes After Major Head and Neck Surgery.
items.abstract: Understanding racial disparities in postoperative outcomes after major head and neck surgery is crucial in improving overall cancer survival. This study aims to investigate the association of race on surgical outcomes after major head and neck surgery. The American College of Surgeon National Surgical Improvement Program is a nationally representative dataset with data collected via systematic sampling methods. Patients who underwent major head and neck cancer surgery were identified between 2014 and 2021 and grouped based on self-reported race/ethnicity. Continuous variables were compared using one-way ANOVA, while categorical variables were analysed using Pearson's chi-square test. Multivariate logistic regression controlled for preoperative factors was performed to identify independent predictors of postoperative outcomes and generate odds ratios. 68.2% of the cohort were White, with Black, Hispanic, Asian and unknown/not reported comprising 6.0%, 4.9%, 4.0% and 16.9%, respectively. In multivariate analysis, Black patients compared to White patients had significantly greater odds of experiencing overall complications (OR = 1.73; 95% CI 1.38-2.19), and severe complications (OR = 2.09; 95% CI 1.71-2.56) (definitions provided in Methods section). Significant racial disparities exist in complications following major head and neck cancer surgery, with a higher rate of complications in Black patients. Further research is required to identify those factors responsible for the disparity.

items.title: Temporal changes in immunization information systems across U.S. states and jurisdictions, 2000-2024.
items.abstract: Statewide immunization data are essential for monitoring vaccination trends and evaluating immunization program impact. In the United States, Immunization Information Systems (IIS) were established in the early 1990s to collect these data; however, operational, legal, and procedural details vary across states and over time. This study summarized differences in IIS characteristics, such as legal requirements and reporting procedures, across U.S. states and jurisdictions over time. We compiled jurisdiction-level IIS regulatory data from published studies and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) surveys conducted in 2000, 2012, 2018, and 2024 to compare changes in age-group coverage, provider reporting requirements, consent procedures, operating authority, and data-sharing regulations. Between 2000 and 2024, legal frameworks and reporting practices for immunization registries expanded across U.S. states and jurisdictions. The number of states with laws or administrative rules authorizing immunization registries increased from 24 states in 2000 to all 50 states, Washington, D·C., five metropolitan areas, five U.S. territories, and three Freely Associated States in 2024. Over the same period, reporting requirements also became more widespread. The number of states and jurisdictions mandating providers to report immunization records increased from 12 (24% of 51) in 2000 to 54 (84% of 64) in 2024. Consent policies also changed over time. By 2024, most states and jurisdictions had adopted implicit consent for reporting children's immunization records (41/64; 64%), while a smaller proportion required explicit parental consent (7/64, 11%) or implemented mandatory participation without consent (14/64, 22%). IIS infrastructure and reporting requirements have expanded across U.S. states and jurisdictions over the past two decades, while heterogeneity in consent policies and reporting practices persists. These temporal changes may need to be considered when interpreting IIS data, particularly in longitudinal and cross-jurisdictional analyses.
