items.title: The Effect of Implementing Orem's Self-Care Model on Balance and Fatigue in Patients With Diabetic Neuropathy: A Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of applying Orem's self-care model on balance and fatigue in patients with diabetic neuropathy. Randomized clinical trial. Seventy diabetic neuropathy patients referred to Shahid Mofateh Clinic, affiliated with Yasuj University of Medical Sciences (YUMS), were chosen for this clinical trial study via convenience sampling and randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 35) or a control group (n = 35). The intervention group received care based on Orem's self-care model from a graduate nursing student over 2 months, followed by 1 month of self-care at home. The control group received no intervention. Both groups completed the research questionnaires (the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory and the Berg Balance Test) at pretest and posttest. Data were analysed in SPSS version 27 using an ANCOVA test. Before the intervention, there were no significant between-group differences (p > 0.05). After the intervention, fatigue was significantly lower in the intervention group, with an adjusted mean difference of -9.40 points (95% CI: -11.09 to -7.71; p < 0.001; partial η2 = 0.647). Balance scores were significantly higher in the intervention group across low, mean, and high baseline levels, with adjusted mean differences of 7.01, 5.77, and 4.52 points, respectively (all p < 0.001). The group × baseline balance interaction was significant (F(1,66) = 5.69, p = 0.020; partial η2 = 0.079). Nurses are recommended to apply Orem's self-care model as an effective structured intervention to reduce fatigue and improve balance in patients with diabetic neuropathy. Patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (diagnosed by an internist using TCSS) who participated in this randomized clinical trial evaluating Orem's self-care model effects on balance and fatigue.

items.title: Janus Kinase Inhibitor Use Among People With Inflammatory Disease in Australia.
items.abstract: Aim To describe Australian trends in JAKi uptake, where there are no restrictions on the sequence of their use in clinical practice. Methods We included all people aged 18 years and over initiating a JAKi between 1 October 2015 and 31 August 2022. We used national dispensing claims data for a random 10% sample of Australians to: describe the number of people initiating JAKi per quarter; the characteristics of new JAKi users including demographics, use of other medicines to manage cardiovascular comorbid disease; and use of prior targeted therapy (biologics or small molecule inhibitors). We used Kaplan-Meier analysis to estimate the proportion of initiators who were persistent on their initial JAKi to 365 days. Results We identified 2904 people initiating JAKi treatment between 1 October 2015 and 31 August 2022; new use increased consistently during the study period. 45% of initiators had not been dispensed a prior subsidised targeted therapy in 365 days prior to JAKi initiation; 72% of new users were female and 62% were aged 55 years or older. Almost half of people initiating JAKi had at least one marker of higher cardiovascular risk, with 30% dispensed medicines to treat or prevent cardiovascular disease in the year prior to initiation; and 34% being aged 65 years or older. 60% of people persisted on their initial JAKi therapy to 365 days. Of those who stopped, 51% switched to a biologic and 15% switched to a different JAKi. Conclusion In a setting where JAKi are permitted to be used in any line of therapy, 45% of new users of JAKi were naïve to targeted therapy and half had at least one marker of cardiovascular risk. Continued monitoring is required to understand the risk profile of JAKi, particularly in those with high baseline cardiovascular disease risk.

items.title: Predicting for Malignancy in Congenital Lung Malformations: A Single-Center Study of the "At Risk" Pediatric and Adult Population.
items.abstract: Introduction Congenital lung malformations (CLMs) are often identified on antenatal scanning and malignant transformation is cited as an indication for early resection. Long-term follow-up of asymptomatic lesions managed nonoperatively is lacking. Herein, we prospectively follow up children with antenatally identified CLMs and reviewed adult patients diagnosed with adenocarcinoma to look for background CLM changes. Methods This is a single-center cohort study of pediatric patients with antenatal or early postnatal diagnosis of CLMs and a retrospective review of adult patients with lung adenocarcinoma. In children, data collected included type or location of CLMs and subsequent follow-up. In adult patients, we reviewed radiology for background CLMs. Results One hundred and twenty-nine pediatric patients diagnosed with CLMs: congenital pulmonary airway malformations (n = 79; 61%), bronchopulmonary sequestrations (n = 26; 20%), congenital lobar emphysema (n = 11; 9%), resolved lesions (n = 10; 8%), bronchogenic cysts (n = 2; 2%), and an unknown lesion (n = 1; 1%). The patients were followed up for 6.7 (IQR: 3.4-10.5; range 0.08-20.6) years. No pediatric patient was subsequently identified on the Northern Ireland Cancer Registry. Three hundred and twenty-three adult patients were diagnosed with lung carcinoma: 37 (11%) were mucinous adenocarcinomas and 21 (57%) had a KRAS mutation. No CLMs were identified on review of radiological imaging in adult patients presenting with malignancy. Conclusion In children with CLMs, no resected malignant lesions could be identified on medium-term follow-up. Furthermore, no CLMs were identified in adult patients presenting with resected mucinous adenocarcinoma. Prospective collaborative databases are needed to determine true malignancy risk in asymptomatic CLM lesions and CPAMs.

items.title: Polarizing Views About Feminists and Gender Egalitarianism in Canada.
items.abstract: International evidence reveals growing ideological divisions between women and men. On average, in industrialized countries, women are leaning more liberal, men more conservative. Among young men especially, anti-feminist sentiment is growing, while simultaneously more women are embracing feminist causes. Little recent national research in Canada has explored these trends. Analyzing pooled national surveys conducted between 1993 and 2025 (N > 130,000), I examine longitudinal trends in how women and men place themselves on the political right or left, feel about feminists, and support gender egalitarianism. Four key findings emerge: (i) evidence of an expanding gender gap across several core measures; (ii) a subtle yet notable increase in opinion diversity among men; (iii) a recent surge among women in support for feminist causes; and (iv) recent period effects that appear to be driving the growing gender gap. Together these results offer a nuanced portrait of gendered realignments in contemporary Canada.

items.title: Ixodes ricinus-Contact Phase Inhibitor Promotes Functional Recovery and Attenuates Neutrophil Associated Neuroinflammation After Experimental Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
items.abstract: Aims Neutrophil-associated inflammation contributes to secondary brain injury after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). We evaluated whether Ixodes ricinus-Contact Phase Inhibitor (Ir-CPI), a selective factor XIa/XIIa inhibitor with reported thromboinflammatory modulatory properties, improves outcome after experimental ICH without worsening bleeding. Methods In a collagenase-induced mouse ICH model, Ir-CPI was administered as an intravenous bolus followed by a 3-day infusion. Vehicle animals served as controls and enoxaparin as an anticoagulant comparator. Cohorts evaluated hemorrhage and lesion volumes, endothelial activation, neutrophil-associated inflammation, and longitudinal functional recovery. Ir-CPI association with human neutrophils was evaluated in vitro. Results Ir-CPI did not increase hemorrhage or lesion volumes versus PBS through Day 14, whereas enoxaparin showed a higher Day 1 hemorrhage volume than Ir-CPI. Flow cytometry showed Ir-CPI association with human neutrophils. In the mouse model, Ir-CPI produced region-specific reductions in neutrophil infiltration and NET formation and reduced neuronal degeneration at the injection site and caudal level, without affecting VCAM-1-associated endothelial activation. Ir-CPI accelerated functional recovery, improving neurological scores and sensorimotor asymmetry by Day 5, with restoration of baseline corner test performance by Day 14. Conclusion Ir-CPI improves recovery after experimental ICH without exacerbating bleeding and is associated with reduced neutrophil-associated secondary brain injury. These findings support its translational potential as a therapeutic strategy for ICH.

items.title: Maximum Gape in Developing Macaca mulatta.
items.abstract: Objectives Maximum gape and bite force are two key metrics of primate craniodental performance, but without mitigating adaptations, large gapes are associated with reduced bite force. Primate craniodental morphology undergoes functional transitions across development, but how these performance variables vary with life-history transitions is unknown. Material and methods Maximum gapes of 211 rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) spanning infancy to post-prime developmental stages from Cayo Santiago (Puerto Rico) were collected in vivo, and jaw leverage, a contributor to bite force, was calculated from skeletal measurements of the same individuals post-mortem. Allometric relationships were tested using a combination of OLS regressions and mixed-effects models with developmental stage and sex as interaction terms. Results In vivo gape did not differ from isometry relative to body mass and jaw length across developmental stages by sex, but jaw leverage was significantly lower in larger compared to smaller macaques. The largest developmental differences occurred between pre-prime and prime individuals. Canine length scaled with positive allometry against body mass and jaw length in males but not females, while maximum gape scaled with negative allometry relative to canine length in both sexes. Discussion These results indicate that macaques undergo a functional tradeoff between jaw leverage and gape around the onset of sexual dimorphism. Pre-prime macaques exhibit relatively greater jaw leverage, whereas adults maintain proportionate gape relative to body and jaw size at reduced mechanical advantage. The eruption of large canines in males does not influence linear gape outside of size differences captured by body mass and jaw length.

items.title: Asymmetric Migration Shapes Genetic Structure of the Invasive Avian Vampire Fly (Philornis downsi) Across the Galápagos Islands.
items.abstract: Biological invasions on islands provide a natural framework to study how dispersal and connectivity influence evolutionary and ecological processes. The avian nest parasitic fly, Philornis downsi-first recorded in Darwin's finch nests in 1997-causes high mortality in endemic land birds, yet its inter-island and sex-specific patterns of dispersal and genetic structure remain poorly understood. We use low-coverage whole genome sequencing to investigate genome-wide patterns of genetic diversity, directional migration and effective population size in P. downsi across five major Galápagos Islands and its native range in mainland Ecuador. We find evidence for a genetic bottleneck in the Galápagos, isolation by distance, and evidence that the island closest to the Ecuadorian mainland, San Cristóbal, is genetically divergent from the other four islands sampled, despite retaining the highest genetic diversity. No evidence was found for sex-biased dispersal; however, sex-biased genetic structure was detected using only markers from inferred autosomal scaffolds. We found asymmetric gene flow with higher migration rates from San Cristóbal westward to the other islands, matching the direction of both southeast trade winds and major cargo shipping routes. Our results suggest both natural and human-mediated colonisation of P. downsi from the mainland through San Cristóbal to the other islands, followed by high inter-island dispersal among closely situated sink islands. Our findings are critical for prioritising islands for control strategies that will reduce P. downsi impacts on vulnerable endemic birds and underscore the value of understanding directional migration patterns for managing invasive species in metapopulations.

items.title: Early-Life Polyethylene Microplastic Exposure Exacerbates ADHD-Like Behaviors in Mice via PI3K/AKT1/Nrf2 Signaling: Evidence From the Pilot Cohort and Multi-Omics Analyses.
items.abstract: Microplastic pollution may influence neurodevelopment, yet its relationship with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remains unclear. We integrated a pediatric cohort, multi-omics analyses, network toxicology, and animal experiments to investigate polyethylene (PE) microplastic exposure in ADHD vulnerability. Among 90 children, PE was the predominant polymer detected in blood and was more abundant in children with ADHD. Higher PE burden was associated with greater symptom severity, increased IL-6, and reduced antioxidant capacity. Multi-omics and network analyses converged on PI3K/AKT1/Nrf2 signaling. In a perinatal nicotine mouse model, developmental PE co-exposure exacerbated ADHD-like behaviors, dopaminergic dysfunction, and oxidative injury. Melatonin partially alleviated these abnormalities by restoring PI3K/AKT1/GSK3β and Nrf2 signaling, whereas AAV-mediated PI3K knockdown weakened its protective effects. Collectively, the human findings identify circulating PE burden as an environmental correlate of ADHD-related neurodevelopmental vulnerability, while the animal experiments provide evidence that developmental PE co-exposure can aggravate ADHD-like abnormalities in a susceptible background.

items.title: Risky Alcohol Use in Individuals With Anxiety Disorders: Relationships and Predictors Based on Early Maladaptive Schemas and Attachment Styles.
items.abstract: Background and aim This study aims to evaluate the differences between the groups with and without risky alcohol use (RAU) in terms of sociodemographic characteristics, anxiety level, adult attachment styles (AASs) and early maladaptive schemas (EMSs) in individuals diagnosed with anxiety disorders (ADs). Furthermore, we aim to investigate whether RAU in individuals with ADs can be predicted by EMS or AAS. Methods In this prospective study, a total of 128 individuals diagnosed with ADs were divided into two groups based on the Michigan Alcoholism Screening Test (MAST) cut-off score (≥ 5). Scores from the Adult Attachment Style Scale, Young Schema Questionnaire and Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), as well as demographic and clinical variables, were analysed. Results The RAU group showed higher rates of suicide history and higher scores on the abandonment and unrelenting standards (US) schemas. Higher scores on abandonment and US schemas were associated with a greater likelihood of RAU. MAST scores positively correlated with emotional deprivation, failure to achieve, pessimism, social isolation, AS, dependence, abandonment, vulnerability schema scores and BAI scores in individuals with RAU. Hierarchical regression showed that attachment and schema subscales accounted for 42% of the variance in MAST scores. The higher scores on emotional inhibition, defectiveness, vulnerability schemas and anxious attachment style significantly predicted MAST scores. Conclusion These findings support the theoretical basis for attachment-based and schema therapy-based interventions, highlighting the importance of assessing especially abandonment, US, defectiveness, vulnerability schemas and anxious attachment style.

items.title: Intraoperative hypotension in older adults with hip fracture: a comparative analysis of different definitions.
items.abstract: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with adverse outcomes, but its definition varies widely and most definitions are derived from younger or mixed-age populations. Older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery are particularly susceptible due to reduced physiological reserve. This study compared absolute, relative, and duration-based definitions of IOH and evaluated their associations with postoperative adverse outcomes. This retrospective single-center cohort study included all patients aged ≥ 65 years who underwent hip fracture surgery at Maastricht University Medical Centre+ between January 2021 and December 2022. IOH was defined using absolute thresholds (MAP < 65 mmHg, SBP < 100 mmHg), relative reductions (≥ 20%), post-induction decreases, and duration below thresholds. Outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI, KDIGO criteria), and 30 day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, ASA classification, medication use, and nursing home residency. A total of 473 patients were included (mean age 80.9 years, 69.8% female). Postoperative AKI occurred in 9.9% and 30 day mortality in 5.5%. Absolute and relative IOH thresholds were not significantly associated with outcomes. In contrast, longer IOH duration (SBP < 100 mmHg) was associated with 30 day mortality (OR 1.09 per minute, 95%CI 1.02-1.16). After adjustment, higher ASA classification remained associated with AKI, while IOH duration remained significantly associated with mortality. In older patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, the duration of IOH, rather than static thresholds, appeared more strongly associated with adverse outcomes, particularly 30 day mortality. These findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of hypotension duration and support further prospective research to establish geriatric-specific IOH definitions and optimal perioperative blood pressure management strategies.

items.title: Navigating social space: transgender inclusion in Guwahati city, Assam, India.
items.abstract: This qualitative study examined the lived experiences of people with transgender identities in the urban social spaces of Guwahati, India, through an intersectional lens. The study was informed by data drawn from three key informant interviews with gender rights activists, one focus group discussion with kinnar community members, and eight in-depth interviews with persons identifying as trans women, trans men, gender fluid or non-binary. The social spaces of Guwahati, considered in this study, were categorised into public spaces and education and workplaces. Using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis , the study provided insights into the experiences of people with transgender identities in the city's different social spaces. The findings reveal their experiences are not uniform but are impacted by the intersection between an individual's gender identity and social location, including their socio-economic status and educational attainment. The work contributes to an understanding of the complex relationship between transgender and social spaces in regional cities such as Guwahati, underscoring the importance of adopting an intersectional approach when working to create inclusive and equitable environments for gender minorities in the Global South.

items.title: Membrane-Targeted Nanoparticles for Neuronal Photomodulation.
items.abstract: Selective targeting of nanoparticles to the neuronal interface is central for the tailored development of precision neurotechnologies. Here, we report the targeting of gold bipyramids, as a model nanomaterial, on the membrane of primary neurons using a bioorthogonal approach. In a two-step process, linker molecules anchor to receptors that expose trans-cyclooctene, which forms a covalent bond with the tetrazine functional group on nanoparticles, leading to the retention of hundreds of nanoparticles per cell. Selective labeling of neuronal membranes with plasmonic nanoparticles via a bioorthogonal strategy enabled inhibition of neuronal activity through photothermal effects under NIR laser irradiation in synchronized cell cultures. The linker and/or nanoparticles alone have a negligible effect on neuromodulation. Nanoparticle retention at the membrane is rapid, requiring only one hour of total incubation, with no cytotoxic effect. These results expand the repertoire of light-activated nanomaterials for non-invasive neuromodulation.

items.title: Lower waitlist failure without loss of transplant or exception access after the 2023 pediatric liver allocation update: a national interrupted time-series study.
items.abstract: The 2023 Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network pediatric medical urgency update revised the Pediatric End-Stage Liver Disease (PELD) calculation, pediatric Status 1A/1B rules, and National Liver Review Board guidance. Using registry data linked to exception records, we performed an interrupted time-series analysis among candidates younger than 12 years listed from January 2019 through December 2024, excluding June-July 2023 as the implementation interval (2,791 registrations; 368,761 person-days). The primary outcome was waitlist death or delisting for clinical deterioration. The update was not associated with an immediate change in this outcome (incidence rate ratio [IRR], 1.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57-2.46), but was associated with a lower post-policy trajectory (slope-change IRR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99; P=0.047). This association attenuated when severity was measured identically in both eras (IRR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.90-1.01; P=0.14). Removal for death was unchanged (0.21 vs 0.20 per 1,000 person-days), whereas removal as too sick to transplant fell (0.21 vs 0.09). Transplant rates, exception request rates, and exception approval probability did not decline. The update was associated with lower severity-adjusted waitlist death/delisting without detectable loss of transplant or exception access; however, era-invariant severity adjustment and component analyses indicate that the magnitude and mechanism of this association remain uncertain.

items.title: COMBO-RATE: An Experimentally Validated Bioinformatic Tool to Identify Promiscuous HLA Restrictions.
items.abstract: Defining HLA restriction of T cell epitopes is essential for understanding immune responses in infectious disease, autoimmunity and vaccine design. Current bioinformatic programmes, including the IEDB RATE tool, enable inference of single-HLA restrictions from immune response data of HLA-typed donors. However, T cell epitopes are frequently presented by multiple HLA alleles, a phenomenon termed promiscuous restriction, limiting the utility of single-allele approaches. To address this limitation, we developed COMBO-RATE, an extension of RATE that systematically evaluates combinations of HLA alleles to identify multi-allelic restriction patterns. Analysis of three independent datasets spanning distinct antigen systems and different epitope discovery strategies revealed that promiscuous restriction is a near-universal feature of immunodominant epitopes. Focusing on the 43 immunodominant CD4 + T cell epitopes identified in a B. pertussis genome-wide screen, COMBO-RATE outperformed conventional RATE, identifying restrictions for 35 of 43 epitopes, compared to 24 by RATE alone, and uncovered 64 additional allele restrictions, including 29 unique alleles. Experimental validation using single-HLA transfected cell lines and antigen presentation assays confirmed COMBO-RATE-inferred restrictions, demonstrating that a single epitope can be independently presented by distinct HLA alleles. Overall, COMBO-RATE provides a robust and scalable framework for defining complete HLA restriction profiles from existing population response data, with important implications for the design of vaccines requiring broad HLA coverage across genetically diverse populations. This pipeline is available as both a Python package and a user-friendly web application.

items.title: Maximising Cancer Prevention and Early Detection in the Australian Cancer Plan: Where Are We Now and What Should Come Next?
items.abstract: Cancer accounts for three in 10 deaths in Australia, yet many cases are preventable or can be detected at an early stage. Maximising cancer prevention and early detection is one of the six strategic objectives of the 10-year Australian Cancer Plan. This perspective article reviews the current progress and challenges of reducing the cancer burden, along with future opportunities. It explores how to address modifiable risk factors, particularly tobacco smoking, alcohol use and sun exposure and the advances in screening programs for bowel, breast, cervical and lung cancers. It highlights the potential for risk-stratified and genomics-informed screening, emphasising the need to support participation through equitable and culturally safe approaches.

items.title: Cortical long-range dynamics track excitation-inhibition balance across cognitive states and organizational principles
items.abstract: A fundamental question in systems neuroscience is how the brain's excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance shapes the temporal structure of neural activity and whether we can non-invasively recover this relationship from neural scaling properties. We show that MRS-derived E/I balance is expressed in long-range temporal dynamics and constrained by cytoarchitecture. The laminar organisation of inhibitory circuits, spanning agranular to granular cortex, determines how faithfully regional dynamics reflect E/I balance. This neurochemical signature is state-dependent: its relationship with cortical dynamics reverses during task engagement, consistent with traversal of dynamical regimes around a critical point. It extends beyond fMRI to arousal-linked dynamics, indexed by pupil diameter and microsaccades, indicating a global mode of cortical state rather than a regionally isolated property. The imprint of E/I balance on long-range dynamics follows the sensory-association axis at rest, and is reconfigured during task engagement. These findings establish E/I balance as a neurochemical quantity with structured, scalable signatures across the temporal and spatial organization of the human cortex.

items.title: "We Desperately Need More Training": A Qualitative Exploration of Emergency Department Nurses’ Experiences with and Training Needs for End-Of-Life Communication
items.abstract: Abstract Background Approximately 75% of decedents aged ≥ 65 years visited the emergency department in their last six months of life, underscoring the emergency department as a pivotal setting for end-of-life communication. Nurses play a significant role in palliative care, however, little research has been performed on their end-of-life communication experiences and training needs. Methods A qualitative descriptive study reported with reference to the COREQ checklist was conducted. A total of 12 ED nurses from a tertiary hospital in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, China, were recruited through a purposive sampling method. Semi-structured interviews were conducted from April to June 2026, audio-recorded, and transcribed verbatim. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis with an inductive coding approach. Results Four overarching themes were identified, including: (1) Complex emotional experiences (Powerless and conflicted; Compassionate and sorrowful; Fear of communication missteps; Compassion fatigue; Sense of mission and achievement) ; (2) Multidimensional barriers (Environment-related; Patient-related; Family-related; Nurse-related barrier ) ; (3) Core knowledge and skills needs (Disease-related knowledge; Psychology-related knowledge; Breaking-bad-news skill; Empathy and emotion regulation skill) ; and (4) Expectations for future training (Specialized teaching content; Practical teaching method; Accessible teaching format) . Conclusions Participants perceived a need for practical and ED-specific EOL communication training. Future programs should adopt blended, simulation-based, and context-specific pedagogical frameworks to address the identified gaps.

items.title: A Safe–Connect–Evolve positive psychology-informed support pathway for a university student with prior bullying victimization: a qualitative single-case study in China
items.abstract: Abstract Background Bullying victimization can have psychological and social consequences that persist beyond the original school context and into university. This study examined the longer-term support process of a university student with prior bullying victimization and developed a staged, practice-oriented support framework. Methods This retrospective qualitative single-case study focused on Student Z at University A in China. Existing case materials generated during routine student support between 2024 and 2026 included case conversations and collateral information, observational and support records, psychological assessment summaries, counseling records, and multisystem coordination records. A case-oriented, process-focused analysis examined presenting difficulties, support systems, support activities, and changes over time. Results Student Z’s difficulties after university entry were associated with delayed recognition of earlier bullying, limited emotional support, and fragmented professional support. The case record showed a gradual progression from establishing psychological safety and trust, to rebuilding family, peer, academic, and professional support, and subsequently to greater agency and campus participation. Psychological screening scores for interpersonal sensitivity, depression, anxiety, and hostility were lower at later assessment points than in October 2024 and remained within the reference range in March 2026. Retrospective synthesis of the case yielded a three-stage Safe–Connect–Evolve pathway. Conclusions The Safe–Connect–Evolve pathway provides a case-derived, practice-oriented framework for organizing support for university students with prior bullying victimization. It should not be regarded as a validated intervention protocol. Further multi-case research using prospectively defined qualitative procedures, standardized outcome measures, and longer-term follow-up is needed to examine its transferability.

items.title: Travel time to Nutrition Rehabilitation Centers: Measuring equity of access using road network data in Nandurbar district and implications for public health service design
items.abstract: Abstract Background Maharashtra’s Nandurbar district, a predominantly tribal and hilly region, faces high child undernutrition and access barriers to facility-based care. Families and providers cite distance, transport constraints, and terrain as major obstacles to nutritional rehabilitation center (NRC) use and follow-up. This study aimed to measure spatial access to NRCs and identify gaps in geographical coverage and accessibility in Nandurbar district in Maharashtra. Methods We conducted a district-wide drive-time analysis using Google road network data to estimate minutes to the nearest NRC for every village. Villages were classified into 30/60/90/120-minute driving bands and child burden. NRC facility and villages were mapped, and numbers of children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) were obtained from a district-wide joint screening in April 2025. Numbers of children admitted to NRC were obtained from district health records. Results The mean drive time to the nearest NRC was 41 minutes (range: 2–228). The analysis was conducted for a sample of 2804 children with SAM across 952 villages. 19.2% of villages and 23.7% (665 children) of SAM cases were ≥ 60 minutes from an NRC; 4.4% of villages and 7.3% (205 children) of SAM cases were ≥ 90 minutes. Clusters of high SAM and long travel were concentrated in Akrani, Shahade, and Akkalkuwa. The admissions/SAM ratio varied widely—Akkalkuwa 0.37, Akrani 0.32, Nawapur 0.31, versus Shahade 0.11 and Taloda 0.09 (the latter with the highest SAM burden). The analysis highlighted villages where setting up treatment centers based at primary health centers and provision of referral transport could yield immediate gains. Conclusions Drive-time modeling reveals actionable geographic inequities in access to NRCs in Nandurbar. Travel time is one aspect of the challenges families face, as many people do not have access to vehicles or financial resources to pay for easy transport. Establishing additional treatment options at select PHCs in far–high-burden corridors, strengthening transport, and coordinating care at border areas of the district can reduce time-to-care for severely malnourished children.

items.title: Teleophthalmology for preventable blindness screening in semi-urban primary care: a cost-effectiveness study from Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract Background Visual impairment from preventable causes remains a critical public health challenge in Brazil, where over 34% of the population has never undergone ophthalmic examination and specialist access is severely maldistributed. Diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, and cataract are leading causes of preventable blindness, yet systematic screening in primary care remains rare in semi-urban municipalities. This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a teleophthalmology-based active screening pathway versus the standard Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS) passive referral pathway, assessed acceptability among professionals and patients, and estimated quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) gained through early detection. Methods A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted across eight Primary Health Care Units in a semi-urban municipality in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil (October 2025–March 2026). A total of 1,290 patients aged 50 years or older and/or with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) were screened using a portable non-mydriatic fundus camera with remote specialist reporting assisted by artificial intelligence (AI)-based segmentation. A two-arm decision tree compared intervention costs (bottom-up micro-costing) against standard pathway costs (SIGTAP 2024/SISREG 2024) from the public payer perspective. The primary effectiveness measure was time to diagnosis. A QALY scenario analysis was performed using Brazilian-validated utility coefficients. Acceptability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUScale; n = 13 professionals) and the Telehealth Usability Questionnaire – Brazil (TUQ-Brazil; n = 99 patients). Results Of 1,290 patients, 41.79% had abnormal findings and 2.32% had ungradable images. Mean time to diagnosis was 1.26 days versus 83 days via standard referral. Cost per detected case was R$50.64 versus R$70.82, a reduction of 28.5%. Teleophthalmology was absolutely dominant across all sensitivity scenarios. A QALY analysis (n = 376) yielded an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of –R$4,330/QALY, well below the SUS threshold (~ R$132,000/QALY). Professionals rated the platform 90.96 ± 5.91 (SUScale; “Excellent”). Patients reported a mean TUQ-Brazil score of 6.61 ± 0.32 out of 7.00, with 93.9% willing to reuse the service. Conclusions Teleophthalmology demonstrated absolute dominance over standard SUS referral in both cost-effectiveness and QALY analyses, delivering earlier diagnosis at lower cost. High bilateral acceptability supports scalability within the SUS, and these findings offer actionable evidence for policymakers considering portable fundus camera integration into semi-urban primary care networks.

items.title: Building Resilient Health Systems: Experiences and Lessons from Implementing Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) in Northeast Nigeria Amidst Insecurity and Fragile Systems
items.abstract: Abstract Background Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) is a comprehensive strategy adopted by countries in the WHO African Region to strengthen disease surveillance and public health response across all levels of the health systems. However, Nigeria’s northeast region has had prolonged armed insurgency and complex humanitarian emergencies, resulting in widespread insecurity, fragile health systems, and disrupted health services. Despite these challenges, surveillance personnel continue to implement IDSR activities in this region. This study documents the experiences, challenges, adaptations, and lessons learned by surveillance personnel implementing IDSR in this conflict-affected setting during the post-surge phase of COVID-19 pandemic. Methods We employed a qualitative phenomenological study design to capture the experiences of surveillance personnel implementing IDSR in northeast Nigeria. Data were collected through key informant interviews (KIIs) with state-level officials and focus group discussions (FGDs) with Local Government Area (LGA) personnel and facility-based surveillance officers. Participants included state epidemiologists, disease surveillance and notification officers (DSNOs), and other health workers, selected purposively using maximum variation sampling to ensure representation across diverse roles and operational contexts. Data were transcribed and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis enhanced with NVivo software. Results Six major themes were identified: security and access constraints, human resource shortages, infrastructure and logistics limitations, data management challenges, psychosocial stress among health workers, and adaptive innovations leveraging community informants, vigilante networks, mobile reporting tools, and existing polio and COVID-19 platforms to sustain surveillance operations. Insecurity significantly restricted access to several LGAs, delayed outbreak investigation, and disrupted both reporting and response. Severe workforce shortages and high staff turnover further strained surveillance capacity. Infrastructure gaps—such as destroyed facilities, unreliable power supply, and limited transport—impeded sample collection and reporting. Data management remained largely paper-based, leading to delays and occasional loss of records. Conclusions In northeast Nigeria, IDSR is implemented in a complex environment shaped by insecurity, fragile infrastructure, and human resource constraints. However, locally driven adaptations and strong community engagement have enabled continuing surveillance. Strengthening IDSR in humanitarian settings requires investments in workforce capacity, digital reporting systems, mental health support for frontline workers, and institutionalization of community-based surveillance approaches.

items.title: Building HPV Vaccine Confidence with and for Healthcare Workers in Nigeria: A Co-Design Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer, primarily caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), is a global public health concern, particularly affecting women in low- and middle-income countries, including Nigeria. The HPV vaccine prevents cervical cancer, yet uptake remains low due to supply and confidence barriers. While vaccine confidence among women and girls, and their families has received wide attention, less attention has focused on healthcare workers (HCWs), despite their key role in improving uptake. Co-designing interventions with HCWs could yield better-tailored programs addressing context-specific communication and information needs. Here, we describe the co-design process with HCWs in Nigeria, the strategies and delivery mechanisms identified, and provide methodological reflections. Methods We conducted a co-design study guided by human-centred design and the Ideate, Design, Evaluate, and Share (IDEAS) framework, in Oyo and Jigawa states, Nigeria, between September 2024 and September 2025. Co-design participants included doctors, nurses, and community health extension workers, recruited using purposive and snowball sampling. Data were collected through participatory workshops using audio recordings, field notes, and visuals of co-produced materials, and analysed using content analysis, with findings iteratively refined and validated with participants across workshops. Results Through a series of five workshops and three rounds of sense checks involving 45 HCWs, participants identified gaps in access to HPV vaccine knowledge, difficulty addressing rumours, and a lack of confidence in counselling. In response, we jointly developed content for intervention approaches: in-person and digital. The in-person intervention is planned to be delivered in the health facility by a trained HPV champion. The digital intervention in planned to be delivered through WhatsApp. Both use four short educational videos, which were co-designed with the HCWs, to increase HCWs’ knowledge and confidence in the HPV vaccine, covering: 1) general knowledge on cervical cancer, HPV, and HPV vaccine; 2) counselling parents on HPV vaccine, and 3) strategies for addressing rumours around the HPV vaccine. Conclusion The co-design study enabled successful development of co-designed videos, and in-person and digital intervention delivery strategies to strengthen HPV vaccine confidence among HCWs in Nigeria.

items.title: District level weekly surveillance data on notifiable infectious diseases in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pakistan from 2023 to 2026
items.abstract: Abstract This article presents a structured, long-format panel dataset of district-week notifiable infectious disease case counts for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, Pakistan, covering 164 weekly epidemiological bulletins published between April 2023 and July 2026. The data were extracted from Table 4 of the National Institute of Health (NIH) Pakistan Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) weekly Public Health Bulletins, which reports district-level case counts for the most frequently reported notifiable conditions in KP each week. The dataset comprises 59,824 district-week-condition observations spanning 44 canonical district- and sub-division-level reporting units and 16 distinct notifiable conditions. Six conditions — acute diarrhoea (non-cholera), malaria, influenza-like illness, acute lower respiratory infection in children under five, bloody diarrhoea, and typhoid — are reported in all 164 bulletins. Ten further conditions appear only in a subset of weeks, because the non-core columns of the source table rotate according to that week’s case volume: from 2023 week 32 onward the table reports the highest-ranking conditions by provincial case total rather than a fixed set, producing 106 distinct column orderings across the corpus. The dataset documents this rotating-column structure explicitly, and is accompanied by a time-scoped district-name crosswalk resolving administrative-boundary changes over the study period — including one reporting label whose underlying geography is redefined mid-series — a week-by-week column-order log, a condition presence matrix, and machine-readable flags for identified source-side data-quality issues. No comparable structured, validated dataset derived from Pakistan’s national disease surveillance bulletins is currently available in the public domain.

items.title: Maternal and child healthcare utilization and associated factors in private health institutions in Nepal
items.abstract: Abstract Background Private health institutions play a significant role in providing maternal and child health services globally. This study examines the utilization of maternal and child health services in Nepal and assesses socio-economic factors associated with the choice of private institutions, using data from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS). Methods The study used NDHS 2022 data. Maternal healthcare was assessed by the institution of antenatal care (ANC) and the place of delivery; child healthcare by the institution sought for fever/ARI and diarrhea treatment. Adjusted logistic regression identified socio-demographic determinants of private health-seeking behavior. Results Private institutions were used more for childhood illnesses—fever/ARI (81.3%) and diarrhea (77.2%)—than maternal healthcare, with 40% of women receiving ANC and 22.4% receiving delivery services privately. Children in the Terai had higher odds of private care for diarrhea (AOR 7.5; 95% CI: 1.6–35.4) and fever/ARI (AOR 10.1; 95% CI: 4.4–23.2) than those in the Mountain region. Household wealth was positively associated with private care for childhood illnesses, with the richest households showing markedly higher odds for fever/ARI (AOR 18.4; 95% CI: 4.4–76.3). Private maternal healthcare use was associated with ecological region, maternal education, and caste/ethnicity; the wealthiest women had higher odds of private ANC (AOR 9.2; 95% CI: 5.2–16.1), and greater maternal schooling predicted private delivery care. Conclusions Private institutions play a major role in Nepal's healthcare, particularly for childhood illnesses, with use shaped by agroecological zone, wealth, and education. Policies should promote equitable access across socioeconomic groups while strengthening both public and private services.

items.title: How Does Mazu Festival Affect the Well-being of Elderly Tourists?An Empirical Study from the Perspective of Restorative Experience
items.abstract: Abstract Restorative environment research has predominantly focused on natural settings, with limited attention to short-duration, high-density folk festivals and elderly populations. Drawing upon the stimulus–organism–response (S-O-R) framework, this study integrates attention restoration theory and place attachment theory to construct a serial mediation model of “Perceived Restorative Environment through Place attachment and psychological recovery to Hedonic Well-being.” Using the Mazu Festival on Meizhou Island as the case site, a questionnaire survey was conducted among 552 elderly tourists aged 55 and above, and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test the hypotheses. The results indicate that Perceived Restorative Environment enhances Hedonic Well-being through dual mechanisms—a direct emotional gain pathway and a sequential cognitive–affective pathway via Place attachment and psychological recovery. Legibility exhibits robust explanatory power in the festival context. Short-term festival participation primarily yields attentional recovery, while deep psychological restoration is constrained by limited stay duration. At the theoretical level, this study proposes the “Dual-Pathway Model of Festival Restorative Experience,” extending the applicability of restorative environment theory from natural landscapes to cultural festival settings, and reveals how temporal constraints and cognitive aging shape the restoration pathways, thereby offering a new theoretical framework for understanding elderly well-being generation in culturally intensive tourism contexts. At the practical level, the findings provide concrete pathways for the age-friendly design of folk festival spaces and offer empirical support for transforming folk cultural tourism resources into public mental health intervention tools for the elderly, contributing to the improvement of active aging social service systems.

items.title: Association of National Health Insurance Scheme Card Validity and Socio-demographic Characteristics with Recommended Antenatal Care Contacts among Postpartum Women in Kassena-Nankana Municipality: A Facility-Based Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Antenatal care is a key intervention for enhancing pregnancy outcomes as maternal health remains a public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa. Although Ghana’s National Health Insurance Scheme offers free maternal healthcare services to eliminate financial obstacles, ANC attendance in rural areas like Kassena-Nankana Municipal remains below ideal levels. This study assessed the association of national health insurance scheme card validity and socio-demographic characteristics with recommended antenatal care contacts among postpartum women in kassena-nankana municipality Methods The study employed a facility-based cross-sectional design among 290 postpartum women who had given birth in the previous 12 months prior to the study. A structured questionnaire was used to gather data with the aid of electronic kobo collect app. Descriptive statistics, Fisher’s exact tests, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression were used to analyze the data using SPSS version 27. Results The study revealed that only 46.9% of women in Kassena-Nankana Municipal achieved the WHO-recommended minimum number of ANC visits (8 times or more). Even though almost all the participants (97.6%) possessed valid NHIS cards, having a valid card was associated (unadjusted) with completing the recommended visits (p = 0.016): NHIS validity, and all women with invalid cards failed to meet the required visits. After adjusting for confounders, wealth status and educational level emerged as the predictors of ANC completion. Women with no formal education were 96% lower odds of completing the recommended ANC visits compared to those with tertiary education [AOR = 0.04; 95% CI: 0.02–0.12, p = 0.001], while women from rich households were 3.72 times more likely to complete the recommended number of visits than those from poor households [AOR = 3.72; 95% CI: 3.05–5.14, p = 0.001] Conclusion Less than half of expectant mothers completed the WHO-recommended minimum of eight or more ANC visits. NHIS enrolment alone did not ensure optimal ANC attendance, as socio-demographic factors have a major impact on ANC attendance. Socio-economic barriers must be addressed with targeted interventions focusing on disadvantaged women to improve equitable access to maternal healthcare services in Ghana

items.title: An Ultra-Long-Acting Buprenorphine Prodrug Ion-Pair for Opioid Use Disorder
items.abstract: Abstract Opioid overdose is a significant global public health concern. While buprenorphine (BUP) is a safe and effective treatment for opioid use disorder (OUD), requirements for frequent dosing and patient tolerability to organic solvent based monthly injectables limit its use. These challenges were overcome by the development of a scalable ultra-long-acting (ULA) BUP (NM6BUP-Pamoate). The binding of a lipophilic BUP prodrug to a hydrophobic counterion generated an organic-solvent-free formulation. A single dose of NM6BUP-Pamoate administered to Sprague–Dawley rats at 45 mg/kg produced sustained effective plasma BUP levels for six months. Brain BUP concentrations exceeded the recorded plasma levels. Safety evaluations demonstrated the absence of off-target toxicities, with local and systemic tolerability. NM6BUP-Pamoate simplifies OUD treatment to optimize clinical outcomes.

items.title: One Health drivers of zoonotic Taenia solium in rural districts of low and middle-income countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Abstract Background Infection with Taenia solium in humans and pigs continues to be a public health problem in rural districts of low and middle-income countries (LMICs). This is attributed to weak collaboration in surveillance, prevention, control and diagnosis among different sectors. Free-ranging pigs act as reservoirs of T. solium , increasing human infection risk through close contact, poor sanitation, and consumption of undercooked pork. This systematic and meta-analysis was aimed at estimating pooled prevalence of T. solium in human, porcine cysticercosis and identify their One health drivers in LMICs. Methods A systematic search of Medline/PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane database, Global Health online, Scopus and African Journals Online. ClinicalTrials.gov, Google Scholar. Open Grey database, WHO reports, FAO/WHO/WOA, and government or NGO technical reports were searched for studies published in January 2015 onwards. The systematic review was registered under PROSPERO CRD 420251023448. Random effects meta-analysis using the Der Simonian–Laird method estimated pooled prevalence. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Egger’s regression test while subgroup and sensitivity analysis was used to explore heterogeneity. Results Fifty-nine studies meet the inclusion criteria for systematic review and 29 studies for meta-analysis. The pooled prevalence of porcine cysticercosis was 10.9% (95% CI: 5.1%-21.8%) based on 14 of fourteen studies involving 8,904 pigs. The pooled prevalence of human T. solium was 13% (95%CL 8.00%-20%) based on 15 studies including 25,184 participants. Most frequently studies reporting risk factors were poor sanitation and free-range pigs with each (41; 69.5%) follow by open defecation with (36; 61%), poor hygiene (26; 44.1%), poor knowledge (23; 39%), lack of meat inspection (20; 33.9%) and backyard slaughtering (17; 28.8%). Human, animal and environmental risk factors were consistently associated with transmission and highlighting the need for One health integrated interventions. Conclusion T. solium remains highly prevalent in endemic areas of LMICs. Strengthening One health surveillance, prevention, diagnosis and control strategies in human, animal and environmental sector is essential to reduce disease transmission and burden.

items.title: Are Mid-Level Health Providers Prepared for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy Screening? - A cross-sectional study from South India.
items.abstract: Background: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy is a common yet often underdiagnosed complication of diabetes. This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, perception and practice of regarding Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy in the South Indian state of Karnataka. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted among 260 Community Health Officers (CHO) employed in Ayushman Arogya Mandirs of the district. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire that covered details of CHOs, training of DPN, knowledge, practice, and perceptions of DPN and its screening, as well as barriers encountered during screening of the condition. Results: Among the 260 participants, 77.3% and 22.6% were females and males. The mean age of the participants was 30.9 years. We found that 66.5% of the participants had moderate knowledge regarding DPN. The majority (76.1%) of participants did not have equipment to screen for neuropathy. Though all of them received training on NCD, 11.5% received training on DPN. Overall, 82% of the participants, of whom 23.5% strongly agreed and 58.5% agreed that they were confident in their ability to screen for DPN. Around 43.5% responded that they currently screen for DPN. Lack of screening equipment was one of the main barriers to the screening of DPN. Conclusion: The study showed a moderate level of knowledge regarding DPN. Nearly half of the participants never screened for DPN routinely, which is driven largely by insufficient in-service training and a critical shortage of screening equipment. Integrating structured DPN training into their education curriculum and ensuring the availability of equipment at the centres represent high-priority policy interventions to reduce the burden of preventable diabetic complications.

items.title: The impact of periodontitis in cardiac autonomic dysfunction by hrv analysis.
items.abstract: Introduction: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. This research ascertains periodontitis and its correlation to autonomic dysfunction by HRV analysis. Methodology: In total, 54 periodontitis patients were involved in the study, categorized under four groups, namely Gingivitis (n=14), Mild Periodontitis (n=13), Moderate Periodontitis (n=13), and Severe Periodontitis (n=14). Kubios HRV software version 3.5 was used for the analysis of time-domain and frequency-domain parameters of lead II ECG for HRV analysis. The indices of SNS and PNS were calculated for the assessment of autonomic balance. The correlation between the HRV parameters with the severity of periodontal disease was performed statistically. Results: The SNS index was higher in the periodontitis groups than in the gingivitis group (Gingivitis: 1.09 ± 0.60; Mild: 4.25 ± 2.4; Moderate: 3.82 ± 2.2; Severe: 4.45 ± 1.5; p < 0.001), although the pattern was not strictly progressive. Conclusion: Differences in autonomic regulation, including higher SNS index and lower PNS index values, were associated with periodontal disease categories. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study lacked a healthy control group and was cross-sectional.

items.title: Mapping Anaesthetic Syringe Labelling Practices, Perceived Standards Alignment and Educational Needs Among Anaesthesia Trainees and Technicians in India: A National Online Cross-Sectional Survey.
items.abstract: Background: Unlabelled or incompletely labelled anaesthetic syringes create preventable wrong-drug risk. This study evaluated syringe labelling practices, perceived standards alignment and educational needs among anaesthesia trainees and technicians in India. Methods: A national online cross-sectional survey was conducted across India from February to May 2025 using non-probability recruitment through professional networks and academic forums. Because recruitment did not use a closed centre-specific sampling frame, the number invited, exact number of contributing centres and conventional response rate were not available. An expert-reviewed and pilot-tested 21-item questionnaire assessed labelling frequency, timing, label completeness, exposure to unlabelled syringes, response behaviour, training, barriers and improvement priorities. Formal quantitative psychometric indices were not estimated. Data were summarized descriptively, and an exploratory Chi-square test assessed the unadjusted association between formal training and consistent labelling. Results: Of 421 complete responses, 344 (81.7%) respondents handled anaesthetic syringes daily. Consistent labelling was reported by 391 (92.9%), but pre-labelling of empty syringes was reported by 71 (16.9%). Expiry date documentation was never performed by 179 (42.5%), and only 111 (26.4%) included expiry details as a label component. Exposure to unlabelled or improperly labelled syringes occurred frequently or occasionally in 177 (42.1%). Although 278 (66.0%) discarded such syringes, the remainder used verification, self-labelling or confirmation-based workarounds. Formal training was reported by 361 (85.8%); an exploratory unadjusted analysis indicated an association with consistent labelling (P=0.039). Participant-level demographic and institutional covariates were unavailable for adjusted analysis. Only 137 (32.5%) perceived their practice as fully aligned with recommended standards. Conclusions: High self-reported labelling frequency coexisted with clinically important gaps in timing, completeness and disposal-related safety behaviour. The findings identify potentially important targets for structured training, readily available standardized labels, protocol reinforcement, audit-feedback cycles and safer workflow design. Because the study was cross-sectional and self-reported, the observed training association should not be interpreted as causal.

items.title: Who decides when the AI disagrees? A defensibility-threshold theory of accountable AI adjudication
items.abstract: Research on algorithmic advice explains whether people trust, accept, or weight an AI recommendation, but says little about what an accountable professional does when their own judgment and that recommendation point to different actions. We theorize this situation as accountable AI adjudication, in which the professional settles the disagreement through deference, override, verification, or escalation, ending in a final allocation of decision authority. We argue that the choice follows a defensibility standard expressed as two thresholds on the professional’s belief that the AI recommendation is correct. Below the lower threshold the professional overrides, above the upper threshold they defer, and between the two the case is unresolved. Error-cost asymmetry and the joint condition of accountability and evidentiary auditability move the thresholds, while the cost and availability of verification and escalation decide how unresolved cases are settled. The same AI, equally accurate and equally trusted, can therefore be deferred to in one case and rechecked in the next. Developed for accredited testing laboratories, the theory yields nine falsifiable propositions, separates defensibility from trust, and links reliance research to organizational theory on authority. It implies that raising AI accuracy or trust will not by itself improve decisions, because evidentiary records, decision rules, and escalation design also determine whether AI advice helps.

items.title: Tangible AI in the Elementary Classroom: Effects on AI Literacy, Computational Thinking, and Learner Dispositions
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly ubiquitous, yet AI literacy remains underdeveloped in elementary education, where young learners often view AI in anthropomorphic or magical terms. This study examined changes in computational thinking (CT), AI concept mastery, learning motivation, and programming self-efficacy following a tangible AI intervention, and explored the teacher's implementation experience. Guided by a framework integrating the AI Literacy Framework and the SEAME Model, a four-week intervention (4 × 60 minutes) was implemented with 36 fifth-grade students and one teacher in a public elementary school, using a single-group pretest–posttest design within a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANCOVA, with prior computing experience as a covariate; qualitative data from semi-structured teacher interviews (during and after the intervention) and observations of all four sessions were analyzed thematically. Significant pre–post gains were found for all four composite outcomes, largest for AI concept mastery (M = 8.4 to 15.1; η²p = .70) and total CT score (η²p = .56), although the CT abstraction subdimension did not improve (M = 2.3 to 2.1). Students able to explain how machine learning models learn from data rose from 28% to 83%. Anthropomorphic descriptions of AI decreased from 89% to 25% of students, with post-intervention explanations increasingly referring to sensors, data, and training. Three qualitative themes emerged: strong pedagogical confidence but limited AI content knowledge, persistent infrastructural constraints, and reduced technical anxiety through gradual mastery. Tangible AI may offer a promising bridge to early AI literacy; however, without a control group, changes cannot be causally attributed to the intervention, and these single-school findings are preliminary.

items.title: Navigating Reading Challenges: Phenomenological Study of Teachers Supporting Struggling Readers in Philippine Context
items.abstract: Struggling readers are a persistent concern in Philippine elementary education, yet research has largely examined student reading outcomes rather than the professional, emotional, and instructional experiences of the teachers who support these learners in resource-constrained, multilingual classrooms. This study investigated the lived experiences of elementary English teachers in identifying and supporting struggling readers, and how they adapt their pedagogy and negotiate contextual barriers. Transcendental phenomenological design was employed. Fifteen proficient public elementary English teachers in Baguio City, Philippines, were selected through criterion purposive sampling and interviewed using semi-structured, face-to-face interviews. Transcripts were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis, and trustworthiness was supported through member checking. Four themes emerged: (a) diagnostic triage through standardized literacy assessments, (b) pedagogical flexibility and differentiated scaffolded instruction, (c) ecosystemic collaboration via remedial and peer networks, and (d) socio-contextual barriers, including parental illiteracy and resource constraints. The findings suggest that Vygotskian scaffolding must be extended to account for ecological and linguistic barriers in post-colonial multilingual classrooms, because its effectiveness is bounded by the educational and socioeconomic capital of the home. Implications for teacher professional development, curriculum localization, language-in-education policy, and parental partnership are discussed.

items.title: Urban and peri-urban agriculture in the Global South: Nexus and policies to reduce territorial inequalities and improve social welfare
items.abstract: In the Global South, rapid urbanization intensifies pressures on natural resources, food security, and social equity, progressively displacing agriculture toward vulnerable peri-urban areas. Urban and peri-urban agriculture (UPA) has emerged as a strategic approach not only for food production but also for strengthening social cohesion, climate resilience, and territorial integration. Despite growing relevance, the literature lacks systematic understanding of how Nexus frameworks are operationalized in UPA research and how they inform inclusive policy design. This study aims to systematically review UPA-Nexus research to identify emerging trends, regional patterns, governance arrangements, and policy pathways for reducing territorial inequalities in the Global South. Following the PRISMA protocol, a systematic literature review was conducted in the Scopus database (2017–2024) using Boolean operators related to UPA and Nexus frameworks. Of 92 identified documents, 49 met inclusion criteria (peer-reviewed, open-access, English-language, explicit UPA-Nexus focus). Data were systematically extracted on Nexus categories, territorial scope, governance arrangements, implementation scale, and reported outcomes. An inductive thematic analysis identified patterns and gaps across the reviewed literature. The review reveals three major contributions. First, we identify 17 distinct Nexus categories—demonstrating substantial conceptual diversification beyond the traditional Water-Energy-Food (WEF) Nexus, with emerging frameworks incorporating health, waste, climate, and social dimensions. Second, comparative analysis shows a marked regional divergence: Global North research emphasizes technological efficiency, optimization, and participatory innovation, while Global South literature addresses structural constraints, subsistence strategies, and institutional fragmentation, with studies concentrated in Africa, Asia, and Iran. Third, the analysis identifies critical governance gaps: despite policy recognition, implementation remains fragmented, with regulatory instruments ranking most effective yet predominantly locally focused, limiting territorial integration. UPA-Nexus approaches can reduce territorial inequalities when supported by enabling institutional frameworks, participatory governance, and context-sensitive policies. The review advances a conceptual framework integrating Nexus configurations, territorial dynamics, and institutional arrangements to inform integrated policy design. Findings highlight the need for strengthened institutional coordination, secure land tenure, and inclusive governance mechanisms to realize UPA's potential for advancing the SDGs in the Global South.

items.title: Recollection of Leontopodium stracheyi (Gnaphalieae, Asteraceae) from the Indian Western Himalaya after nearly a century, with notes on its taxonomy, distribution and typification
items.abstract: Floristic exploration in Uttarakhand, India, resulted in the recollection of Leontopodium stracheyi (Hook.f.) C.B.Clarke ex Hemsl. from Gunji valley, Pithoragarh district after a lapse of 95 years. The last known collection from India was made in 1929 from Ralam valley, in the same district. The present study confirms the continued occurrence of L. stracheyi within its historical Indian range. A detailed taxonomic account is provided, including an updated morphological description, habitat, and distributional information, a digital photoplate, and a diagnostic comparison with morphologically similar and nomenclaturally associated taxa. The nomenclature of the species is further reassessed, and a lectotype is designated. The newly collected georeferenced vouchers provide an important contemporary reference for future taxonomic, ecological and conservation assessments of L. stracheyi .

items.title: Beta diversity analysis reveals high turnover in benthic assemblages between tropical coral and subtropical rocky reefs
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding species distributions and biodiversity patterns is an old challenge in ecology and biogeography. This approach is especially important because of the current increase in anthropogenic pressure on coastal ecosystems. The Brazilian coastline is a mosaic of complex marine habitats, including extensive rocky shores and the largest coral reef formation in the Atlantic. By decomposing beta diversity into nestedness and turnover components, we investigated how benthic assemblages are structured and how species composition changes along the transitional zone between rocky and coral reefs. To assess the spatial components of alpha diversity, we also analyzed how species richness varies between neighboring habitats. The pairwise comparison of beta diversity revealed the highest turnover rates between the southern and northern assemblages, suggesting differentiation between the two bioprovinces. Southern provinces were characterized by suspension feeders, whereas northern provinces were dominated by stony corals along a north‒south diversity gradient. Redundancy analysis indicated that temperature was the most important environmental driver shaping benthic composition and distribution. Based on these results, we recognize different diversity patterns among two provinces and detect different levels of vulnerability should a stochastic event occur. Considering that human interference tends to increase in this area, the use of beta diversity partitioning can be a useful analytical tool to recognize communities with different levels of priority for monitoring and establishing conservation efforts.

items.title: An outlook on varied ecological engineering solutions for landslide prevention
items.abstract: This review assesses ecological engineering solutions for landslide prevention and slope stabilization by synthesizing evidence identified through scientific databases. The review encompasses the idea of applying vegetation-based techniques, including live stakes, brush layering, revegetation, grasses, herbaceous plants, bamboo plantations, and lithophytic life forms, together with conventional and structural measures such as natural geotextiles, live wooden crib walls, wattle fences, live silt fences, and live gully breaks. The reviewed evidence highlights the importance of species with strong root systems, which can influence the effectiveness of bioengineering interventions. Species such as Vetiver, Bermuda Grass, Ryegrass, Alder, selected Ficus species, and bamboo show deep-rooted control over soil reinforcement, erosion, and slope stabilization, while lithophytic life forms and pioneer colonizers may support the restoration of exposed rocky and landslide-affected surfaces. The review also examines the contribution of artificial intelligence, remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles, LiDAR, interferometric synthetic aperture radar, and machine learning models in landslide susceptibility assessment, monitoring, and advance warning. Overall, the findings revealed that integrated ecological engineering and data-driven monitoring may complement conventional stabilization measures, reduce landslide risk, restore degraded slopes, and inform sustainable land-management planning.

items.title: Deep Learning for Sequential Decision Making Under Uncertainty: Foundations, Frameworks, and Frontiers
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving increasingly beyond prediction to support decisions in complex, uncertain, and dynamic environments. This shift creates a natural intersection with operations research and management sciences (OR/MS), which have long offered conceptual and methodological foundations for sequential decision-making under uncertainty. At the same time, recent advances in deep learning, including feedforward neural networks, LSTMs, transformers, and deep reinforcement learning, have expanded the scope of data-driven modeling and opened new possibilities for large-scale decision systems. This tutorial presents an OR/MS-centered perspective on deep learning for sequential decision-making under uncertainty. Its central premise is that deep learning is valuable not as a replacement for optimization, but as a complement to it. Deep learning brings adaptability and scalable approximation, whereas OR/MS provides the structural rigor needed to represent constraints, recourse, and uncertainty. The tutorial reviews key decision-making foundations, connects them to the major neural architectures in modern AI, and discusses leading approaches to integrating learning and optimization. It also highlights emerging impact in domains such as supply chains, healthcare and epidemic response, agriculture, energy, and autonomous operations. More broadly, it frames these developments as part of a wider transition from predictive AI toward decision-capable AI and highlights the role of OR/MS in shaping the next generation of integrated learning–optimization systems.

items.title: The Effect of High-Performance Work Systems on Financial Management Behavior of Healthcare Professionals
items.abstract: This study was conducted to examine the effects of high-performance work systems on the financial management behaviors of healthcare professionals. The relationship between employees’ perceptions of high-performance work system practices and their individual financial decision-making processes was evaluated. The research population consisted of healthcare and administrative personnel working at Mersin University Faculty of Medicine Hospital. The sample size was determined as 325 individuals, and survey data were collected from 330 participants and analyzed. Descriptive statistics were used for data analysis, model significance was tested with ANOVA, and multicollinearity was evaluated through VIF values. Reverse-coded items in the dataset were corrected, and analyses were performed using a free statistical software. The findings indicated that the perception of employment security played a significant role in determining financial management behaviors. Employment security had a positive and significant effect on cash and credit management, while it showed a negative and significant effect on savings/investment and insurance management. Perceived compensation showed a positive and significant relationship with insurance management behavior. The effects of other variables were not found to be statistically significant. The study demonstrated that human resource strategies influence both organizational and individual financial decision-making. This finding contributes to the understanding of financial behaviors in healthcare institutions. Future studies are recommended to examine similar variables in different sectors.

items.title: Foundations of Reinforcement Learning and Control: Connections and New Perspectives
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning and control theory are two adjacent scientific fields that focus on optimizing the controller of unknown dynamical systems using feedback. While both fields have common roots in dynamic programming, they have evolved with distinct methodologies, goals, and cultures. Despite decades of mutual influence, a significant gap persists between the two communities. This tutorial introduces adaptive control, actor-critic reinforcement algorithms, and a new way to combine these two paradigms for data-driven decision making on a classical locomotion control problem. Our aim is to provide a foundation for understanding the core differences between the two approaches and insights to help experts in each field better understand and engage with the tools and approaches of the other.

items.title: Frequency and Risk Factors of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction in Patients Receiving Chemotherapy: A Prospective Cohort Study at a Tertiary Centre.
items.abstract: Background: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is an increasingly recognised consequence of contemporary oncological treatment. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is insensitive to subclinical myocardial injury, and locally validated thresholds for global longitudinal strain (GLS) are lacking in Vietnamese patients. Objectives: To determine the frequency and risk factors of CTRCD in patients receiving chemotherapy, and to validate a localised GLS threshold and a biomarker-based surveillance strategy for early detection. Methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 235 patients at Cho Ray Hospital (September 2023-December 2025). Patients were assessed at baseline and every three months with two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (GLS), high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). CTRCD was defined by international consensus criteria. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis; as the outcome was common, associations were quantified as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated by modified Poisson regression. Results: CTRCD occurred in 82 patients (34.9%). Incidence was highest with anthracyclines (41.2%) and HER2-targeted therapy (37.2%). A relative GLS reduction ≥12.1% predicted CTRCD with 73% sensitivity and 83% specificity. hs-TnT achieved a 100% negative predictive value (NPV), and combining GLS with hs-TnT in parallel retained a 100% NPV. Hypertension (RR 2.50, 95% CI 1.78-3.50), coronary artery disease (RR 2.47, 95% CI 1.82-3.35) and dyslipidaemia (RR 2.10, 95% CI 1.49-2.97) were associated with CTRCD. HFA-ICOS stratification was strongly predictive, with a stepwise increase in risk up to the very-high-risk category (RR 18.6, 95% CI 7.94-43.6 versus low risk; 100% event rate). Conclusions: CTRCD affected one-third of patients. A locally validated GLS threshold combined with hs-TnT enables early, resource-efficient detection, supporting a shift from reactive to proactive cardiac surveillance.
