items.title: Dual-Pathway Peroxymonosulfate Activation on FeNi-CNT@Al 2 O 3 for Efficient Tetracycline Hydrochloride Degradation.
items.abstract: Transition metal alloy catalysts are promising for advanced oxidation processes, but their application is often limited by insufficient interfacial electron transfer and poor stability. Herein, we engineered a robust FeNi-CNT@Al2O3 catalyst, derived from waste aluminum ash, for the activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and tetracycline hydrochloride (TCH) degradation. The catalyst features nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with encapsulated Fe-Ni alloy nanoparticles grown on an alumina-rich carbon matrix, creating an efficient interfacial catalytic platform through the synergy between CNT-mediated electron transfer and Fe-Ni-enhanced redox cycling. The optimized Fe1Ni2-CNT@Al2O3/PMS system achieved 100% TCH degradation with 73.5% chemical oxygen demand (COD) and 69.3% total organic carbon (TOC) removal within 30 min. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the degradation is dominated by a non-radical 1O2 pathway, with radical species ( and ) and direct electron transfer as secondary contributors. Density functional theory calculations further elucidated the critical role of Fe-Ni alloy loading in enhancing interfacial PMS adsorption and charge transfer. Notably, the catalyst maintained 91.8% TCH removal after 100 h of continuous operation. This work provides a sustainable strategy for upcycling solid waste into high-performance catalysts and elucidates the mechanism of 1O2-dominated PMS activation for persistent organic pollutant remediation.

items.title: Preferential Adsorption of Perfluoroalkyl Carboxylic Acids with Different Chain Lengths via Hydrophilic-Hydrophobic Interface Regulation.
items.abstract: Recently, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pollution has gradually shifted from a pattern dominated by traditional long-chain PFAS to a more complex situation where both short-chain and long-chain PFAS coexist. This poses significant challenges to conventional adsorbents such as activated carbon (AC) and ion exchange resins, whose adsorption performance is strongly influenced by PFAS chain length, adsorbent surface chemistry, and multiple interactions. Herein, we designed and prepared aminated polyurethane (PU) sponge materials by introducing alkylamines with different carbon-chain lengths, denoted as PPU-C2, PPU-C6, and PPU-C14 according to the carbon-chain lengths of the grafted alkylamines, thereby constructing interfaces with progressively tuned hydrophilic-hydrophobic characteristics. The resulting material exhibited chain-length-dependent adsorption preferences toward perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acid (PFCA) of different chain lengths. Specifically, PPU-C2 achieved a removal efficiency of 72% for ultra-short-chain trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) with a maximum adsorption capacity of 596 mg g-1, whereas PPU-C6 exhibited the highest adsorption capacity toward perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) (829.2 mg g-1) with a removal efficiency of 89%. In contrast, PPU-C14 showed superior affinity toward long-chain perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), achieving a removal efficiency of 96% and a maximum adsorption capacity of 848.2 mg g-1. Experimental and theoretical results supported a chain-length-dependent matching relationship between PFCA molecular structure and local interfacial polarity. Appreciable PFCA adsorption performance was also retained in natural water samples. The material also exhibited good reusability. This study highlights the role of interfacial hydrophilic-hydrophobic regulation in governing chain-length-dependent PFCA adsorption and provides a basis for designing adsorbents with tunable affinity toward PFCA of different chain lengths.

items.title: Alleviation of ammonia inhibition associated with enhanced quorum sensing signaling system under trace elements supplementation during biomethanation.
items.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) represents a mature and extensively adopted technique to dispose organic waste, yet ammonia toxicity remains a major bottleneck for stable AD operation. For activating methanogenesis-related enzymes, regulating the microbial community structure, and optimizing the reaction efficiency of AD process, supplementation of trace elements has been validated as an effective approach to counteract ammonia inhibition. However, mechanisms of how different trace elements modulate the biosynthesis and release of N-acyl homoserine lactones (AHLs), as well as the subsequent relieving ammonia inhibition are still unknown. Therefore, the current study investigated the effects of different trace elements on the secretion of AHLs under ammonia stress. The results showed that optimal concentrations of Fe, Co and Ni could enhance the secretion of AHLs, mainly N-butyryl-DL-homoserine lactone (C4-HSL) and N-hexanoyl-L-homoserine lactone (C6-HSL), and adjust microbial social behaviors under high ammonia levels. In addition, microbial community changes (enriched Bacteroidetes_vadinHA17, Syntrophomonas and Methanosarcina) were closely associated with increased methane production and stimulated AHLs accumulation by trace elements. Furthermore, increased AHLs signals correlated with intercellular communication could regulate critical genes transcription (glk, pgk, and yhdR) and enzymes synthesis (glucokinase, acetate kinase, and Coenzyme-B sulfoethylthiotransferase) to alleviate ammonia inhibition during the whole AD process. Trace elements could serve for multiple enzymes, which could be beneficial for AHL secreting hydrolytic-acidogenic consortia. The current study could provide primary insights for applying trace elements to relieve ammonia stress via AHLs regulation.

items.title: Scale-dependent associations between land use and dissolved organic matter in the mainstem and tributaries of the Three Gorges Reservoir region.
items.abstract: The spatial patterns of dissolved organic matter (DOM) in the Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR) are highly heterogeneous, yet how land use regulates these patterns across different spatial scales remains poorly understood. In this study, we characterized DOM composition and optical properties in the mainstem and representative tributaries of the TGR. After rigorous False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction, most bulk DOM optical properties did not show statistically significant differences between the two systems, suggesting a macroscopic homogenization. Model selection based on the Akaike Information Criterion corrected for small sample sizes (AICc), however, revealed distinct scale-dependent associations: the mainstem DOM was optimally explained by broader-scale land use (500 m buffer), whereas the tributary DOM was highly sensitive to local-scale land use (100 m buffer). In the tributaries, agricultural runoff strongly enhanced DOM aromaticity, whereas urban impervious surfaces reduced it. This macroscopic homogenization is likely driven by the massive water volume and longer hydraulic retention time of the mainstem, which buffer and dilute these localized inputs. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that hydrological mixing drives macroscopic homogenization while land-use control remains highly scale-dependent. This dual perspective provides a scientific basis for developing zone-specific pollution control measures tailored to different spatial scales in the TGR region.

items.title: How far do we need to go to upscale carbon elongation from bench- to industrial-scale?
items.abstract: Microbial carboxylate chain elongation (CCE) can convert biowastes into medium-chain fatty acids via the reverse β-oxidation pathway. Although the microbial mechanisms, metabolic pathways, and community ecology of CCE have been extensively investigated, the translation of CCE from bench-scale systems to industrial biorefinery applications remains unresolved, particularly when realistic biowastes are used instead of model substrates. This review classifies biowaste according to the biochemical compositions of carbohydrate, lignocellulosic, protein, and lipid to evaluate their compatibility with CCE. The required pretreatment strategies of biochemical compositions are discussed before secondary fermentation. We further discuss scale-dependent constraints associated with gas-liquid mass transfer, pH control, biomass retention, and product recovery. Thermodynamic analysis indicates that the responses of CCE and competing reactions to gas composition depend on substrate. Decoupling hydraulic retention time and solids retention time through biomass retention may facilitate stable continuous operation, although flux, fouling, and cost of membrane remain to be further investigated. This review proposes a conceptual integrated biorefinery framework for CCE from biowaste, and emphasizes that the industrial applicability should be evaluated using carbon recovery, productivity, energy and chemical demand, process stability, greenhouse-gas mitigation, and product-recovery efficiency.

items.title: Plasmid-plasmid interactions reshape extracellular vesicle cargo and antimicrobial resistance gene transfer potential.
items.abstract: Plasmids are major drivers of bacterial horizontal gene transfer, including transfer of antimicrobial resistance. Plasmid dissemination extends beyond conjugation to include extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated transport. Although bacterial EVs can carry plasmid DNA, mechanisms governing which plasmids are incorporated into EVs remain poorly understood. Here, we tested whether principles of conjugative plasmid transfer, including effects of plasmid mobility type and plasmid-plasmid interactions, extend to EV-mediated export. Using model conjugative (pKJK5) and mobilizable (RSF1010) resistance plasmids in two independent hosts, we quantified plasmid incorporation into EVs under single- and dual-plasmid conditions. Despite its lower intracellular copy number, the conjugative pKJK5 was preferentially incorporated into EVs, exceeding RSF1010 by 10- to 23-fold under single-plasmid carriage. Under co-residence, this pattern reversed: RSF1010 enrichment increased by 13- to 39-fold, whereas pKJK5 incorporation decreased by 2- to 7-fold, strongly deviating from stochastic expectations based on intracellular abundance, with effects conserved across hosts. This indicates that mobilizable plasmids exploit conjugative transfer machinery to access membrane-associated sites of preferential EV formation, thereby increasing their likelihood of EV incorporation. This demonstrates that EV cargo composition is not stochastic but is actively reshaped by plasmid-specific properties and plasmid-plasmid interactions, revealing a previously unrecognized mechanism influencing gene transfer in microbial communities.

items.title: Elevated CO 2 mitigated warming-enhanced carbon loss from northern peatland.
items.abstract: Peatlands store one-third of the global soil carbon (C) on only ∼3% of Earth's land surface but risk becoming C sources to accelerate climate change due to warming-induced C loss. Elevated CO2 (eCO2) may mitigate this loss by boosting plant C uptake. However, how eCO2 and climate warming interact to influence peatland C dynamics remains unclear. Here, we investigated peatland C fate at five warming levels (+0°, +2.25°, +4.5°, +6.75°, and + 9°C), each under ambient CO2 (aCO2) and eCO2 (+500 parts per million), by model-guided synthesis of 18 measured variables for each of the 10 treatments from an experiment. Our results showed that the peatland C loss increased with warming at a rate of 62.6 g C m-2 year-1°C-1, reaching 476.5 ± 104.7 g C m-2 year-1 at +9°C under aCO2, primarily because of increased Sphagnum mortality and accelerated decomposition. eCO2 reduced the loss rate to 17.3 g C m-2 year-1°C-1, nearly halving the C loss at +9°C (269.4 ± 80.5 g C m-2 year-1), mainly due to enhanced tree and shrub growth. Methane emissions increased with warming, similarly under aCO2 and eCO2. Our findings suggest that northern peatlands likely become major C sources under climate warming, although rising atmospheric CO2 concentration may partially slow down the C loss. Climate-driven shifts in plant community structure, rather than peat decomposition alone, play a critical role in regulating peatland C fate and may threaten the stability of peatland ecosystem functions and services in the future.

items.title: The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps.
items.abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. Yet, despite this well-established risk, data on extraction and trade are both incomplete and highly fragmented. The IPBES Global analysis estimated 50,000 species to be in trade, yet our review of wildlife trade monitoring programs found at least double that, at 107,356 species in use and trade globally. This included up to 47,685 animal species, covering 42% of all described vertebrate species. Most countries lack any systematic data on trade for species not listed in Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), with the exception of the US-specific dataset Law Enforcement Management Information System, which frequently had higher diversity of species in trade than global databases. This highlights the importance of national monitoring efforts and the need for standardized collation of wildlife trade data beyond CITES-listed species. Without these changes, global indicators on trade meant to guide sustainability and conservation will continue to focus on less than 2% of traded species.

items.title: Genome compartmentalization in a fungal insect pathogen reveals a second mating-type locus on an accessory chromosome.
items.abstract: The genomes of many fungal pathogens include rapidly evolving regions with high transposable element densities. Such regions often contain genes important for pathogenicity and may be non-core genomic elements carried on accessory chromosomes that are variably present among isolates considered to be members of the same species. Here we present a pangenomic analysis of a fungal insect pathogen, Metarhizium acridum, using six chromosomal assemblies that include isolates from four different continents. We show that the pangenome of M. acridum exhibits a continuum of compartmentalization, with a core genome that contains most of the carbohydrate-active enzymes, while accessory genes are primarily located in gene-sparse regions which encode many small secreted proteins, termed effectors, that are active during host interaction. Furthermore, we identified the first accessory chromosome in M. acridum. In contrast to the accessory chromosomes of many other fungal species, this chromosome does not encode any known effectors or secondary metabolite proteins related to pathogen-host interactions. Instead, the accessory chromosome is enriched in functions related to sexual reproduction and carries genes from both the MAT1-1 and MAT1-2 mating-type idiomorphs, in addition to the canonical MAT locus found on the core chromosomes. Notable as, within the genus Metarhizium, M. acridum is one of few species considered to regularly reproduce sexually. Our findings suggest that the presence of this accessory chromosome further facilitates sexual reproduction, possibly even primary homothallism, in the otherwise heterothallic M. acridum. Overall, our study suggests a novel mechanism in which an accessory chromosome may enhance the capacity for a fungal pathogen to undergo recombination.

items.title: Deep mutational scanning of the GPCR rhodopsin reveals pleiotropic mutational effects and their roles in modulating receptor signaling.
items.abstract: Biophysical pleiotropy, the phenomenon in which a mutation affects multiple protein properties, underlies many genetic diseases and shapes protein evolution, yet remains poorly understood, limiting synthetic biology and therapeutic development. Although extensively studied in soluble proteins, little is known about how pleiotropic effects shaped the evolution of receptor protein functions. Here, we developed a cell-based assay designed to assess pleiotropic effects in G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), the largest receptor class in eukaryotes. Because our assay allows for multiple GPCR molecular phenotypes (basal activity, ligand-dependent signaling, and cellular receptor abundance) to be simultaneously assessed, we applied it to study rhodopsin, a visual GPCR that evolved for high phototransduction capabilities by maximizing light-driven responses while minimizing noise. To investigate this, we integrated our assay with deep mutational scanning to test the impacts of ~2,000 single-residue substitutions in rhodopsin across all three molecular phenotypes (~6,000 measurements). By analyzing these data in the context of rhodopsin's protein structures, we found complex pleiotropic effects that act asymmetrically to impose joint constraints, restricting mutational tolerance in rhodopsin's retinal binding pocket and G protein interaction interface. A dose-response analysis of rhodopsin signaling revealed that these pleiotropic constraints arise from the dual functions of its chromophore, which acts as an agonist upon light-driven isomerization but also an inverse agonist in darkness. Because these constraints reflect mechanistically driven limitations in the evolution of receptor signaling, these findings reveal a role for biophysical pleiotropy in shaping the signaling capabilities of receptor proteins.

items.title: Ecology and epidemiology of multidrug resistance Salmonella in fruit Bats and shared water sources in Bangladesh.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global threat to both animal and human health, underscoring the importance of AMR surveillance across all sectors of the One Health triad, including wildlife. Fruit bats in Bangladesh frequently inhabit areas in close proximity to human settlements and livestock facilities, creating ecological conditions that facilitate the co-occurrence of AMR bacteria through direct contact or shared contaminated environments. A cross-sectional study was conducted to determine the prevalence of Salmonella spp. isolation and the proportion of antimicrobial-resistant isolates among confirmed positives, characterize resistance patterns across multiple antimicrobial classes, and identify associated risk factors in fruit bat populations and environmental water sources in Bangladesh. We collected 369 fecal samples from the roosts of two bat species, Pteropus medius and Rousettus leschenaultii, along with 22 water samples from water bodies utilized by humans, livestock, and bats. Salmonella spp. isolates were identified using selective agar culture, followed by biochemical testing and confirmation via polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Confirmed isolates underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing via the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method against 12 antimicrobials. The prevalence of AMR Salmonella spp. was 7.9% (95% CI: 5.3-11.1%) in bat's roost fecal samples and 31.8% (95% CI: 13.9-54.9%) in environmental water samples. Bat-derived isolates showed high resistance to tetracycline (93%), nalidixic acid (86%), sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (80%), and azithromycin (76%). Among the identified AMR isolates, 28 (96.5%) met the criteria for multidrug resistance (MDR), defined as resistance to three or more antimicrobial classes. Water-derived isolates also demonstrated high resistance, particularly to tetracycline (86%), amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (75%), azithromycin (73%), ceftriaxone (72%), and ciprofloxacin (71%). Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that the odds ratio (OR) of detection of MDR Salmonella spp. in fruit bats was 5.1 times higher during the summer season compared to winter. These findings highlight the evidence of MDR Salmonella spp. in fruit bats and shared environmental water sources in Bangladesh. The co-occurrence of resistant isolates across wildlife and environmental samples highlights the need for integrated AMR surveillance encompassing wildlife reservoirs and shared ecological interfaces. Strengthened antimicrobial stewardship, improved wastewater management, and coordinated One Health surveillance strategies are essential to mitigate the risk of zoonotic spillover and reduce further ecological overlap of MDR bacteria at the wildlife-livestock-human interface in Bangladesh and the broader South Asian region.

items.title: Phytogenic feed additives for climate-resilient camel production in arid and semi-arid regions: current evidence and research priorities.
items.abstract: Camels play a vital role in supporting food security and livelihoods under the harsh feed, water, and environmental conditions of arid and semi-arid regions (ASARs), owing to their remarkable ability to tolerate heat stress and prolonged dehydration, travel long distances, and efficiently utilize low-quality forage resources available in these regions. Nevertheless, increasing climatic stress, coupled with fluctuating feed availability, infectious and parasitic diseases, and limited access to veterinary services, continues to constrain camel production in ASARs. Phytogenic feed additives are increasingly being explored as nutritional strategies to support foregut function, animal health, and product quality; however, the strength and directness of the available evidence for these effects in camels remain critically underexplored. This structured narrative review, grades available evidence from controlled camel studies, camel-specific mechanistic investigation, other foregut fermenters, and biologically more distant animal models. Its novel contribution is a camel-centered evidence hierarchy that separates demonstrated effects from comparative mechanisms and hypothesis-generating evidence while linking each candidate additive to specific research requirements. Potential applications include the modulation of foregut fermentation, oxidative and inflammatory status, microbial ecology, immune responses, parasite management, and milk and meat quality. However, direct camel evidence remains insufficient to establish effective doses, long-term safety, residues, sensory effects, or economic returns. Phytogenic feed additives therefore merit investigation as potential nutritional interventions, but current evidence does not support their routine use in camels. Future studies should use chemically characterized preparations, dose-response designs, clinically and economically meaningful outcomes, together with integrated assessments of foregut function, immune status, animal health, product quality, safety, and feasibility under dryland production conditions.

items.title: Insights into Copper Hazards and Species Sensitivity in Freshwater and Saltwater Ecosystems.
items.abstract: Over the past few years, copper (Cu) has been considered the contaminant posing the greatest risk in aquatic environments. This study, therefore, aimed to evaluate species sensitivity and Cu hazards to aquatic organisms in freshwater and saltwater ecosystems. The results showed that there was no significant difference in Cu hazards between the two environmental matrices, with 5% hazardous concentrations (HC5s) of 6.21 µg/L for freshwater organisms and 9.42 µg/L for saltwater counterparts. However, obvious differences were observed among taxonomic groups; for instance, freshwater algae exhibited the highest sensitivity (HC5 = 0.93 µg/L), whereas marine fish showed the greatest tolerance (HC5 = 39.75 µg/L). These findings provide valuable insights into Cu hazards and associated ecological risks, thereby guiding water quality management and strategies to safeguard aquatic ecosystems from Cu contamination.

items.title: Paired 15N-labeling evidence for efficient nitrate utilization by mature temperate broadleaved trees.
items.abstract: Different nitrogen (N) forms might be used by various plant functional groups to reduce competition and promote coexistence. Broadleaved trees are generally considered prefer to take up nitrate, whereas conifers prefer to ammonium. However, this belief lacks in situ evidence from mature trees under field conditions. We conducted in situ paired 15N labeling on mature trees of six common species (three broadleaved, three conifers) in northeast China to assess their 15N-ammonium and 15N-nitrate uptake and reveal mechanisms underlying interspecific variation in N form utilization. All six species had higher uptake rates for 15N-nitrate than for 15N-ammonium, with 15N-nitrate rates 1.5- to 4.8-fold higher than those of 15N-ammonium. On average, the studied broadleaved species took up 15N-nitrate 3.4 times faster than 15N-ammonium (2.6 ± 0.4 vs.0.8 ± 0.1 μg 15N g-1 d-1). 15N-nitrate contributed 75% to total N uptake of broadleaved trees and 66% to that of conifers. Whole plant 15N-nitrate recovery was 2.7-fold higher than 15N-ammonium in the broadleaved species and was substantially higher than that in conifers (15.0 ± 1.8% vs. 2.8 ± 0.4%). Soil pH greatly affected 15N-nitrate uptake, possibly through soil pH modulation on soil nitrification and nitrate availability. Leaf nitrate reductase activity (NRA) and mycorrhizal colonization were also partially correlated with interspecific variation in nitrate acquisition. Our field experiments provided empirical evidence that common broadleaved species and conifers in northeast China predominantly take up nitrate over ammonium, particularly the studied broadleaved species, which may facilitate their growth and dominance in the future under changing climate.

items.title: Ecological role of the heterotrophic protist Aurantiochytrium (Labyrinthulomycetes) as a key consumer of viral-induced dissolved organic matter following the lysis of the red tide-forming microalga Heterosigma akashiwo.
items.abstract: Marine algal blooms play a vital role in oceanic carbon cycling. However, the ecological consequences of the organic matter released following bloom collapse via viral infection are poorly understood. Recent studies have shown that viral infection dramatically alters the intracellular metabolite composition of the host, and that the resulting viral lysate selectively promotes the growth of specific prokaryotic populations. This study aimed to elucidate the effects of organic matter derived from healthy and virus-infected cells of the bloom-forming alga Heterosigma akashiwo on the growth of heterotrophic eukaryotes, specifically labyrinthulomycetes. These marine protists are primarily saprotrophic or predatory and contribute to dissolved organic matter (DOM) decomposition and nutrient cycling. Field monitoring conducted in Osaka Bay over a 12-month period revealed that, although the overall Labyrinthulomycetes community showed no clear seasonality, specific populations of these protists co-occurred with Heterosigma akashiwo . To mechanistically investigate the potential trophic linkage suggested by these field observations, a co-culture system comprising H. akashiwo , its specific virus (HaV53), and Aurantiochytrium sp. NBRC102614, used as a model labyrinthulomycete, was established. In co-culture experiments, viral lysis of H. akashiwo led to a significant increase in the cell density of Aurantiochytrium sp., demonstrating that Aurantiochytrium can thrive on substrates derived from virus-infected algae, including viral-induced dissolved organic matter (vDOM). These findings highlight that heterotrophic Labyrinthulomycetes are key consumers of virus-modified organic matter, playing a pivotal role in carbon cycling following the collapse of harmful algal blooms and influencing carbon transfer within coastal microbial food webs. Importance Marine ecosystems are shaped by interactions among microalgae, viruses, and heterotrophic eukaryotes, although the ecological roles of heterotrophic protists remain poorly understood. This study investigated the dynamics of oceanic microalgae and heterotrophic eukaryotes, namely Heterosigma species and Labyrinthulomycetes, and examined the effects of viral infection of Heterosigma akashiwo on the growth and proliferation of Aurantiochytrium species, members of the heterotrophic Labyrinthulomycetes. Our results revealed the dynamics of several Labyrinthulomycetes associated with Heterosigma populations and suggested that Aurantiochytrium species can redistribute carbon by utilizing the vDOM released during Heterosigma bloom termination induced by viral infection. These findings also reposition Aurantiochytrium from a passive heterotrophic component to an active ecological agent associated with Heterosigma viral infection, thereby influencing microalgal community dynamics. Overall, this study provides new insights into the fate of virus-infected Heterosigma in coastal marine systems, mediated by heterotrophic Labyrinthulomycetes, particularly Aurantiochytrium species, thereby filling an important knowledge gap in microbial ecology.

items.title: Diversity and connectivity of microbial eukaryotes in High Arctic terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
items.abstract: High Arctic ecosystems are being rapidly altered by climate change. Increased permafrost thaw and rainfall are making terrestrial landscapes more hydrologically active, increasing the input of organic and inorganic material into freshwater systems and freshening coastal marine ecosystems. Understanding the ecological implications of this environmental change requires an improved taxonomic and ecological resolution for less-studied microbial eukaryote communities. Microbial communities were investigated from freshwater, terrestrial, and coastal marine ecosystems on Ward Hunt Island, Ward Hunt Ice Shelf and Ellesmere Island along the coastal margin of the Last Ice Area, Canadian High Arctic. For the first time, Arctic microbial eukaryotic diversity was assessed using full-length 18S rRNA gene metabarcoding sequencing. Terrestrial microbial eukaryotic richness correlated with soil moisture, extending biogeographical patterns observed in lower latitudes. A greater connectivity between terrestrial and freshwater, than to coastal communities was identified, with a predicted input of terrestrial microbial eukaryotes into the Ward Hunt Lake microplankton. As Arctic catchments become more hydrologically active, increased transport of microbial eukaryotes may strengthen connectivity and homogenisation between terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems, while greater freshwater inputs may alter microbial diversity in adjacent coastal waters.

items.title: Living evidence map of the global climate and health literature.
items.abstract: Objectives This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (flexible). The objectives are as follows: The objectives of this living evidence map are to: systematically map the breadth, scope, and characteristics of the global literature on the relationship of climate change, climate variability, weather, climate-forcing agents, and fossil fuels with human health and well-being; enable ongoing, up-to-date access to the evolving evidence base through a living approach (encompassing content currency and adjustment of methods); enable identification of clusters of well-researched areas and evidence gaps; enable flexible, accelerated identification, visualization, selection, analysis, and export of records according to the needs of a diverse group of interest holders via an interactive interface and filtering via a dedicated taxonomy; enable the continuous monitoring of a specific topic of interest; and evaluate the rigor, legitimacy, and utility of an AI-supported living evidence mapping approach. Specifically, we envision the map to enable: researchers to identify, collate, and select existing evidence and diverse study designs, explore clusters and gaps, and produce evidence syntheses in a more efficient way; policymakers and international and intergovernmental organizations (such as the World Health Organization or the Sustainable Development Goals Synthesis Coalition) to understand the scope, scale, and distribution of the evidence; research funding bodies to take a more evidence-based approach to funding decisions and identify and fund priority topics, where evidence is most needed and duplication of efforts is avoided; science assessment bodies such as the IPCC or the Lancet Countdown on Climate Change and Health to obtain a comprehensive overview of the research landscape and obtain easy access to relevant lines of evidence for their assessment; health professionals and health systems decision-makers to monitor emerging evidence and evidence syntheses in specific areas that can inform clinical and public health practice and guidelines; and patients and communities directly affected by climate change to gain an overview of the literature relevant to the health risks they face and support the development of evidence-based preparedness and resilience strategies.

items.title: Analysis of Factors Associated with Early Childhood Caries in Jinan City: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Purpose Early childhood caries (ECC) remains a global public health challenge characterized by high prevalence and low treatment rates. This study investigated factors associated with ECC among 3- to 5-year-old children in Jinan through oral examinations, questionnaires, and caries activity testing, aiming to support early prevention. Materials and methods A total of 733 children aged 3-5 in Jinan were enrolled. Sociodemographic information, feeding patterns, and oral health behaviors were collected via questionnaires completed by legal guardians. The number of decayed, missing, and filled surfaces (dmfs) was recorded. Oral plaque was collected for Cariostat caries activity testing. Statistical analyses were conducted to identify factors associated with ECC and the relationship between ECC and caries activity. Results Among 733 participants, the prevalence of ECC was 76.8%. Factors statistically significantly associated with caries severity included age, gender, primary caregiver's educational attainment, frequency of sweet-snack consumption, and the habit of nighttime milk feeding or falling asleep with a nipple (all p 0.05). The proportion of high-risk children (by Cariostat) progressively increased across the caries-free, low-caries, and high-caries groups (p 0.001). Conclusion Low educational attainment of the primary caregiver, inappropriate feeding practices, frequent sugary food intake, and poor oral hygiene habits are risk factors for ECC. Oral health education and promotion of proper oral hygiene habits are therefore needed. Furthermore, the acid‑producing metabolic activity of oral plaque microorganisms increased significantly with caries progression, suggesting that Cariostat test values may serve as a potential indicator of cumulative caries severity in preschool children.

items.title: Effects of Gonadal Suspensions of Disk Abalone Haliotis discus discus on Egg Laying, Sperm Release, and Fertilization Rate.
items.abstract: Marine organisms often respond to chemical cues released by conspecifics, and such cues can trigger reproductive behavior. In abalone, gamete release by one individual may stimulate spawning in nearby individuals. In this study, gonadal suspensions prepared from the ovaries and testis of disk abalone Haliotis discus discus were incubated for approximately 1 h at different temperatures and then exposed to sexually mature individuals to evaluate their egg-laying- and sperm-release-inducing activity, as well as the quality of the resulting gametes. Suspensions incubated at room temperature (20 ± 0.3°C) or at 40°C generally retained their egg-laying- and sperm-release-inducing activity relative to freshly prepared suspensions. However, egg-laying-inducing activity of the ovarian suspension in females appeared to begin to decline at 40°C, although the difference from the control was not statistically significant (p = 0.086). Overall, the inducing activity of the gonadal suspensions decreased sharply at 50°C, at which egg laying and sperm release were significantly reduced. However, when gametes obtained after exposure to the gonadal suspensions were artificially fertilized, fertilization rates did not differ significantly among treatment groups. These results indicate that incubation temperature had little effect on subsequent fertilization success. In contrast, the gamete-release-inducing activity of components present in the gonadal suspensions was sensitive to heating, with a marked decline at 50°C. The findings provide insight into the thermal sensitivity of gamete-release-inducing activity in abalone gonadal suspensions and may contribute to a better understanding of chemical communication during reproduction in marine invertebrates.

items.title: Carotenoid Cleavage Dioxygenase 8 Enhances Interspecific Facilitation in Maize-Soybean Intercropping via Arbuscular Mycorrhiza Symbiosis Under Phosphate Limitation.
items.abstract: Carotenoid Cleavage Dioxygenase 8 (CCD8) regulates strigolactone (SL) biosynthesis, which mediates the establishment of arbuscular mycorrhiza fungal (AMF) symbiosis. This symbiosis makes a major contribution in nutrient uptake, thereby improving crop productivity, mostly without the need for specific inoculation. Quantifying the extent of this contribution in typical intercropping systems remains challenging. A pot experiment was conducted using ZmCCD8 knockout (zmccd8), overexpression (ZmCCD8-OE), and wild type (WT) maize lines, grown in sole cropping or intercropping with soybean under low phosphate (LP) and control conditions. Intercropped ZmCCD8-OE and soybean showed a 61.9% higher overyielding effect, partially attributed to a 72.7% greater AMF colonisation rate in ZmCCD8-OE than WT counterparts under LP. Together with the greater root, AMF promoted P accumulation by 58% and 35% in the ZmCCD8-OE shoot and root, respectively. Conversely, intercropped zmccd8 conferred negative impacts under LP, corresponding to 47.6% and 63.4% less overyielding and AMF colonisation, respectively. Consistent with these results was differential expression of genes (CCD8, D14, CCaMK, CYCLOPS, RAM1, PT6/PT8) regulating AMF symbiosis and P uptake in maize and soybean. Collectively, ZmCCD8 enhances interspecific facilitation by stimulating root growth and AMF symbiosis, providing a genetic approach for higher crop productivity in intercropping systems without inoculation.

items.title: Site-Specific Functional Response of the Tibetan Plateau's Forests to Climate Change Over the Past 200 Years - A Tree-Ring Isotope Perspective.
items.abstract: Global warming challenges forest resilience on the Tibetan Plateau by disrupting tree's physiological adjustments. However, understanding the physiological adjustments between autotrophic and heterotrophic metabolism under shifting moisture regimes remains challenging. We investigated 200-year tree functioning across a moisture gradient using tree-ring width and carbon isotope variation (δ 13 C) to indicate water stress, and the covariation between tree-ring cellulose δ 18 O and δ 2 H (O▬H relationship) to indicate shifts in autotrophic and heterotrophic metabolism. The moist site exhibited strong and stable O▬H coupling, reflecting dominant hydroclimatic control, though recent droughts induced decoupling and reduced growth. In contrast, the semi-arid site showed lower and variable O▬H relationship, reflecting repeated transitional functional state. The arid-site forest showed increased growth due to recent wetting, yet persistent OH decoupling indicated ongoing physiological adjustments. Combined with the instrumental data, we found that O▬H coupling strength depended on site-specific hydroclimatic baselines, appearing stronger in dry years at arid sites but in wet years at semi-arid sites. Overall, our framework provides a quantitative, time-resolved perspective on trees' physiological response across moisture regimes. The O-H relationship serves as an early-warning tool for detecting forests undergoing functional shifts under ongoing climate change.

items.title: Repeatability of adaptation in interacting species.
items.abstract: In many evolving systems, mutations have background-dependent fitness effects due to genetic interactions between loci within a genome (intragenomic epistasis). In coevolving species, genetic interactions can span across genomes, a phenomenon described as intergenomic epistasis. It is known that intragenomic epistasis can make adaptation more repeatable by constraining accessible mutational paths from a specific starting genotype, generating path repeatability. Here, we investigate how endpoint repeatability - how often adaptation from different starting genotypes reaches the same states in the genotype and fitness space - is influenced by the interplay of intra- and intergenomic epistasis. To this end, we model a two-species community in which the fitness of each genotype depends on the combination of present genotypes of both species. We implement this by constructing and simulating adaptation on coevolutionary fitness landscapes using an NKC(S) model, an extension of Kauffman's NK model of evolution that includes intergenomic epistasis. On these fitness landscapes, we simulate adaptive walks that alternate between mutations in a focal and a partner species. To quantify the repeatability of adaptation, we track the endpoints of adaptive walks and record the fitness of both species at the evolutionary endpoints. We find that individual fitness landscapes with intergenomic epistasis can maintain high endpoint repeatability. Yet, intergenomic epistasis causes highly variable fitness outcomes across different fitness landscapes. Thus, patterns of repeatability deviate from expectations based on single-species adaptation in the presence of intragenomic epistasis, due to varying fitness trade-offs between species, which can lead to cycling and large coevolutionary fitness loads.

items.title: Fixed mindset-signalling peer behaviours predict impostor feelings and evaluative concerns.
items.abstract: Beliefs that ability is fixed can make challenges feel like evidence of inadequacy rather than opportunities to learn. Peers play a powerful role in communicating these beliefs through their everyday words and behaviours, yet prior research has relied primarily on cross-sectional surveys or hypothetical scenarios. This research examined how peers' mindset-signalling behaviours relate to impostor feelings and evaluative concerns as they unfold in daily life and as they are remembered. Study 1 included 130 undergraduates (670 daily reports) enrolled in at least one STEM course, and Study 2 drew on follow-up interviews with 18 of these students. Study 1 used a 10-day daily diary design with Bayesian multilevel modelling to examine within-day associations between peer behaviours, impostor feelings and evaluative concerns. Study 2 used retrospective interviews to explore how students interpreted and made meaning of these experiences. On days when students observed peers expressing fixed-mindset cues, such as fixed-ability statements or self-deprecating remarks, they reported higher levels of impostor feelings and evaluative concerns. Observing peers persist through difficulty predicted lower impostor feelings that day. Retrospective interviews echoed these patterns, although different moments stood out in memory. Students most often recalled peers sharing their struggles or offering help as emotionally meaningful experiences. Peer mindset signals matter both in daily experience and in later memory. Daily verbal cues were associated with same-day impostor feelings and evaluative concerns, whereas remembered moments of vulnerability and support became incorporated into broader emotional narratives.

items.title: Can LLMs Take Psychological Surveys? A Case Study Using DeepSeek Models on Studies of Jealousy and Consent.
items.abstract: Online platforms such as Amazon's MTurk enable researchers to collect large amounts of data quickly and efficiently, but the potential presence of bots threatens the validity of such data. These concerns have been mitigated to some extent by the ease of detecting bot-produced data. The present study tested whether data generated by DeepSeek, a large language model (LLM), might prove less detectable by (1) avoiding tell-tale signs characteristic of data produced by unsophisticated bots, and (2) producing results that mirror results from human samples. We tested this in two sexuality-related research contexts. First, we examined whether DeepSeek was able to replicate the sex difference in jealousy (Buss et al., 1992). Second, we examined whether DeepSeek rated safewords as more important for pick-up play than for BDSM scenes conducted between romantic relationship partners (Tarleton et al., 2025). We tested DeepSeek's performance with four models, each with increasing parameter count, corresponding to sophistication and computational cost to use. For the sex difference in jealousy, the highest-level model produced a significant, theory-consistent sex difference but lower-level models failed to do so. For safewords, one of the four models replicated the effect observed in humans, with the highest-level model producing homogeneous results in which nearly all "participants" indicated that safewords were extremely important in both contexts and lower-level models producing noisier results with no difference between contexts. In addition, DeepSeek had particular difficulty reflecting assigned demographics on questions with select-all-that-apply formats, sometimes selecting all options in a manner that would be implausible in human respondents. Although in the present study, DeepSeek generally failed to mirror results from human samples, LLM survey responses on closed-ended questions are likely to be difficult to detect at the individual-response level, especially when intermingled with human data. Further, current LLM costs are substantially lower than typical compensation paid for survey completion, underscoring concerns that LLM fraud might be occurring already.

items.title: Shear-wave elastography in rotator cuff tears: a systematic review of measurement properties, tissue-stiffness findings, and clinical interpretability.
items.abstract: Shear-wave elastography (SWE) may quantify rotator cuff mechanical properties, but its measurement performance and clinical interpretability remain incompletely established. This work sought to synthesize evidence on the feasibility, measurement properties, and interpretability of rotator cuff SWE in adults with rotator cuff tears (RCTs). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies were in vivo primary studies in adults (≥ 18 years) with suspected or symptomatic rotator cuff disease in whom partial- or full-thickness RCT was confirmed by an imaging or surgical reference standard, including conventional ultrasound, MRI, CT, or arthroscopy, and/or studies including clinically relevant comparator shoulders or asymptomatic controls. Studies had to use ultrasound SWE with quantitative outputs, including shear-wave speed/velocity or modulus, in the supraspinatus tendon and/or rotator cuff muscles. Thirteen SWE studies were retained from 6273 records. Two primarily assessed reliability/repeatability. Intra-rater reproducibility was high in the primary reliability studies, including ICCs > 0.87 and 0.96, whereas inter-rater reproducibility was lower and variable, ranging from ICCs > 0.73 to 0.45. Eleven studies contributed construct-validity or known-groups evidence, one provided strict criterion-validity evidence against intraoperative passive stiffness, and two provided longitudinal postoperative evidence. SWE findings varied across tissue targets, devices, regions of interest, arm positions, comparators, and reference standards. Only one study explicitly defined chronicity, and direct postoperative/prognostic evidence was limited. SWE appears useful as a complementary quantitative imaging tool for selected rotator cuff tissue-characterization and measurement-property applications. However, inter-rater reproducibility, measurement error, chronicity assessment, and prognostic validity remain insufficiently established. Question Can shear-wave elastography (SWE) address the unmet need for reliable quantitative rotator cuff tissue assessment beyond conventional imaging in adults with tears? Findings Thirteen studies showed high intra-rater reproducibility but variable inter-rater reproducibility. Evidence for chronicity assessment and prognosis remained sparse and heterogeneous. Clinical relevance SWE may complement ultrasound or MRI by quantifying selected rotator cuff mechanical properties, but current evidence does not justify using it alone to determine tear chronicity, reparability, or prognosis.

items.title: A metacognitive approach to learning and performance in human-AI interaction.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly becoming a pervasive technology across education, work, research, and everyday life. Yet growing evidence suggests that fluent, coherent, and seemingly transparent AI assistance can improve task performance while weakening the metacognitive engagement and deeper processing required for durable learning. This tension raises a central question about how does offloading to AI reshape human learning, and under what conditions do performance and learning decouple? In this Perspective, we introduce the Synergetic Notion of Human-AI Skills and Knowledge Construction (SYNC) model. The model offers a metacognitive account of human-AI interaction by conceptualising metacognitive offloading and metacognitive onloading. The SYNC model aims to explain how human-AI interaction unfolds across learning and performance dimensions, clarifying how learners may drift into overreliant AI-supported performance or move toward human-AI synergy. We further identify key pitfalls in ineffective human-AI interaction and outline strategies to address them through metacognitive onloading and support human-AI synergy.

items.title: Role of the BLA-NAc pathway on recovery from frustrative nonreward.
items.abstract: Unexpected reward downshifts induce transient suppression of consummatory behavior through a process involving frustrative nonreward. We hypothesized that the recovery of behavior rests on the extent to which the downshifted reward becomes an acceptable reward. We argued that this requires the basolateral amygdala (BLA) to switch from activating the central amygdala (CeA), which leads to suppression, to activating the nucleus accumbens (NAc), which enhances rewarding effects. This hypothesis was tested using Cre-dependent inhibitory and excitatory DREADDs expressed in BLA neurons projecting to the NAc. Rats were trained to consume 32% sucrose in preshift sessions and exposed to 2% sucrose in postshift sessions, generating transient consummatory suppression. Histology showed that an estimated 25-32% of BLA cells were involved in the projection to the NAc in each group. Virus controls treated with CNO were not different from vehicle-treated animals. Inhibition of the BLA-NAc pathway by the DREADD activator clozapine N-oxide (CNO) delayed recovery of normal licking behavior across postshift sessions relative to vehicle-treated animals. This effect was not attributable to locomotor interactions with licking. Excitation of the BLA-NAc pathway exhibited only a nonsignificant trend toward increased licking, but also a nonsignificant trend toward reduced activity in the conditioning box. These results provide support for the hypothesis that the BLA-NAc projection is involved in the recovery of consummatory behavior following violations of reward expectancies.

items.title: An ERP Study of the Effects of Category Knowledge and Contextual Knowledge Using a Cue-Target Matching Paradigm.
items.abstract: Object categorization depends not only on the current visual input but also on prior knowledge. However, whether different types of prior knowledge influence object categorization with the same temporal profile remains unclear. In this study, we combined a cue-target matching paradigm with event-related potentials (ERPs) to compare the effects of category knowledge and contextual knowledge on object categorization. Category knowledge was manipulated at the superordinate, intermediate, and basic levels, whereas contextual knowledge was based on typical color and scene information. The behavioral results showed that cue-target congruency affected task performance, with different patterns observed across cue conditions. The ERP results further revealed that prior knowledge influenced multiple stages of processing, but the temporal pattern varied across conditions. Category knowledge showed level-dependent effects across intermediate, conflict, and later processing stages, whereas contextual knowledge was associated mainly with P2 and N400 modulation. These findings suggest that different types of prior knowledge contribute to object categorization with different temporal dynamics and that these differences may be related to how the relevant information is structured and used during cue-target matching.

items.title: Brain systems supporting the narrative self and psychopathology.
items.abstract: Disturbances in the narrative self are implicated across psychiatric disorders, with abnormalities in the neural systems supporting its generation and regulation constituting a transdiagnostic risk factor for mental illness. This review highlights how alterations in these brain systems underlie prevalent clinical features, including diminished, rigid, and sustained negative beliefs within the narrative self. The narrative self is framed as a higher-order construct that emerges from multiple systems, with reward, punishment, and motivational signals biasing which experiences are encoded as self-defining and which self-beliefs are reinforced over time. We discuss recent evidence demonstrating how the narrative self is supported by distributed brain networks in which subcortical inputs from the basal forebrain, habenula and mediodorsal thalamus modulate default mode network activity, with the salience, frontoparietal, cingulo-opercular, and hippocampal-parahippocampal networks regulating how self-beliefs are established or updated. Adolescence is emphasized as a developmental period uniquely vulnerable to disturbances in the formation of a coherent, flexible narrative self, wherein asynchronous subcortical and cortical development and pubertal changes interact to confer risk for diminished and rigid self-beliefs. Belief-updating tasks, hierarchical computational models, and ecological momentary assessment are proposed as approaches to quantify how self-beliefs form and shift across time, linking neural signatures of the narrative self to momentary variability. We propose that treating the narrative self as a primary level of explanation for psychopathology positions it as a testable target for future neuroimaging research, providing a clearer bridge from self-referential cognition to interventions in daily life.

items.title: Sex differences in the clinical phenotype of difficult-to-treat asthma in adults.
items.abstract: Sex disparity has been demonstrated within difficult-to-treat (difficult) asthma, with females reported to have greater disease severity and more comorbidities. Deeper understanding of these differences could help personalise management approaches. To assess differences in disease characteristics between males and females with difficult asthma. The Wessex AsThma CoHort study collected data from 500 patients across Southern England. Patient demographics, asthma and its treatment history, allergies, comorbidities, radiology, biological samples, lung function, and questionnaire data were subjected to univariable analyses to identify sex differences. Variables were then further assessed in multivariable regression models. Males were older at disease onset and were more often ex-smokers. In multivariable regression models they had higher serum immunoglobulin E (ratio 1.95, 95% CI 1.19 to 3.20) and plasma inflammatory cytokine expression (interleukin-17, tumour necrosis factor - alpha, C-C motif ligands 3 and 11 and chitinase 3-like 1). Males had poorer lung function (forced expiratory volume in 1 second effect -9.98, 95% CI -15.21 to -4.74) and more frequently had nasal polyps. Females had higher Body Mass Index, and in multivariable regression higher plasma adipokine (ratio 1.25, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.37) and interleukin-5 expression (effect 3.52, 95% CI 2.65 to 4.39), multimorbidity burden (score effect 0.60, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.92), anxiety/depression, and inducible laryngeal obstruction (odds ratio 2.38, 95% CI 1.20 to 4.76). They self-reported worse Hull Cough Hypersensitivity, Nijmegen and Sino-Nasal Outcome Test scores. We observed no difference in treatment and healthcare utilisation, or composite asthma severity score. Sex influences difficult asthma phenotype but contrasting factors are associated with similar overall disease severity in both sexes. Males have worse lung function and systemic inflammatory profiles, whilst females experience greater psychophysiological comorbidity and multimorbidity burden. Recognising differences and considering them clinically to fine-tune management may help improve difficult asthma outcomes.

items.title: Brain CYP2D alters orally administered oxycodone induced conditioned place preference in rats.
items.abstract: Oxycodone is an opioid analgesic metabolized by the CYP2D enzyme to oxymorphone. We investigated in rats the impact of CYP2D metabolism in the brain on oxycodone-induced reward and aversion, assessed by conditioned place preference (CPP). During conditioning rats were confined to one compartment for 60 minutes after gavage with oxycodone (or oxymorphone) or with water; treatment and compartments were alternated daily for six days. Rats then underwent 60 minutes of posttests for five days where CPP was assessed. Pretreatments with the CYP2D inhibitor propranolol, or vehicle, injected intracerebroventricularly 24 hours - prior to first and third of six conditioning sessions blunted CPP and with a trend for increased aversion to the oxycodone paired compartment. Pretreatment with the brain CYP2D enzyme inducer nicotine, for 12 days prior to oxycodone conditioning, did not change CPP to oxycodone but tended to reduced aversion to oxycodone paired compartment. Oral oxymorphone induced a CPP with no observed aversion; it was unaffected by CYP2D inhibitor pretreatment. Together this indicates that oral oxycodone and oral oxymorphone both induce CPP. Inhibiting brain CYP2D, previously shown to reduce the relative concentrations of oxycodone to oxymorphone, reduces CPP and tended to increase aversion suggesting that variation in CYP2D activity in the brain could be a source of interindividual differences in oxycodone induced reward and abuse liability.

items.title: A deadly intersection: The role of race and mental illness in 11 years of police killings.
items.abstract: People of color and people with mental illness are at increased risk of police use of force. The aim of this study was to determine how the intersection of race and mental illness affects the risk of being killed by police and quantify compounded vulnerability relative to single-identity risk. A cross-sectional study conducted in 2026 of all U.S. police killings from 2013-2023 using the Mapping Police Violence database. Deaths were coded for signs of mental illness and race/ethnicity. Relative risk (RR) was calculated by dividing subgroup killings by corresponding adult population counts. The analytic sample included 9,318 individuals aged ≥18 killed by police after excluding cases with missing data. People with signs of mental illness were over seven times more likely to be killed by police than those without (RR=7.41). Black people were over three times more likely than White people (RR=3.06). Intersectional analyses showed compounded risk: Black people with signs of mental illness were over 19 times more likely to be killed than White people without (RR=19.31). Race and mental illness independently increase risk, but their intersection produces extreme vulnerability. Findings underscore the need for reforms addressing racial inequities, mental health care gaps, and police-based crisis response.

items.title: Parietal tDCS and tactospatial working memory: Evidence for a behavioral benefit in a sham-controlled crossover study.
items.abstract: The posterior parietal cortex (PPC) contributes to spatial working memory (WM), but whether parietal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) can modulate tactospatial WM remains unclear. Thirty-two adults completed a double-blind, sham-controlled, within-subject crossover study with two counterbalanced visits comprising baseline, intervention, and post-intervention phases of a retro-cued tactospatial delayed match-to-sample task. During the intervention phase, active tDCS (2mA, 15min) or sham tDCS (30-s ramp-up followed by ramp-down) was applied with a left-parietal anode and right-supraorbital cathode. A sliding-window analysis identified a temporally localized Active-Sham improvement during the later part of the task. This contrast was significant under the hypothesized directional test (p = 0.041), but not under two-sided testing across the primary temporal search interval (p = 0.083). A supplementary analysis using narrower common temporal bounds yielded a significant two-sided result. The corresponding condition difference was not significant when averaged across the complete intervention phase. Baseline accuracy was negatively associated with the selected stimulation response (r = -0.327), consistent with the directional hypothesis, although this relationship and the covariate-adjusted analyses did not reach significance under two-sided testing. Together, these findings point to a possible behavioral benefit of parietal tDCS in tactospatial WM, while indicating that its magnitude, temporal characteristics, and relationship with baseline performance require further confirmation.

items.title: Facilitators and barriers to lethal means counseling in veterans with substance use disorder: A qualitative analysis of veteran and clinician perspectives.
items.abstract: U.S. Veterans with substance use disorders are at disproportionately high risk for suicide. Lethal Means Counseling is a collaborative approach where clinicians and Veterans discuss strategies to reduce access to lethal means. While evidence is strong for lethal means counseling reducing suicide risk broadly, the unique needs and experiences of this population are not well understood. This qualitative study sought to elicit perspectives from U.S. Veterans and Veterans Health Administration clinicians about barriers and facilitators to the delivery of and participation in Lethal Means Counseling for Veterans with substance use disorders. In this pragmatic and postpositivist study, semi-structured qualitative interviews were conducted with 15 U.S. Veterans with substance use disorders identified through electronic health record review and recent completion of lethal means counseling and with 10 Veterans Health Administration clinicians who administered lethal means counseling. Interviews explored experiences with lethal means counseling and substance use in relation to suicide risk. Inductive and iterative thematic analyses were used to code transcripts of interviews for barriers and facilitators at the Individual, Inner Setting, Outer Setting, and Innovation levels of the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. Six themes were identified for barriers, including substance use as a coping strategy, lack of assessment and access to care, nondisclosure and autonomy, ease of access, military culture, and substances increase risk. Three themes were identified for facilitators, including recognition of use as problematic, sharing resources, and providing a rationale for lethal means counseling. Veterans with substance use disorders experience unique challenges that interfere with efforts to reduce suicide risk. The findings of this study highlight current gaps and opportunities for improving conversations during Lethal Means Counseling and may help enhance implementation among those with Substance Use Disorders. Substance use magnifies suicide risk and it will be important for future research to develop strategies to help mitigate this risk.

items.title: Heat anomaly, wildfire smoke, social-material vulnerability, and incident depression in a national EHR-linked cohort: A preregistered secondary analysis.
items.abstract: Recent heat and wildfire smoke may influence depression, yet evidence from longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) cohorts remains limited. We conducted a preregistered secondary analysis in the All of Us Research Program. Adults with a valid index date, residential 3-digit ZIP code prefix (ZIP3) linkage, no EHR-recorded depression before baseline, and post-baseline EHR follow-up were linked to 30-day pre-index PRISM maximum-temperature anomaly, Stanford Environmental Change and Human Outcomes (ECHO) wildfire-smoke PM2.5, and a participant-level social-material vulnerability (SMV) composite. Cox models estimated hazards of first EHR-recorded broad depression. The linked cohort included 179,218 participants and 5484 incident depression cases over a mean follow-up of 371 days. Each standard deviation (SD) higher 30-day temperature anomaly was associated with higher depression hazard in Aim 1 (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-1.10) and Aim 2 (HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.04-1.11). We found no evidence of an association between 30-day mean wildfire-smoke PM2.5 and depression. SMV had a stronger per-SD association (HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.33-1.40) than heat anomaly and was stable under stricter component-completeness rules. Heat and SMV associations were similar across follow-up periods, whereas the smoke association varied over time. Exposure was assigned at ZIP3 level and was not updated after baseline. Depression reflects EHR-recorded diagnosis, and differential health-care access or unrecorded prior depression may affect ascertainment. Higher local temperature anomaly and greater SMV were associated with first EHR-recorded depression. We found no evidence of an association between mean wildfire-smoke PM2.5 and depression in the preregistered primary model, while secondary smoke analyses showed heterogeneity by exposure metric and follow-up period. The SMV association was stronger than the heat-anomaly association.

items.title: Pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus and mortality risk in preterm infants: a Bayesian meta-analysis across gestational age groups.
items.abstract: Recent randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses have questioned the safety of early pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants, suggesting possible increases in the risk of mortality and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Whether these risks vary by gestational age remains uncertain. We aimed to compare the effects of pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks versus those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater. For this Bayesian model-averaged meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for randomised controlled trials enrolling infants with a gestational age less than 32 weeks and echocardiographically confirmed patent ductus arteriosus who were randomly assigned either to pharmacological treatment or to placebo or expectant management. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality before 36 weeks' postmenstrual age and secondary outcomes were moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated. RRs greater than 1 indicated harm. We calculated the posterior probability of harm (Prharm=P[logRR>0]) and Bayes factors comparing harm versus benefit (BFharm/benefit). This study is registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024622527). Ten randomised controlled trials including 2365 infants (1133 female and 1232 male) were analysed; 1045 had a gestational age less than 26 weeks. Pharmacological treatment was associated with increased mortality in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks (RR 1·12 [95% CrI 0·90-1·41], Prharm=0·85, BFharm/benefit=5·48), in those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater (1·22 [0·90-1·77], Prharm=0·89, BFharm/benefit=7·82), and in the overall population (1·23 [95% CrI 1·00-1·54], Prharm=0·97, BFharm/benefit=36·04). For bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite outcome of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, analyses explicitly incorporating the possibility of no effect indicated that the data were more consistent with the no-effect model than with either the benefit or the harm model. The currently available randomised evidence is consistent with an increased mortality risk associated with pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment, without evidence of a compensatory reduction in bronchopulmonary dysplasia. This association was evident both below and above the 26-week gestational age threshold. These findings question the safety of routine pharmacological treatment and underscore the need for more selective, evidence-based approaches for patent ductus arteriosus management. None.

items.title: Negatively valenced stimuli selectively enhance frontal midline theta during inhibitory control.
items.abstract: Frontal midline theta (FMT) is a well-established neural marker of cognitive control, yet the extent to which emotional stimulus characteristics modulate this signal remains unclear. The present study examined whether emotional stimulus valence influences FMT during inhibitory control using a modified Go/No-Go task across two experiments. In Experiment 1, participants completed trials in which action cues were paired with negative or neutral images. Results revealed a significant Emotion × Action interaction, such that FMT power was selectively enhanced for negative relative to neutral stimuli during No-Go trials, with no emotional modulation observed during Go trials. In Experiment 2, positive stimuli were included to distinguish between valence-specific and general emotional salience accounts. Replicating Experiment 1, FMT was significantly greater for negative relative to both neutral and positive stimuli during No-Go trials, whereas neutral and positive conditions did not differ. Secondary analyses of control-related FMT (No-Go minus Go) showed greater FMT for negative relative to positive stimuli, whereas negative and neutral conditions and neutral and positive conditions did not significantly differ. Across both experiments, emotional stimulus valence did not reliably modulate behavioral accuracy or reaction time, indicating a dissociation between neural and behavioral indices of control. Together, these findings suggest that negatively valenced stimuli are associated with selective modulation of FMT during inhibitory control, a pattern more consistent with a valence-specific response than a generalized emotional salience interpretation. The absence of reliable behavioral effects further suggests that increases in FMT may reflect enhanced recruitment of control-related neural systems rather than improved performance.

items.title: Longer cue duration supports stable spatial gradients in multiple-cue inhibition of return.
items.abstract: When multiple cues are presented simultaneously, inhibitory orienting effects can become organized around the center of gravity (CoG) of the cue array rather than individual cue locations. However, recent work using brief 50-ms cues found that this CoG-organized inhibition of return (IOR) was attenuated at longer cue-target intervals and failed to emerge even in single-cue conditions (Christie et al., 2021), leaving open whether cue duration contributes to durable, spatially organized inhibitory tagging. Here, we tested this possibility using 200-ms cues (the duration used in prior work establishing the CoG effect) across cue-target onset asynchronies (CTOAs) of 400 and 1000 ms, while recording saccadic reaction times (SRTs) in a multiple-cueing task. The 400-ms CTOA replicated conditions known to produce robust CoG effects, and the 1000-ms CTOA provided the novel empirical test. SRT decreased as the distance between the target and the cue-array CoG increased, particularly for cued targets, with CoG-related gradients evident at both CTOAs. Model comparisons on uncued trials indicated that neither CoG distance nor local distance independently accounted for a significant share of variance, suggesting that their relative contributions cannot be separated with the present dataset. These findings are consistent with cue duration being an important parameter in sustained, spatially organized IOR in multiple-cue displays.

items.title: Depressive Symptoms and 6-Year KCCQ Health Status in Chronic Heart Failure: Findings From the Cognition.Matters-HF Cohort.
items.abstract: Long-term disease-specific health status trajectories in ambulatory chronic heart failure (HF) are incompletely characterized, and the contribution of depressive symptoms remains uncertain. The objectives of the study was to characterize 6-year Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score (KCCQ-OSS) trajectories and distinguish persistent and visit-specific depressive symptom associations with health status. In the prospective Cognition.Matters-HF cohort, 148 patients with HF underwent assessments at baseline and 6, 12, 36, and 69 months. Linear mixed-effects models estimated KCCQ-OSS trajectories and prespecified correlates. Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores were decomposed into between-person and within-person components. Sensitivity analyses addressed missingness, and exploratory lagged analyses assessed whether recent PHQ-9 worsening predicted subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events. KCCQ-OSS remained stable over 69 months (78.0-76.6; change: -1.4; 95% CI: -4.6 to 1.8; P for time = 0.065), despite substantial individual variation. Higher between-person PHQ-9 burden (β: -3.44 per point; 95% CI: -4.00 to -2.88; P < 0.001) and within-person PHQ-9 worsening (β: -1.80; 95% CI: -2.50 to -1.11; P < 0.001) were associated with lower concurrent KCCQ-OSS. Recent PHQ-9 worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ-OSS, a ≥5-point KCCQ decline, or all-cause death/HF hospitalization. NYHA functional class and 6-min walking distance, but not N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, left ventricular ejection fraction, or executive function, were independently associated with KCCQ-OSS. In ambulatory chronic HF, average KCCQ-based health status remained stable over 6 years despite substantial individual variation. Depressive symptoms were strongly associated with concurrent health status, but recent worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events.

items.title: The effect of language on the orienting of spatial attention and inhibition of return.
items.abstract: This study examined whether neutral words in native and alternative languages can serve as exogenous cues that elicit spatial attention and inhibition of return (IOR), a hallmark of reflexive attentional disengagement. Across six experiments, participants performed a modified Posner cueing task in which peripheral word cues (in Hebrew, Arabic, English, or Chinese) were followed by an asterisk target at varying stimulus onset asynchronies (SOAs; 100-850 ms). A robust IOR effect was observed across experiments, with slower responses on valid trials compared to invalid ones regardless of language familiarity or orthographic similarity. While IOR emerged at the earliest SOAs in Experiments 1-5, its onset was delayed until 350 ms under conditions of lower cue-target contrast in Experiment 6. While cue language did not interact with validity, subtle SOA × Language interactions revealed modest processing delays for alternative-language words, particularly at intermediate SOAs. These findings demonstrate that neutral words can serve as effective exogenous cues, though the current design cannot definitively isolate responses to their visual properties from automatic orthographic processing. The consistent IOR effects at early SOAs indicate that attentional capture by these stimuli is robust, extending prior research by demonstrating that this holds even across scripts that are orthographically dissimilar. Thus, this study contributes to models of exogenous attention by showing that low-level orienting mechanisms respond to linguistic input with surprising flexibility and speed.

items.title: Parental factors in screen time of schoolchildren: A systematic literature review.
items.abstract: Digital devices have become an inevitable part of modern daily life, and the time spent on screens has increased across all age groups in recent years, including among children. Children's screen time is associated with various factors, among which parental factors remain important. Although numerous studies have explored their relationship, evidence synthesis on the association between parental factors and schoolchildren's screen time behavior remains limited. This study aims to systematically review cross-sectional quantitative empirical studies on parental factors associated with screen time among schoolchildren aged 5-15 years. Systematic literature searches in SCOPUS and PubMed were conducted to identify original research, applying a set of inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in the selection of 25 studies. We identified six major parental factors and the corresponding practices and behaviors associated with screen time in schoolchildren. These include parental screen time rules, parental educational level, parenting styles, parental perceptions of environmental factors, parents' screen-viewing behavior, and parental attitudes toward screens. The study results suggest that children's screen time is associated with parental and family-level factors. Therefore, interventions targeting children's screen time should consider these factors to yield positive outcomes. Addressing excessive screen time by partnering with parents is crucial for supporting children's well-being and potentially reducing the risk of psychosocial difficulties in childhood and adulthood.
