items.title: Acute stress attenuates the coupling between gastric interoception and snack consumption.
items.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of the mechanisms underlying eating behavior is crucial for preventing and treating obesity and eating-related disorders. Gastric interoceptive sensitivity, defined as the perceptual threshold of satiation and fullness, is a key physiological marker of meal termination. Although stress is known to influence eating behavior, its impact on the relationship between gastric interoception and food intake remains insufficiently understood. This study behaviorally examined the association between gastric interoceptive sensitivity and snack consumption under high- and low-stress conditions, while accounting for individual eating traits. In 61 fasted adults, gastric interoceptive sensitivity and self-determined snack intake were assessed following both a stress and a control task across four laboratory sessions. Gastric interoceptive sensitivity was measured using a novel paradigm, the Magic Table (MT). Multilevel analyses showed that both satiation and fullness perception thresholds were significantly associated with snack consumption. Under stress, however, only the fullness threshold remained significantly related to snack intake. Higher emotional and restrained eating scores were linked to a weaker association between gastric interoceptive sensitivity and snack intake, whereas higher uncontrolled eating scores showed the opposite pattern. These findings suggest that satiation and fullness signals guide snack termination under low stress, whereas acute stress and certain eating styles weaken the coupling between gastric signals and behavioral regulation. Dysregulated eating may therefore reflect impaired integration of interoceptive input into decision-making, particularly under stress. Beyond enhancing interoceptive sensitivity, studies on interoceptive-focused interventions may benefit from strengthening the integration of satiation signals into eating decisions, especially in stressful contexts.

items.title: Multimodal Analysis of Child-Horse Therapeutic Interactions Using Vision-Language Models in an Australian Aboriginal Equine-Assisted Learning Program for Social and Emotional Well-Being: Development and Evaluation Study.
items.abstract: The human-horse bond has played a role in human development throughout history and has more recently been applied to mental health promotion through equine-assisted learning (EAL) programs. In EAL settings, therapeutic documentation and assessment commonly rely on practitioner observations documented through behavioral checklists, structured interviews, and progress notes, which can pose challenges due to time demands, subjectivity, and inconsistent standardization across practitioners and contexts. This study aimed to address these challenges in the context of mental health promotion programs. This study developed an AI-powered digital health framework based on vision-language models (VLMs) to analyze child-horse therapeutic interactions in EAL settings. The framework was developed in collaboration with the Yawardani Jan-ga EAL program, which supports the social and emotional well-being of Aboriginal youth in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. The proposed framework comprises three core components: (1) an activity classification module using a VLM with few-shot learning based on Sigmoid Loss for Language-Image Pre-training 2 (SigLIP2) to identify 9 therapeutic activities; (2) a proxemics analysis module using a Qwen2.5-VL-7B VLM to classify physical contact between the child and horse; and (3) a body posture analysis module applying multimodal chain-of-thought prompting and self-consistency techniques to classify children's body posture into confidence-related states with interpretable reasoning. The framework was developed and evaluated using real-world images collected during therapeutic sessions with Aboriginal children participating in the Yawardani Jan-ga program. The activity classification module achieved an accuracy of 90.6%, with macroaveraged precision, recall, and F1-scores of 92.0%, 91.1%, and 91.1%, respectively, under the selected 2-shot configuration. The proxemics analysis module achieved an accuracy of 88.6%, with macroaveraged precision, recall, and F1-scores of 89.0%, 88.0%, and 88.5%, respectively, under the 1-shot configuration. For the body posture analysis module, system reliability was assessed using internal consistency metrics, achieving an average consistency of 0.916, an agreement rate of 0.705, a rationale coherence of 0.857, and a vote entropy of 0.174. Overall, the findings suggest that AI- and VLM-based approaches can provide complementary support for practitioner-led documentation and assessment of observable child-horse therapeutic interactions in EAL settings. These approaches may help reduce practitioner burden and strengthen the assessment of programs that promote children's social and emotional well-being.

items.title: Promotion of Tanning Behaviors on Instagram: Content Analysis.
items.abstract: Adolescents and young adults may be particularly susceptible to social media content that promotes tanning and appearance-based beauty standards. This study examined the characteristics and messaging of pro- and antitanning Instagram posts and the extent to which they promoted health damaging- or health enhancing-behaviors. A cross-sectional content analysis of 100 Instagram posts using the hashtag #tanning assessed creator characteristics, tanning practices, commercial promotion, tanning-related messaging, beauty standards, and health risks and benefits. χ2 and Fisher exact tests were used to determine differences between pro vs anti stances for categorical and dichotomous variables, and the Mann-Whitney U test was used for continuous variables. Most videos were protanning (79/100). Protanning videos were significantly greater than antitanning videos to have been posted in 2026 (77.2% vs 47.6%; P=.02), feature teen and young adult creators (87.3% vs 52.4%; P<.001), and include shopping tags promoting tanning products (30.4% vs 0%; P<.001). Overall, messaging focused on promoting tanning (76%) and advocating for tanned skin as a standard of beauty (63%) and downplayed the use of sun protection (11%) and the risks associated with tanning (20%). Messaging varied significantly by tanning stance, with antitanning videos focused on sun protection and health risk. Findings indicate an urgent need for clinicians to lead content creation on popular social media platforms to counter the health-damaging effects of unreliable, incomplete, and potentially misdirected information that is posted under popularized hashtags.

items.title: Real-World Implementation and Evaluation of a Digital Health Platform for Children Living With Type 1 Diabetes: Protocol for a Real-World Implementation Study.
items.abstract: Digital platforms that integrate continuous glucose monitoring, patient-generated data, and clinical decision support could enable more proactive pediatric type 1 diabetes (T1D) care. Sustained uptake of digital platforms in routine practice is limited, and the evidence of effectiveness is mixed. Implementation science approaches are needed to clarify how context, workflows, and strategies shape adoption and outcomes. Haibu Diabetes is a new platform that brings together wearable, patient-reported, and clinical diabetes data to generate personalized, data-driven insights for patients and clinicians. This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness and implementation processes of Haibu Diabetes in routine pediatric T1D care using a hybrid design guided by an Implementation Research Logic Model. We will conduct a nonrandomized, quasi-experimental, type 2 hybrid implementation-effectiveness trial at a hospital that provides multidisciplinary pediatric diabetes care. Youth aged 3 to less than 18 years with T1D and caregivers will be onboarded to Haibu Diabetes as part of routine workflows; health care providers will use a clinician dashboard to review data, assign tasks/forms, and communicate asynchronously. Effectiveness analyses will compare Haibu Diabetes users to a matched control group drawn from the BC Pediatric Diabetes Registry. Effectiveness outcomes are hemoglobin A1c, continuous glucose monitoring device-derived time in range over 12 months, and diabetes self-care behaviors. Implementation outcomes will be assessed using mixed methods guided by an Implementation Research Logic Model that links determinants, implementation strategies, mechanisms, and outcomes. These outcomes will include reach, adoption, feasibility, acceptability, and maintenance. Health care improvement outcomes will include patient and caregiver experience, clinician experience, and operational workflow indicators. Study funding commenced in January 2023. Patient recruitment began in September 2026, and 7 participants had consented as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by December 2027, with analysis to follow. Study findings are expected to be published in summer 2028. This trial will generate real-world evidence on both effectiveness and the conditions required to implement and sustain a data-integrating digital platform in pediatric T1D care, informing scale-up and optimization.

items.title: Momentary emotion regulation and executive function in daily life.
items.abstract: Emotion regulation (ER) strategies are theorised to impose differing cognitive demands. However, little is known about the momentary association between ER strategy use and executive function (EF) in daily life. To address this issue, 224 young adults (Mage = 22.59, SDage = 3.52 years) completed an experience-sampling protocol (4x/day for 7 days), reporting use of engagement (positive reappraisal, acceptance) and disengagement (detached reappraisal, distraction) ER strategies, as well as positive and negative pre-regulation emotional intensity for the focal event. At each sampling occasion, participants also completed EF tasks assessing the core components of inhibition, updating, and shifting. We tested whether ER strategy use would be negatively (depletion account) or positively (facilitation account) linked to fluctuations in EF performance. Consistent with the facilitation account, findings indicated that, at the within-person level, use of engagement ER strategies was associated with better EF performance. Conversely, the within-person use of disengagement ER strategies was not linked to EF. However, on occasions when participants reported high (but not low) pre-regulation positive emotional intensity, greater use of disengagement strategies was associated with better EF performance. These findings suggest that momentary shifts in both ER strategy use and emotional intensity jointly relate to EF in daily life.

items.title: Does trauma-focused psychotherapy alter pre-existing memories? A survey of German psychotherapists.
items.abstract: Little is known about how pre-existing trauma memories change under trauma-focused therapy. We surveyed 224 German therapists trained in trauma therapy regarding observed memory changes, therapeutic practices, and beliefs about trauma and memory. Most reported using trauma-focused interventions primarily for PTSD, although some reported using them to complete fragmented memories (49%) or recover inaccessible memories (19%). Most agreed that traumatic experiences are usually remembered, but some endorsed scientifically questionable beliefs about inaccessibility or recovery being a therapeutic goal. Many reported observing memory changes (82%), and among these, a substantial proportion reported the emergence of new traumatic memories (81%), although such experiences were relatively uncommon overall (12% reported them as occurring "often" or "very often"). Memory changes usually involved emotional meaning, narrative expression, and retrospective reappraisal. Problematic changes, such as alterations in temporal-spatial context (39%) and substantial changes in core event details (18%), were less frequent. Reports of recovered memories, but not of changes in existing memories, were associated with potentially problematic beliefs and attempts to complete or recover memories, and such patterns were more common among psychodynamic therapists than among cognitive-behavioural therapists. Taken together, these findings add to the complex picture of how trauma-focused interventions may affect memory and diverge from laboratory evidence generally indicating no effects on memory. They highlight the importance of evidence-informed training on trauma, memory, and suggestibility, as well as longitudinal research on trauma memory changes during therapy.

items.title: The effects of drawing and writing encoding methods on item and associative recognition in younger and older adults.
items.abstract: Age-related decline in associative memory is well documented, and drawing has consistently been shown to enhance memory. However, whether the mnemonic benefits of drawing extend from item memory to associative memory remains unclear. The present study examined the effects of encoding method (drawing vs. writing) and encoding strategy (standard memorisation vs. relational encoding) on item and associative recognition in younger and older adults. Two complementary experiments were conducted. In Experiment 1, participants encoded word pairs by drawing the words or repeatedly writing them, without instructions to integrate the two words. In Experiment 2, the same encoding methods were examined under relational encoding instructions encouraging meaningful integration of the two words. Across both age groups, drawing consistently enhanced item recognition relative to writing. Without relational encoding instructions, however, this advantage did not extend to associative recognition. Under relational encoding, drawing continued to benefit item recognition, whereas writing produced superior associative recognition. Cross-experiment analyses further showed that the relationship between encoding methods and memory performance differed as a function of encoding strategy. These findings suggest that the effectiveness of an encoding method depends on both the encoding strategy adopted during learning and the type of information to be remembered, identifying an important boundary condition of the drawing effect.

items.title: Linkshänder, Gaucher or Lefty: Does left-handedness identity need to be considered when expanding handedness classifications?
items.abstract: Understanding the meanings of handedness is important when defining and labelling different handednesses. Although the majority group of right-handers may not consider their handedness often, this is not the case for left-handers. Human environments are constructed to facilitate ease for the majority, reinforcing privilege and making handedness somewhat "under the radar" for right-handers, whilst left-handers, as a minority group, have a long history of being oppressed and discriminated against. Social psychology, particularly social identity theory, tells us that categories are powerful psychological constructs. Humans are intrinsically drawn towards identifying with groups and becoming members, with resultant influences of membership on individuals. Group identity plays an important part in people's lives and can have a psychological impact or influence. Due to structural barriers and cultural influences, how we investigate differences between individuals from separate groups can be important depending on how they view the saliency of that membership. Empirical evidence shows that left-handers regard their handedness as more meaningful, central and important than right-handers. We suggest that researchers consider the influence of (handedness) categorization on individuals and that the overt nature of handedness makes an everyday binary split of right and left a powerful entity and especially meaningful to left-handers.

items.title: The hidden mental health burden of corruption in healthcare: Findings from a scoping review and key informant interviews.
items.abstract: Corruption in healthcare is a pervasive global challenge that undermines equity, efficiency, and trust in health systems. Whilst its economic and governance impacts are well documented, the psychological consequences for patients, providers, and those involved in anti-corruption reform remain under-explored. Understanding these mental health effects is critical for designing anti-corruption strategies that safeguard wellbeing and strengthen health systems. An exploratory mixed-methods study was conducted to map an emerging evidence base. A scoping review of 25 peer-reviewed and grey literature sources was complemented by four key informant interviews, which were used to interpret and contextualise the review findings. Findings were synthesised into a conceptual framework mapping pathways between corruption and mental health outcomes. Corruption was reported to be associated with psychological distress among patients, providers, and anti-corruption actors. This included stress, anxiety, depressive symptoms, and moral injury. At a community level, corruption eroded trust and collective agency, whilst institutional effects included normalisation of unethical practices. Structural determinants were found to perpetuate corruption's harms. Anti-corruption efforts produced mixed outcomes: reform targeting high-level officials improved public mental health modestly, whereas punitive measures against frontline workers exacerbated fear and demoralisation in the workforce. Protective factors such as moral agency, and robust reporting systems were found to buffer harm but were context dependent. Policy recommendations are made for practice, research and capacity building. These include framing corruption as a public mental health issue, strengthening whistleblower protections, commissioning further research, and adapting reform to local political economy and social norms. These findings indicate that corruption is a plausible but under-recognised social determinant of mental health requiring further research. Integrating mental health considerations into anti-corruption policy and health system reforms is essential to mitigate harm and strengthen resilience.

items.title: The loneliness paradox: a scoping review of cognitive biases in loneliness.
items.abstract: Loneliness motivates reconnection, yet paradoxically fosters hypervigilance to negative social cues and cognitive biases that may serve self-protection. This scoping review mapped studies of three biases, attention, interpretation and approach-avoidance, through the lens of Social Information Processing model, to identify patterns and methodological gaps. Searches of PsycINFO, MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science identified 50 studies using behavioural, eye-tracking, psychophysiological, self-report and neural measures. Findings depended on how each bias was measured. Behavioural evidence for attention bias towards negative social cues was mixed, whereas neural evidence more consistently showed heightened responses to such cues. Interpretation bias was the most consistent finding in which lonely individuals interpreted ambiguous social cues as hostile or rejecting. Evidence on approach-avoidance bias was limited but theoretically informative. Situational loneliness was linked to approach and chronic loneliness to avoidance. Because almost all studies were cross-sectional, they reflect between-person differences rather than the within-person processes that evolutionary accounts describe. Future research needs within-person and experimental designs, reliable bias measures, more studies of children and adolescents, and a clearer distinction between situational and chronic loneliness.

items.title: Alcohol use and its associations with mental health across the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.abstract: While the COVID-19 pandemic caused major disruptions to social connections and lifestyles, many countries continued the sale of alcohol as an essential commodity. Evidence on change in alcohol use, and its association with mental health and wellbeing during the pandemic is, however, mixed and limited to initial periods of the pandemic. This study aimed to address these research gaps. Data were drawn from the COVID-19 Risks Across the Lifespan (CORAL) Study, a three-wave longitudinal study conducted between May 2020 and April 2021. The present sample included 2,369 participants (ageM = 38.81 ± 16.94 years, range = 11-100; 90% females) from the United Kingdom, United States, and Australia. Measures included pre-pandemic alcohol use and changes in consumption frequency, quantity, drinking behaviours (e.g., drinking earlier in the day), and motivations (e.g., drinking for enjoyment) during the pandemic. General perceived stress, COVID-19-related stress, loneliness, and symptoms of depression and anxiety were also assessed. Drinking frequency and quantity remained stable across the first year of the pandemic; however, non-linear age associations were found. Young individuals aged between 11 to 20 years, and mid-aged individuals aged between 50 to 70 years, had the highest probability of increased alcohol use frequency and quantity. Drinking behaviours and motivations also remained largely stable, although age- and country-specific differences emerged, potentially reflecting policy differences such as alcohol access restrictions and lockdown measures. Finally, loneliness unidirectionally predicted subsequent alcohol use quantity. These findings highlight the heterogeneous alcohol use patterns across age groups and countries during the pandemic, and underscore loneliness as an important public health issue with implications for alcohol misuse.

items.title: Metabolic signatures accompany exploratory movement in climbing plants.
items.abstract: Climbing plants rely on exploratory movements to locate and reach supports in the environment. Circumnutation is central to this exploratory behavior, yet little is known about the physiological signaling dynamics that accompany this movement. Here we show that the presence or absence of a climbing support is associated with distinct volatile organic compounds (VOCs) intensity profiles in Pisum sativum plants. Using temporal analyses aligned with circumnutation cycles, we detected distinct VOCs patterns in plants growing with or without a potential support in the surrounding environment, even before physical contact occurs. Overall VOCs intensity and the coupling between VOCs signals and circumnutation movement descriptors were higher when supports were absent. This pattern suggests that support-seeking movements are associated with metabolic changes that are in line with early physiological adjustment associated with the environmental context. Our findings identify a previously undescribed association between VOCs dynamics and circumnutation modulation during support searching in climbing plants.

items.title: Capturing experienced invisibility among people with multiple stigmatized identities: The experienced invisibility scale protocol.
items.abstract: Invisibility is the experience of not being attended to, remembered, differentiated from others, or given credit for contributions. In the current registered report, we aim to validate the Experienced Invisibility Scale (EIS), a measure designed to capture experiences of invisibility, which are most likely to be experienced by people with multiple stigmatized identities. As proof of concept, we first present a pilot study testing the factor structure of the EIS, in which we found that: 1) a bifactor model ("unheard" and "unnoticed") best represents the structure of experienced invisibility, but that calculating a total score is likely to be sufficient for most purposes, 2) the EIS is most likely to be experienced by those with multiple stigmatized identities, and 3) initial tests of convergent, discriminant, and predictive validity were supported. We then propose three studies to further validate the EIS and its links to social identities. Study 1 will distinguish the EIS from related constructs of social exclusion, objectification, rejection sensitivity, positive and negative affect, and other experiences of discrimination, test the temporal stability of the EIS, and examine relationships with well-being. Study 2 will examine whether the EIS predicts additional outcomes including health, low felt impact, perceived powerlessness, and denial of services or power. Study 3 will test hypotheses that Black women (compared to White women and Black and White men) will report experiencing more invisibility, and will show stronger relationships between invisibility and negative outcomes. We hope this work will aid scholars in better understanding invisibility as a form of discrimination.

items.title: Empowering scientific performance and health: MERIT - A survey study and research perspective.
items.abstract: Academic performance involves achieving one's goals and reaching one's full potential while staying mentally, emotionally, and physically well. This can be challenging across all career paths. This article presents results from a new survey examining key psychological factors and how early-career researchers evaluate them in relation to their scientific performance and health as they pursue their career goals. A total of 475 participants (e.g., in Germany, Switzerland, or Austria) evaluated psychological factors that, according to previous research and psychological theories, influence academic success. The evaluations included participants' assessments of their self-competence, motivation, and work effort; achievement emotions (including negative and positive experiences that influence well-being); perceptions of supervision; and views on reasons for staying or leaving academia. Gender differences and differences between PhDs and postdocs were also analyzed. Overall, PhD students and postdocs felt confident in and satisfied with their academic performance. They evaluated their competencies, effort, and motivation as key to achieving their career goals. Satisfaction, effort, and self-efficacy showed no gender differences, but women reported higher levels of worry and negative emotions, particularly among postdocs. Challenges such as time and financial constraints, as well as the benefits of working outside academia, influenced self-perceptions of career decisions. Most participants reported regular supervision; a few had experience with or were participating in early-career initiatives. The study emphasizes the need to consider young scientists' beliefs, feelings, and expectations about their academic performance, achievement, and health when developing early-career strategies to reduce perceived barriers and reflect career decisions. The current approach and results are discussed in relation to previous studies, the observed challenges, and the gaps this research addresses.

items.title: Scientific reasoning promotes elementary school science learning: A longitudinal study.
items.abstract: This longitudinal study investigates how early scientific reasoning relates to the development of science knowledge from kindergarten through elementary school. We followed 161 children recruited from urban and rural regions in southern Germany (89 girls, 72 boys, aged 6.12 years ± 4.04 months; 11% spoke a language other than German at home) over 5 years, assessing competencies annually, starting in 2014. Scientific reasoning was assessed with the Science-Kindergarten Inventory (SK-I) and the Science-Primary School Reasoning Inventory (SPR-I), targeting experimentation, data interpretation, and understanding the nature of science. Science knowledge was measured with tasks on melting, evaporation, density, and displacement. Controlling for cognitive abilities, language, and socio-educational background, results show that scientific reasoning in kindergarten predicts later gains in science knowledge. These findings highlight the foundational role of scientific reasoning in domain-specific learning across middle childhood.

items.title: Trusting the AI rather than the expert? Evidence from sports-related assessments in relation to the Olympic Games 2024.
items.abstract: We investigated how predictions regarding the outcome of sports competitions are affected by concurrent predictions which were believed to originate from either a human sports expert or an AI system. Participants were asked to estimate the probability of a certain team to win a group match against the respective opponent in various matches of the 2024 Olympic Games and to report their confidence in that estimate. Moreover, they received numerical estimates for that probability which were either high or low, and which were believed to originate from a human expert or an AI system. Participants' estimates were biased towards these supplementary estimates, thus reflecting an anchoring effect. Yet, this effect's size was independent of the believed source of the anchor and even non-significantly higher for AI support. Confidence in provided judgments was even significantly higher when the believed origin of supplementary estimates was AI rather than human. Altogether, the results suggest no bias against AI-generated sports outcome predictions, highlighting the task-dependency of reliance on AI.

items.title: From Little Kids, Big Kids Grow: The Development of Emotion Regulation Abilities from Childhood to Adolescence.
items.abstract: Less effective emotion regulation abilities during childhood represent a significant factor of risk for healthy child development. However, despite much research into less skilled emotion regulation abilities, findings about the outcomes of emotion regulation ability trajectories in adolescence are inconsistent. This may reflect methodological challenges in undertaking prospective longitudinal research, or a lack of clarity about factors that influence developmental outcomes. Therefore, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine the prospective relation between early childhood (ages 3-6) emotion regulation abilities and adolescent outcomes (ages 13-16). Peer reviewed prospective longitudinal research studies published in English since 2015 were included in the review if they examined emotion regulation abilities in early childhood; assessed subsequent outcomes in adolescence; and examined risk, protective, or promotive factors associated with emotion trajectories. Statistical analyses utilized random effects models and reported pooled effect sizes within groups. Of 27,490 records identified, 16 studies were included in the systematic review, and 10 in the meta-analysis. Early emotion regulation abilities that were less adaptive predicted subsequent less adaptive regulation, psychiatric difficulties, academic concerns, and social challenges in adolescence. Risk and promotive factors for early childhood emotion regulation abilities included pregnancy-related factors, parental mental health, socioeconomic status, child characteristics, cognitive and behavioral traits, and family dynamics. This highlighted the complex interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors. There was conflicting evidence about sex, suicidality, and externalizing behaviors, and quantitative analyses revealed high heterogeneity among the studies. The findings offer insights about the identification of youth at risk, and the development of targeted clinical interventions to enhance adolescent developmental outcomes.

items.title: Supporting Children of Parents with Mood Disorders, Anxiety or Substance Use Problems: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Psychosocial Interventions.
items.abstract: Psychosocial interventions for children of parents with mood disorders, anxiety and/or alcohol and substance use problems may reduce their vulnerability to negative developmental outcomes and strengthen their resilience. However, existing studies vary in quality, making it difficult to identify best practices. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled studies evaluating psychosocial interventions for children (aged 0-18) of parents with mood disorders/anxiety and/or alcohol/substance use problems. A total of 34 studies, involving 3205 children (51.7% female), identified through PubMed, PsycINFO, and Scopus, met the inclusion criteria. Results showed that these interventions are effective in reducing internalizing symptoms both in the short (g = - 0.25) and long term (g = - 0.21), and in decreasing externalizing symptoms in the short term (g = - 0.16). However, there was insufficient evidence for significant effects on theoretical mechanisms such as family related factors or children's coping skills. Furthermore, program effectiveness did not differ based on the type of intervention or its underlying theoretical framework. These findings support the general efficacy of psychosocial interventions in improving mental health outcomes in at-risk children, regardless of program type or approach.

items.title: Proposal of Gender-Sensitive Diagnostic Indicators for the Detection of Gambling Disorder in Women: An Exploratory and Qualitative Approach to Women's Narratives.
items.abstract: Women and men exhibit a different clinical profile, as there are numerous individual, social or cultural factors that influence how women involve themselves in gambling, interpret the risks, and experience the consequences. The experiences of female gamblers are underrepresented in research related to gambling disorder (GD), since, in the absence of including gender perspective, the findings mostly represent the characteristics of male gamblers. Since the publication of the DSM-5 several studies point to gender biases in the diagnostic criteria. In the present study, focus groups were used to collect the reported experiences of 28 women with GD. The main objective was to review the current framework and develop an exploratory proposal of gender-sensitive diagnostic indicators for GD in women, in order to incorporate specific clinical indicators and severity markers in the female population. The results reveal that the most prominent factors in women with GD are having suffered gender violence, sexual abuse, caregiving, loneliness, motherhood, relational conflicts, low family support and stigmatisation. Understanding the differences in the clinical manifestations of women with GD is essential for visibility, assessment and diagnosis.

items.title: Beyond the Universal and the Culturally Determined Human: Reframing the Biosocial Problem Under Neo-Structuration.
items.abstract: The biosocial problem concerns how biological and sociocultural factors condition human mentality and development. Throughout the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was framed primarily in terms of the relative influence of nature and nurture: biology ensured stability, whereas culture operated as a transformative force. The rise of cross-cultural, indigenous, culture-inclusive, and global psychologies added another question: whether psychological characteristics presented as universal by mainstream theories are in fact culturally specific. Yet both formulations focused on how biology and culture shape human beings. We argue that the growth of the pace of societal transformations due to changes of their causal forces in the context of neo-structuration require a new formulation of the biosocial problem. Biology and culture remain causally consequential, but their direct conditioning power is increasingly mediated by human agency. Agency becomes an ontologically irreducible causal factor, as human beings not only develop within biological and cultural conditions but also select, recombine, and transform those, thereby reshaping themselves and their technological, cultural, and institutional environments. To reconstruct conceptual resources for this argument, we draw on theories focusing on the transformability of the human in the history of psychology and in contemporary discourse. Soviet theories recognized human plasticity but generally presumed that the direction of transformation was institutionally prescribed, though Rubinstein's concept of Subjekt and Ananiev's account of self-determination and individuality offer resources for moving beyond this limitation. We propose a recursive model in which biology and culture condition human development but agentic action transform those, thereby changing subsequent living contexts.

items.title: Auricular point acupressure for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: a randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is common and persistent, with limited management options. This trial primarily examines whether auricular point acupressure (APA) improved CIPN outcomes versus usual care; a secondary pragmatic aim compared in-person mobile support (mAPA) with virtual (vAPA) delivery. Two hundred twenty-seven cancer survivors with CIPN were randomized to mAPA (n = 80), vAPA (n = 75), or usual care (n = 72). Both APA arms received the same 4-week auricular point protocol; mAPA received in-person seed placement, and vAPA received video instruction for self-placement, with one coaching session for both. Usual care was standard oncologic and supportive care with no study-delivered APA. Primary outcome was a ≥20% reduction from baseline in an individualized composite outcome (ICO); each participant's highest-rated symptom-by-location item at baseline. Secondary outcomes were neuropathy interference, functional status, and quality of life. Intention-to-treat analyses used generalized estimating equations with multiple imputation and delta-adjusted sensitivity analyses. At Week 1, both APA arms exceeded usual care (mAPA OR = 2.60, 95% CI 1.27-5.33; vAPA OR = 3.22; 95% CI 1.48-7.01; p < 0.01). The mAPA advantage persisted at Week 2 (OR = 2.49, p = 0.02). For neuropathy interference, mAPA benefits exceeded usual care every week (OR = 3.29-4.28, all p < 0.01). Among exploratory domains, anxiety, depression, and pain interference improved only in mAPA. APA produced a short-lived advantage in CIPN severity and more consistent improvement in interference, specifically with in-person delivery. Findings are preliminary: no blinding or attention control, differential attrition (52% vAPA versus 96% usual care), and exploratory quality-of-life analyses. items.title: Internalized stigma and lifetime suicidal thoughts and behaviors among gay and bisexual men of color: a cross-sectional investigation.
items.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined associations of internalized racism and internalized heterosexism with lifetime suicidal thoughts and behaviors among ethnoracial minority gay and bisexual men. Participants were 471 gay (46.5%) and bisexual (53.5%) ethnoracial minority men (Black American, 49.5%; Asian American, 23.2%; Latino/Hispanic American, 18.0%, and 9.3% Other ethnoracial minorities) recruited through Qualtrics Panels for an online survey conducted from September to December 2020. Lifetime suicidal ideation, planning, and attempts were assessed separately. Endorsement of at least one indicator defined a composite outcome reflecting any lifetime suicidal thoughts or behaviors. Lifetime suicidal ideation, planning, and attempts were reported by 43.6%, 27.5%, and 25.1% of participants, respectively. Internalized racism scores were significantly higher among participants reporting each indicator or the composite, whereas internalized heterosexism scores were significantly higher only among those reporting attempts or the composite. In Model 1, which included both forms of internalized stigma and demographic characteristics, internalized racism, but not internalized heterosexism, was associated with greater odds of any lifetime suicidal thoughts or behaviors. The association between internalized racism and any lifetime suicidal thoughts or behaviors was no longer statistically significant in Model 2, which added discrimination and perceived stress. These findings suggest that internalized stigma warrants consideration alongside broader psychosocial stressors in research on suicidal thoughts and behaviors among ethnoracial minority gay and bisexual men. Longitudinal research is needed to establish temporal ordering and clarify whether and how these factors may inform suicide prevention efforts.

items.title: Daring-impulsive (DI) traits versus ADHD features in adolescent girls with conduct problems.
items.abstract: The current study examined differential associations between daring-impulsive (DI) traits and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) features in relation to conduct disorder (CD) and clinically relevant characteristics in 115 criminal justice-involved and non-criminal justice-involved girls (ages 16-17 years). Adolescents provided self-ratings of DI traits, ADHD features, externalizing and internalizing concerns, impulsivity, and academic and social outcomes. A semi-structured diagnostic interview to assess CD symptoms was also used. We estimated associations using bivariate correlations to examine the dimensional overlap and convergent and discriminant validity of DI and ADHD total, inattention, and hyperactivity-impulsivity scores. We also examined the criterion-related validity of DI scores in distinguishing adolescents with and without CD using independent samples t-tests. Finally, we tested the incremental validity of DI scores in explaining outcomes over and above ADHD scores using multiple hierarchical regression analyses. Results indicated weak to moderate associations between DI and ADHD scores (r's = 0.22-0.26). Further, DI and ADHD scores differed in relation to indices of CD symptoms (e.g., total number of CD symptoms: r's = 0.19-0.31), externalizing (e.g., proactive aggression: r's = 0.13-0.38) and internalizing concerns (e.g., anxiety: r's = -0.06-0.41), impulsivity (e.g., sensation seeking: r's = -0.03-0.40), and academic and social outcomes (e.g., number of detained friends: r's = 0.13-0.27). DI scores significantly distinguished adolescents with CD (p < .01), but ADHD scores did not. Additionally, over and above ADHD scores, DI contributed incremental variance in explaining CD, externalizing concerns, distinct domains of impulsivity, and academic and social outcomes (ΔR2 0.04 to 0.18). These findings have important implications for understanding the usefulness of DI traits in better understanding the heterogeneity of CD among criminal and non-criminal justice-involved girls.

items.title: Prevalence and Predictors of Death-Related Distress Among Cancer Patients in a Multi-Ethnic Asian Setting: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: This study examined the prevalence, pattern, and predictors of death-related distress among 156 cancer patients in a multi-ethnic Malaysian setting. The main concerns related to the dying process and its consequences, particularly prolonged dying, becoming a burden to others, the impact of death on loved ones, and unfinished life goals. Moderate-or-greater distress affected 39% of patients for prolonged dying and approximately one-third for the other major concerns. Multivariable analysis showed that greater death-related distress was independently associated with younger age, mild functional decline reflected by ECOG performance status 1, higher anxiety, and greater suffering. These factors collectively explained a substantial proportion of variation in distress scores. The findings indicate that death-related distress is common among cancer patients and may not be limited to those with advanced physical impairment. Routine screening should therefore focus particularly on younger patients, those showing early functional deterioration, and individuals experiencing significant anxiety or global suffering.

items.title: Meaning of work: Perception of employment among veterans with substance use disorders.
items.abstract: BackgroundEmployment plays a significant role among veterans including facilitating their transition into the civilian society and is an important indicator of treatment progression for veterans presenting with substance use issues. While the Veterans Health Administration has instituted programs aimed at increasing employment outcomes among veterans, unemployment continues to be a significant problem among veterans presenting with substance use disorders (SUDs) in the United States.ObjectiveThe present study explored the perception and experience of work among veterans with a substance use history with a goal of understanding the complex meanings participants ascribe to employment.MethodsThe study utilized a qualitative research design. 25 veterans with self-identified history of substance use participated in the study.ResultsFour overarching themes were identified through thematic analysis: (a) source of economic support and independence, (b) provides structure, purpose and sense of accomplishment, (c) contribute to society and social connection, and (d) consequences of drug use on employment.ConclusionOverall, our findings indicate that despite the high unemployment rates among veterans with SUD, they are conscious of the benefits associated with being employed, which transcends the conventional role of employment as a mere source of income. Rehabilitation counselors and other professionals involved in the care for veterans with SUD should utilize an integrative treatment approach to care that includes employment as a critical component of recovery.

items.title: Exploring Quality of Life Through Residents' Voice in Nursing Homes: A Qualitative Study of a Montessori-Based Person-Centered Model of Care.
items.abstract: Person-centered care (PCC) is the gold standard for improving the quality of life (QoL) of people living with dementia. The Montessori method represents a practical model for implementing PCC in Nursing Homes (NHs). To date, no study has documented how residents describe their QoL in NHs implementing this method using a self-report approach consistent with PCC principles. This study explores residents' perceptions of their QoL, as well as how they relate it to the care model, using a qualitative self-assessment tool. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twenty-nine residents from two NHs with high levels of Montessori implementation assessed using a validated tool. All interviews were analyzed using thematic analysis. Three interconnected themes emerged. The first examines the components of QoL that matter most to residents. The second explores how the care model influences these determinants. Finally, the third describes residents' self-assessment of QoL shaped by individual factors. Our study contributes to a better understanding of the Montessori method as a comprehensive PCC model from residents' perspectives and deepens knowledge of the extent to which it can shape their QoL. These findings also provide practical and methodological insights for evaluating QoL and guiding care models promoting QoL.

items.title: The association between social support, policy support, postpartum depressive symptoms, and quality of life in China: A chain mediation analysis.
items.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the associations of policy support and social support with postpartum depressive symptoms and quality of life among 528 postpartum women in China. Data were collected from June to December 2024. Higher policy support was associated with greater social support and fewer postpartum depressive symptoms. Greater social support was also associated with fewer postpartum depressive symptoms and better quality of life. Serial mediation analysis identified statistically significant indirect associations linking policy support with quality of life through social support and postpartum depressive symptoms. These findings were consistent with an associative serial mediation model but should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal or causal relationships.

items.title: Psychometric properties of a DTD self-report scale among Portuguese adolescents from the community.
items.abstract: Background: Developmental Trauma Disorder (DTD) has been proposed as a developmentally informed framework to describe the pervasive dysregulation associated with chronic interpersonal trauma in childhood. DTD has been assessed by a validated structured interview, but no study has validated a self-report measure of DTD symptoms or examined its factorial structure in community adolescent samples. In addition, measurement invariance across sex has not been investigated, despite evidence of sex differences in trauma exposure and trauma-related symptoms. Objective: To evaluate the psychometric properties of a self-report measure of DTD symptoms in a community sample of Portuguese adolescents by testing factorial structure, internal consistency, convergent and discriminant validity, and measurement invariance across sex. Methods: A school-based sample of 444 adolescents aged 11-16 years completed a self-report DTD symptom scale and other theoretically related measures. Confirmatory factor analyses compared alternative models of DTD symptom organisation. Measurement invariance across sex was tested using the best-fitting model. Convergent and discriminant validity were examined using Pearson correlations and group comparisons based on trauma exposure criteria. Results: A second-order model with three first-order factors provided the best fit. Configural and metric invariance across sex were supported, with partial scalar invariance after freeing two intercepts. Internal consistency was good to excellent, and evidence for convergent and discriminant validity was observed. Conclusions: The findings provide the first evidence that DTD symptoms can be assessed using a self-report measure with acceptable factorial validity, reliability, and cross-sex comparability in a community adolescent sample.

items.title: 'You'll never account for every client scenario' perceived facilitators and barriers of a co-designed financial incentive intervention for smoking cessation in Ireland: A qualitative investigation.
items.abstract: Financial incentive interventions for promoting smoking cessation are complex, but effective. We conducted workshops with 59 community members and Stop Smoking Professionals (SSPs) to co-design a pilot financial incentive intervention for smoking cessation targeting disadvantaged communities in Ireland. Following contributions from 27 participants (mostly SSPs), we qualitatively examined perceived facilitators and barriers to implementation. Results aligned with 8 out of 14 domains of the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) - a validated framework to understand implementation determinants of health behaviour change. Example facilitators included: establishing clear guidelines, providing staff training, appropriate targeting for public defensibility. Example barriers included: an inability to account for all potential challenges, disruption to work dynamics if training is insufficient, biological-testing concerns, public disapproval, limited technology. Eligibility precision, staff role clarity, objective cessation verification and media management were particularly salient. Identifying perceived facilitators and barriers aligned to theory allows for more specific strategies for design and implementation.

items.title: When faces shape places: person trustworthiness influences contextual threat.
items.abstract: Social perception rarely occurs in isolation: people and places mutually shape one another's meaning. Prior research has shown that threatening contexts can bias impressions of facial trustworthiness, suggesting that evaluative meaning flows from the environment to the person. Here, we consider the reverse causal direction, testing whether individuals' trustworthiness can alter evaluations of environmental threat. Across three preregistered experiments (total N = 367), participants judged the threat level of ambiguous visual contexts that included individuals varying on perceived trustworthiness. Experiment 1 showed that untrustworthy faces increased perceived contextual threat relative to neutral or absent faces, an effect that correlated with attributing danger to the target individual. Experiment 2 revealed that this effect was contingent on perceiver perspective: untrustworthy faces heightened threat only when participants evaluated the context from their own viewpoint, not when adopting the target's perspective. Experiment 3 showed that this face-to-context influence emerged when faces varied in trustworthiness but not competence, indicating that it does not reflect a general negativity bias. Together, these findings establish face-context integration as a process in which social meaning propagates dynamically between person and environment, revealing a fundamental mechanism of relational meaning construction in social cognition.

items.title: The impact of leukocyte-associated RNA retention on platelet RNA-based cancer detection.
items.abstract: Platelet RNA profiling is a promising liquid biopsy approach, offering minimally invasive insights into systemic diseases, such as cancer. Yet, the effect of leukocyte-associated RNA retention on platelet transcriptomic signatures remains unclear. This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of how leukocyte-associated RNA retention influences platelet RNA sequencing and machine learning (ML)-based cancer detection. Using the largest publicly available platelet transcriptomic dataset (2351 human RNA samples) and single-cell/single-platelet RNA sequencing from 29 donors, we quantified leukocyte-associated RNA retention in matched sample groups (low vs. high retention) via a novel 132-gene leukocyte marker panel. Diagnostic implications were assessed using 10 ML algorithms for binary classification (cancer vs. healthy), examining the contribution of leukocyte-derived transcripts. Interestingly, models trained on high-retention samples often showed slightly improved performance, suggesting complementary diagnostic value from leukocyte signals. Importantly, post hoc correction using remove unwanted variation (RUV) and linear modeling effectively mitigated retention effects. However, adding the leukocyte-associated RNA retention score to the full-cohort classifier changed cancer-detection AUC only minimally (0.9247 to 0.9249). Thus, whether this signal should be corrected, recalibrated, or reported should depend on the study question rather than assuming routine removal.

items.title: Comparison of HPV Antibodies Measured Prior to Diagnosis of Anal, Cervical, Oropharyngeal, Penile and Vaginal Cancers in the HPV Cancer Cohort Consortium.
items.abstract: Antibodies against HPV proteins can provide pre-diagnostic information about cancer development. We described the prevalence of antibodies to proteins of oncogenic HPV types prior to diagnosis of HPV-related cancers. We analysed pre-diagnostic blood from 1700 participants with incident HPV-related cancers (anal = 387, cervical = 274, oropharyngeal = 788, penile = 168, vaginal = 83) and 6221 controls from nine prospective cohorts in Europe, North America and Australia in the HPV Cancer Cohort Consortium. We measured antibodies against E6, E7 and L1 proteins for 6 HPV types, and additionally against E1, E2, E4, E6, E7 and L1 proteins of HPV16 and 18. We described seroprevalence by lead time from blood draw to cancer diagnosis (range: 0-43 years). We found that among oropharyngeal cancers, seroprevalence increased approaching diagnosis for HPV16 E1, E2, E4, E6, E7, L1 and HPV18 E1, E2, L1 (HPV16-E6: from 10.4% at > 20 years to 35.8% at 0-5 years, vs. 0.3% in controls). Anal cancer showed similar patterns for HPV16 E1, E2, E4, E6 and L1 and HPV18 E2 (HPV16-E6: from 3.8% at > 20 years to 29.8% at 0-5 years). No trends were observed for cervical, penile, or vaginal cancers. In a multivariable model fit among cases, HPV16-E6 seropositivity was higher at shorter lead times and more recent calendar periods, lower among US non-Hispanic Blacks, and varied by cancer type (highest in oropharyngeal followed by anal, vaginal, penile and cervical) (all p < 0.03). In conclusion, pre-diagnostic HPV antibody responses vary by cancer type, with seroprevalence of 6-9 HPV proteins increasing approaching diagnosis for oropharyngeal and anal cancers, but not cervical, penile or vaginal cancers.

items.title: Dose-Response Relationship Between Triglyceride Glucose-Waist Height Ratio Index and Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity Among Chinese Middle-Aged and Older People.
items.abstract: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is a growing public health challenge. The triglyceride glucose-waist height ratio (TyG-WHtR) is a novel index linked to metabolic disorders. This study explores the dose-response relationship between TyG-WHtR and CMM. Data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including the 2011 baseline survey and the 2018 follow-up survey with an average follow-up duration of 7.0 years, were analyzed. Multivariate logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models assessed the TyG-WHtR-CMM relationship, adjusting for covariates. The study enrolled 6674 individuals, and 1140 patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity and 5534 patients with non-cardiometabolic multimorbidity were documented over an average follow-up duration of 7.0 years. The fourth TyG-WHtR quartile group (Q4) had the highest CMM risk, with an odds ratio of 1.23 and a 95% confidence interval of 1.20-1.26. The restricted cubic spline regression model showed a nonlinear (p < 0.001) association between TyG-WHtR and CMM. Subgroup analyses showed that the positive association between TyG-WHtR and CMM was evident among females and ex-smokers. A notable interaction was observed between TyG-WHtR and variables like age and marital status. TyG-WHtR is a potential CMM predictor, and maintaining it within a moderate range may help prevent CMM.

items.title: Efficacy of a training program to support the application of the Guideline Evidence-based Health Information: a randomized controlled trial and process evaluation.
items.abstract: The Guideline Evidence-based Health Information addresses health information providers and aims to improve the quality of health information. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a training program for health information providers to support the application of the guideline. We expected the intervention to improve the quality of health information compared with providing the guideline alone. In this superiority randomized controlled trial, providers responsible for producing and publishing health information were allocated 1:1 to the intervention (guideline and training program) and control (publicly available guideline) groups using computer-generated block randomization. The e-learning program (31 h, offered over 6-7 weeks) comprised modules on evidence-based medicine and the application of the guideline. Each provider committed to producing a single piece of health information informing a health-related decision on the topic of their choice. The primary outcome was the quality of health information, operationalized as adherence to the guideline recommendations, as measured using the Mapping Health Information Quality (MAPPinfo) checklist. Means were compared between groups using a t-test. The assessment and analyses were blinded to the group allocation. An accompanying process evaluation was conducted. We included 18 health information providers (nine in each group), with a total of 54 individual participants. Eight health information items were assessed in each group. The primary analysis estimated the mean MAPPinfo checklist values at 30.2% (95% CI, 24.6 to 35.9) for the intervention and at 22.7% (95% CI, 17.4 to 27.9) for the control group. The difference between groups was estimated at 7.6% (95% CI, - 0.2 to 15.3; p = 0.055). Individual and structural implementation barriers of the guideline recommendations were identified. We did not achieve the targeted sample size of 26 providers. A lack of resources was one of the main barriers to recruitment. Although our study did not provide conclusive evidence regarding the primary outcome, the participants rated the training program as relevant. Therefore, the training program will be made available to health information providers upon request. ISRCTN registry, ID: ISRCTN96941060. Registered on March 7, 2019. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13063-020-04287-1 (Trials 2020).

items.title: Phosphorylation of RpoD upregulates suilysin and enhances Streptococcus suis virulence.
items.abstract: Streptococcus suis (S. suis) is a prevalent zoonotic pathogen that severely threatens the swine industry and human public health. Suilysin (SLY), a major pore-forming toxin of S. suis, is indispensable for bacterial hemolytic activity and systemic pathogenicity, yet the upstream regulatory mechanism controlling SLY production remains unclear. Serine/threonine kinase (STK) has been characterized to modulate bacterial physiology and virulence by phosphorylating multiple substrate proteins. Our previous phosphoproteomics analysis indicated that the housekeeping sigma factor RpoD was a potential STK substrate. In vitro phosphorylation assays combined with mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation and site-directed mutagenesis confirmed that STK directly phosphorylated RpoD at Thr-208 residue. Phenotypic tests revealed that RpoD phosphorylation had no obvious impact on bacterial growth and biofilm formation but specifically promoted the thermotolerance and hemolytic activity of S. suis. Notably, the rpoD overexpression mutant strain SC19-rpoD significantly upregulated the transcription and protein production of SLY, whereas the phosphorylation-deficient mutant SC19-rpoD T208A abolished this promotion effect, indicating that Thr-208 phosphorylation is required for sly upregulation, although the underlying molecular mechanism remains to be fully defined. Furthermore, mouse infection models demonstrated that the SC19-rpoD T208A mutant exhibited alleviated splenic pathological injury, reduced bacterial loads in multiple organs, and significantly improved host survival, indicating that the loss of RpoD phosphorylation impairs S. suis virulence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that STK-mediated phosphorylation of RpoD at Thr-208 is required for sly upregulation and contributes to the S. suis pathogenesis.

items.title: Association of Maternal Immune Activation With Pruritic Urticarial Papules and Plaques of Pregnancy: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPPP) is a common dermatosis of pregnancy, but its etiology remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify whether maternal immune activation (MIA) is associated with PUPPP. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of pregnant patients using a population-based administrative cohort of all live births in California from 2016 to 2021. Patients with PUPPP were identified using ICD-10 code O26.86. MIA was defined by ICD-10 diagnoses of infection, autoimmune disease, or atopic disease during pregnancy. Poisson log-linear regression was used to estimate crude and adjusted risk ratios (RR, aRR) for associations between PUPPP and MIA. Among 2,275,929 pregnancies, there were 3286 (0.14%) patients with PUPPP. Compared with patients without PUPPP, patients with PUPPP had higher rates of gestational hypertension (6.2% vs. 4.0%, p < 0.0001) and preeclampsia (10.9% vs. 5.2%, p < 0.0001). Atopy was associated with increased risk of PUPPP (aRR 1.7, 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.6-1.9), as was autoimmunity (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2-2.1) and maternal infection (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.4-1.7). Patients with PUPPP were less likely to have a pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m2 (21.2% vs. 25.4%, p < 0.0001) but more likely to exceed recommended gestational weight gain (64.3% vs. 52.4%, p < 0.0001). MIA during pregnancy, including atopy, autoimmunity, and infection, was independently associated with increased risk of PUPPP. These findings suggest immune dysregulation may contribute to PUPPP pathogenesis. The association with excessive gestational weight gain further supports a potential role for inflammation secondary to connective tissue injury from abdominal distension.

items.title: What do older adults think about involvement in health research through a citizen science lens? A situated qualitative study.
items.abstract: Citizen science (CS) has emerged as a promising approach to foster public involvement in the production of scientific knowledge, including in the field of health. However, for involvement to be effective, it is essential to examine the circumstances surrounding participation particularly from citizens' perspectives in order to understand motivations, perceived benefits, and the conditions that may enable or hinder meaningful involvement in the process. To explore community-dwelling older adults' perceptions and expectations regarding prospective involvement in health research through a citizen science lens. An exploratory, descriptive qualitative study was conducted using a focus group with community-dwelling older adults. Data were analysed using content analysis, supported by ATLAS.ti software. Three themes were identified: (1) Between volunteering and science; (2) Becoming a future citizen scientist: identity, motivations, and perceived benefits; and (3) Becoming a future citizen scientist: challenges and conditions for involvement. Participants associated involvement with volunteering and social contribution, highlighting motivations such as contributing to society, staying active, and strengthening social ties. Anticipated benefits included lifelong learning, personal validation, and wellbeing. Key barriers included the need for training and ongoing support, technical language, and balancing involvement with personal routines. Role clarity, accessible communication, and alignment of expectations emerged as central conditions for effective involvement. This exploratory study provides preliminary and situated insights into how older adults perceive prospective involvement in health research through a citizen science lens. The findings suggest that future citizen science initiatives in health should make citizens' roles, expectations and opportunities for influence explicit, while ensuring accessible communication, training, support, flexibility and recognition. These elements may help researchers move beyond symbolic involvement and support older adults in assuming a more confident and meaningful role in the research process.

items.title: Stroke care in Germany: evidence gaps and priorities for health services research and quality assurance.
items.abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in Germany and worldwide. Within this position paper by the Commission Health Services Research and Quality Assurance of the German Stroke Society, we summarize current data on stroke epidemiology, healthcare delivery, and quality assurance of stroke in Germany, identify evidence and knowledge gaps across the stroke care pathway, and derive priorities for future health services research and quality assurance. Based on registry and routine administrative data, approximately 253,000 incident and recurrent strokes were estimated to occur in Germany in 2023. Although age-standardized stroke mortality rates had declined substantially since the 1980s, this trend has reached a plateau since 2018. Acute care is predominantly administered in certified stroke units, characterized by high process and outcome quality. However, areas for improvement remain in post-acute care and in structured outpatient aftercare, particularly regarding appropriate care for patients with persistent functional impairments and unmet needs. Future research priorities include for example the utilization of real-world data to document long-term outcomes, the expansion of quality assurance to specific entities such as subarachnoid hemorrhage, and the evaluation of telemedical frameworks in pre-hospital settings. Systematic implementation of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) in research and clinical practice could facilitate the identification of unmet needs and the development of patient-centered care models. In light of recent legislative advancements (e.g., the Health Data Use Act, European Health Data Space) and technological innovations (e.g., AI-driven applications), new opportunities are emerging to bolster health services research and further optimize the management of stroke patients.

items.title: Polygenic and classical risk integration reshapes breast cancer screening recommendations in 9,761 Asian women.
items.abstract: Age-based mammography screening fails to account for individual breast cancer risk variation, particularly in Asian populations where prospective evidence is absent. The BREAst Screening Tailored for HEr (BREATHE) study is a multicentre prospective cohort of 4,513 women aged 35-59 years recruited across six Singapore clinical sites (2021-2023). Risk-stratified screening recommendations were assigned using a five-year absolute risk threshold of 0.9% (equivalent to the population-average risk of an average 50-year-old Singaporean woman) to initiate screening based on polygenic risk score (PRS) and Gail model, as well as mammographic density, family history, abnormal prior screening. Two independent breast cancer case cohorts provided comparative analyses: Singapore Breast Cancer Cohort (SGBCC, n = 2,782) and Malaysian Breast Cancer Genetic Study (MyBrCa, n = 2,466); combined n = 9,761. Among 2,003 healthy women aged 40-49 years currently recommended annual mammography, risk stratification downgraded 776 (38.7%) to no screening and 960 (47.9%) to biennial as they were not in the top 2.5th percentile of PRS and Gail risk and did not have any additional risk indicators. Of 41 breast cancers diagnosed after BREATHE enrolment, 35 (85.4%) occurred in women assigned to screening-eligible categories at baseline. Risk stratification combining PRS and Gail model captured 68-69% of cases aged 40-49 in SGBCC (n = 1,184) and MyBrCa (n = 1,122), versus ~ 54% by PRS alone. Relative to cases meeting screening criteria for both PRS and Gail model, PRS-missed cases were enriched for progesterone receptor negativity (OR 1.24; 95% CI 1.01-1.52), tumour size ≥ 50 mm (OR 1.43; 95% CI 1.02-2.00), and germline protein-truncating variants (PTVs) in breast cancer predisposition genes (OR 1.53; 95% CI 1.03-2.29). Risk stratification combining PRS with classical risk factors reshapes mammography recommendations in Asian women. However, due to the limited number of events in BREATHE, this finding requires evaluation in larger prospective studies. PRS-missed cancers exhibit a biologically aggressive profile, defining the current limits of common-variant prediction and identifying the biology that future precision screening tools must address.

items.title: Strain and cell type dependent induction of tunnelling nanotube-like projections by African swine fever virus.
items.abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a devastating viral disease of pigs, causing mortality rates of up to 100%. The causative agent, African swine fever virus (ASFV), preferentially targets cells of the mononuclear phagocytic system (MPS). Despite its severe economic and animal health impact, effective antiviral treatments remain unavailable in Europe. We previously showed that ASFV strain Belgium 2018/01 induces tunnelling nanotube (TNT)-like projections in monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs), enabling physical connections between distant cells. Here, we investigated the broader relevance of this phenomenon across porcine myeloid cell populations and ASFV strains. We assessed TNT-like projection formation in monocytes, pulmonary alveolar macrophages (PAMs), splenic macrophages, polarized and non-polarized MDMs and Vero cells following ASFV infection. We further compared 20 ASFV strains representing diverse genotypes and virulence levels. Interestingly, luminal monocytes and PAMs did not develop ASFV-induced projections, whereas projection formation increased during monocyte differentiation into MDMs. Splenic macrophages also formed projections, suggesting that interstitial tissue macrophages acquire the ability to induce protrusions. Polarized MDMs exhibited reduced projection formation compared with non-polarized MDMs. Similar structures were induced in Ba71V-infected Vero cells, providing a standardized model for mechanistic studies. Importantly, all 20 ASFV strains induced TNT-like projections in MDMs, although the extent varied substantially and was independent of viral genotype or virulence. Our findings demonstrate that ASFV-induced TNT-like projection formation is a conserved, cell-state-dependent phenotype across diverse ASFV strains. These findings provide a foundation for identifying the cellular and viral determinants of TNT formation and defining its potential contribution to ASFV dissemination and pathogenesis.

items.title: Beyond Access: Social Inequities and Discriminatory Experiences Among Brazilian Medical Students.
items.abstract: Universities are expected to promote diversity and inclusion; however, medical schools may continue to reproduce discriminatory practices. In Brazil, Law No. 12,711/2012 expanded access to higher education through affirmative action, yet evidence on how discrimination is experienced during medical training remains limited. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 143 medical students (years 1-6) at a Brazilian federal university in 2025. Discriminatory experiences were assessed using the Explicit Discrimination Scale (EDS). Group differences were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Participants were predominantly White (66.7%), female (77.5%), and from higher-income backgrounds (60.1%), although half entered through affirmative action (50.4%). Higher discrimination scores were significantly associated with lower socioeconomic status, racial/ethnic minority identity, disability status, public secondary school attendance, use of affirmative action policies, and first-year academic standing (p < 0.05). Despite expanded access to medical education in Brazil, disparities in student experiences persist. These findings underscore the need for targeted institutional strategies to foster inclusive learning environments and support student well-being and progression.

items.title: Types of adult intensive care units and admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023: a nationwide cohort study.
items.abstract: Türkiye has one of the highest intensive care unit (ICU) bed capacities among middle-income countries but also globally. Nevertheless, little is known about the characteristics of ICUs in Türkiye, their temporal trends, and ICU admissions and readmissions. We sought to analyze the structural characteristics of all adult ICUs and the clinical profiles of ICU admissions across Türkiye. We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using data from the Turkish Ministry of Health National Electronic Database. We analyzed adult ICU admissions across all levels and types over 6 years (2018-2023) and documented patient demographics, comorbidities, admission diagnoses, and ICU outcomes. We retrieved data on 3,362,539 ICU admissions. Among 22 ICU types, mixed ICUs accounted for the highest proportion of admissions (31.4%), followed by coronary (23.7%), anesthesiology (14.3%), medical (6.1%), and surgical (6.0%) ICUs. The proportion of mixed ICU beds decreased from 44.0% in 2018 to 25.1% in 2023. Most ICU beds were in state (public) hospitals (50.8%), followed by private hospitals (34.8%). The number of ICU beds increased from 2019, with a notable rise in state hospitals after 2020. The average number of ICU admissions was 659 per 100,000 population annually. The median patient age was 65 [interquartile range, 39-91] yr, and the ICU mortality was 15.5%. The leading admission diagnoses were respiratory failure (10.1%), cerebrovascular disease (7.1%), and acute kidney injury (5.2%). Hypertension (67.5%) and coronary artery disease (44.8%) were common comorbidities, particularly in nonsurvivors. The 7-day ICU readmission rate was 3.0%. The present comprehensive analysis of ICU admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023 highlights a shift toward specialization with a decrease in mixed ICUs. The impact of ICU diversity on resource use and patient outcomes requires further evaluation.

items.title: Same Data, Different Constructs: A Scoping Review Exploring the Use of 311 Data as a Social Construct in Studies of Injury, Crime, and Violence.
items.abstract: Non-emergency service requests, often known as "311" calls, provide residents opportunities to report non-urgent concerns, such as loud noise or graffiti, to local municipalities. In the United States, 311 data have been increasingly used to represent complex neighborhood social processes in studies of injury, crime, and violence. However, the same 311 data have been operationalized as varying constructs. This scoping review aims to characterize the use of 311 data and examine the theoretical frameworks used to justify their inclusion in studies related to injury, crime, and violence prevention. We searched four databases from inception through March 4, 2024, and included peer-reviewed articles with a focus on any injury, crime, or violence topic area within the United States utilizing 311 data. After titles and abstract screening and full-text review, study characteristics were extracted from included papers with double-coding procedures. A total of 1681 titles and abstracts were screened, from which 46 were advanced to full-text review. A total of 20 articles met inclusion criteria. Half of the studies (n = 10) employed 311 data for analytic studies, while the remainder were either descriptive (n = 9) or methodological demonstrations (n = 1). The 311 data were positioned as proxies for several constructs, including physical disorder (n = 9), social disorder (n = 4), direct measures (n = 3), civil/political engagement (n = 3), policing/control (n = 3), and collective efficacy (n = 1). Although 311 data represent a promising source of data for research investigating injury, crime, and violence, the varied theoretical frameworks and operational definitions used across studies present a challenge for comparison. Explicit descriptions of theoretical rationale are critical in future work.
