items.title: Quantified Brain Atrophy and Risk of Severe Mass Effect in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
items.abstract: Large middle cerebral artery (MCA) infarctions can result in life-threatening cerebral edema. Quantitative brain atrophy may improve risk stratification for severe edema. We examined whether quantitative brain atrophy is associated with severe midline shift after large ischemic stroke and whether incorporating atrophy improves prediction beyond established clinical and radiographic predictors. This was a retrospective observational cohort study of patients with greater than or equal to half MCA ischemic infarction, presentation within 24 h of last known well time, and at least one follow-up head computed tomography (CT), admitted to two academic hospitals with comprehensive stroke centers between 2006 and 2024. The study was approved by the institutional review boards of both centers. Brain atrophy was quantified as the inverse of standardized brain volume on admission head CT. The primary outcome was severe radiographic mass effect, defined as midline shift ≥ 5 mm on follow-up CT. The secondary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable regression models assessed associations between quantified atrophy and outcomes. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing models with and without atrophy using measures of goodness of fit, calibration, and discrimination. Among 565 patients (mean age 67.5 ± 15.7 years; 49.9% female), 223 (39.5%) developed severe mass effect. Greater atrophy was associated with lower odds of midline shift ≥ 5 mm [odds ratio (OR) 0.44, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34-0.58], but not with in-hospital mortality. Incorporation of atrophy improved prediction of severe mass effect compared with the baseline model [likelihood ratio test χ2 (1) = 41, p < 0.001; Akaike information criterion (AIC) 703 vs. 741; Bayesian information criterion (BIC) 733 vs. 767; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.68 vs. 0.60]. Quantified brain atrophy is independently associated with a reduced risk of severe mass effect after large MCA stroke and improved the performance of established predictive models. Incorporation of this imaging biomarker may enhance early risk stratification, monitoring, and intervention planning for patients at risk of life-threatening cerebral edema.

items.title: Irrational antibiotic prescriptions in pediatric care across Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Inappropriate antibiotic use, including deviations from guideline recommendations, incorrect dosages, and over-prescription, is a critical public health concern. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the prevalence and factors associated with inappropriate antibiotic use in pediatric populations across Africa. A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and African Journals Online, following PRISMA guidelines and the PICOC framework. Study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Meta-analysis was performed with STATA 17 using a random-effects model. From 3,085 records, 11 studies met inclusion. The pooled prevalence of inappropriate antibiotic use was 44%. Rates reached 75.1%, 73.9%, and 71.5% in some countries, while lower rates of 11% and 19.3% were reported elsewhere. Retrospective studies showed a pooled prevalence of 51.2% (I² = 99.5%), and prospective studies 35.4% (I² = 99%). Commonly prescribed antibiotics included cotrimoxazole, amoxicillin, and ceftriaxone. Inappropriate practices involved incorrect dosages (10.1%-19.5%) and durations (17.47-18.8%). Risk factors included younger age, three or more antibiotics (AOR: 2.8, 95% CI: 1.245-6.462, p = 0.013), and prolonged hospitalization. Inappropriate pediatric antibiotic use in Africa is highly prevalent, driven by age, hospitalization, and polypharmacy, underscoring the need for targeted stewardship interventions. This study is the first to bring together evidence across Africa showing that nearly half of antibiotics prescribed to children are used inappropriately. The findings call for stronger, targeted antibiotic stewardship efforts to improve prescribing practices and curb the growing threat of resistance in African healthcare settings.

items.title: Climate change threatens malaria elimination in the Asia Pacific.
items.abstract: Climate change threatens decades of progress toward malaria elimination across the Asia Pacific. In recent years, reported cases have increased sharply in several regions, including Pakistan following the 2022 floods. However, current research and adaptation strategies have largely focused on gradual warming and shifting transmission seasons and may not fully capture acute operational disruptions in endemic settings. Here we examine how climate change influences malaria through cascading disruptions to health systems, population displacement and ecological change. As a multidisciplinary group of policymakers and researchers, we identify priority actions: integrating malaria control into disaster response, deploying adaptive vector control for displaced populations, strengthening cross-border data sharing, linking early warnings to anticipatory action, and incorporating land-use data into surveillance. Leveraging existing advances in climate policy, digital surveillance and community engagement will be critical. Sustaining elimination will require complementing long-term projections with preparedness for near-term system shocks.

items.title: Hospitalisation and subsequent fracture risk-a national matched cohort study in Denmark.
items.abstract: In a national matched cohort study in Denmark, time-to-event analyses described binary and dose-response associations between hospitalisation and subsequent fracture events. Hospitalisation was confirmed as a risk factor for subsequent MOFs, with sex differences and dose-dependencies observed. Major osteoporotic fractures (MOFs) are a cause and, importantly, a consequence of hospitalisation. Frailty and osteoporosis are risk factors of major osteoporotic fractures (MOFs) and associated mortality. Moreover, hospitalisation is associated with a subsequent increase in frailty, partly due to immobilisation. This national matched cohort study was performed using Danish registry data available for individuals aged >45 years. Individuals with at least one day in hospital during 2023 were matched to controls using age, sex, and comorbidities. The end date of the last hospitalisation in 2023 was used as the start of follow-up. Days hospitalised in total, during the last hospitalisation, and the count of hospitalisations in an exposure window reaching 364 days past the last day of the last hospitalisation were collected for dose-response analyses. Cumulative incidence of MOF was estimated with a two-step adjustment for the competing risk of mortality, complemented by cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for confounders. Hospitalisation was associated with a higher risk of MOF. The fully adjusted model showed a greater risk of MOF in the hospitalised sample at 14 days (HR: 1.77; 1.47-2.14), 30 days (HR: 1.28; 1.12-1.47), one year and complete follow-up (HR: 1.03 and 1.10, respectively). Females had consistently higher MOF rates and, in contrast to males, showed temporary normalisation of MOF cumulative incidence and cause-specific risk at 90 days (HR: 0.93; 0.84-1.03). Significant dose-response associations were reported for hospitalisation duration and count. There is a time-dependent sex-specific association between hospitalisation and MOF, supported by several dose-dependencies.

items.title: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper.
items.abstract: Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains threaten the current empirical gonorrhoea treatment. We designed and analytically validated SensiTyper, a rule-based framework that predicts antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and generates susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations. SensiTyper was applied to 13,701 gonococcal genomes from 68 countries in 1928-2024, including cultured isolates and clinical molecular samples, and benchmarked predictions against previous genomic and phenotypic data. Susceptibility predictions for ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, spectinomycin, and zoliflodacin had 98.9-100% sensitivity and specificity. Azithromycin susceptibility predictions had 92.5% sensitivity and 97.1% specificity, and gepotidacin susceptibility prediction 100% sensitivity, but 0% specificity, illustrating that low-level phenotypic gepotidacin resistance is not caused by the only known resistance determinants (GyrA A92T plus ParC D86N). The SensiTreat module integrates antimicrobial susceptibility profiles into sequential treatment logic, providing susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations while also enabling alternative stewardship strategies prioritizing, e.g., ciprofloxacin. SensiTyper flags XDR isolates for expert follow-up, test-of-cure and comprehensive contact tracing. In conclusion, SensiTyper is a robust and adaptable approach for gonococcal antimicrobial susceptibility prediction, individualized gonorrhoea treatment and antimicrobial stewardship.

items.title: Investigation of individual and cohort-level temporal changes to legacy and emerging endocrine disrupting chemical exposures and their relationship with birth outcomes.
items.abstract: Phthalates, parabens, and phenols co-occur in personal care and consumer products (PCPs). While policy and market-based campaigns have led to changes in product formulations, few studies have examined intra- and inter-individual changes in PCP chemical biomarkers in pregnant populations with birth outcomes. Investigate changes in exposure to PCP-derived chemicals within and between pregnant women. Additionally, examine if exposures-individually and as a mixture-are associated with gestational age (GA) and birthweight z-scores (BWZ). We collected maternal third-trimester urine samples from 299 Mothers and Newborns (MN, 2001-2006) and 246 Fair Start (FS, 2013-2021) New York City-based participants. A subset of MN (n = 62) provided urine at a subsequent pregnancy (Siblings cohort). We analyzed samples using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry for 16 phthalate, 4 paraben, and 5 environmental phenolic biomarkers. Paired t-tests and linear regression models compared intraindividual biomarker concentrations for participants that provided urine at two pregnancies. Linear regressions evaluated the interindividual differences in biomarker levels between cohorts. Linear regression and quantile g-computation were used to estimate the single- and multi-chemical relationships, respectively, with GA and BWZ for each cohort. Biomarkers of emerging contaminants di-(2-propylheptyl) phthalate and bisphenol S were higher in the FS cohort compared to the MN cohort in the interindividual analyses, and in subsequent pregnancies in the intraindividual analyses. Conversely, biomarkers of legacy chemicals (e.g., di-n-hexyl phthalate, di-(2-ethylhexyl phthalate)) were lower in the FS cohort and subsequent pregnancies compared to the MN cohort. Mono-hexyl phthalate was associated with earlier GA (β [95%CI]: -0.14 [-0.23, -0.05]) in the MN cohort. No significant mixture associations with GA and BWZ were observed. Exposure to emerging contaminants has increased and exposure to legacy contaminants has decreased when assessing inter- and intra-individual urinary biomarker levels. Continued research is critical to better understand the health implications of emerging contaminants. Higher levels of emerging chemicals (e.g., di-(2-propylheptyl) phthalate, bisphenol S) were found in a New York City-based cohort of women who provided urine samples between 2013 and 2021 compared to women who provided urine samples between 2001 and 2006. This demonstrates the need to include these contaminants in environmental epidemiologic studies to better understand their impacts on health. When exploring associations with birth outcomes, we identified a metabolite of di-n-hexyl phthalate, a legacy compound, to be associated with earlier gestational age only in the cohort from 2001 to 2006. This may indicate that temporal changes in exposure are important to health outcomes.

items.title: A Cross-Sectional Study Exploring the Nature, Contributing Factors and Consequences of Violence Against Nurses in Emergency Departments.
items.abstract: To explore the nature, contributing factors, and consequences of violence against emergency department nurses by patients and visitors in tertiary hospitals in a major city in China. A cross-sectional descriptive study. Data were collected between December 2023 and February 2024 using a translated and adapted questionnaire examining the prevalence, forms, contributing factors, and consequences of violence. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory logistic regression. A total of 336 emergency nurses were included, of whom 66.7% reported violence exposure within the past year. Visitor-perpetrated violence was reported more frequently than patient-perpetrated violence. Psychological violence was more common than physical violence and most frequently involved verbal abuse, disruptive speech, and blame. Illness-related impairment was prominent in patient-perpetrated physical violence, whereas alcohol impairment was frequently reported in visitor-perpetrated violence. Dissatisfaction with medical staff outside the emergency department and delayed or inadequate security responses were also commonly reported as contributing factors. Among the variables included in the exploratory regression model (n = 298), uncertainty or absence of workplace violence policies was the only factor significantly associated with reported lifetime violence exposure. Peer support was more commonly reported than managerial assistance following incidents, and visitor-perpetrated incidents generally received higher short-term impact ratings, including impacts on work motivation and personal and psychological well-being. Violence against emergency department nurses was common, with visitors reported more frequently as perpetrators than patients. Patient- and visitor-perpetrated violence showed different patterns, particularly in the circumstances surrounding incidents and in short-term impact ratings. The findings support differentiated prevention and response strategies, together with clearer workplace violence policies, timely security responses, and structured post-incident organisational support. Emergency nursing education and organisational responses should distinguish between patient violence associated with illness-related impairment and visitor violence occurring in contexts such as alcohol impairment, dissatisfaction, or unmet expectations. De-escalation for patient-perpetrated violence should consider the patient's clinical condition, whereas visitor-related incidents may require expectation-focused communication, behavioural boundaries, and timely security involvement. Structured post-incident support should form part of the organisational response to both types of violence. This study adhered to the STROBE reporting guidelines. There was no patient or public involvement in the design, conduct, or reporting of this study. WHAT PROBLEM DID THE STUDY ADDRESS?: Violence against emergency nurses is a persistent global problem, yet limited evidence has examined patient- and visitor-perpetrated violence separately in Chinese emergency care settings. WHAT WERE THE MAIN FINDINGS?: Visitor-perpetrated violence was reported more frequently than patient-perpetrated violence and generally received higher short-term impact ratings. Illness-related impairment was prominent in patient-perpetrated physical violence, whereas alcohol impairment was frequently reported in visitor-perpetrated violence. Among the variables examined in the exploratory regression, uncertainty or absence of workplace violence policies was associated with reported lifetime violence exposure. WHERE AND ON WHOM WILL THE RESEARCH HAVE AN IMPACT?: The findings may inform nursing educators, hospital administrators, and policymakers developing differentiated prevention, visitor management, and organisational response strategies for emergency nurses.

items.title: Baroreflex Failure After Surgical Resection of Bilateral Carotid Body Tumors: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Surgery remains the definitive treatment for carotid body tumors (CBTs); however, concern persists regarding the risk of baroreflex failure (BRF) following bilateral CBT resection. The true incidence and long-term clinical course of BRF remain poorly defined. We performed a systematic review to examine the risk and clinical course of BRF after surgical resection of bilateral CBTs. PubMed/Medline, Scopus, and Cochrane. A systematic review was performed based on a population, intervention, comparison, and outcome search (PICOTS) of reports on BRF in surgical resection of bilateral CBTs. Additional articles were added by citation searching. The study was reported per the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. This systematic review included 15 single case reports and 8 case series of BRF in surgical resection of bilateral CBTs. No higher quality studies of clinical trials or cohort studies were available. Results from this systematic review showed that BRF symptoms most commonly occurred immediately after the second surgery in bilateral CBT resections, and that many reported cases demonstrated improvement over time, although long-term outcomes were inconsistently reported. Commonly used treatments of BRF included clonidine and benzodiazepines. Despite the commonly perceived high risk and debilitating clinical outcomes, the reported clinical course of BRF following bilateral CBT resection appears more variable and, in many cases, less severe than historically perceived. The optimal management of CBTs remains unclear, though surgical resection of bilateral CBTs warrants individualized consideration based on age, tumor characteristics, genetic risk, and treatment goals.

items.title: Cured but What's Next? Rethinking Survivorship Care for Adolescent and Young Adult Testicular Cancer Survivors.
items.abstract: The excellent cure rates achieved in testicular cancer represent one of oncology's major success stories. Decades of research have optimized survival, leading to cure for nearly all patients with localized disease and most with metastatic disease. As a result, attention is increasingly shifting from survival alone to reducing treatment burden and long-term toxicity while improving quality of life in this predominantly young population with decades-long life expectancy. However, many adolescent and young adult survivors experience persistent physical, psychological, and social consequences that are insufficiently addressed by conventional follow-up care. Current survivorship models remain largely centered on relapse surveillance and provide limited education or support for understanding late effects, managing uncertainty, or developing long-term self-management skills. Limited empowerment may undermine sustained engagement with follow-up care and long-term well-being. This article makes the case for a shift from hospital-centered information delivery models toward more engaging, experiential, patient-centered survivorship frameworks. We propose extended reality-based immersive and interactive digital technologies as enabling tools within a broader survivorship framework designed to support understanding, early symptom recognition, engagement, and shared decision-making beyond scheduled hospital visits. Using the TRANSCEND-XR consortium as an illustrative example, we discuss how co-designed digital interventions may help bridge the gap between cure and long-term quality of life while addressing key clinical, ethical, and implementation challenges relevant to scalability. PATIENT SUMMARY: Many young people cured of testicular cancer experience long-term physical and emotional challenges that are not fully addressed by routine follow-up care. We describe a new approach using extended reality technologies to help survivors better understand late effects, recognize symptoms early, and take a more active role in their care. Such approaches aim to improve quality of life, support long-term well-being, and facilitate a successful transition from cancer treatment to life beyond cancer. items.title: Work Stress, Burnout and Depression among Radiology Residents: The Moderating Effect of Environment.
items.abstract: This study aimed to explore the modulating role of work environment in the association of work stress with burnout and depression during standardized residency training (SRT) in China. Nationwide cross-sectional survey. A nationwide cross-sectional online survey was conducted among radiology residents in China from December 2020 to April 2021. Participants self-assessed work stress, burnout, depressive symptoms, and work environment satisfaction. Multiple linear regression was used to examine whether the work environment modulated the associations between work stress and burnout and depression. Among 3666 radiology residents surveyed, the average age was 28 years, with 58% identifying as female. Approximately 25.8% reported experiencing burnout, while 24.4% indicated symptoms of depression. Work environment significantly modulated the association between work stress and burnout symptoms (β = -0.23, p = 0.004), but did not significantly moderate the association between work stress and depressive symptoms (β = -0.03, p = 0.423). This study found that the work environment significantly moderated the positive association between work stress and burnout among radiology residents, but not the association between work stress and depressive symptoms. A work environment characterized by a stronger sense of safety and a better workplace atmosphere may improve residents' satisfaction with the work environment, thereby enhancing work efficiency and well-being.

items.title: Personal nighttime indoor temperature and sleep characteristics in adults with type 2 diabetes.
items.abstract: To examine whether personal nighttime indoor temperature is associated with actigraphy-derived sleep outcomes among community-dwelling adults with type 2 diabetes. We analyzed repeated-night data from 108 adults with type 2 diabetes, contributing 1307 paired sleep-temperature nights. Personal nighttime indoor temperature was measured with temperature loggers and averaged across each participant-specific nocturnal sleep episode. Sleep outcomes included sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset, total sleep time, and number of awakenings. Linear mixed-effects models examined within-person and between-person temperature-sleep associations. Generalized additive mixed models evaluated nonlinearity. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic, clinical, and seasonal covariates. Personal nighttime indoor temperature and sleep outcomes varied across nights, with both showing seasonal patterns. In adjusted linear mixed-effects models, warmer-than-usual nights were associated with higher sleep efficiency and fewer awakenings, whereas between-person average temperature was not associated with any sleep outcomes. Generalized additive mixed models showed nonlinear associations with sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset, and awakenings, but not total sleep time. Model-predicted sleep outcomes remained largely unchanged across moderate nighttime indoor temperatures. Above approximately 27 °C [80.6 °F], the fitted curves suggested higher sleep efficiency, lower wake after sleep onset, and fewer awakenings; however, observations in this upper range were sparse, and sensitivity analyses excluding these observations attenuated the nonlinear patterns. Among adults with type 2 diabetes, personal nighttime indoor temperature was associated with actigraphy-derived sleep outcomes in a within-person, nonlinear, and outcome-specific manner. Findings suggest that nighttime indoor temperature may be relevant to sleep health promotion and diabetes-related sleep counseling, particularly for adults reporting poor sleep or limited control over indoor temperature.

items.title: Performance-Metacognition Dissociation During Fear Memory Recall: Role of Task Sequence and Prefrontal TMS.
items.abstract: Metacognitive processing-the ability to monitor and evaluate one's decisions-has been extensively studied in perceptual tasks but never examined in fear conditioning. We investigated whether metacognitive sensitivity can be quantified in emotional learning and how testing order and neuromodulation of the anterior prefrontal cortex (aPFC) influence metacognitive access to the memory of a shock-associated cue. Eighty-one participants (51 females and 30 males) underwent fear conditioning and received either active or sham TMS over the aPFC. They were tested with implicit (skin conductance) and explicit (two-interval forced-choice with confidence ratings) tasks in counterbalanced order. Behavioral performance (d') and metacognitive sensitivity (meta-d') were quantified using signal detection theory. While d' remained stable across conditions, meta-d' and confidence were significantly higher when the explicit task preceded the implicit task. TMS did not affect metacognitive sensitivity. To our knowledge, these results provide the first evidence that metacognitive frameworks can be applied to a fear-conditioning paradigm, revealing that confidence judgments are dynamically modulated by task sequence and remain intact even when bodily arousal is reduced. We propose that metacognitive sensitivity may decline faster than first-order performance, pointing to a functional dissociation between decision accuracy and metacognition in emotionally salient contexts.Significance Statement This study provides the first evidence that metacognitive monitoring can be quantified within a fear-conditioning paradigm, extending metacognitive research beyond perceptual decision-making into emotional learning. We show that confidence in recognizing a shock-associated cue can be dissociated from first-order performance: task sequence critically modulates metacognitive sensitivity even when first-order performance remains stable. Notably, confidence judgments persist despite reduced autonomic arousal following prefrontal stimulation, suggesting that metacognitive access does not require intact bodily signals. These findings indicate that fear conditioning offers a viable paradigm for investigating metacognition and suggest a partial dissociation between first-order performance and self-monitoring in emotional memory. This work opens new avenues for understanding confidence disruptions in anxiety disorders in which threat detection and metacognitive evaluation are impaired.

items.title: Modeling Frailty Risk Based on Biochemical and Hematological Parameters Using Multiple and Logistic Regression: Cross-Sectional Analysis of the Toledo Study for Healthy Aging.
items.abstract: Frailty is a complex syndrome characterized by diminished physiological reserves, resulting in increased vulnerability among older adults. Scalable tools that leverage routinely collected laboratory data could enable earlier risk stratification in aging populations. The aim of the study is to model frailty risk using Frailty Trait Scale (FTS)-12 scores and biochemical or hematological parameters, and to examine sex-specific patterns in predictors and performance. This study analyzed data from a population-based cohort of 1485 individuals aged 65 years or older, drawn from the Toledo Study for Healthy Aging (TSHA). Multiple and logistic regression analyses were used to investigate the relationships between biochemical and hematological parameters, and the FTS-12 score. Predictive models were developed separately for female and male participants, incorporating both single and composite risk factors. Model performance was evaluated using correlation coefficients, coefficients of determination, Akaike information criterion, log-likelihood values, and receiver operating characteristic curves, which summarize how well the models distinguish between higher and lower frailty risk. The regression models accounted for approximately 40% of the variability in FTS-12 scores, revealing distinct risk factors for each sex. Gamma-glutamyl transferase, albumin, and age were kept as key predictors in the selected models. Several composite risk factor functions were also significantly associated with the FTS-12 score. Correlations between observed and predicted FTS-12 scores were moderately strong, with values of 0.621 (P<.001) for female participants and 0.615 (P<.001) for male participants. Logistic regression models showed moderate-to-good discriminative performance for high frailty probability, achieving receiver operating characteristic area under the curve values of 0.799 for female participants and 0.824 for male participants. This analysis is an exploratory proof-of-concept study, and the developed models do not constitute validated clinical prediction tools. Routine laboratory profiles demonstrate moderate, sex-specific predictive performance for FTS-12-defined frailty and may, in principle, complement comprehensive geriatric assessment by facilitating the early identification of patients who could benefit from further evaluation and closer clinical follow-up. External validation in independent cohorts is required before any clinical use, alongside longitudinal designs with repeated biomarker measures and integration of additional biological layers, to enhance generalizability and confirm clinical utility. Within these limits, the analysis highlights the potential of routine laboratory data to support digitally enabled frailty screening and workflow-integrated risk stratification in primary care and remote geriatric care settings.

items.title: Oral nicotine pouch extracts disrupt osteogenic differentiation in human embryonic stem cells.
items.abstract: Oral nicotine pouch (ONP) use has increased in recent years due to the perception that these products are a safer alternative to combustible tobacco products. However, little is known about the potential developmental toxicity of ONPs, particularly during bone formation. In this study, we evaluated the effects of ONP extracts from multiple ZYN flavors and nicotine concentrations on osteogenic differentiation using a human embryonic stem cell (hESC) model. H9 hESCs were differentiated toward the osteogenic lineage and continuously exposed to ONP extracts throughout differentiation. Cellular metabolic activity was assessed using the MTT assay, while ATP content, total protein content, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activity, and calcium deposition were evaluated using biochemical assays and Alizarin Red S staining. Gene expression was assessed using RT-qPCR and single-cell RNA sequencing, followed by pseudotime trajectory and transcriptomic point of departure (tPOD) analyses. ONP exposure caused concentration-dependent reductions in MTT activity, ATP content, total protein content, ALP activity, GPx activity, and calcium deposition. Expression of the osteogenic marker RUNX2 was generally decreased following ONP exposure, while TWIST1, SOX10, and TBX5 expression were increased in several treatment groups. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrated significant alterations in cell cluster distribution and pseudotime trajectory following ONP exposure, suggesting disrupted osteogenic lineage progression. Transcriptomic analysis further identified widespread perturbation of bone development-related genes across treatments. Wintergreen 6 mg had among the greatest transcriptomic potency metrics. Together, these findings reveal that ONP extracts disrupt osteogenic differentiation in hESCs and alter developmental lineage progression. This study provides mechanistic evidence that oral nicotine pouch extracts perturb early osteogenic differentiation in a human stem cell model and supports further evaluation of their developmental toxicity.

items.title: Epidemiology of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis and performance of molecular genotypic drug susceptibility testing in Papua New Guinea, 2022-2023.
items.abstract: Papua New Guinea (PNG) is a high burden country for multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB). Contemporary data is needed given the introduction of a new MDR-TB treatment regimen. We aimed to describe the epidemiology of MDR-TB from 2022 to 2023 and evaluate the performance of the Xpert MTB/XDR assay in PNG. Molecular testing was conducted at district/provincial laboratories and the Central Public Health Laboratory (CPHL), and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST) at the Queensland Mycobacterium Reference Laboratory. We included cases with Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and MTB/XDR results to describe the epidemiology of MDR-TB. Specimens with Xpert MTB/XDR and phenotypic DST results were used to evaluate the performance of molecular testing modalities compared to phenotypic DST. 206 MDR-TB and 20 pre-XDR-TB diagnostic cases were included, predominantly from Western Province (111, 49%; 18.5 referred cases/100,000 population/year) and National Capital District (86, 38%; 5.7 referred cases/100,000 population/year). The most common risk factor was MDR-TB exposure (67/226, 30%). The Xpert MTB/XDR assay showed high sensitivity and specificity for isoniazid and fluoroquinolone resistance. PNG continues to have a remarkably high incidence of MDR-TB. Risk factor data highlights the importance of contact management. Despite challenges, molecular diagnostics perform well and can improve MDR-TB detection.

items.title: Ivermectin Mass Drug Administration Coverage Against Onchocerciasis in Cameroon, 2000-2025: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Persistent onchocerciasis transmission has been documented in some Cameroonian foci despite long-term ivermectin mass drug administration (MDA). We synthesized treatment coverage, adherence and determinants. We systematically reviewed seven databases and grey literature (2000-2025). District-year coverage observations were standardized to total-population epidemiological coverage and pooled using logit-transformed random-effects meta-analysis with Restricted Maximum Likelihood estimation and study/district cluster-robust inference. Adherence, infection prevalence and barriers to treatment were described separately. Thirty-two studies/reports were included among which 20 independent sources contributed 116 observations to the primary meta-analysis. Standardized survey coverage averaged 66.5% (range 32.0-88.3%); 45/116 (38.8%) observations were below the 65% recommendation. Programme-reported coverage exceeded survey estimates in 97/98 paired observations by a mean 21.7 percentage points. Pooled coverage was 67.3% (95% CI 65.0-69.5%; I²=98.5%; prediction interval 40.6-86.1%); the cluster-robust 95% CI was 56.8-76.3%. Five-year adherence ranged from 24% to 67%, while systematic non-adherence ranged from 6.8% to 35% across reported settings. Qualitative synthesis identified setting-specific combinations of missed contact, absence, distribution failures, refusal or hesitancy, adverse-effect concerns, information and trust barriers, mobility and temporary ineligibility. Microfilarial prevalence declined substantially from baseline (52% to 95%) but remained highly heterogeneous across long-treated settings, with the latest reported post-CDTI prevalence ranging from 0% to 47.0%. Ivermectin mass drug administration (MDA) coverage in Cameroon was highly heterogeneous, mirroring variations in infection prevalence. Programme-reported coverage consistently exceeded survey-based estimates. Coverage gaps reflected context-specific operational and community acceptance barriers. Elimination monitoring should therefore triangulate survey-based coverage and adherence, local delivery barriers, and transmission indicators to guide targeted programme improvements and onchocerciasis elimination decisions.

items.title: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever in Spain (2016-2025): Epidemiology, public health coordination and laboratory diagnosis at the National Reference Laboratory.
items.abstract: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF) became a mandatory notifiable disease in Spain after the first autochthonous human cases in 2016. This study characterised suspected cases referred to the National Reference Laboratory (NRL) between 2016 and 2025 and compared them with laboratory-confirmed infections. A retrospective analysis was conducted using data from patients tested for suspected CCHFV infection at the NRL. Demographic, temporal, and geographical variables were analysed. Diagnosis combined two RT-PCR assays targeting different genomic regions and serological methods. Of the 174 suspected cases tested between 2016 and 2025, 18 (10.3%) were laboratory-confirmed. Investigated cases increased from an annual average of 11 (2016-2020) to 23.8 (2021-2025). Confirmed cases were detected annually from 2020. Most suspected cases (89%) occurred between April and October, peaking in June-July; confirmed cases were diagnosed between April and September and peaked in July-August. Men represented 74.1% of suspected and 83.3% of confirmed cases, with most confirmed infections in males aged 61-70 years. The increase in suspected cases reflects enhanced surveillance, awareness, and broader testing rather than a proportional rise in confirmed infections. Annual detection supports endemic CCHFV circulation in Spain, underscoring the importance of surveillance, laboratory preparedness, and rapid diagnostic capacity.

items.title: A Probabilistic Inference Framework for Nonlinear Compartmental Systems with Application to Blood Alcohol Dynamics.
items.abstract: Rising blood alcohol concentration (BAC) may result from continued absorption following alcohol ingestion, ongoing alcohol consumption, or endogenous ethanol production by the gut microbiota (auto-brewery syndrome). Distinguishing these possibilities is a common clinical and forensic challenge, yet the duration over which a rising BAC remains compatible with alcohol ingestion alone has not been quantified. We developed a physiologically based probabilistic framework to estimate the expected timing of peak BAC under ingestion-only conditions. Ethanol pharmacokinetics were modeled using a compartmental model incorporating gastric emptying, intestinal absorption, systemic distribution, and Michaelis-Menten elimination. Inter-individual variability in physiological and behavioral parameters was incorporated using Monte Carlo simulation of 10,000 virtual individuals. Peak BAC timing was calculated from both the start and the cessation of drinking, with the latter representing the clinically relevant endpoint. The median time from cessation of drinking ) to peak BAC () was 81.1 minutes, with 95th and 99th percentiles of 103.4 and 111.0 minutes, respectively. In the baseline simulation, the maximum post-cessation peak time was 122.4 minutes. Sensitivity analyses identified ethanol dose and elimination capacity as the strongest determinants of delayed peak BAC, with the largest simulated post-cessation peak time reaching 149.6 minutes in the combined-parameter analysis. In the baseline simulation, 0.04% of peaks occurred more than 120 minutes after cessation, and none occurred after 135 or 150 minutes. In the most delayed combined scenario, the probabilities of peak BAC occurring more than 120, 135, and 150 minutes after cessation were 100%, 48.16%, and 0%, respectively. Rather than defining a fixed physiological cutoff, this study provides the first probabilistic framework for estimating whether a continued rise in BAC remains compatible with alcohol ingestion alone or warrants consideration of alternative explanations, including endogenous ethanol production in auto-brewery syndrome.

items.title: Informing sample size and power calculations for clone-censor-weight analyses: a Monte Carlo simulation study of the variance inflation factor relative to the underlying target trial.
items.abstract: Clone-censor-weighting (CCW) is a causal inference method used in target trial emulation in settings in which the time of application of the treatment occurs during follow-up. An important component of study design is determining the sample size required for a specified level of statistical power or to determine the statistical power associated with a specific sample size. Determining statistical power is relatively straightforward for the underlying randomized controlled trial (RCT) that one is emulating. In contrast, conducting power and sample size calculations for observational studies that employ CCW is not straightforward because the analysis incorporates inverse probability of censoring weights, which are only known at the analysis phase, and not during the design phase. Monte Carlo simulations (270 scenarios varying sample size, treatment prevalence, threshold for defining early treatment, and covariate-treatment odds ratios) were used to estimate the variance inflation factor (VIF) of a CCW analysis compared to the underlying target RCT, across two estimands: the risk difference and the relative risk. In settings with 10 baseline covariates, the use of a CCW design tended to result in more precise estimation of risk differences and relative risks compared to the underlying RCT when the magnitude of confounding was low to moderate. The magnitude of the VIF depended on treatment prevalence, sample size, the time horizon at which risk was estimated, and the strength of the baseline covariates' association with treatment initiation. In secondary simulations, it was observed that the VIF comparing a CCW design to the underlying RCT tended to increase as the number of baseline covariates increased. Researchers designing CCW studies can use the simulation results and the accompanying R code, available in a public GitHub repository, to obtain study-specific VIF estimates for incorporation into a priori power calculations.

items.title: Pre-Matriculation and Bridging Programs in Health Professions Education to Support Student Success.
items.abstract: A decreasing Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) applicant pool has occurred as an increasing need for representative healthcare providers has emerged. Although changing admissions and recruitment practices have opened the door for additional students to become successful pharmacists, so has the potential for admitting learners with lower levels of academic preparedness. Thus, many institutions have implemented programs to meet students where they are and bridge prerequisite experiences and abilities to the rigor and expectations that are necessary for success in health professions education. This Narrative Review examines published literature on pre-matriculation and bridging programs in pharmacy, medicine, and nursing education. Articles describing programmatic and educational strategies related to pre-matriculation preparation, bridging, orientations, or readiness boot camps were examined. A total of 25 studies were evaluated, describing programs that varied from one day to three years, occurring primarily over the summer. Findings were compiled into a data summary matrix describing format, duration, and topics covered. A present/future perspective was used to summarize and discuss program design and application strategies from multiple health professions educational programs. In turn, successful approaches and suggestions for preparing students for their first year of professional school and beyond are included. Methodologies and approaches from the pharmacy, medicine, and nursing education literature are examined and can be used to identify successful strategies that can be replicated across disciplines and institutions. Challenges, opportunities, and differences between program structures are discussed, as are guidance for application in PharmD educational programs and opportunities for future research.

items.title: Ergonomic workplace injuries as predictors of opioid-related outcomes in New York.
items.abstract: Ergonomic injuries are a common and preventable type of workplace injury that may result in persistent pain and opioid use or misuse, and previous studies have linked occupational injuries to subsequent opioid misuse. Despite a decrease in opioid prescriptions, opioid-related overdose deaths in New York State (NYS) continue to increase, requiring further exploration of contributing factors. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between ergonomic workplace injury rates and opioid-related outcomes in NYS. METHODS: County-level rates of NYS Workers' Compensation Claims (WCC) from 2015-2021 were analyzed, focusing on sprain, strain, and tear injuries. These injury claim rates were compared with county-level opioid-related data from the NYS Opioid Data Dashboard. A linear mixed-effects model, with year fixed effects and county-level clustering, was used to estimate the association between opioid prescription rates, WCC rates, and opioid-related mortality rates. The association between prescribing and mortality outcomes was modified by WCC rates was also examined. There was a greater overlap between high WCC rates and high opioid indicator rates observed in non-metro counties over metro counties. Health Care and Social Assistance, Public Administration, Retail Trade, and Educational Services were the most represented industries in ergonomic WCCs across the state. There was evidence of effect modification by WCC injury rates on the association between opioid prescription and overdose mortality rates, for opioids (B=-3.03, 95% CI: -4.58, -1.48) and opioid pain relievers (B=-3.75, 95% CI: -5.34, -2.17), showing that the association between opioid prescribing and mortality rates weakened among counties with higher WCC injury rates. Despite progress in reducing opioid prescription rates in NYS, workplace ergonomic injuries resulting in strains, sprains, and tears may be contributing to overdose deaths, including from opioids. Workplace ergonomic safety campaigns may be an avenue for prevention of opioid-related overdoses in NYS.

items.title: Implementation and Impacts of Maternal and Perinatal Quality Collaboratives across U.S. States: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Maternal and Perinatal Quality Care Collaboratives (M/PQCs) are voluntary state-based initiatives that leverage shared data systems, evidence-based toolkits, and quality improvement science to reduce preventable maternal and infant harm. A scoping review of academic and grey literature was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and registered in Open Science Framework. Seven databases were searched for U.S.-based M/PQC studies published between January 2000 - November 2024, analyzed in 2025. Two independent reviewers screened 456 deduplicated records; 31 met eligibility criteria. Quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by implementation theme and intervention topic. Thirty-one studies spanning 16 states and one national analysis were included. Five themes were identified across two domains. Implementation approaches included: (A) building statewide governance infrastructure; (B) translating evidence into practice through standardized toolkits; and (C) strengthening communication, teamwork, and process outcomes. Impacts included: (D) demonstrated reductions in maternal and birth morbidity, including 45-95% reductions in early elective deliveries, 76-87% improvements in timely hypertension treatment, and national-level reductions in eclampsia and intensive care unit admissions; and (E) expansion of the collaborative mission toward contraceptive access, opioid use disorder care, and racial health equity. M/PQCs function as a form of primary and secondary prevention, institutionalizing evidence-based protocols before obstetric emergencies occur. M/PQCs' evolution from clinical safety bundles toward equity, access, and social determinants signals an expanding mandate. Future initiatives should prioritize disaggregated outcome reporting, health equity frameworks, and inclusion of community birth and outpatient settings to ensure M/PQC gains are equitably distributed.

items.title: TAK0104 suppresses intracellular Toxoplasma gondii proliferation through disruption of adenosine kinase-associated purine metabolism.
items.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii relies predominantly on purine salvage pathways for intracellular survival due to the absence of complete de novo purine biosynthesis. Targeting parasite purine-associated metabolism, therefore, represents a promising therapeutic strategy for toxoplasmosis. An integrated computational and experimental workflow was employed to identify candidate inhibitors targeting T. gondii adenosine kinase (AK). High-throughput virtual screening of the ChemBridge library was performed, followed by molecular docking, 100ns molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA binding free energy analysis. Biological evaluation included RH-2F β-galactosidase proliferation assays, purine rescue experiments, intracellular ATP depletion assays, DCFDA-based ROS quantification, and JC-1 mitochondrial membrane potential analysis in infected HFF monolayers. TAK0104 demonstrated favorable binding within the ACP-defined catalytic cavity of adenosine kinase with a docking score of -8.73kcal/mol and stable ligand retention during a 100ns molecular dynamics simulation. Biologically, TAK0104 inhibited intracellular tachyzoite proliferation with an IC50 of 322.6nM and exhibited comparatively low host-cell toxicity (TD50 = 10,701nM; therapeutic index = 33.2). Purine rescue experiments demonstrated that TAK0104-mediated growth inhibition reduced parasite proliferation to 23.4 ± 4.09% relative to untreated infected controls, whereas hypoxanthine supplementation restored proliferation to 80.8 ± 8.50%. TAK0104 further induced concentration-dependent ATP depletion, intracellular ROS accumulation, and mitochondrial membrane depolarization in infected host-cell cultures, indicating substantial metabolic stress associated with treatment. TAK0104 demonstrated potent anti-Toxoplasma activity associated with disruption of parasite purine metabolism, accompanied by energetic, oxidative, and mitochondrial stress responses. Conclusions TAK0104 demonstrated potent anti-Toxoplasma gondii activity, accompanied by changes consistent with purine-associated metabolic disruption, ATP depletion, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction in infected host-cell cultures. Although computational analyses support a potential interaction between TAK0104 and T. gondii adenosine kinase (TgAK), the current findings do not establish that direct TgAK inhibition causes the observed antiparasitic activity, and potential host-cell-mediated effects cannot be excluded. Further mechanistic validation is required to establish the contribution of TgAK to TAK0104 activity.

items.title: Comprehenders' Error Correction Mechanisms Are Finely Calibrated to Language Production Statistics
items.abstract: An essential feature of human communication is robustness to errors: even when speakers and writers make mistakes, listeners and readers can usually determine the intended meaning. A leading hypothesis is that comprehenders achieve robust error correction by internally deploying a "noisy-channel" model of the language production process. Crucially, to best achieve error robustness, a comprehender's noisy-channel model should be finely calibrated to the environmental statistics of language production, incorporating not only prior expectations about communicative intents but also structure-sensitive likelihoods of different types of speaker error. This environmentally calibrated noisy-channel hypothesis has been difficult to test, because the rates of most types of language production errors are hard to estimate. Here, we test this hypothesis by experimentally investigating comprehenders' interpretations of subject-verb agreement errors, for which context-contingent language production error rates are feasible to estimate. In a novel free-form error correction task, participants edited sentences with subject-verb agreement mismatches to indicate what they think was intended. Bayesian analysis of the resulting data shows that comprehenders' interpretations reflect both item-specific prior expectations and structure-sensitive error likelihoods that closely correspond to error rates in language production. These results provide quantitative evidence that humans closely track prior statistics over linguistic forms and deploy a noisy-channel model finely calibrated to statistics of the linguistic environment to achieve robust language understanding.

items.title: Narrative theory-driven LLM methods for automatic story generation and understanding: a survey
items.abstract: Abstract Applications of narrative theories using large language models (LLMs) deliver promising methods in automatic story generation and understanding tasks. Our survey examines how natural language processing (NLP) research uses LLM methods to engage with diverse concepts from narrative studies. We use established distinctions from narratology to categorise ongoing efforts and discover the following: (a) narrative texts come from diverse sources beyond just literature, (b) theoretical synthesis and validation are potential outcomes, (c) generation tasks lag behind understanding in several ways: theoretical application, post-training methods, exploring non-fiction narratives and addressing narrative levels beyond fabula and discourse. For future directions, instead of the pursuit of a single, generalised benchmark for ‘narrative quality’, we believe that progress can benefit from efforts that focus on the following: defining and improving theory-based metrics for individual narrative attributes; continue conducting large-scale, theory-driven literary/social/cultural analysis; generating narratives in situated contexts; and continuing experiments where outputs can be used to validate or refine narrative theories. This work provides a contextual foundation for more systematic and theoretically informed narrative research in NLP by providing an overview to ongoing research efforts and the broader narrative studies landscape.

items.title: Translating Place Identity into Textile Motif Design
items.abstract: Place identity is expressed through symbols, practices, and visual representations. Translating regional identity into textile motifs requires a systematic approach that connects local visual sources with meaningful design decisions. This study aims to identify Pangandaran's visual identity sources, translate them into textile motif compositions, and evaluate the resulting prototype. A practice-based design research approach was employed using a modified design thinking process incorporating a visual-semantic translation matrix. Five visual sources were identified and classified, with the Marlin Fish Monument serving as the primary motif, supported by coastal landscapes, fishing activities, marine biota, and vegetation. These sources were transformed through stylization, visual hierarchy, and repeat pattern development into three design alternatives. The selected coastal panorama composition was evaluated as a digital prototype by 17 respondents comprising textile industry experts, textile design academics, and potential users. Descriptive analysis revealed favourable perceptions of recognizability, visual distinctiveness, aesthetic quality, and textile applicability, with pooled mean scores ranging from 4.3 to 4.9. The findings provide preliminary evidence of perceived regional associations rather than independently verified recognition. This study contributes a traceable visual-semantic translation approach that connects regional identity sources with textile design decisions, offering a methodological reference for developing place-based textile products.

items.title: Separating experience reporting from content recall in dream reports across sleep stages
items.abstract: Abstract Contentful dream reports are less frequent after non-rapid eye movement (NREM) than rapid eye movement (REM) awakening. This gap could reflect fewer reports of any experience or less recalled content within those reports. Distinguishing them requires retaining white dreams, experiences reported without recalled content. We audited the questions and codes behind all 20 datasets in the Dream EEG and Mentation database. Fourteen supported comparisons of any reported experience, ten supported content recall within experience reports, and one mapping merged white dreams with negative reports. A Bayesian hierarchical model decomposed the gap within six datasets supporting both comparisons at both stages. Averaged equally across datasets, contentful reports were 21.4 percentage points less frequent after NREM awakening. Most of this primary gap came from fewer reports of any experience: 16.6 points (95% credible interval 9.6 to 22.9), compared with 4.9 (− 4.1 to 12.3) for less recalled content. The experience-report contribution remained positive across weighting, sample and model checks. Content contributions depended on the datasets and weights averaged; both contributions were clearly positive in a four-dataset subset with at least ten records per stage. Uncertain-answer coding shifted the balance between negative reports and white dreams. Contrasting contentful with negative reports combined experience reporting with content recall. Theories must explain why any experience is reported less often after NREM awakening. Neural classifiers targeting any reported experience should retain white dreams in the positive class and assess content recall separately.

items.title: From Admired Figures to Ideal Partners: A Developmental Relational Prototype Model of Adult Mate Preferences
items.abstract: Early interpersonal experiences may contribute to adult partner preferences through autobiographical memory, emotional learning, and relational schemas. This study proposes the Developmental Relational Prototype Model (DRPM), which conceptualizes admired interpersonal qualities encountered during childhood and adolescence as one possible developmental source of later relational expectations. Data were collected from 799 participants in India, Oman, and the United Arab Emirates during 2006–2010, comprising 394 unmarried adults aged 18–25 years and 405 married adults aged 35–55 years. Unmarried participants reported desired qualities in an ideal future partner, whereas married participants retrospectively reported positively valued qualities associated with admired opposite-sex figures. Among unmarried participants, culture and clean habits (58.11%) and love (51.00%) were the most frequently reported partner characteristics. Recall of at least one positively valued quality was reported by 91.62% of unmarried and 75.31% of married participants, with a significant association between marital-status group and recall, χ²(1, N = 799) = 38.32, p < .001, OR = 0.28. Findings provide preliminary support for DRPM while indicating associations rather than causal developmental effects.

items.title: Explorando el engagement académico en América Latina: Una revisión panorámica y teórica
items.abstract: La literatura contemporánea reconoce al engagement académico como un constructo fundamental para comprender el rendimiento, la permanencia y el bienestar del estudiantado universitario. No obstante, en América Latina la evidencia empírica continúa siendo fragmentada y concentrada en universidades urbanas, lo que limita su aplicabilidad en contextos rurales, privados e interculturales. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar los enfoques teóricos, metodológicos y las principales tendencias de la investigación sobre engagement académico en la educación superior latinoamericana. Para ello, se realizó una Scoping Review de investigaciones publicadas entre 2014 y 2025 en las bases de datos Scopus y Web of Science. Tras un riguroso proceso de selección, se incluyeron 14 artículos científicos. Los hallazgos evidencian que el engagement actúa como mediador entre los recursos personales y académicos, además de constituir un factor protector frente al agotamiento emocional, la desmotivación y la intención de abandono. Asimismo, se identificó un predominio de estudios correlacionales y un creciente interés por la validación de instrumentos psicométricos y el análisis del compromiso académico en entornos virtuales. Se concluye que el engagement académico representa un factor estratégico para fortalecer el bienestar, la permanencia y el desempeño estudiantil, aunque persisten importantes vacíos de investigación en diversos contextos latinoamericanos.

items.title: Supervisor need-thwarting behaviour and followers' turnover intentions: a conditional moderated mediation model
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how supervisor need-thwarting behaviour relates to employee turnover intentions through needs frustration, and how interactional justice and job insecurity conditionally moderate this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through a two-wave survey of Australian workers (n = 359). The proposed conditional moderated mediation model was tested using Hayes' PROCESS Macro Model 11 in IBM SPSS v28. Findings Supervisor need-thwarting behaviour was positively associated with turnover intentions, both directly and indirectly through needs frustration. The indirect relationship was conditionally moderated by interactional justice and job insecurity. Interactional justice buffered the positive association between need-thwarting behaviour and needs frustration when job insecurity was low. This buffer was nonsignificant at average insecurity, and reversed in slope when insecurity was high, producing a significant index of conditional moderated mediation. Originality/value This study frames supervisor need-thwarting behaviour as an aspect of harmful leadership, and positions needs frustration as the psychological mechanism that connects supervisor behaviour with turnover intentions. Our arguments advance distinct explanatory roles for self-determination theory and conservation of resources theory, and conceptualise interactional justice as a contingent relational resource that provides a buffering capacity which is undermined by job insecurity.

items.title: Tree island area in oil palm agroforests directly and indirectly drives evaporative fraction
items.abstract: Abstract. Evapotranspiration (ET) – the combined water flux from soil and vegetation to the atmosphere – is a key component of water cycling and climate regulation, and strongly affected by land-use changes. The evaporative fraction (EF), representing the proportion of available energy allocated to ET, is often preferred over ET as a target variable in studies involving repeated measurements under varying weather conditions. In Sumatra’s lowlands in Indonesia, (evapo)transpiration of dominant land-use types including oil palm monocultures is well studied; however, there is a lack of studies assessing ET (or EF) across diverse mosaic landscapes and types of land-use such as oil palm agroforests. Across 52 experimental plots – forest restoration patches known as “tree islands” – in an oil palm landscape (EFForTS-BEE), we tested whether the experimental treatments ‘planted tree diversity’ and ‘tree island area’ influence ET and EF as derived from UAV (uncrewed aerial vehicle)-based thermography and subsequent energy balance modeling. A random partition linear model showed that planted tree diversity (1, 2, 3, or 6 species) did not affect plot-level ET or EF, whereas tree island area (25, 100, 400, or 1600 m2) had a positive effect, with EF increasing by 17 % from the smallest to the largest tree islands. A structural equation model revealed that the effect of tree island area on EF was mediated by both direct and indirect pathways. Specifically, a strong direct effect of island area on EF (Std.Beta = 0.44, p < 0.001) was complemented by an indirect pathway through increased observed woody plant diversity and stand structural complexity. Stand structural complexity had a positive effect on EF (Std.Beta = 0.20, p < 0.05), while neither the vegetation index GNDVI nor tree height variability had significant effects. The observed tree-island-area effect can be explained by a decrease of EF along an edge gradient detected inside the larger tree islands. Our findings suggest that larger tree islands enhance ET and EF through structural and biodiversity-related mechanisms. This underscores the importance of tree islands in human-modified landscapes, not only as biodiversity refugia but also as functional elements that support climate regulation.

items.title: Horizontal gene transfer and reciprocal chimerism in Compactonostoc (Nostocales, Cyanobacteriophyta) with evidence for two new species in the genus
items.abstract: The genus Nostoc has long been known to be polyphyletic, and recent taxonomic work has segregated several Nostoc-like lineages into new genera, including Compactonostoc. Until now, C. shennongjiaensis was the only described species in the genus. In a survey of biological soil crusts from Santa Catalina Island (California, United States), we isolated two Nostoc-like strains that phylogenetically affiliate with Compactonostoc. A polyphasic approach based on morphology, 16S rRNA gene phylogeny, 16S-23S ITS rRNA secondary structures, and cloned ribosomal operons revealed that each strain harbored two highly divergent ribosomal operon types. One operon (Type 2) is closely related to C. shennongjiaensis and contains the two tRNA genes in the ITS rRNA region, whereas the second (Type 1) lacks tRNA genes and is strongly allied to the horizontally acquired Type 1 operon previously reported in Kalymmatonema (as Scytonema hyalinum), indicating an ancient horizontal gene transfer event from an unsampled Nostocaceaen lineage. In one of the isolated strains, we additionally detected two reciprocal chimeric operons (Type 2/1 and Type 1/2), with crossovers in a conserved region of the 16S rRNA gene, demonstrating ongoing recombination between operon types. The ITS rRNA region percent dissimilarity, ITS rRNA region domain structures, and 16S rRNA gene percent similarity, together with consistent morphological differences, support recognition of the two strains as new species of Compactonostoc, C. mediiheterocytium and C. chimera, both clearly distinct from C. shennongjiaensis. Our results document rare ribosomal-operon horizontal gene transfer and reciprocal chimerism in Compactonostoc and highlight the need to examine multiple clones and operons when describing cyanobacterial taxa based on rRNA genes.

items.abstract: Дослідження присвячено комплексному аналізу просторової структури та рівню концентрації природно-заповідного фонду (ПЗФ) Рівненської області в системі державного управління лісами після реорганізації колишніх держлісгоспів у надлісництва філії «Поліський лісовий офіс» ДП «Ліси України». Проведено ретроспективну гармонізацію відомчих статистичних матеріалів станом на 1 січня 2023 року від 16 колишніх лісгоспів до 8 сучасних надлісництв. Вперше застосовано коефіцієнт концентрації чотирьох фірм (CR4) та індекс Герфіндаля-Гіршмана (HHI) як просторово-структурні індикатори управлінського навантаження. Здійснено систематизацію документованих збитків, завданих об'єктам ПЗФ та лісовим екосистемам внаслідок збройної агресії РФ, та проаналізовано екологічні наслідки замінування 5-кілометрової прикордонної смуги з Республікою Білорусь. Встановлено високий рівень просторової нерівномірності: чотири провідні надлісництва (Висоцьке – 24.82%, Клесівське – 18.78%, Рафалівське – 16.06%, Соснівське – 13.76%) концентрують 73.42% площі ПЗФ області (CR4 = 73.42%, HHI = 0.1642). Задокументовано, що лісові пожежі внаслідок ворожих атак завдали шкоди довкіллю на суму понад 7 млн грн із викидами більше 2.2 тис. тонн CO2. Замінування прикордоння створило суцільний бар'єр для міграції великих ссавців та унеможливило натурний моніторинг Рівненського природного заповідника. Обґрунтовано необхідність переходу від уніфікованого до просторово-диференційованого управління лісами.

items.title: Rearchitecting Global Oil Security: The UAE Inland Canal as a Systemic Redundancy Solution (A Real-Options and Capacity Reservation Approach to the Sharjah-Fujairah Corridor)
items.abstract: This study addresses a core problem in infrastructure finance and public-goods provision: how to finance and govern a costly, non-excludable, crisis-contingent transit asset that markets systematically underprovide, using a proposed 116-kilometre Sharjah-Fujairah corridor as the empirical case. The paper combines a single-case analysis of the 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure, comparative analysis of canal, tunnel and pipeline analogues, and transparent financial modelling, capital-recovery, break-even-toll, capacity-reservation and real-options valuation, drawing on International Energy Agency, Energy Information Administration, maritime-intelligence, Brookings, OPEC, FATF and Central Bank of the UAE sources. The pipelines cannot structurally replace the chokepoint, leaving only 3.5-5.5 of roughly 20 million barrels per day redirectable. A canal-pipeline hybrid is the only buildable reference design, costing a reference $130-160 billion once documented megaproject-overrun rates are applied. A capacity-reservation fee of about 3 percent of importers' Hormuz-crude value covers the capital charge and, under real-options valuation, is recovered within roughly 16-27 crisis days. Governance must be anchored in enforceable AML/CFT and sanctions controls. The corridor is viable only as a global energy-insurance instrument aligning payment with benefit through reservation contracts, evidence-gated phasing, and engineered financial integrity. The framework generalises to other concentrated transport nodes.

items.title: Indigenous Sea Gardens have been Adapting to Sea Level Change for at least Four Millennia
items.abstract: Abstract Indigenous peoples along the northwest coast of North America have maintained sea gardens (clam gardens), an ancestral form of mariculture, for at least four thousand years. While their occurrence is being increasingly reported, the degree to which Holocene sea level change has obscured existing ancestral structures along parts of the coast was unknown. We used intertidal and subtidal archaeological excavations, ground-penetrating radar, and radiocarbon dating to assess sea garden wall structure, thickness, and site formation processes at two coastal sites in southern British Columbia, Canada. By comparing sea garden wall depth to the local relative sea level history, we found that sea gardens have been continuously modified and maintained for at least four millennia, and that the morphology of sea gardens is different in areas of transgressing versus regressing shorelines. Moreover, we found that different local sea level histories will influence the visibility of these monumental features today. These observations, woven with Indigenous knowledge, demonstrate that not only is sea gardening an enduring, adaptive cultural practice that has been resilient to changes in sea level position for millennia, but also offers a strategy for climate change adaptation today.

items.title: EVALUATING SOIL QUALITY ACROSS MULTIPLE SOIL TYPES FOR SUSTAINABLE OIL PALM PLANTATIONS IN CENTRAL KALIMANTAN, INDONESIA
items.abstract: Assessing soil quality is essential to ensuring the long-term sustainability of oil palm plantations by aligning agricultural productivity with environmental and social dimensions.This study examines the influence of soil type on soil quality in Kotawaringin Timur District, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia.Specifically, it evaluates four representative soil types (Histosols, Inceptisols, Ultisols and Entisols) using the soil quality index (SQI) framework, identifies key indicators through a minimum data set (MDS), and proposes soil-specific management strategies.The methodology includes field surveys, biological and physicochemical soil analyses, SQI computation and statistical evaluation, with six replications per soil type.Results demonstrate significant variation in SQI values: Low for Histosols (0.245) and very low for Ultisols (0.178), Inceptisols (0.180) and Entisols (0.182).Soil organic carbon (SOC), exchangeable magnesium (Ex-Mg) and available phosphorus (Av-P) were identified as critical indicators influencing soil function.To improve soil quality, the application of organic amendments such as compost, biochar and biofertilisers derived from oil palm residues is recommended.Integrating weed biomass may further enhance nutrient availability and soil resilience, supporting sustainable plantation management tailored to site-specific conditions.

items.title: límites planetarios como condiciones de frontera para la sostenibilidad corporativa
items.abstract: El presente artículo expone la problemática del abordaje instrumental, parcial y fragmentado de los límites planetarios en la gestión organizacional. La sostenibilidad corporativa enfrenta una tensión central en el antropoceno: mientras las organizaciones incrementan sus discursos, reportes, estrategias ambientales e innovaciones, la degradación de los sistemas biofísicos que sostienen la vida continúa profundizándose. El objetivo del documento entonces es analizar cómo los límites planetarios pueden ser comprendidos como referencias biofísicas para repensar la gestión organizacional y la sostenibilidad corporativa. En cuanto a la metodología, se desarrolló una revisión crítica e integrativa, la búsqueda se realizó en Scopus y Google Scholar, y esta se dividió en tres bloques; se utilizaron diferentes criterios de búsqueda y selección como: palabras clave, ecuaciones de búsqueda, tiempo (2007-2025) y nivel de relevancia; finalmente, fueron seleccionados 52 documentos temáticos y 3 metodológicos, los cuales fueron sometidos a una revisión y análisis profundo; y posteriormente, se construyó una síntesis integrando desarrollos teóricos de diversos campos disciplinares. Los resultados evidencian que la adopción de los límites planetarios en la gestión organizacional puede permitir el desplazamiento de la sostenibilidad corporativa, desde una lógica de eficiencia, riesgo, reputación e innovación incremental hacia una comprensión sistémica, multiescalar y biofísicamente condicionada.

items.title: Tubastraea coccinea (Cnidaria: Anthozoa) is the globally dispersed species of Sun Coral
items.abstract: Species of the genus Tubastraea (sun corals) have dispersed globally over recent decades, but morphological trait identification has led to taxonomic confusion, with multiple authors proposing conflicting species identifications due to high morphological plasticity and overlapping diagnostic traits. We combined global-scale molecular phylogenetics with chromosome-level genome assemblies to resolve this taxonomic issue. Using mitochondrial and nuclear markers from 287 specimens across five ocean regions, including type localities in Bora Bora (T. coccinea) and Galapagos (T. tagusensis), we reconstructed phylogenetic relationships and inferred demographic history through approximate Bayesian computation. We also generated high-quality, chromosome-level genome assemblies for three morphologically distinct morphotypes from the Brazilian coastline. Phylogenetic and species delimitation analyses revealed two well-supported clades: a small, geographically restricted T. tagusensis clade confined to the Galapagos Islands, and a large cosmopolitan clade containing all worldwide samples, including T. coccinea from its type locality. Comparative genomic analyses of the three morphotypes revealed k-mer spectra compatible with triploidy and assemblies comprising 14 chromosome-scale scaffolds with extensive synteny and gene-tree discordance consistent with incomplete lineage sorting. Dispersal-route analyses identified the Southeastern Pacific (Galapagos) as the ancestral source, with at least two independent, human-mediated colonization events establishing populations in the Southwestern Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico, and Western Pacific. Our results establish Tubastraea coccinea as the cosmopolitan species responsible for global dissemination, while T. tagusensis is endemic to the Galapagos and not involved in the worldwide dispersion.
authors: Danielle Luciana Aurora Soares do Amaral

items.title: LAND USE CHANGE PATHWAYS IN THE BARUMUN WATERSHED: ASSESSING THE ROLE OF OIL PALM EXPANSION
items.abstract: Indonesia is among the world's major palm oil producers, and oil palm expansion is often associated with deforestation.This study examines gradual land use and land cover (LULC) changes from 2000 to 2023 in the Barumun watershed, North Sumatra, using Landsat 5 Thematic Mapper (TM) and Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager (OLI) imagery processed through Google Earth Engine.A Random Forest (RF) machine learning algorithm was applied for supervised classification.The results indicate that forest cover decreased by 5.12% over 23 years.The primary conversion pathway was forest to other land with tree cover (accounting for up to 54.60% of initial forest loss), which was later converted to oil palm plantations.Oil palm area increased by 13.91%, but direct forest-to-oil palm conversion was limited.These findings suggest that oil palm was not the primary cause of initial deforestation in this watershed.The results provide evidence for policymakers to distinguish between direct and indirect land use change pathways when designing sustainable land management strategies.
