items.title: Looking back from the stellar graveyard: inferring the origins of binary black holes with gravitational waves
items.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) have transformed our understanding of binary black holes (BBHs), with hundreds of observations now published since the first direct detection in 2015. Measuring the population properties of many BBHs allows us to statistically infer the of the lives and deaths of their progenitors, which are subject to many overlapping uncertainties. The first source of these uncertainties arises from observational limitations: BBHs likely originate from massive, potentially low-metallicity stars, which are short-lived and hard to observe. Second, predicting the evolution of massive stars is limited by our theoretical understanding of multi-scale stellar evolutionary processes, which for BBH progenitors is further complicated by binary and dynamical interactions. Third, understanding the astrophysics over a population of BBH progenitors is limited by the computational expense of simulating the detailed physics of their progenitors using population synthesis models. The growing number of GW observations offer unique insight into these uncertainties, allowing us to understand the evolutionary pathways that lead to merging BBHs. In this thesis, I investigate the origins of BBHs with new complementary modelling frameworks, exploring correlations between observed masses and mass ratios, and developing emulators of population synthesis simulations. Motivated by evidence that BBHs prefer to merge with similar masses, I develop parametric population models to infer whether the minimum mass of the smaller black hole varies with the mass of the larger black hole. Using GW data from hundreds of observations, I show that big black holes can merge with the smallest black holes, contrary to expectations from previous studies of the BBH mass ratio distribution. I find that the interpretation of population outliers, such as unequal mass ratio observation GW190814, depends on the construction of our population models. This demonstrates how analysing GW observations using new population models furthers our understanding BBH observations and astrophysics Comparing the observed BBH population to population synthesis simulations allows for constraints on astrophysical parameters governing their evolution, and the relative contribution from different formation channels. These simulations are computationally expensive and rely on a wide range of assumptions, therefore achieving robust predictions from population synthesis remains a key challenge in GW astronomy. I demonstrate the effectiveness of normalising flows, a type machine learning algorithm, to interpolate predictions from population synthesis and overcome the necessity of a dense grid of simulations. This framework enables previously intractable constraints over a continuous range of parameters governing the physics of BBH evolution, and probe degeneracies between key assumptions in population synthesis simulations. Extending this framework to ensure consistency between the emulated populations and the observational selection effects, I find that differences in how selection effects are calculated lead to large discrepancies in inference results with O(100) observations. These discrepancies arise from small differences between the emulated populations and the underlying population synthesis models, indicating that more accurate emulation of population synthesis is necessary avoid systematic bias in resulting astrophysical constraints. This is particularly important as we analyse an increasing number of observations, which will drive increasing differences between constraints under these two methods. Showing how these analyses are subject to shrinking statistical and persistent systematic uncertainties with growing GW catalogues, I highlight the future work necessary for robust BBH population inference. Overcoming these systematics will enable the application of new population models, including more flexible parametric models of correlated distributions, and population synthesis models exploring the correlations between more astrophysical parameters and formation channels. The development of robust inference frameworks will allow us to confidently constrain multiple uncertain parameters in BBH evolution, and develop trustworthy simulations of BBH progenitor populations. As we advance further into the era of GW astronomy, these analysis provide crucial steps towards piecing together where and how BBHs form.

items.title: Pulsars and Millisecond Pulsars V: Observational Census of Globular Cluster and Field Pulsars
items.abstract: This fifth paper of a series on pulsars and millisecond pulsars (MSPs) looks at the observational side of the problem. We review the facilities that detect pulsars in different wavebands and the catalogues that collect their parameters, and we compare the pulsars of globular clusters (GCs) with those of the Galactic field (GF), using version 2.9.0 of the ATNF Pulsar Catalogue and the list of 372 GC pulsars in 46 clusters maintained by P. Freire. MSPs make up 94% of the GC pulsars and 15% of the GF pulsars, and GCs host 36% of the MSPs known in the Milky Way. Binary MSPs in GCs have shorter orbits than those in the GF, with median orbital periods of 1.1 and 4.8 days, and are more often eccentric, 16% against 5% with e > 0.1. The isolated fraction of GC MSPs is 86% in core-collapsed clusters and 42% in the others. The spin periods of the two populations differ only when the comparison is restricted to fully recycled MSPs, and 45% of the GC MSPs with a measured period derivative show a negative value, so that fields and ages derived from them are biased. We relate these results to the seven evolutionary scenarios of this series and to current simulations, and end with nine observational benchmarks for cluster models that follow pulsars.

items.title: Annie Jump Cannon (1863–1941)
items.abstract: Chapter 9 . Annie Jump Cannon (1863–1941) The systematic cataloguing and classification of astronomical objects has a long history. But they were not classified according to any known physical principles. Annie Jump Cannon solved this problem. Cannon majored in physics and astronomy. In 1896, she was hired by Harvard Observatory director Edward C. Pickering, as one of a group of women, to catalog stellar photographs taken by amateur astronomer Henry Draper, who categorized stars by their colors and the spectra of hydrogen on their surfaces. Another scheme labeled stellar types in alphabetical order, based on the strength of the hydrogen lines. Using those same lines and letters, Cannon found an organizing principle: classification by surface temperatures. The order was OBAFGKM, whence the pneumonic “Oh be a fine girl/guy kiss me.”

items.title: SYMBIO-SCAN, a full-length 16S rRNA gene-based workflow optimized for bacterial symbiont detection and discovery from long read sequencing
items.abstract: Bacterial endosymbionts are often unculturable, making sequencing-based approaches essential for their discovery and characterization. Here we developed SYMBIO-SCAN, a dedicated workflow for recovering high-quality nearly full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences of symbionts from long reads, which provided an adequate discriminatory power for identification and for accurate phylogenetic analyses. After validation on a mock community, we applied this workflow to 30 beetle (Coleoptera) specimens from 10 species. Beetles were selected since they host a wide variety of bacterial symbionts, able to influence host physiology, ecology, population dynamics, and evolution. Despite their importance, most of these symbionts remain completely unknown or poorly characterized. By the novel approach, we obtained 80 high-quality sequences belonging to diverse bacterial lineages, mostly Rickettsiales and Enterobacterales. Putative reproductive manipulators were among the most frequently detected symbionts, including Wolbachia, Rickettsia, "Candidatus Lariskella", Arsenophonus, and Spiroplasma. Moreover, three putative novel genera and one additional putative novel species were identified, including a possible Enterobacterales nutritional symbiont of the weevil Holotrichapion pisi. Overall, our results support that full-length 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing combined with tailored bioinformatic analyses provide a quick, cost-effective, and robust approach for investigating the diversity of host-associated bacterial symbionts, also allowing the discovery of entirely novel lineages.

items.title: Forest fragmentation, anthropogenic land use, and climate shape sand fly community composition in central Panama.
items.abstract: Background: American cutaneous leishmaniasis (ACL) is endemic in central Panama, where rapid land use change is transforming tropical landscapes and potentially altering the ecology of sand fly vectors. Although researchers have widely studied environmental determinants of individual vector species, community-level responses of sand fly assemblages to landscape modification remain poorly understood. We evaluated how landscape composition, fragmentation, climate, and topography influence sand fly community structure in a rural landscape of central Panama. Methodology/Principal Findings: We combined metacommunity analyses with joint species distribution models (JSDMs) to quantify species-specific and community-level responses to climatic variables, land-cover composition, and forest configuration. We collected 1,692 individuals representing 30 species, including nine anthropportunist taxa of epidemiological importance. Sand fly assemblages had strong nestedness, low species turnover, and predominantly positive residual associations. Several anthropportunist sand fly species occurred across heterogeneous landscapes, although their responses to environmental conditions differed among taxa. Land-cover composition, forest fragmentation metrics, and elevation together explained about half of the variance in species occurrence and abundance, with the remainder attributed to climate and spatial, temporal, and community-level random effects. Grassland cover contributed most strongly to sand fly occurrence and abundance, whereas artificial surfaces consistently reduced both metrics. Fragmentation effects varied by species: edge density often increased occurrence and abundance, whereas more forest patches generally suppressed populations. Increased precipitation broadly enhanced occurrence and abundance, whereas higher temperatures negatively affected several taxa. Conclusions/significance: Landscape heterogeneity predictably structures sand fly communities, and different forms of anthropogenic disturbance exert non-uniform effects on vector assemblages. The nested organization of these assemblages and the co-occurrence of several anthropophilic species suggest that multiple potential vector species may be present across heterogeneous landscapes. These findings highlight the need for landscape-informed surveillance and control strategies that prioritize grassland–forest interfaces and other disturbed ecotones where sand fly species of epidemiological importance frequently co-occur.

items.title: Avoidance or coexistence? Exploring spatio‐temporal niche overlap between two sympatric ungulates barking deer and Himalayan goral in a multi‐use landscape of Uttarkashi district, Western Himalaya
items.abstract: Abstract: Ungulates play a vital role in maintaining the integrity of the high mountain ecosystem by sustaining plant community structure and regulating predator populations. Therefore, it is necessary to understand the interaction of sympatric species in the mountainous landscape. In this study we aim to investigate the seasonal spatial and temporal overlap between two sympatric species namely barking deer ( Muntiacus vaginalis) and Himalayan goral ( Naemorhedus goral) in Uttarkashi, district of Uttarakhand. We employed niche equivalency and niche similarity test, to quantify the niche overlap of these sympatric species. Total of 99 trails were traversed and 134 camera traps were deployed to collect data on the sympatric ungulate species. The finding of non-significant niche similarity test statistics and significant background test statistics indicated that both sympatric ungulates have broad niche similariy relative to the same available environmental space throughout year. Overall niche overlap index showed modrate to high (0.58), however in summer showed modrate (0.54) and in winter showed low overlap (0.34). We also investigate the temporal activity pattern of both species, where barking deer showed diurnal and crepuscular activity pattern with highest peak activity during mid-day hours while Himalayan goral was active throughout the day with peak activity during morning and evening hours. The daily activity index Dhat value showed highest temporal overlap was found in winter season (0.79) and lowest in summer season (0.71). This study provided useful information to understand the coexistence pattern of sympatric ungulates in Himalaya, which will be helpful for their long term conservation and management. Understanding these interactions provides insights into the mechanisms driving community structure and species persistence in increasingly complex ecosystems.

items.title: The missing ultra-faint satellites of the Milky Way
items.abstract: Abstract We combine the highest resolution N-body simulation of a ∼1012M⊙ ΛCDM halo (Aquarius-A) with the semi-analytic model GALFORM to study the full satellite population of Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies. The model assumes that galaxies form only in subhalos whose peak circular velocity exceeds the hydrogen-cooling threshold, and predicts that the total number of satellites ever accreted into the main halo, down to arbitrarily low luminosity, should not exceed a few hundred. The model tracks satellites even after their halos become unresolved (”orphan” galaxies), and includes a novel treatment of dark matter and stellar tidal stripping which takes into account that ΛCDM subhalos survive tidal disruption because of their cuspy density profiles. Our results match the massive end of the observed MW satellite mass function and predict that many ultra-faint dwarfs (UFDs) with MV > −5 are missing from the current MW satellite census. The missing UFDs are predicted to avoid the innermost regions of the host, and have properties overlapping those of the recently-discovered ultra-faint compact MW satellites (UFCSs). If the faintest dwarfs are initially as compact as UFCSs, our results suggest that many UFCSs should be dark matter-dominated dwarfs with velocity dispersions 1 − 3 km/s which survived disruption because they inhabit the cusp of ΛCDM subhalos. UFCSs have predicted densities of 1010-1011 M⊙/kpc3, higher than those of more extended UFDs. If confirmed, our results provide strong support for the cuspy nature of ΛCDM halos and for the hydrogen-cooling threshold for galaxy formation.

items.title: JWST’s Dusty Blue BOAT - GRB 221009A
items.abstract: Abstract GRB 221009A, the Brightest Of All Time (BOAT), presents a challenge for afterglow modelling due to its low Galactic latitude and consequent high line-of-sight extinction. This has led to a wide range of conflicting values for the optical spectral index and dust extinction in the literature. We present a re-analysis of the afterglow spectra, using VLT X-Shooter data at 0.5, 4, and 10.5 days, and JWST NIRSpec/MIRI data at 13.3 days post-burst. We fit the data with single and smoothly broken power-law models and perform a joint fit with a double smoothly broken power-law (DSBPL) across all epochs. Our analysis reveals a strong degeneracy between the assumed extinction and the inferred intrinsic spectral index, particularly in the optical, explaining the diversity of previous results. The joint DSBPL fit yields a total line-of-sight extinction of AV = 4.40 ± 0.01 and a blue continuum, with an intrinsic spectral index of β = 0.447 ± 0.001. Although marginally preferred by the spectral fits, a wind medium can be rejected by the temporal evolution of the afterglow light curve. The fit spectral index and temporal decline are only consistent with a uniform density medium if an early jet break at ∼0.5-1.0 days is invoked. Our results imply a hard electron distribution index of p = 1.89 < 2, challenging standard particle acceleration models and suggesting a narrow, energetic jet core dominates the early optical-to-X-ray emission.

items.title: One-Dimensional Carbon Nanostructures with Periodic Graphitic Nitrogen Substitution
items.abstract: Abstract Heteroatom substitution is a powerful route to tune the chemical and electronic properties of carbon nanomaterials. In particular, replacement of an sp2-hybridized carbon atom in the graphene lattice with a nitrogen atom (denoted as graphitic nitrogen) induces substantial changes in the electronic properties. These include changes in the band structure that can influence electronic transport and magnetism. A key requirement for applications is both the periodic and precise incorporation of the heteroatoms in extended carbon lattices. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis and characterization of two one-dimensional carbon nanostructures─a polymer and a graphene nanoribbon─consisting of periodically incorporated graphitic nitrogen atoms. The on-surface reactions toward the formation of the nanostructures were monitored by scanning tunneling microscopy. The bond-resolved chemical structures of the reaction intermediates and products were investigated by atomic force microscopy, which enabled atomic-scale visualization of the graphitic nitrogen sites. The electronic properties of the nanostructures were studied by scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. Our analyses revealed the presence of localized nitrogen-centered electronic states in the nanostructures. In the gas phase where the nanostructures are in the neutral charge state, these states undergo spin polarization leading to an open-shell ground state. Upon adsorption on Au(111), the nanostructures exhibit electron transfer to the surface, which resulted in a closed-shell ground state. Our results demonstrate a straightforward and generally applicable route to synthesize graphitic nitrogen-substituted carbon nanomaterials with potential applications in spintronics, catalysis, and energy storage.

items.title: A Multi-Wavelength Picture of the Surprisingly Short 2024/25 Outburst from EXO 0748–676
items.abstract: Abstract After sixteen years in quiescence, EXO 0748–676 unexpectedly returned to outburst in March 2024. However, in stark contrast to its previous outburst (1985 - 2008), EXO 0748–676 returned to quiescence in January 2025, after ∼10 months in outburst. Here, we collate data from nine observing facilities, covering wavelengths from radio to X-ray, to provide the first multi-wavelength study of the 2024/25 outburst. Unlike the 1985 outburst, both the rise and decay are fully captured at X-ray and optical wavelengths. The light curves do not exhibit the hallmarks of a canonical transient low-mass X-ray binary outburst. Instead, the X-ray and optical fluxes remain reasonably stable during the 2024/25 outburst. The wealth of optical data of EXO 0748-676 reveals a skewed optical phase curve and an irradiation-dominated optical light curve which lasts until the onset of hydrogen recombination in the outer disc at ∼11000K, triggering a rapid fade at the end of the outburst. X-ray observations by XMM-Newton and NICER revealed that EXO 0748–676 was heavily obscured early on, with spectra exhibiting a dampened soft X-ray contribution. We find that a spectral model including a clumpy, ionised absorber describes the obscuration, although the exact cause of the early-time obscuration remains uncertain. X-ray colour analysis indicates that EXO 0748–676 spent most of the ∼10 month outburst in a faint, hard state. EXO 0748-676 increased marginally in brightness towards the end of the outburst, but never entered a soft spectral state. This behaviour is characteristic of a failed transition outburst.

items.title: Modelling space weather plasma physics
items.abstract: Abstract We start with a brief introduction to the many faces of the Sun, the dynamic star that is the main source of space weather. We explain the need for spacecraft observations, the structure of the solar atmosphere, and the Sun's magnetic cycle. Next, we focus on the Sun's influence on Earth, define what 'space weather' means, and briefly discuss its effects on our technology and their related socio-economic impact. Then, we present data-driven, physics-based simulation models with predictive capabilities that enable forecasting and mitigation. We focus on the models developed by my team at KU Leuven and the results and predictions obtained with them: the heliospheric wind and CME evolution models EUHFORIA and ICARUS, the global solar corona model COCONUT, and the solar energetic particle acceleration and transport model PARADISE. We end with a few take-home messages.

items.title: Hydrogen Dynamics in a Coupled Thermosphere‐Lower Exosphere Model With Charge Exchange
items.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen transport in the exosphere impacts its distribution in the thermosphere, and vice versa, necessitating that the two regions be modeled together to fully capture their coupled dynamics. However, upper atmospheric model development is complicated by the transition of the highly collisional thermosphere into the exosphere, where collisions between atoms are rare. This paper extends work examining the neutral transport and circulation of hydrogen using a two‐way coupled thermosphere‐exosphere model. Neutral interactions with H+ and O+ are introduced into the model exosphere to examine the influence of charge exchange on hydrogen dynamics from the mesopause to ∼20,000 km altitude, that is, the lower exosphere. The resultant model, ExoTherM, shows chemical loss of hydrogen can alter the hydrogen escape flux computed at the exobase. The model reaches an equilibrium without a prescribed balance between thermal and non‐thermal escape methods, resulting in a significantly reduced thermosphere density during solar minimum compared to the model without charge exchange. The three‐cell framework of hydrogen transport and circulation derived from the neutrals‐only exosphere model is retained. Finally, charge exchange is shown to increase the hydrogen velocity distribution width in the lower exosphere, influencing hydrogen's motion in an altitude‐dependent manner. This work is intentionally limited to an upper boundary of ∼20,000 km and is not representative of the entire hydrogen exosphere. Within this scope, this study emphasizes the impact of ion‐neutral chemistry not only on upward hydrogen flux but also on neutral hydrogen dynamics throughout the upper atmosphere due to the coupled nature of the thermosphere‐lower exosphere system.

items.title: ReveaLLAGN 3: Revealing the Infrared Spectral Energy Distributions of Low Luminosity AGN
items.abstract: Abstract The spectral energy distributions of active galactic nuclei (AGN) provide valuable information on the emission mechanisms taking place in their inner regions. Here we use the James Webb Space Telescope to study the near and mid-infrared spectral energy distributions of seven nearby low-luminosity active galaxy nuclei from 1.7 to 24 μm. We cleanly separate the AGN spectrum by performing spatial fits of the two-dimensional images across all wavelengths. We then compare these clean unresolved spectra to aperture-based spectra and show that they effectively remove galaxy contamination. Comparing our infrared measurements to X-ray emission, we find that low-luminosity AGN have enhanced near-infrared emission relative to more luminous AGN, a trend that correlates with radio-loudness, while their mid-infrared-to-X-ray ratios are comparable. A majority of our targets show strong compact silicate emission suggesting the presence of warm dust on parsec scales in these systems. We also quantify the near- and mid-infrared power-law slopes and colors of low-luminosity AGN. In the near-infrared we find AGN of all luminosities have similar spectral slopes and colors, however in the mid-infrared, we find low-luminosity AGN typically have steeper slopes and redder colors than more luminous AGN. Both the strong silicate emission and steep mid-infrared slopes disagree with existing models for low-luminosity AGN spectral energy distributions.

items.title: Quantifying and modeling the storm-induced orbital decay of 11 LEO satellites during 1-14 May 2024
items.abstract: During 1–14 May 2024, the Sun launched several Coronal Mass Ejections towards Earth, causing a series of geomagnetic storms, the strongest of which reached extreme (G5-class) intensity. These events significantly disturbed the Earth’s upper atmosphere and increased atmospheric drag. We investigate the impact of space weather on the orbital decay of 11 low Earth orbit satellites at altitudes from 474 to 1344 km. We find that satellites below ~600 km altitude experienced relative decay rate increases of about four times compared to quiet conditions, while those at higher altitudes experienced up to a twelvefold increase. Orbital response times to geomagnetic storms varied widely from 4 to 26 hours and suggest a possible dependence on storm intensity. During the extreme storm on May 10, all satellites below 815 km decayed substantially, with up to about 200 m day −1 at lower altitudes. Separately, we evaluate the potential of predicting this decay from earlier observations of the solar wind, radio fluxes, and geomagnetic indices. Our models use average response times as lead time and achieve prediction errors of up to 20 and 4 m day −1 for satellites below and above 600 km altitude respectively. Despite the limited dataset and differences between satellites, models reproduce the maximum orbital decay rates during the extreme storm of May 10. Solar wind proton temperature and magnetic field contributed most to models predicting effects on lower-altitude satellites. Overall, results of this study highlight the variable nature of the LEO orbital response to space weather across satellites, orbits, and storm conditions.

items.title: Planetary Accretion Is Less Frequent in Wide Binaries: Evidence from Metal-enriched White Dwarfs in DESI DR1
items.abstract: Abstract Binary stars are common in the Galaxy, and understanding how stellar binarity influences the formation and evolution of planetary systems is an active area of research. In this study, we use metal-enriched white dwarfs in wide binaries as tracers of long-lived planetary systems. With Data Release 1 from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we find that the fraction of cool metal-enriched white dwarfs in wide binaries is 9.8% ± 2.1%, significantly lower (4.7 σ ) than the 20.5% ± 0.9% in a control sample of single systems. Furthermore, we identify a tentative dependence of metal enrichment on projected separation and white dwarf effective temperature, where enrichment fraction decreases at smaller separations and lower temperatures. These findings indicate that, compared to single stars, binary systems either start with smaller initial planetary reservoirs due to suppressed planetesimal formation or undergo more rapid depletion of planetary material during the initial part of the white dwarf stage.

items.title: Making Learning Matter
items.abstract: Undergraduate research is no longer confined to lab benches and computer labs – it belongs in classrooms, studios, archives, and community sites across the liberal arts. Making Learning Matter is a call to action for educators across disciplines to embrace course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs) as a powerful, equitable tool for student learning, engagement, and transformation. This book offers practical guidance, real examples, and theoretical grounding for integrating CUREs into both lab and non-lab settings. Drawing from diverse disciplines, it demonstrates how research can be scaffolded into courses at every curriculum level, starting with introductory courses. We focus specifically on non-major general education courses as vehicles to engage and excite all students in exploring a wide range of disciplines. Whether designing a data-driven research project in a statistics class or incorporating archival inquiry into a literature seminar, faculty will find frameworks and inspiration to make authentic research experiences part of their teaching practice. Grounded in the model of embedded High-Impact Pedagogy, the book makes a case for course-based research as a transformative practice that promotes inclusion, reflection, critical thinking, and collaboration. The book tackles timely tools and topics, integrating generative AI into CUREs, helping students develop not only research skills but also digital and ethical literacies essential for the future. Making Learning Matter speaks to a wide audience: instructors interested in new ways to engage students in STEM, humanities faculty eager to embed research more deeply, as well as any other faculty wishing to create more meaningful, research-based experiences in their classroom. We expect that the book will appeal to institutions seeking scalable, inclusive, and accessible models for undergraduate research. It celebrates what’s possible when curiosity, creativity, and inquiry meet meaningful pedagogical design – making research a common language across the liberal arts.

items.title: The time-dependent Kepler problem and its solution via the time-dependent harmonic oscillator and Ermakov invariants
items.abstract: Abstract We present a method for solving certain time-dependent Kepler problems using the Ermakov-Lewis invariants of the associated time-dependent harmonic oscillator problem. We also show that both the time-dependent harmonic oscillator and the Kepler problems can be further transformed in to time-independent problems. We obtain explicit expressions for the invariants for the time-dependent Kepler system, as well as expressions for the equation of the orbit and the Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector. Finally, we present some examples of time-dependent Kepler problems where the method is used.

items.title: A Study on the geoeffective event of 11 April 2022
items.abstract: Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) are the main drivers of geomagnetic storms. Studying their initial phases is important for understanding their propagation through the heliosphere and the effects they have on the Space Weather. In this work, as a case study, we investigate how SolO/Metis observations improve the accuracy in modelling a geoeffective CME that occurred on 11 April 2022. This event caused a geomagnetic storm of intensity of −81 nT in terms of Disturbance Storm Time (Dst) on 14 April 2022. This moderately geoeffective event serves as a challenging case to model and understand the complex interactions of CMEs with the ambient solar wind. Using coronagraphic data from SOHO/LASCO C2, STEREO/SECCHI COR2-A along with VL observations from SolO/Metis, a Graduated Cylindrical Shell (GCS) analysis was done for 3D reconstruction of the CME flux rope. This provided the input parameters required for running the physics-based propagation models (DBM and DBEM, WSA-Enlil and EUHFORIA) which we have used to calculate the CME arrival times at Earth. SolO/Metis provides an additional viewpoint for the above analysis leading to a more precise determination of the GCS parameters and the 3D speed of the CME. By constraining the initial parameters, the 3D MHD models better resolve the interaction of the CME with the ambient solar wind. Including SolO/Metis data for this particular event leads to a lower error in the predicted arrival times at Earth for WSAEnlil and EUHFORIA (≈ 3 hours) than the typical ≈ 8–10 hours error estimates found in literature. Plain Language Summary Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) are large expulsions of plasma and magnetic field from the Sun. When directed towards Earth, these can affect the space environment around Earth. Accurate predictions of the arrival time of CMEs is therefore important to mitigate their effects. In this work, we chose a case study of a CME that erupted on April 11, 2022 and caused a moderate geomagnetic storm at Earth two days later, on April 13. The CME was observed by a constellation of spacecraft from different view points, which allowed building a 3D model of the CME during its initial evolution. We then employed three physics-based models to evaluate how the CME interacted and propagated through the ambient solar wind medium. We were then able to demonstrate the crucial role of the initial 3D model of the CME obtained from multi-viewpoint observations in improving the accuracy of the predictions of the arrival time at Earth.

items.title: METHODOLOGY FOR ORGANIZING STUDENTS’ SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH WORK IN GRADE 6 WITHIN THE INTEGRATED COURSE “EXPLORING NATURE”
items.abstract: The article substantiates a methodology for organizing scientific research work of Grade 6 students in the integrated course “Exploring Nature” and presents the results of its experimental testing. The essence, stages and forms of students’ research work are clarified, and basic, tactical, and strategic research skills are characterized. The methodology comprises four components (motivational-target, content, procedural, resultative) and five pedagogical conditions (situation of success, educational environment, pedagogical support, professional orientation, motivational environment). The experiment was conducted in 2023–2024 in two Grade 6 classes (experimental group – 13 students, control group – 14 students); 26 teachers were surveyed beforehand. In the experimental group, the mean level of research skills rose from 2.02 to 2.36 points on a four-level scale, and the share of the initial level fell from 30.5% to 16.7%, whereas in the control group the indicators remained practically unchanged. Positive dynamics of the motivational-target component was recorded in the experimental group. Methodological recommendations for teachers are proposed.ReferencesAntonova, O. Ye. (2014). items.title: Impacts of Game-Based Learning (GBL) in Science Education: An Evidence Synthesis
items.abstract: Digital game-playing has become a part of human lives, given the swift rate of technological advancement. Several research studies have examined the possibilities and potential of incorporating games into educational settings through game-based learning (GBL). Particularly, science education has attracted the attention of game-based scholars because of the need for scientific practices and personnel for global development. However, there is a need to synthesize the literature to identify trends in game-based science learning, provide insights into current teaching practices, and initiate future transformation in society. This article provides a rapid review of relevant studies between 2013 and 2023 to identify commonly addressed science learning outcomes and establish research trends in terms of design and educational level. Using a standard methodology (Garritty et al., 2021), articles were included from Education Source, Academic Search Complete, and ERIC databases. Findings indicate that games have great potential in promoting effective science education. Most of the reviewed studies focused on scientific knowledge acquisition, suggesting a need to conduct more research on advanced scientific competencies, especially argumentation and scientific creativity competencies. Only one study focused on scientific attitudes and emotional outcomes, suggesting this as a potential area for further research. The review reported a prevalence of quasi-experimental studies with secondary level studies. Researchers are encouraged to conduct more qualitative studies to reveal the pattern of game interaction and mechanics that account for the reported learning gains and investigate these impacts with other educational levels.

items.title: Management Information Systems: Redefining Management in the Digital Age – Volume I
items.abstract: Digital transformation, artificial intelligence, and data-driven technologies are reshaping the operations, decision-making processes, and management approaches of contemporary organizations. This book examines these transformations from a Management Information Systems perspective, adopting an interdisciplinary approach to their technological, organizational, managerial, and human dimensions. The chapters comprehensively address AI-driven organizational change, human–AI collaboration, generative AI in innovation management, big data architectures, cybersecurity in cloud computing, digital twin technologies, prompt engineering in knowledge management, programmatic advertising, technological innovativeness, and digitalization in public administration. Integrating theoretical perspectives, empirical findings, and conceptual models, the book explores how technological capabilities are transformed into organizational value. By providing a holistic examination of the opportunities and managerial challenges of the digital age, this volume serves as a comprehensive academic resource for researchers, scholars, students, and practitioners.

items.title: Solar‐Blind Polarization Sensitive Photodetection Based on β‐ Ga 2 O 3 Microwires With Super‐High Polarization Ratio (>5000) Enabled by Intrinsic and Morphological Anisotropy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐blind polarization photodetectors are highly desirable for next‐generation intelligent sensing and imaging systems, yet achieving a high polarization ratio remains a major challenge for current devices. Here, we report a solar‐blind polarization photodetector based on mechanically exfoliated β ‐Ga 2 O 3 microwires, in which intrinsic crystal anisotropy and morphology‐induced anisotropy are synergistically combined to enable enhanced polarization‐sensitive photoresponse. First‐principles calculations reveal that the intrinsic anisotropic optical absorption of β ‐Ga 2 O 3 originates from its low‐symmetry monoclinic crystal structure, leading to polarization‐dependent interband transitions. The finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations reveal that the microwire morphology introduces additional polarization‐dependent optical anisotropy. A simple metal‐semiconductor‐metal photodetector is constructed using a single β ‐Ga 2 O 3 microwire, achieving outstanding solar‐blind ultraviolet detection performance with an ultrahigh polarization ratio (PR) of 5200. Furthermore, by integrating the anisotropic photoresponse into a polarization convolution (pCONV) and combining it with an artificial neural network, high‐accuracy fingerprint recognition is achieved with an accuracy of about 99%. This work establishes β ‐Ga 2 O 3 microwires as a promising material for high‐performance solar‐blind polarization photodetection and highlights the effectiveness of morphology engineering in boosting polarization‐sensitive optoelectronic performance.

items.title: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning
items.abstract: Radiologists' visual attention can supervise medical image learning, but how reader panel composition affects its value remains untested. We evaluated GazeRIB (Gaze-guided Radiologist-Informed Blackout), which masks unviewed regions during training and uses unmasked images at inference. Eight experts repeatedly read the same 80 chest X-rays (CXRs). We compared individual readers with three-, five- and eight-reader panels across seven architectures and 10 seeds, evaluating 910 models on a separate 2,897-CXR cohort for four-class severity prediction. Every panel improved macro F1 over the no-gaze baseline by 5.33-7.47 percentage points (pp; Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.007); no individual reader reached significance on this endpoint. Three readers captured 73-80% of the eight-reader gain in macro F1, the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AU-PRC). On external validation without retraining, all four panels improved ROC-AUC on SIIM-FISABIO-RSNA by +1.93 to +4.24 pp (p <= 0.004); on MIMIC-Eye no panel differed significantly from baseline, whereas the single-reader average declined (-1.40 pp, p = 0.008). Reader composition therefore influenced performance, although transfer depended on the cohort.

items.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
items.abstract: Agentic workflows are increasingly shifting towards long-horizon tasks, such as open-ended scientific work, where models benefit from long context windows. However, at ultra-long context (above 1M tokens), full attention is prohibitively expensive. A promising approach is sparse attention, in which a dedicated indexer selects a subset of keys for the attention. Yet current methods of indexing either still have quadratic cost in context size or lose accuracy at ultra-long context scale. We address this with Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), an efficient attention method that maintains accuracy at ultra-long context. In LSA, keys are hierarchically clustered in a learned latent space, and queries score the hierarchy of clusters instead of scoring every key, making prefill, decode and training faster at long context. We propose two variants, Distilled-LSA (D-LSA), which can be applied to pre-trained models via distillation, and Native-LSA (N-LSA), which is trained natively on the next-token loss alone. On GLM-5.3-FLASH (QWEN-3.8-27B) at 10M tokens, D-LSA speeds up one attention layer by 22.7x (72.4x) in prefill and 4.6x (42.5x) in decode over its original sparse attention (full attention), while keeping similar accuracy across a variety of tasks. N-LSA matches the accuracy of full attention with a training speedup of 1.6x per layer at 128k tokens. LSA offers practical and efficient attention for models to benefit from ultra-long context.

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.abstract: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our framework utilizes a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level world model as an inverse dynamics solver to ground these transitions into precise actions. This allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details. By prioritizing local physical feasibility over global behavioral patterns, ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, transcending the specific behavioral modes seen during training. We demonstrate its effectiveness across three navigation and manipulation suites, achieving a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners. Crucially, by leveraging this hierarchical structure to mitigate compounding errors, our approach yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks. Videos can be viewed at https://id-wm.github.io

items.title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
items.abstract: Recent work shows that a frozen robot policy performs far better inside an agent harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools, or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup. In RoboArchitect, a coding model observes a robot's rollouts, diagnoses failures, and iteratively revises the harness around the frozen policy. The harness evolves on a set of episodes for its optimization and is evaluated on held-out scenes and tasks. Without updating any model weights, RoboArchitect raises average success from 9.7% to 43.3% on unseen scenes (4.5x) and from 12.7% to 40.2% on unseen tasks (3.2x), across multiple benchmarks and policies. The gains are largest where the benchmark is far from the policy's training data: wrapping a general-purpose policy, the evolved harness yields a specialist that often outperforms even the finetuned version. Intuitive control strategies are automatically designed, such as lifting a jammed arm clear or reaching in horizontally when an obstacle blocks the way from above. The harness also evolves its own persistent memory, carrying learned experience, such as effective grasp depths, into later decisions. These results suggest that substantial headroom in robotic manipulation lies in the agent harness, and its design can be effectively automated and optimized without weight updates.

items.title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
items.abstract: In real-world deployments, large language model (LLM) systems are increasingly evolving from single-model invocation toward heterogeneous deployments in which different models are dynamically invoked for inference. When the same context is reused across models, however, each newly selected target model typically has to process it again, repeatedly incurring substantial computational costs. Therefore, we propose ACCT (Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer), which targets KV cache transfer between models of different scales within the same model family. ACCT transforms the KV cache produced by a source model into sparse KV states that can be directly consumed by a target model, thereby enabling cross-model reuse of context computation and decoupling context computation from downstream inference. ACCT consists of three lightweight components: the Cartographer identifies query-relevant context tokens for each target layer and KV head; the Allocator determines how many context tokens each target layer and KV head retains under a shared total KV budget; and the Compiler transforms selected source KV into sparse target KV. The target model can therefore perform inference using the transferred KV without reprocessing the original context. We evaluate ACCT in two complementary settings comprising five general-capability benchmarks and six highly context-dependent tasks. Experiments show that ACCT matches or exceeds the target model's original inference performance even when reducing the KV cache size by 75%. At a context length of approximately 19K tokens, ACCT's KV conversion achieves a 6.5-21.2 times speedup over target context prefill. These results demonstrate the feasibility of transferring context computation across models under a limited KV budget.

items.title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer
items.abstract: The quadratic scaling of attention is a fundamental bottleneck limiting the long-context capabilities of large language models (LLMs). A variety of approaches have attempted to circumvent this, but they either fail to match attention's expressiveness (e.g., sliding-window or linear attention variants with fixed-size state) or only achieve constant-factor speedups (e.g., sparse attention methods whose indexers themselves scale quadratically). In this paper, we derive an asymptotically subquadratic sparse attention method based on a hierarchical, tree-structured indexer, which we call Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA). ZHA constructs a tree of recursively compressed key summaries over the KV cache, which future queries traverse from the top down to retrieve a sparse subset of keys. Crucially, by iteratively growing the tree's depth, the total cost including routing and final attention grows sublinearly in sequence length, resulting in overall subquadratic (but superlinear) scaling for attention. We demonstrate that ZHA can be cheaply applied to existing pretrained models with only a short KL distillation training stage over a few billion tokens, and maintains performance on long-context retrieval and challenging reasoning, mathematical, and agentic coding evaluation tasks. Moreover, we show that our method is highly robust to tree geometry including very deep trees of up to 6 levels. Finally, we develop a detailed performance model and show that our approach scales subquadratically, dramatically outperforms competing methods beyond 1 million context, and ultimately has the potential to extend effective context windows to the hundreds of millions or billions of tokens.

items.title: CausalWAM: Learning the Causes of Actions in World Action Models
items.abstract: World action models (WAMs) learn latent variables from observations and use these to both predict the evolution of the scene and to generate actions. The prediction has to be of the whole scene, whereas only a portion of the scene causes actions. WAMs fitted to demonstrations do not, in general, guarantee that they will generate actions solely from the latent causes of the demonstrated actions (the action-relevant latent variables), as the model could just as well learn to imitate in this way whilst entangling the action-relevant latent variables with the nuisance variables. We therefore separate out what causes action from what prediction depends on. We prove that under a sparsity constraint the latent variables used to generate actions are an invertible function of the action-relevant latent variables alone and the true structure is identified up to a permutation of the latent variables. This requires neither sufficient temporal dependence nor any assumptions on how the unobserved regimes evolve and holds even when the action-relevant latent variables are statistically dependent on the rest. We therefore propose CWAM (Causal WAM), which incorporates the constraint into a pretrained WAM by adding a sparse routing path to its action head, with the world modeling objective remaining unchanged. Experiments on both synthetic data and real-world robots validate the theory as well as showcase the improved efficiency in closed-loop success.

items.title: The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results
items.abstract: AI answers require more than apparent correctness: reviewers need to inspect their recorded basis. We introduce the Knowledge Layer Model (KLM), an open, implementation-neutral specification for inference records with versioned epistemic assessments, evidence relations, and explicit unknowns. SEDIM, the knowledge and evidence architecture of Nage AI OS, is a reference implementation. We reference KLM v0.3 (repository tag v0.3.0). Empirical material consists of separate internal experiments, not end-to-end validation. A historical platform-domain routing benchmark reports 137/150 classifications across 15 classes (91.3%; nominal 95% Wilson interval 85.7-94.9%); the numerator is recovered from a rounded summary, and historical example membership is unverified. A native-model weight-path configuration yielded 0/15 successful answers in a corrected two-source test. A capacity-growth comparison could not establish a reliable effect because of a defective legacy scorer and missing original outputs. Lexical and scoped diagnostics each yielded AUC 0.008 for silent-versus-contradicted examples, below the registered minimum of 0.65. Legacy packing lost gold-containing text in 118/221 selected cases; repaired packing retained it in 221/221. These measure text presence, not answer quality. Python and TypeScript verifiers reportedly agreed on six checks per synthetic fixture; a separate production disclosure was not accepted. Restoration, re-derivation, human-rubric support, boundary isolation, and bounded-response evaluations remain proposed. Findings are internal and author-reported; historical observations are distinguished from later reproductions. Evidence visibility does not establish correctness, causal reliance, security, or regulatory compliance. Independent replication and a complete public audit package remain future work.

items.title: CRoS: Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs Improves Accuracy and Reasoning Faithfulness
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become the standard method for training language models to reason. However, RLVR typically relies solely on outcome correctness, which does not guarantee that the CoT causally contributes to the final answer. Without this connection, outcome rewards may fail to reinforce high-quality reasoning. Existing causality metrics assess CoT causality by perturbing the CoT, such as deleting reasoning steps or injecting errors, and measuring changes in the final answer. However, these perturbations inevitably alter information in each step. Consequently, high causality scores may reflect sensitivity to information changes introduced by perturbation rather than true causality. Such confounding effects further induce undesirable reasoning behaviors when these metrics are used as training rewards, including generating less informative CoTs and reducing exploration and self-correction. To address this problem, we propose CRoS (Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs), a novel CoT causality metric that perturbs the order of reasoning steps without altering content, thereby preserving information within each step. On Reasoning Gym with Gemma-3-4B, CRoS outperforms existing causality and outcome rewards in out-of-domain accuracy, CoT quality, and CoT faithfulness. Specifically, CRoS achieves 46.8% accuracy on five unseen logic and games datasets, outperforming the strongest baseline (43.8%). It also achieves better CoT quality, consistently outperforming baselines in CoT-Pass@K from K=1 to 128, averaging 43.4% vs. 41.4%. For CoT faithfulness, CRoS achieves a hint acknowledgment score of 34.0% vs. 20.2%.

items.title: Near-Optimal Second-Order Convex Finite-Sum Optimization under Individual Smoothness
items.abstract: We study the stochastic second-order oracle complexity of solving smooth convex finite-sum optimization with $n$ components. Very recently, Tsedenov \& Kovalev (2026) showed that the minimax optimal complexity under averaged smoothness and convexity is $\tildeΘ(n + n^{6/7} ε^{-2/7})$ by establishing nearly matching upper and lower bounds. In this paper, we show that individual smoothness and convexity provably enable further acceleration, where the lower complexity bound is $Ω(n+ n^{5/7} ε^{-2/7})$ under this stronger assumption. Then, by establishing a novel second-order self-bounding inequality, we design a new Taylor-corrected lazy Newton method, which can lead to a better complexity of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n + n^{5/7} ε^{-2/7})$ by applying the optimal Monteiro-Svaiter acceleration, matching our lower bound up to only logarithmic factors.

items.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
items.abstract: Hundreds of millions of people now ask large language model (LLM) chatbots for health advice, which raises a question that is simple to pose and hard to answer: does everyone get the same advice? We audit six widely deployed LLMs from four providers on smoking cessation, a domain with codified clini- cal guidance and substantial public-health stakes, by putting the same four cessation questions to twelve user personas that differ in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, for a total of 2,880 responses. What the models say depends on who appears to be asking. Every model named FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often to teen personas than to adult personas, by 32 to 67 percentage points, and in five of six models a persona presenting health- care expertise received fewer facts than a persona presenting none. We then evaluate one deployable intervention: a short system prompt specifying a factual floor, the set of core med- ical facts every user should receive when they are relevant, while leaving tone, vocabulary, and framing free to adapt. The prompt narrows persona differences in every model, but its effect on overall fact coverage varies in both magnitude and direction across models, so a prompt validated on one system cannot be assumed to transfer to another. Two cautions frame these results. Equal mention rates are not always the correct clinical target, because prescription cessation pharmacother- apy is not recommended for minors, so a defensible factual floor must be age-aware rather than uniform. And because our personas vary on several attributes at once, we report scenario- level differences rather than isolated effects of age or expertise. We release all 2,880 responses and the analysis code.

items.title: Learning Clean Generative Processes from Noisy Measurements
items.abstract: We study how to learn a generative model of clean images using only noisy observations. Diffusion processes and their generalizations to non-Gaussian noise require posterior predictions at every noise level. We first show that it is possible to learn these predictions from independent noisy views using Noise2Noise regression, but only at or above the noise level of the training data. To learn the predictions below that level, needed to generate clean images, we impose consistency: a prediction should equal its expectation after continuing the sampling process. We derive conditions under which consistency uniquely determines the continuation to the clean image distribution and verify them for Poisson, binomial, Gamma, and negative-binomial measurements. Experiments on CIFAR-10, photon-counting microscopy, and synthetic aperture radar show that the required posterior predictions can be learned from noisy views alone and that the consistency relation repairs the continuation beyond the noise level of the data, which severely deteriorates without consistency.

items.title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?
items.abstract: Looping re-applies a block of layers so that each token passes through the block more than once. Adding a loop to a trained model is attractive because it leaves the parameter count, and hence the disk size, the memory footprint and the training cost unchanged. Unfortunately, every generated token pays for the loop. Re-applying m of N layers makes each token about (N+m)/N times as expensive. Loops that a model learns during large-scale pretraining justify this price, but whether loops added after pretraining justify this cost remains unclear. We compare a looped model with two simple baselines. We first compare it with the same model trained identically without the loop (equal parameters). Secondly, we compare it with the best unlooped use of the same inference floating-point operations (equal FLOPs). Across Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B parameters, only the looped 0.8B model beats both baselines. At 4B and 9B, the looped model does not beat the first baseline, i.e. the same model trained without the loop. This is not because the benchmarks are too easy, since on the same benchmarks the unlooped 9B model still scores up to 13 points higher than the 4B model, showing that there is ample room for improvement. Introducing loops in an already pretrained model therefore only pays for small models with a fixed parameter budget.

items.title: Know When the Equation Is Wrong: Structural Uncertainty for LLM-Guided Symbolic Regression under Extrapolation
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can help discover mathematical equations from data, but most LLM-guided symbolic regression methods focus on a single best equation without quantifying uncertainty over alternative functional forms. This is challenging because distinct equations can fit the observed data similarly while producing substantially different extrapolations. Our experiments on the LLM-SRBench dataset show that standard conformal intervals achieve nominal in-distribution coverage but frequently fail under extrapolation. To tackle this challenge, we introduce LLM-SR-UQ, a framework that retains competing equation structures and uses their disagreement to characterize uncertainty about the underlying functional form. We extend the standard fixed-width conformal approach to quantify structural intervals, which measure disagreement among candidate equations and identify where prediction intervals should widen. Extensive experiments show our framework substantially improves coverage attainment by incorporating structural disagreement while preserving in-distribution coverage. Our approach also shows good generalizability when it is applied to other symbolic-regression methods.

items.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
items.abstract: Multi-turn negotiation remains a challenging problem for large language model (LLM) agents. While LLMs can conduct natural-language dialogue, existing benchmarks predominantly assess only agreement rates, overlooking whether negotiated commitments actually create value once executed. To address this gap, we introduce TradeWar, a multi-country simulation benchmark that translates negotiation dialogues into concrete tariff and trade-share policies, enforces capacity and network constraints during settlement, and evaluates outcomes via an Economic Health Index (EHI). To solve this execution-grounded task, we propose TACTIC (Trade-aware Adaptive Consolidation and Theory-of-mind for International Commerce), an agent that iteratively refines its negotiation strategy across episodes-without updating base LLM weights-by leveraging prior experience, opponent behavior, and past settlement outcomes. Despite using zero-shot chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, PromptLLM attains a 75% agreement rate but only 57.1 final EHI (*100), whereas TACTIC reaches 68.8. Across 20 sequential episodes and three seeds, TACTIC's final EHI improves from 58.2 to 73.2, compared with 65.2 for an ablation without cross-episode updates. Under technology-controls and energy-crisis shocks, TACTIC also exhibits smaller performance degradation than PromptLLM and MemoryLLM. These results indicate that CoT deliberation and interaction memory alone do not fully address delayed execution feedback, whereas settlement-grounded adaptation improves long-horizon negotiation in TradeWar.

items.title: AutoAnalysis: An automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more capable and widely used, understanding when and how humans should work with these systems is becoming increasingly important. However, the empirical evidence in this space offers conflicting recommendations, which leaves individuals and organizations without clear guidance on when to combine human and AI capabilities. Existing meta-analyses can help reconcile these findings, but they require substantial manual effort and cannot readily incorporate new evidence as it emerges. To address this challenge, we introduce AutoAnalysis: an automated, self-updating meta-analysis of when humans and AI work better together, and when they work better alone. AutoAnalysis' most recent run synthesizes 1,955 effect sizes from 420 papers. Across this body of work, we found that, on average, human-AI combinations performed significantly better than humans alone, but they performed significantly worse than the better of humans or AI alone. These findings highlight the important distinction between improving human performance and achieving human-AI synergy and underscore the need to evaluate collaboration against both human and AI performance alone. As new studies emerge, AutoAnalysis will integrate their findings into the meta-analysis, providing cumulative evidence about when humans and AI perform better together and how human-AI performance varies across AI agents, tasks, and processes.

items.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
items.abstract: Recognized as a top threat to AI agents, prompt injection allows instructions from untrusted data (email, documents, websites) to manipulate the agent's operation. The existing best-defended LLM, Meta-SecAlign, is trained with the DPO loss but still suffers from attack success rates (ASRs) approaching 100% under adaptive prompt injections. One reason is that DPO anchors the model around the undefended reference model, which is insecure. We show an idealized reference model---an injection-invariant, utility-preserving oracle---can nevertheless be approximated, as its output distribution in training is interestingly accessible. This new observation motivates a theoretically principled SecPO loss. Another Meta-SecAlign shortcoming is that it trains on weak simulated attacks. We implement an efficient adversarial training (AT) pipeline that synthesizes strong injected inputs (best@240), and train the model on them. Our AT reduces ASRs by 1.5-14.5$\times$ across three SoTA adaptive attacks, compared with Meta-SecAlign; the SecPO loss reduces them by a further 2.4-4.6$\times$ compared with using DPO loss. In agentic workflows, our SecPO + AT Qwen3.6-27B is much more secure than Meta-SecAlign: 8.8% vs. 78.8% AgentDojo ASR@800 under the AttackerMovesSecond attack. Moreover, our defended model shows no noticeable reduction in benign utility in nine benchmarks covering agentic tool calling, instruction following, science, and math. We release our $\href{//github.com/Sizhe-Chen/SecPO}{\text{code}}$, $\href{//huggingface.co/datasets/Sizhe-Chen/Qwen3.6-27B-Instruct-SecPO-trainset}{\text{training data}}$ (with optimized injections from AT), and $\href{//huggingface.co/Sizhe-Chen/Qwen3.6-27B-Instruct-SecPO}{\text{model}}$.

items.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
items.abstract: Linear attention scales linearly with sequence length, but its finite-state memory can limit long-context retrieval. In gated linear recurrences, memory retention depends on state decay, which is shaped jointly by gate parameters A_log and dt_bias and by input activations. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) experiments, both parameters remain highly correlated with their initial values after training, highlighting the importance of initialization. Therefore, we introduce Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI), which jointly configures these parameters before training. DAMI assigns geometric timescales across heads for varied retrieval distances and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers. A small activation sample calibrates the GDN-family implementation to match both behavioral targets without adding trainable parameters. Across GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7, DAMI improves average RULER-style retrieval accuracy by 5.29 to 16.71 percentage points over the corresponding random-initialization baselines. Performance on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and 2K real-world retrieval remains broadly comparable to those baselines. Our code is available at https://speedai.com/research/dami.

items.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models
items.abstract: Large-scale behavioral pretraining offers a promising route to generalizable representations in online payment systems. However, high-cardinality identity fields such as card, device, and account IDs, though rich in behavioral signals, remain underexploited. Their continually growing vocabularies and limited semantic meaning make existing vocabulary-based and semantics-based encodings ill-suited. Their generalizable signal lies not in specific values, but in the identity behavior patterns they exhibit across a transaction sequence. Building on this insight, we propose ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework that brings these patterns into transaction foundation models. ID2Pattern first encodes identity fields with a Local Anonymous ID (LAID) tokenizer, which captures how each identity appears and recurs within the sequence, independent of its specific value. It then pretrains a multi-scale pattern codebook on unlabeled sequences, which abstracts LAID sequences into discrete behavior patterns for downstream prediction. Experiments on an industrial dataset with over 100M sequences and six public datasets show that ID2Pattern consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving industrial by 4.13% and public datasets by 8.83% on average. Notably, ID2Pattern remains equally effective even when all identity values are unseen during training, highlighting its potential to generalize to new users and markets.

items.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
items.abstract: World-action models increasingly apply test-time scaling, spending extra inference computation on candidate selection and adaptive allocation to improve control. Such gains are credible only when candidates carry exploitable signal, nominal compute savings become real speedup, and evaluation stays reliable. We audit all three on Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa with a premise-first, pre-registered methodology. On clean data, a learned value selector is 1.66 pp worse than random; a hindsight oracle gains only 1.40 pp, with an episode-level interval spanning zero; and 82% of states show identical candidate outcomes, leaving little selection headroom. Token pruning cuts per-forward FLOPs by up to 47% but yields at most a measured 1.15$\times$ end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.25$\times$ on a decode-excluded path), short of a 1.5$\times$ target, and our adaptive-allocation experiment is inconclusive under a power gate. We further identify and fix a silent rendering corruption whose rate rises sharply along compute-heavy planning paths while leaving the official direct-policy result unaffected, and release a detector, fix, and scripts. These findings show why test-time scaling should be audited as a chain of premises (decision signal, realized efficiency, evaluationintegrity) rather than by success rate alone. Conclusions are scoped to the tested configuration.

items.title: Prune Gradually, Adapt Sparsely: Efficient Pruning of Large Language Models at Extreme Sparsity
items.abstract: Weight pruning can reduce the storage and inference cost of large language models (LLMs), but preserving quality at high sparsity levels remains challenging. Existing methods face a quality-cost trade-off in this regime. One-shot pruning is cheap but degrades sharply as sparsity increases, even when followed by post-pruning recovery. A growing line of work instead optimizes the mask directly from the dense model under the end-to-end objective; among these methods, [Lee et al.,2026], the recent state of the art at extreme sparsity, reaches high quality but at the cost of model-sized optimizer state and auxiliary variables. To address this gap, we propose ETAPS, which prunes gradually and adapts sparsely: it tightens a global sparsity constraint in progressive stages while training a sparse delta with a small, fixed budget. Our key observation is that gradual weight removal keeps each pruning step small enough for sparse adaptation to compensate, allowing the adapted model to provide end-to-end gradients that guide the next pruning decision without model-sized optimizer state. Across six models from 125M to 13B parameters, ETAPS achieves lower perplexity than ELSA at every evaluated sparsity from 50% to 90%, with perplexity reductions of up to 42%. ETAPS is also far cheaper: at 90% sparsity, it prunes LLaMA2-7B on a single H200, where ELSA uses four, with $5.0\times$ smaller total persistent state and 49% fewer GPU-hours. Together, our findings point to a promising direction for achieving high quality in demanding regimes such as extreme sparsity at substantially lower cost.

items.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
items.abstract: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external drivers. Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the interactions between multivariate time series and heterogeneous covariates, which commonly arise in scientific applications. The model infers relationships among time series directly from historical context and generates probabilistic forecasts without task-specific treatment. Across various benchmarks, Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on average by improving skill scores by 5.2 percentage points relative to the strongest baselines and increasing win rates by 10 percentage points. Chronos-2 is also computationally efficient, generating forecasts for 100 time series in under one second on a single mid-range GPU, 50x and 1000x faster end-to-end than the best task-specific point and probabilistic forecasters, respectively. In addition, we demonstrate its effectiveness in diverse scientific settings -- including infectious-disease forecasting, macroeconomic modeling, carbon-flux prediction, and runoff simulation -- where the model matches or surpasses specialized methods developed for each domain. These results show that a single pretrained model can capture structure shared across temporal systems.

items.title: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions
items.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance across a wide range of reasoning tasks, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations and decision criteria align with the latent structure of human cognition. In this work, we propose a novel framework to align MLLMs with the multidimensional mental representations underlying human similarity judgements. We build on a previously established behavior-derived semantic embedding space, in which objects are represented along 66 interpretable dimensions derived from 4.70 million human Odd-One-Out (O1O) judgements. For each triplet, we infer the most salient decision dimension and convert it into a dimension-grounded linguistic rationale. This enables MLLMs to learn both the final choice and a justification consistent with the inferred behavioral criterion. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves model consistency with human similarity judgements while retaining competitive performance on standard multimodal benchmarks. Furthermore, using searchlight Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) on an independent fMRI Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), we observe increased representational alignment between model and human. Ultimately, our findings point to a data-driven route for incorporating human cognitive structure into MLLMs alignment. The code is available \href{https://github.com/ening-open/cogalign}{here}.

items.title: Optimizing Stochastic Policy Geometry for Few-Step Flow Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Few-step flow models generate samples through a handful of large denoising transitions. Applying GRPO to such models requires introducing stochasticity into the denoising transitions, and when a single transition spans a wide range of noise levels, the choice of the resulting stochastic policy becomes a major factor in optimization. Recent constructions constrain the policy to preserve the target flow coefficients, but this constraint admits a family of policies and offers no criterion for choosing among them. We introduce Geo-FSRL (Geometry-Optimized Few-Step Reinforcement Learning), built on a selection principle: at a fixed conditioning state and timestep pair, choose the admissible policy that minimizes the conditional KL divergence induced by any given nonzero velocity-output update. Within a coefficient-preserving family of isotropic Gaussian transitions, this criterion reduces to minimizing a single scalar geometry factor that determines the conditional KL for every velocity-output update. The same factor governs velocity-space Fisher information and conditional transition log-likelihood-ratio variance. We derive the unique closed-form optimizer within this family, shared across all nonzero update magnitudes and directions, with transition coefficients determined by both the source and target noise levels. Because the minimized geometry factor still varies across timesteps, we further adopt gradient-scale matching from prior work and derive closed-form policy-gradient and KL weights that normalize explicit score scales and reference-KL curvature. Geo-FSRL trains on the original few-step schedule and retains the deterministic solver at inference. Our method achieves higher final reward scores than Flow-GRPO and Flow-CPS on both image generation and video generation models under the 4-step setting. Code is available at https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/tree/main/lightx2v_rl

items.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
items.abstract: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup. We present Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and ROS2 middleware. The library combines operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and episodic dataset generation. We evaluate Sensorium across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments involving multiple surgical tasks and sensing configurations, and report preliminary usability feedback.
