items.title: Observable-Specific Validity Tests for Scientific AI: Controlled Approximations and Intervention Response
items.abstract: An approximation can reproduce an energy while missing its response, or satisfy an error tolerance without being certified by a given bound. We formulate observable-specific validity records for scientific artificial intelligence (AI) that link a reduction to its reference model, error measure, tolerance, parameter domain, and transformations or interventions. Explicit displacement and velocity certificates for a singularly perturbed oscillator recover distinct convergence orders and provide sufficient validity guarantees. Exact Hubbard dimer relations resolve the different coupling domains accepted by energy and response criteria. Across 16 repeated neural fits, imposing dimensional homogeneity reduces energy scale transfer error from 52.3% to 0.0768% and raises the median fraction jointly satisfying gap and response tolerances from zero to 100%. Paired transformations verify the protected scaling relation, while a coupling crossover identifies the additional information needed for response transfer. A causal model recovers a positive intervention response beneath a strong negative observational association. For two mechanisms observed with Gaussian noise whose responses first differ at order $x^k$, we derive an exact fixed control query requirement scaling as $x^{-2k}$ and verify its full success curve numerically. Together with a 256-task evaluation interface, these results provide independently checkable tests of controlled approximation, physical transfer, and mechanism discrimination in scientific AI.

items.title: Structure-Aware Skill Retrieval and Arbitration for Optimization Modeling
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can turn natural-language optimization tasks into solver-checked answers, but current agents remain brittle under narrative rewrites and often store reusable experience at the instance level. We introduce \textsc{ArchOR}, an archetype-centric skill agent that builds on \textsc{OptSkills} by adding two retrieval-focused modules. \emph{Centroid-Aware Representation Learning} (CARL) refines the ordering of cached skill representations through a low-rank prototype residual. \emph{Signature-Guided Retrieval} (S\textsuperscript{3}R) attaches open-dimensional structural signatures to skills, prioritizes candidates by weighted Jaccard overlap, and bounds semantic re-ranking to a top-$K$ set. A baseline-preserving arbitration rule determines when the structural route should replace the original selector. With the same DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone and released skill library, \textsc{ArchOR} reaches 65.00\% Micro-Avg.\ Pass@1 across five benchmarks, improving over \textsc{OptSkills} by 1.64~pp Micro-Avg.\ and 2.68~pp Macro-Avg.

items.title: ReX-GG: a LLM Ensemble Pipeline for Relation-extraction and Graph Generation
items.abstract: Current LLM ensemble frameworks focus on multi-step setups with additional modules for answer ranking, often opting for token and span analysis rather than structured outputs, leading to heavyweight architectures with potential fail states along the pipeline. Faster, lighter solutions are more vulnerable to hallucination propagation and can lack output control in more complex pipelines. This paper proposes a customisable, lightweight ensemble workflow of coordinated Large Language Models that leverages JSON-structured outputs and anonymous peer-review ranking to mitigate hallucinatory outputs and single-model failure points. The pipeline is demonstrated on a relation extraction task applied to popular science articles in English, targeting four ontologically-grounded relation types (strong causation, weak causation, contrastive, and compositional), with semantic node canonicalisation and interactive, colour-coded HTML causal graphs as the final output. Performance is evaluated through an anonymous user study, achieving an average perceived accuracy of 0.778 against a human-annotated gold standard. The modular architecture supports flexible deployment across both API-based and in-house LLM setups, and the full framework is released under an open license to foster reproducibility and collaborative research.

items.title: Using Machine Learning to Measure Self-Efficacy Belief Through Learners' Interaction Traces in Technology-Enhanced Learning
items.abstract: Self-efficacy beliefs play a critical role in learners' performance, academic choices, and, more broadly, in their future career trajectories. As Technology-Enhanced Learning (TEL) environments have demonstrated strong potential for supporting both performance and motivation, investigating self-efficacy within such environments is of particular interest, especially for implementing remedial practices as early as possible to support learners' self-efficacy beliefs. Our research aims to develop a system capable of detecting low self-efficacy based on learners' interaction traces while they solve exercises in a TEL system. In this paper, we present initial results and future perspectives on a detection approach based on data mining and machine learning techniques to identify features indicative of low self-efficacy beliefs. Because the detection of learners' self-efficacy beliefs through their use of TEL systems remains largely unexplored, this work is exploratory in nature. To this end, we conducted an experiment across two universities to collect interaction traces and self-reported measures of self-efficacy. We then developed a machine learning pipeline comprising multiple classification models, enabling us to highlight the importance of closely monitoring of learners' self-efficacy beliefs for improved prediction performance, given their highly dynamic nature during learning.

items.title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
items.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) learn reusable representations from large collections of unlabeled data. In chemistry the corresponding data mainly consists of molecular structures, which are abundant, whereas experimental measurements are scarce. Chemical FMs such as ChemBERTa and MoLFormer were therefore trained on diverse molecular structures to enable fine-tuning on small experimental datasets (less than 100 datapoints in most realistic scenarios) and subsequent property prediction. At the same time, general-purpose FMs such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were trained on virtually all publicly available data, including knowledge of the humankind on molecular properties and laws governing them. Here we compare accuracies of chemical and general-purpose FMs on tasks from various areas of chemistry. Strikingly, general-purpose GPT-6 Astra outperforms the currently eligible chemical FMs on five physicochemical and quantum-chemical regression tasks when only 60 experimental datapoints are available. Only when provided 10x datapoints do the best chemical FMs reach performance of GPT-6 Astra: on 1,000 and 10,000 points they show performance on par with Astra on 60 and 1,000 points, respectively. Thus, counterintuitively, frontier general-purpose FMs are better suited for guiding chemical research in data-scarce areas than specialized chemical FMs, suggesting that learning relevant primitives (e.g. chemical structures) does not substitute training on relevant humankind knowledge.

items.title: Automated Keyword Generation Using LLMs in a High-Volume Data Virtualization Service
items.abstract: In modern data infrastructure, a data virtualization service (DVS) allows users to create many versions of source datasets for different processing tasks. For example, a multivariate or multi-modality dataset can be used for different machine learning tasks (e.g., classification, detection, segmentation, forecasting, and so on). Data selection, participation, integration, and preprocessing in different tasks result in many virtual datasets [Khan et al., SSC 2026]. Meanwhile, different users need to discover existing virtual datasets frequently and easily to avoid duplicate efforts. To enable an effective search engine in a DVS, it is desirable to automatically generate keywords for each virtual dataset. In this work, we present a solution for generating keywords for virtual datasets using large language models (LLMs). We propose five strategies for selecting different collections of text data for processing by the LLMs. We applied the five strategies to virtual datasets created in five application case studies with different source datasets. We conducted experiments with three LLM generators and two embedding techniques. The experiments show that the performances of the five strategies depend on the quality of the text descriptions. The results help us adopt a multi-strategy implementation of a new keyword generation service (KGS) as part of an extended DVS. The work demonstrates that the capability of automated keyword generation is indispensable for a high-volume DVS that is dataset-rich and frequently accessed.

items.title: Fuzzy selective state model for forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences
items.abstract: We consider forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences of retail chain customers. A customer's preference is described by a triangular fuzzy number. The evolution of the preference over time is governed by a Mamba-type selective state space model whose hidden state is a triangular number, with computations carried out in M.G.~Matveev's two-component algebra of fuzzy numbers. The recurrence parameters are computed from crisp features, while the fuzzy part of the model remains linear with non-negative coefficients. We show that the state then always remains a proper triangular number and is a convex combination of past observations, so that the fuzziness of the forecast does not accumulate over time and the algebraic computations coincide with Zadeh's extension principle. On a synthetic example with competitor promotions and customer switching, a lightweight 107-parameter model reaches a mean absolute error of the forecast centre of 0.154 versus 0.163 for the constant-inertia evolution operator and 0.179 for the naive forecast, matches a crisp model of the same architecture and additionally provides a linguistically interpretable estimate of forecast vagueness. We also show how the linguistic readout of the forecast can be used to detect a permanent switch of a customer to a competitor.

items.title: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality
items.abstract: Job applicants increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to write cover letters, while employers deploy LLMs to screen them. In this all-AI setting, we ask whether the \emph{choice of model} affects hiring outcomes independently of candidate qualifications. We introduce a multi-model auditing framework pairing eleven LLM writer agents with nine API-hosted evaluator agents across ten job descriptions and fifty candidates per job. Four findings emerge. First, we identify a generative preference hierarchy: a consistent global ranking of writer models by evaluator acceptance, in which locally hosted models are systematically disadvantaged regardless of their license, compounded by self-preference bias where evaluators favour their own outputs. Second, evaluator models differ substantially in how much bias they introduce based on applicants' tool choice, offering actionable guidance for fairer screening design. Third, this hierarchy has measurable competitive consequences: in the most adverse pairing, approximately two (1.8) out of twenty-five qualified candidates are filtered out purely due to model mismatch. Fourth, a common mechanism explains the patterns above: writer preference and self-preference trace to a combination of how much each writer leans on specific stylistic cues and how strongly evaluators, often unanimously, reward or penalise those same cues. A further check finds little evidence that an unmeasured "writer fingerprint" remains once these same features are accounted for. We discuss implications for algorithmic fairness in employment, regulation of AI-assisted screening, and the design of auditing frameworks that can be reapplied as the model landscape evolves.

items.title: Learning to Interact and Direct: Co-Evolving Video Director Agents
items.abstract: Video director agents orchestrate multistage production to realize users' creative visions. Emerging research on their self-evolution advances screenplay planning effectively. However, the mutual reinforcement between directing and user interaction remains largely overlooked. Improved interaction clarifies user intent and informs workflow refinement, while more reliable execution shifts collaboration from troubleshooting to creative decisions. To this end, we introduce LIT (Learning to Interact and DirecT), a framework comprises a director agent, a simulated user, and a meta engineer. Simulated user assigns creative tasks to probe the director's weaknesses, while the meta engineer uses the task traces to revise the director's interaction and production strategy. Although this approach can address discovered interaction and production issues, it still relies on passive attribution by the meta agent. This limits its ability to adapt to broader user interaction patterns and production techniques. To solve this problem, we equip LIT with a co-evolution paradigm. The meta agent proactively learns external knowledge, thereby improving its ability to discover problems and propose solutions. The meta agent, simulated user, and director together form an evolutionary closed loop, collaboratively enhances the system's directing and interaction capabilities. Across the Test and OOD Test splits, LIT improves production and Interaction scores by 19.1% and 32.0%, respectively, relative to the initial pipeline. Controlled ablations reveal the correlation between improvements in production and interaction, where the co-evolution mechanism further encourage directing skill and interaction mode exploration.

items.title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
items.abstract: Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents often use GUS-style architectures with separate modules for intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response generation. While faithful to the underlying XAI methods, these pipelines are hard to adapt and often struggle with context-dependent follow-up questions. We present SimXAI, a lightweight LLM-centric conversational layer that replaces these modules with a single tool-calling LLM that bridges access to existing XAI resources. Rather than a standalone agent, SimXAI serves as a modular interface that enables conversational access to external XAI resources. We further introduce an evaluation suite for single- and multi-turn parsing, faithfulness, and contextualization. Across existing and new datasets, SimXAI achieves strong function-selection accuracy and high faithfulness while better handling context-dependent requests. In a user study replacing only the conversational layer of TalkToModel, a representative GUS-based agent, users completed tasks more accurately and in fewer turn. Overall, SimXAI improves GUS-based design while preserving faithfulness and improving conversational quality.

items.title: Dynamical Memory Transformer: Selective Recurrent Memories with Constant Cost Attention
items.abstract: Transformers retain an explicit history of the sequence, allowing attention to directly retrieve past representations. However, the size of the KV-Cache and the cost of a new token increase with the context length. State Space Models compress the past into a fixed-size recurrent state, at the cost of reduced addressability. We present the Dynamical Memory Transformer (DMT), a hybrid architecture that separates sequence encoding from information reading. The encoder uses several memory units, each implemented by a dynamical system with a complex diagonal recurrent matrix. An input-dependent leak rate controls their updates. The decoder then uses attention to read and combine their outputs, without going through the token history. The formulation of the recurrence allows an associative scan with O(T ) total work and O(log T ) parallel depth, with fixed dimensions. During autoregressive inference, the recurrent states and the convolution cache remain fixed in size. We compare DMT with Mamba and Transformer on cognitive and language modeling tasks, and show its strengths and limitations: DMT achieves the best results on several cognitive tasks and language modeling performance close to that of Transformer, but remains behind Mamba in language modeling. On selective copy, DMT also shows stronger length extrapolation than Mamba and Transformer. These results demonstrate that parallel dynamical memory units are a promising mechanism for retaining and using information over sequences.

items.title: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024
items.abstract: We develop ReuScope, a protocol for auditing data reuse and evaluation sensitivity, using Capsule Vision 2024 as a case study. It combines measurements of data relationships with two comparisons: changing the evaluation population while holding predictions fixed, and changing training data while holding evaluation fixed. Byte-identical files cross the public training-validation boundary, and all 41 Kvasir-Capsule recordings that contribute frames occur in both partitions. Shared source recordings establish cross-split overlap; missing cross-recording patient identifiers prevent counting unique shared patients. Across ten paired seeds, removing all training rows attributed to Kvasir-Capsule, plus five rows from other sources flagged as near-matches to it, lowers public-validation balanced accuracy from 82.5% to 61.2%. Evaluating the same fitted models on the validation rows of the other sources reverses the comparison: removal improves balanced accuracy by 1.38 percentage points. The public-validation drop measures sensitivity to source removal, not an amount of leakage-induced inflation. Matched controls show that sample size and class counts alone do not explain the observed score differences. An exploratory experiment removes the training neighbors of validation frames that have close training matches, or equally many distant training rows, and yields a difference-in-differences estimate, relative to matched unflagged frames, of -0.355 percentage points in true-class probability; the paired-t interval for accuracy spans zero. The resulting procedure distinguishes observed reuse from conditional performance sensitivity and specifies the population, class support and uncertainty unit for each conclusion.

items.title: RECAST: REconstruction of Chain-of-Thought via Auditable Structured Traces
items.abstract: Large closed-source reasoning models expose only their final answers. The intermediate reasoning that produces those answers is hidden behind API surfaces, tool-call policies, and safety filters. Existing chain-of-thought (CoT) extraction methods assume a side channel: a visible reasoning field, a scratchpad carried through tool calls, or a signed/encrypted reasoning block. We reproduce three representative state-of-the-art extraction methods and find that, on Claude-Sonnet-5.5 accessed through the standard chat-completions interface, all three return zero CoT tokens. The failure is structural rather than a bug: the reasoning field is absent, named tool selection is rejected, free-text scratchpad arguments are filtered, and no replayable reasoning block is exposed. We therefore take a different route. We present RECAST, a reconstruction-based framework that conditions a decoder on the question and the target model's final answer, reconstructs a first-person structured rationale, cleans it, and builds SFT-ready data. To the best of our knowledge, RECAST is the first system to reconstruct CoT from frontier closed models such as Claude-Sonnet-5.5, GPT-6.1, and Gemini 3 without using hidden reasoning channels. We instantiate RECAST on Claude-Sonnet-5.5 and additionally obtain successful qualitative reconstructions on GPT-6.1 and Gemini 3 with the same answer-only protocol. The system is open-source and packaged as an agent skill: one prompt deploys it and runs the complete pipeline to produce SFT-ready CoT data. This preprint describes the system, its threat model, and a controlled artifact validation; it does not claim large-scale benchmark improvements.

items.title: Backpropagation-free Deep Learning for Time-Series Classification
items.abstract: Deep neural networks for time series classification (TSC) are trained almost exclusively by error backpropagation, which imposes update locking and the weight-transport problem. Backpropagation-free learning rules such as Direct Feedback Alignment (DFA), Direct Random Target Projection (DRTP), and the diffusion-inspired NoProp relax these constraints but have been evaluated almost exclusively on 2D image benchmarks. We adapt these three learners to univariate TSC with 1D convolutional architectures and present the first systematic study of them across 112 datasets from the UCR time series archive, with one hyperparameter-optimized configuration per method. The optimized learners reach mean F1 scores of 0.76 to 0.79, below ROCKET (0.83) and InceptionTime (0.84). We propose an analysis framework that relates the per-dataset gap to InceptionTime to dataset properties and tests convolutional feature learning by replacing the flatten readout with global average pooling, measured as a difference-in-differences (DD) against a backpropagation control on the identical architecture. Intra-class temporal variability is the dataset property most consistently associated with the gap for all three learners (partial Spearman $ρ$ from $0.28$ to $0.40$). Pooling harms DFA and DRTP more than backpropagation (DD $-0.025$ and $-0.055$), consistent with near-random convolutional features, whereas NoProp tolerates pooling as backpropagation does (DD $+0.013$). Relative to backpropagation on the same architectures, DRTP reduces training floating-point operations (FLOPs) by 33% and trains faster only on series longer than about 700 time steps, DFA yields no computational reduction, and NoProp reduces peak memory by 38% at the cost of 48% longer training.

items.title: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks
items.abstract: Physicians read electrocardiograms (ECGs) from waveform shape and timing, yet accurate deep-learning classifiers rarely show which waveform regions drive their predictions. We introduce LYNX-ECG, a graph neural network that represents each heartbeat as a sparse visibility graph of timestamped turning points. On CODE-Test, LYNX-ECG reaches a macro F1 score of 0.889, outperforming five baselines including the ECGFounder foundation model, while its graphs need about 14% of the storage of graphs built from every sample. Because each node maps to a specific ECG time, we can delete clinically defined waveform regions and alter beat timing to audit predictions. For conduction disorders, the clinically expected region was the strongest evidence in more than 90% of correct predictions. Bradycardia and tachycardia calls follow heart rate with conduction intervals held fixed, and atrial fibrillation calls vanish when beat-to-beat variation is removed. Sparse visibility graphs thus pair accurate ECG classification with clinically grounded, testable explanations.

items.title: Whose Values, Which Contexts, and What Signals? Grounding Cultural Value Alignment with Re3Culture
items.abstract: Cultural value alignment requires not only model optimization but also a well-specified target grounded in real-human evidence. Yet how such targets should be grounded in human data remains largely unexplored, raising three fundamental questions: (1) whose values should be represented? (2) where should cultural values be observed? and (3) what signals reveal underlying values? We investigate these questions through Re3Culture, a large-scale dataset linking (i) Representative communities: 700+ human participants across four cultures recruited through cultural-affiliation screening and demographic-aware sampling; (ii) Realistic scenario: culturally sensitive scenarios selected by community members, e.g., family and kinship; and (iii) Revealed value signals: 1,400+ value surveys, 20,000+ topic-grounded behavioral principles and explicit value priorities with responses for 6,000+ situated questions. Our analysis shows why these choices matter for defining the target, with three implications. First, estimating cultural values requires both community affiliation and broad internal coverage. Substituting other cultures or restricting subgroup coverage shifts value estimates. LLM simulations also disproportionately reflect particular subgroups. Second, values must be observed in concrete, community-guided situations. Abstract questionnaire profiles weakly recover situated priorities, and communities differ in which scenarios they identify as culturally value-revealing. Third, value priorities should be elicited explicitly, not learned from response preferences or bottom-line answers alone. Preferences conflate value agreement with other response-level qualities, and similar answers can be derived from different value priorities. By addressing these requirements, Re3Culture provides the first human-grounded resource that explicitly informs target definition for cultural value alignment.

items.title: Implicit Assumptions About Tasks in Continual Learning
items.abstract: Continual learning is the study of how a model accumulates knowledge from data received over time, rather than all at once. In practice, this is typically achieved by dividing a dataset into tasks and presenting them sequentially. Explanations of the resulting measurements take into account factors such as the similarity between segments, the rate at which the data changes and the order of presentation. Each of these factors can be defined in terms of the underlying data, the partition imposed on it, or the learner that encounters it. These levels do not necessarily coincide, and it is usually left implicit which level a reported quantity refers to. We separate these and identify which properties acquire a value at each level. In controlled teacher--student experiments, we demonstrate that partitioning the same underlying trajectory at different levels of granularity, changing the order of presentation, and varying the similarity structure of the underlying data all result in different measured outcomes. We review representative benchmarks to determine which of these properties are stated. Where the underlying data cannot be inspected, as in foundation models built on undisclosed pre-training corpora, its properties are inherited by the model's initial state, and the training applied on top of it can be described.

items.title: Different Models, Shared Failures: Auditing Frozen-Encoder Pools for Medical Segmentation
items.abstract: Average segmentation accuracy and model count do not reveal whether models fail on the same cases. We present CoFailMed, an audit of correlated failures in pretrained-encoder pools for medical segmentation. Across five 2D tasks, we evaluate 11 public pretrained encoders (a controlled sample, not a census) using frozen features and separately trained $1\times 1$ readouts with four seeds per encoder. Shared-checkpoint pairs have the highest mean per-case Dice correlation. An expanded 17-encoder analysis shows that distinct checkpoints within the same encoder family remain more correlated than cross-family pairs. At the pooled 33rd-percentile Dice threshold, four-member pools drawn from distinct encoders have mean effective sizes of 1.56-2.92, estimated from failure correlations in pools with enough failures and passes per member. In the primary pool, richer readouts and fine-tuning narrow the Dice-correlation gap between pairs sharing a checkpoint (or the DINOv2-B/S release) and all other pairs. Yet dependence between different encoders can increase, and fine-tuning does not consistently increase effective pool size at 33rd-percentile thresholds recomputed for each training recipe. A smaller between-group gap can coexist with greater dependence. Pool evaluation should therefore report absolute dependence and threshold-specific effective size alongside accuracy and nominal pool size. The CoFailMed release provides aligned per-case traces, analysis scripts and study code to reproduce the central audit results.

items.title: Clinical-Protocol-Aware Cyber Resilience for Connected Clinical Technologies Under AI-Enabled Adversarial Conditions
items.abstract: Healthcare increasingly relies on connected medical devices, clinical information systems, cloud services, and distributed-care technologies, creating cybersecurity risks across clinical workflows. AI-enabled capabilities can accelerate vulnerability discovery and attack-path analysis, increasing the need to limit compromise propagation. This paper proposes a clinical-protocol-aware cyber-resilience framework based on bounded clinical micro-networks and controlled interconnections. The framework integrates clinical factors into cybersecurity design, management, and evaluation, covering prevention, containment, and incident response. A parameterized Monte Carlo simulation distinguishes technical cyber exposure from modeled clinical consequence. Experiments investigate architectural connectivity, adversarial capability, security controls, protocol dependency, risk alignment, communication directionality, lifecycle integration, and response timing. Under the simulation assumptions, connected architecture increases mean cyber exposure by 56.3% relative to segmented architecture, while combined prevention and containment reduce exposure by 60.1% relative to no controls. Increasing protocol dependency raises the modeled clinical-impact index from 1.021 to 7.567 without changing mean cyber exposure, demonstrating that technical exposure and clinical consequence can diverge. Risk-alignment experiments further indicate higher modeled clinical impact when greater technical risk corresponds to greater clinical significance. The findings support comparative architectural analysis, not calibrated estimates of real-world cyber risk, control effectiveness, or patient harm. The framework provides a clinical-context-aware approach to security-boundary design, control prioritization, and coordinated containment in connected healthcare environments.

items.title: MERIDIAN: Memory-Encoded Rituals for Intimacy across Distance in an Interactive, Asynchronous Neighbourhood
items.abstract: How can shared memories become playable structures for partners who live in different time zones? We present MERIDIAN, a pre-deployment design case of Yi Town, a bilingual browser game developed by one member of a long-distance couple as a gift for the other. Nine levels translate personally meaningful events, places and cultural references into tasks within a navigable pixel town. A birthday prologue and a fictional wedding frame the intended experience. Drawing on research through design, we reconstruct four design changes from 109 development commits, 28 changelog versions and three design specifications. These records support six situated design commitments, including memory-derived mechanics, staged access, local progress storage and bilingual coverage. The implementation combines a union-based progress model with manually exchanged, checksummed codes and time-zone-dependent scenery. An implementation audit reproduced 153 passing unit tests and examined all 1,024 canonical progress codes, while identifying limits involving resets, unversioned level registries and residual transcription errors. The application has no author-operated backend for progress, but external media services and browser speech recognition limit its privacy and offline guarantees. No recipient evaluation or relationship outcomes are reported. The contribution is an inspectable account of design decisions and their trade-offs, including the tension between authoring a personal gift and preserving the recipient's freedom to interpret, decline or reshape it. The game is playable at https://jingyifan.love and its source is public at https://github.com/rayford295/yi-town.

items.title: Hyperbolic embedding of higher-order simplicial networks
items.abstract: Many biological interactions involve groups rather than pairs, as when several proteins assemble into a multi-protein complex. Simplicial complexes naturally capture these collective interactions. Existing hyperbolic embeddings represent network hierarchy and similarity through a few interpretable coordinates, but rely only on pairwise links: they cannot distinguish three units engaged in a common interaction from three units connected only in pairs. We introduce here the hyperbolic higher-order (HHO) embedding, which embeds a simplicial complex into the Poincaré disk, while incorporating its group interactions. The hyperbolic area of the triangle spanned by three interacting nodes then measures how compactly their interaction is represented. Testson synthetic and real-world networks, including a co-authorship network and the protein interaction network of \textit{Escherichia coli}, show that HHO reduces the hyperbolic area of triangles representing simplices relative to those obtained from pairwise network embeddings. HHO also recovers node groups more accurately than pairwise embeddings and a weighted-clique alternative, with performance competitive with Euclidean embeddings, while providing a low-dimensional representation that can be analyzed with the tools of network geometry.

items.title: Transmission and filtering of stochastic rhythms in bursty gene expression
items.abstract: How stochastic rhythms in upstream regulatory signals are transmitted to downstream gene expression is a fundamental question in systems biology. Although experiments have shown that molecular degradation strongly influences downstream rhythmic responses, a general quantitative theory explaining how degradation, stochastic bursting, and upstream timing variability jointly govern rhythm transmission remains lacking. Here we develop a general analytical framework based on a martingale-based orthogonal decomposition, applicable to arbitrarily complex upstream dynamics, including memory effects. We derive exact autocorrelation and power-spectrum transmission laws, establish an oscillation-efficiency contraction principle, and identify a critical degradation rate that provides a necessary and sufficient condition for stochastic rhythm transmission. An explicit rhythm-transmission relation reveals that increasing burst frequency and modulation depth promotes rhythm transmission, whereas greater variability in upstream cycle duration suppresses it. In particular, increasing burst size leaves oscillation efficiency unchanged. The predicted degradation threshold correctly separates all ten pulsing and nonpulsing p53 target proteins reported in previous experiments. These results provide a theoretical foundation for understanding how cells selectively preserve or integrate rhythmic regulatory signals.

items.title: Distinguishing N$_2$-Dominated from O$_2$-Dominated Atmospheres on Terrestrial Exoplanets with Reflected-Light Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Reflected-light spectra of Earth-sized exoplanets promise to probe habitability and biosignatures, but interpreting atmospheric oxygen can be challenging because $O_2$ can arise from both biological and abiotic processes. In addition, reflected-light retrievals exhibit degeneracies among atmospheric composition, clouds, surface reflectance, and gravity. We use the Bayesian retrieval framework ExoReL$^\Re$, leveraging recent model developments that incorporate (i) $O_2$-$O_2$ collision-induced absorption (CIA), which produces the $O_4$ bands, and (ii) a wavelength-dependent (step-function) surface albedo parameterization. Focusing on a modern Earth analog, we compare retrievals with and without $O_2$-$O_2$ CIA using spectra within 0.25-1.8 $μ$m, and perform signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) sweeps for two observing configurations motivated by the Habitable Worlds Observatory: a resolved-visible case ($R_{VIS}=140$) and a broadband-visible case (three broad bins). Omitting $O_2$-$O_2$ CIA allows the retrieval to fit the spectrum with an incorrect $O_2$-dominated atmosphere. Including $O_2$-$O_2$ CIA leverages the $O_4$ bands to break this degeneracy and recover the correct $N_2$-dominated, $O_2$-rich solution without requiring a tight mass prior. Adopting a robustness criterion of $\ge95\%$ posterior mass in the $N_2$-dominated region, both configurations require SNR $\gtrsim20$ at 0.75 $μ$m (SNR $\approx14$ near the 1.27 $μ$m $O_4$ band for $R_{NIR}=70$) to identify the correct dominant gas, with higher cloud fraction increasing this threshold. Reducing near-IR coverage to 1.4 $μ$m prevents recovery of the correct $N_2$-dominated solution across the explored SNR range, and instead favors a spurious $O_2$-dominated, $CO_2$-rich atmosphere. These results support near-IR coverage to $\sim1.7$ $μ$m and SNR $\gtrsim20$ at 0.75 $μ$m for robust oxygen interpretation on Earth-like planets.

items.title: An end-to-end CNN search for ultra-short-period planets in TESS: from the blend ceiling to the independent validation of TOI-6662 b
items.abstract: We trained a convolutional neural network to detect ultra-short-period planets in TESS photometry, following the procedure now standard in the field: synthetic transits as positives, eclipsing binaries as negatives. Measured that way it reaches an area under the ROC curve of 0.97. Keeping the same model and the same planets, but replacing the negatives with false positives that the TESS Follow-up Observing Program has actually rejected, the area falls to 0.50 -- the value of a random classifier. The conventional benchmark had been measuring a problem that does not exist. The reason is physical, and it bounds what is possible. Of 145 such false positives examined at pixel level, 42% are blends: eclipses belonging to a neighbouring star, diluted into the target aperture. Their light curves are indistinguishable from shallow transits, capping the attainable area at 1 - f/2 = 0.79. Retraining on real false positives reaches 0.80 +/- 0.06, confirming the ceiling independently. No classifier reading a single-band light curve can do better. A detector alone is the wrong instrument. We built CASCADE-USP, a pipeline chaining the network with difference-image centroid analysis, scene modelling with high-resolution imaging and the Gaia astrometric solution, supplying in sequence what the light curve lacks. Its output is a prioritisation, not a verdict: it records what evidence each candidate still needs. Only the classifier is domain-specific; the other stages apply to any transit candidate. Of 435 unresolved TESS candidates it isolates 20; 19 prove false positives, traced to causes invisible in TESS photometry. The twentieth is TOI-6662 b, an Earth-sized planet (0.94 +/- 0.03 Earth radii) orbiting an M dwarf every 7.05 hours. Our validation, independent of a concurrent one, agrees with it in planetary parameters and classification, closing the CASCADE procedure with an external check.

items.title: Combinatorial Calculations of the Most Probable Short-term Return of Single Company Stocks on the Stock Market
items.abstract: The combinatorial method is used to calculate the quantity of distribution variants for the number of stockholders of one individual company as well as the quantity of stocks in the stockholder portfolio. These quantities may change as a result of the stocks buy and sale that is taken into account also. The total number of stocks the units at the lower level of the problem is obviously preserved, while the number of portfolios - the structural units at the upper level may change. The most probable distributions of the number of portfolios and stocks in each of them are determined depending on the expense to add a stock to the portfolio (the purchase price). The application of the developed method to determine the most probable short term return on stocks in a combinatorial sense is demonstrated.

items.title: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta
items.abstract: Presolar graphite grains with supernova isotopic signatures provide direct evidence that large graphite grains formed in supernova ejecta. However, theoretical calculations of dust formation in supernovae have typically predicted graphite grains smaller than $0.1\,{\rm μm}$, leaving unclear the physical conditions required to form those grains with radii of order $1\,{\rm μm}$. We systematically investigate graphite nucleation and growth in expanding supernova ejecta by varying the explosion energy, ejecta mass, initial ejecta radius, and ejected $^{56}$Ni mass. We use a simplified one-zone model that follows the temperature and density evolution including adiabatic cooling, radiative cooling, and heating by radioactive nickel. We show that the final graphite grain size is mainly determined by the product of the mass density of atomic carbon available for grain growth and the local cooling timescale, both evaluated at a reference temperature of $2000\,{\rm K}$. Our models show that graphite growth is favored by lower explosion energy, larger ejecta mass, and smaller initial ejecta radius, which keep the gas denser near the graphite-condensation temperature. When radioactive heating and radiative cooling are included, explosions with $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{50}\,{\rm erg}$ and $M_{\rm Ni}\lesssim10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ can form $1$-$10\,μ{\rm m}$ graphite grains in the ejected helium layer or carbon-oxygen core, whereas $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ models do not. These results suggest that micron-sized presolar supernova graphite preferentially forms in faint-supernova-like explosions with low explosion energies, little ejected nickel, and helium layer or carbon-oxygen core ejecta.

items.title: Current Sheets and Magnetic Reconnection statistics by Solar Orbiter at few to tens of Ion Inertial Lengths I: Energy Dissipation
items.abstract: In this work, we study the turbulent origin of ion-scale Current Sheets (CSs) and the dissipation of energy via magnetic reconnection. We analyze 103 hours of high-cadence (4 samples/s) in-situ ion data from Solar Orbiter, collected between July 2020 and September 2022. We apply an automatic detection algorithm that finds current sheets (CSs) of thickness (length in the normal direction, $λ$) near the ion inertial length ($δ_i$), and classifies them as Alfvénic or reconnecting. We compile a catalog of 974 CSs of thickness in the range of few to 90 ion inertial lengths, of which 53 contain an ion reconnection jet. We estimate that Solar Orbiter spends $\sim 1 \%$ of the dwell time inside a CS of few to 90 $δ_i$ thickness, and 0.06\% inside a reconnecting CS of the same thickness range. By comparing these results with previous studies we estimate that the abundance of CSs and of Reconnecting CSs evolves with heliocentric distance ($r$) as $r^{-0.9}$ and $r^{-1.5}$, respectively. We estimate that magnetic reconnection dissipates $ε_{rec}\sim 30 \hspace{5pt} \text{J} \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-1},$ in the $\sim 1 - 40$ $δ_i$ scale-range, by assessing the amount of plasma that interacts with a reconnection exhaust. We show how the dissipation of turbulence energy cascade by magnetic reconnection at scales smaller than 90 $δ_i$ is more effective closer to the Sun, and decays as $r^{-3.6}$. The current density of Alfvénic CSs thicker than the ion inertial length presents scale invariance, obeying $J_0/J_A=0.9(λ/2δ_i)^{-0.71}$, suggesting that CSs generated locally from solar wind turbulence.

items.title: Recommendation Feedback Loops Shape Urban Income Segregation and Venue Visitation
items.abstract: Location-based recommender systems shape where people go in cities and learn from the visits they steer, forming a human-AI feedback loop. This feedback loop shapes whom people share places with across income groups and which venues keep attracting customers. Yet platforms judge these systems by their offline accuracy on past visits, a test in which the suggestions never change where people go and which therefore cannot capture long-term effects. Studying these effects in cities is challenging because, unlike online resources, travel constraints and limited venue capacity shape where people can go, while each recommended visit also changes whom other visitors encounter. To capture such features, we build a long-term simulation framework based on fine-grained human mobility data from four U.S. metropolitan areas, with distance and capacity constraints. Focusing on food venues, we study two urban consequences: how unevenly people's exposure is distributed across income groups (experienced income segregation) and the share of venues receiving no visits from simulated residents (venue disappearance). We find that, under every algorithm and in every metropolitan area, at least a fifth of venues stop receiving visits, and that more than half of this loss arises from retraining. More importantly, more accurate algorithms leave people more segregated, and the most accurate algorithm leaves people 15-21% more segregated than they actually are. We then test a re-ranking intervention that favours less popular venues and runs on top of a platform's existing algorithm. It lowers both venue disappearance and segregation across algorithms, largely without directing people to venues where they may feel less comfortable. Our results suggest that impact assessments of recommender systems should account for the feedback loop and report segregation and venue disappearance beyond accuracy.

items.title: Resonant Amplification of Demographic Noise in Stochastic Common-Pool Resource Dynamics
items.abstract: Common-pool resources are vulnerable to overexploitation, yet many social-ecological systems exhibit persistent oscillations. We introduce a stochastic eco-evolutionary model in which harvesting strategies and resource availability shape one another. In the infinite population limit the system approaches a stable state through damped oscillations. Demographic noise continually excites these modes, generating instead robust macroscopic quasi-cycles, whose frequencies depend on the noise ratio, the relative timescale between strategy and resource, and the harvesting pressure. The model reproduces the distinct frequency peaks, observed in empirical global fish-landings data for high- and low-income countries, showing that persistent environmental fluctuations can emerge naturally from demographic noise.

items.title: From Anoxic to Oxic Earth: Detectability of Atmospheric Biosignatures across Stellar Hosts with ELT/ANDES
items.abstract: Earth's atmosphere evolved from an anoxic, methane-bearing Archean state through Proterozoic oxygenation to the O$_2$-rich modern atmosphere. However, most biosignature detectability studies focus on modern Earth, leaving earlier atmospheric states comparatively unexplored. We investigate how atmospheric evolution and stellar environments influence the detectability of O$_2$, CH$_4$, H$_2$O, and CO$_2$, and their potential to distinguish anoxic from oxygenated atmospheres. We construct two complementary photochemical grids: representative Archean, Proterozoic, and modern-Earth scenarios around the Sun, and four geological epochs (3.9, 2.0, 0.8 Ga, and modern Earth) across FGKM hosts. Combining one-dimensional photochemical modeling, high-resolution transmission spectral simulations, and instrument-noise modeling, we assess molecular detectability with ELT/ANDES under optimistic photon-noise-limited conditions. For solar-host Archean and Proterozoic models, CH$_4$ requires approximately 33 and 42 transits, respectively, to reach the adopted 5$σ$ criterion, whereas O$_2$ remains below 3$σ$ within the observing limits. Modern-Earth O$_2$ reaches 3$σ$ after approximately 38 transits. Across the FGKM grid, O$_2$ does not reach 5$σ$ for the 3.9 Ga models. However, For the M3V, K2V, and M8V proxies, modern-Earth O$_2$ reaches 5$σ$ in 9, 15, and 20 transits, respectively, whereas CH$_4$ requires 11, 12, and 28 transits at 3.9 Ga and only 2--4 transits across the oxygenated epochs. These results reveal a strong O$_2$ detectability contrast around M and K-dwarfs, but not Sun-like hosts in the YJH bands. Robust biosignature interpretation requires complementary molecular constraints, including informative non-detections, within the context of atmospheric evolution and stellar environment.

items.title: Why delivered costs understate prices in an integrated global hydrogen market
items.abstract: Delivered-cost estimates are often used as proxies for hydrogen import prices. Yet they measure average supply-chain costs, whereas marginal prices measure the system value of an additional unit. Market interactions can make the two diverge, potentially biasing long-term price assumptions. We quantify this gap using an 81-region global hydrogen-market model, comparing each region's costs and prices when only its demand is active and when all regions' demands are active. The 2045 price-cost gap is positive in 78 regions and averages 63 EUR/MWh (52% of the single-buyer cost) on a demand-weighted basis. Only 12 EUR/MWh reflects higher average sourcing costs due to competing demand. The remaining 51 EUR/MWh is the difference between the global-market price and the delivered portfolio's average cost. In several regions, wholesale prices rise while average delivered costs fall. Hydrogen strategies should distinguish delivered-cost benchmarks from market-price expectations, as low-cost supply does not guarantee low regional market prices.

items.title: Understanding LLM-Based Bargaining of Driving Agents in Mixed-Autonomy Traffic
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a flexible computational approach for modeling social interactions among heterogeneous agents. This paper develops a novel framework towards characterizing and understanding LLM-based population-level bargaining of shared road space between autonomous vehicle (AV) and human-driven vehicle (HV) agents in mixed-autonomy traffic. Through controlled experiments varying traffic density, agent objectives, and traffic-domain knowledge, we first characterize bargaining outcomes and observe heterogeneous agreement rates across different experimental conditions. To understand how the bargaining process shapes the outcomes, we introduce a behavioral taxonomy that jointly characterizes numerical bidding actions and communicative attitudes. We examine two complementary aspects of social interaction: inter-agent bargaining dynamics and private-to-public behavioral transformation. Results reveal distinct interaction patterns associated with agreement and breakdown, including greater constructive reciprocity in agreement trials and more frequent conflict escalation in breakdown trials. Furthermore, private and public communicative attitudes often differ even when numerical bids remain unchanged. These findings illustrate how LLM-based bargaining simulations can support a structured analysis of social interaction behaviors in mixed-autonomy traffic.

items.title: Terminal-state theorems for a two-stage Maki--Thompson rumor model: final size, stifler composition, and non-identifiability from pooled statistics
items.abstract: Rumor models of the Daley--Kendall and Maki--Thompson family anchor the statistical mechanics of social contagion, yet the stifler composition a rumor leaves behind has resisted closed-form analysis. Inspired by the asymmetric two-step pairing (A2SP) process of step-growth polymerization, we import its common-factor cancellation into a minimal two-stage MT variant in which re-contacted spreaders are re-activated into a senior class at rate $αk_1$ rather than stifled, and obtain exact terminal-state theorems. (i) Saturation: the rumor exhausts the ignorant pool for every stifling-to-recruitment ratio $μ>0$, with a three-way tail classification and a logarithmically critical line at $μ=1$. (ii) Final size: the terminal stifler pool splits as $(x_1,x_2)=(μ/(α+μ),α/(α+μ))$, independent of seed size; the fingerprint inverts linearly ($α=μx_2/x_1$) and matches Gillespie simulations within $0.95\%$. (iii) Pooled versus history-resolved: pooled statistics are exactly $α$-free on any static graph; only the history-resolved composition carries $α$. Restoring the classic teller-retires channel breaks the exact closure beyond quantified gates (contact rates of $1$--$3\%$ of $k_1$ for spreader channels at $μ\leq1.5$, up to $32\%$ at $μ=2$), and on configuration-model networks the composition bias decays as $\langle k\rangle^{-0.71}$. An exploratory inversion of 354,930 Higgs--Twitter retweet episodes, screened by an identity check and four negative controls, yields $\hatα=2.21\%$ (joint cluster-bootstrap CI $[1.6\%,3.0\%]$; $\approx3.7\%$ after calibration at the matched threshold). Terminal compositions identify this effective re-activation rate, an upper bound on contact-coupled re-activation; the mechanism itself requires timing information beyond the terminal state.

items.title: Entropy-based classification of core-collapse supernova gravitational waves for nuclear equation-of-state inference
items.abstract: Abstract Gravitational waves from core-collapse supernovae provide a unique probe of the physical processes occurring during stellar collapse and of the properties of dense nuclear matter. In this work we investigate the classification of supernova gravitational-wave signals associated with different nuclear equations of state using an entropy-based machine learning framework. The analysis combines signal decomposition, feature extraction, and feature selection techniques to identify informative characteristics of the waveforms and distinguish between different equation of state models. We evaluate the performance of several machine learning classifiers using a compact set of selected features and assess their robustness in the presence of detector noise. We find that entropy-based representations capture the underlying differences between waveform classes and enable accurate classification while maintaining better performance compared to raw data under noisy conditions. These results demonstrate the potential of complexity-based feature extraction as an efficient and interpretable approach for gravitational wave studies of core-collapse supernovae.

items.title: From ASTRID to BRAHMA – The role of overmassive black holes in little red dots in cosmological simulations
items.abstract: We investigate the origin of Little Red Dots (LRDs) using a realization of the BRAHMA cosmological hydrodynamic simulation that produces overmassive black holes at z ∼ 4 - 8 . We generate mock JWST observations by modeling galaxy spectral energy distributions (including dust attenuation) together with AGN emission using cloudy-based templates, and test whether such systems reproduce the observed LRD population. We consider both a standard low-redshift AGN emission model and a gas-enshrouded AGN emission model, in which the AGN is embedded within unresolved dense gas that produces a strong Balmer break, and find that LRDs emerge in significantly larger numbers with the latter model. Assuming that all AGN reside in this gas-enshrouded phase, we recover LRD number densities ( Φ ∼ 2 × 10 − 4 M p c − 3 ), close to the observed abundance. This implies an effective gas-enshrouded duty cycle approaching unity, which is not predicted by current theoretical models. Current JWST constraints on the high-z black hole mass function suggest that this tension may arise from a deficit of low-mass () LRDs in BRAHMA. Applying the same gas-enshrouded model to the ASTRID simulation, which lacks overmassive black holes, we find that the LRD abundance remains below observations. Overall, while the overmassive black holes in this BRAHMA realization substantially enhance the production of LRD-like systems, reproducing the observed LRD abundance requires them to reside in dense gas environments with unrealistically high duty cycles. We therefore conclude that overmassive black holes are unlikely to be the sole origin of the observed JWST LRD population, and may instead account for only a subset of these systems.

items.title: Doppler effect of the Milky Way rotation on mHz gravitational waves
items.abstract: The galactic background of gravitational waves (GWs) is expected to be anisotropic due to the spatial distribution and kinematics of sources in the Milky Way. In this work, we model the stellar density and velocity profiles of the Galaxy and compute the resulting GW spectrum as a function of direction. We account for the Doppler shift induced by the peculiar velocities of stars and the observer's motion. Using a Fisher matrix formalism, we forecast the ability of future detectors (e.g., LISA) to distinguish between models that include or neglect these kinematic effects. We find that if one does not take into account the rotation of the galaxy, the inference of the parameters describing the galactic background can suffer observable biases.

items.title: Horizontal magnetic fields dominate the weak-field quiet Sun in Sunrise III observations. Evidence from traditional and transformer-based inversions
items.abstract: The relative prevalence of horizontal and vertical magnetic fields in the quiet-Sun remains debated, owing to the weak linear polarisation signals that make the inferred magnetic inclination distributions sensitive to observational quality and inversion methodology. We investigate the magnetic topology of the quiet-Sun in Sunrise iii observations by independently applying transformer-based and traditional inversion techniques to the same spectropolarimetric dataset. We analysed observations obtained with the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared spectroPolarimeter (SCIP). Transformer-based inversions (SINN), trained exclusively on synthetic Stokes profiles generated from a large radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulation, were compared with independent inversions performed using the DeSIRe code. We separated the selected pixels into weak- and strong-field populations according to their circular-polarisation amplitudes. Linear polarisation exceeding 4σ is detected in 34.6% of the field of view, enabling the magnetic topology to be constrained over a substantially larger detected population than in typical short-integration Hinode observations. Both inversion methods recover a quiet-Sun magnetic topology in which the weak fields are strongly dominated by the horizontal component, whereas strong fields exhibit a substantially more balanced topology. At łogτ=-1, the median horizontal and unsigned line-of-sight field components in the weak-field population are 63 and 7 G with DeSIRe, and 60 and 6.5 G with SINN, respectively, corresponding to a horizontal-to-line-of-sight ratio of approximately nine for both methods. The agreement between the two fundamentally different optimisation methodologies indicates that the weak-field quiet-Sun in this dataset is characterised by a substantially stronger horizontal than vertical magnetic field component. These results demonstrate that transformer-based inversions can be successfully transferred from synthetic training data to real spectropolarimetric observations, while providing inference orders of magnitude faster than traditional inversion techniques.

items.title: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks
items.abstract: Humans possess a remarkable ability to draw inferences from limited data. While some inferences are made intuitively from past experience, others require online reasoning based on novel information given in context. Here, we formalize these strategies, which we term geometric and algebraic inference, and study their computational tradeoffs in humans and neural networks. The geometric strategy gradually shapes representational geometry to reflect underlying relational structure, making subsequent inference cheap. The algebraic strategy flexibly attends to and reasons over novel relations given in context, but costs additional computation at inference time. We identify opposing signatures of these two strategies in transitive inference, a domain widely studied across species, and characterize the conditions under which each is observed. Our framework predicts that the geometric strategy should be dominant when relations are familiar, whereas the algebraic should emerge to support de novo inferences drawn in context. Multiple experiments demonstrate these opposing signatures in humans, neural networks trained from scratch, and large language models (LLMs). Causal interventions in the neural networks reveal that the geometric and algebraic strategies depend on representational geometry and selective attention mechanisms, respectively, and reproduce the effects of analogous neurobiological disruptions in humans. Our framework unifies these effects with disparate phenomena, including content effects observed in human and LLM reasoning and data-distribution effects observed in machine learning. Our findings reconcile competing views of cognitive flexibility that emphasize either representational geometry or algebraic manipulation by showing that each can have unique strengths, and can characterize different aspects of both human and neural network behavior.

items.title: Siting and Curtailment Depth Limit the Grid Headroom Available to New Large Loads
items.abstract: Data center demand is increasing faster than generation can be built, encouraging proposals to interconnect large loads on condition that they reduce consumption during high-stress periods. Estimates of how much load can be added via flexibility rest on simplified accounting and report only annual curtailed electricity. Here we use a national energy systems model that co-optimizes hourly generation and load curtailment across 16 U.S. regions to characterize the flexibility and power system impacts of enabling headroom. While 50 GW can be served while curtailing less than 0.1% of its annual energy, small annual curtailment conceals potentially severe operating requirements. Most regions require curtailment deeper than 90% in at least one hour, so the load must disconnect or have sufficient on-site resources to provide full back up. Furthermore, announced data center locations are not aligned with modeled headroom and relying on existing generation fleets raises CO2 emissions and wholesale electricity prices.

items.title: HD 210058 b and BD+37 4838 b: A precessing eccentric hot Jupiter and a misaligned substellar companion around two A-type stars
items.abstract: The number of A- and F-type stars known to host exoplanets is relatively low, as is the number of planets with measured spin-orbit angle, which is the angle between the planet's orbital axis and the star's rotational axis. Expanding the sample of such systems is important for constraining the formation and migration mechanisms of close-in giant planets around early-type stars. We aim to measure the sky-projected spin-orbit angles of HD~210058b (TOI-1355b) and BD+37~4838b (TOI-1414b), two objects still listed as candidate exoplanets, and to assess the planetary nature of these systems. Both of their host stars are fast rotators. We analyzed TESS photometry together with transit time-series of HARPS-N spectra. For both objects, we created cross-correlation functions from the spectra to analyze Doppler tomography and detect and model the Doppler shadow, while we also used the photometric observations to refine a number of previously poorly constrained photometric and spectroscopic parameters of both the host stars and the companions. When possible, we used the derived results to constrain the companion masses. We verified the planetary and substellar nature for both objects respectively. We report HD~210058~b to be a giant hot Jupiter with a mass of 10 M_Jup, residing on a slightly misaligned orbit with the sky-projected spin-orbit angle λ=-32 -6 +4 deg. Archival photometry reveals continuously changing inclination and impact parameter, pointing to a nodal precession with period of 860 yr, and giving availability of only about six upcoming years for any further transit observations. The second target, BD+37~4838~b, orbits a hybrid γ~Dor-δ~Sct pulsator on a misaligned orbit with λ=56.9 +1.4 -2.3 deg. Since we could not reliably recover its mass, we only report an upper limit of approx. 24.3 M_Jup, leaving the possible planetary nature of this object unresolved.

items.title: Exploring Collaborative Debating Models for the future of science
items.abstract: AI is expanding what researchers can produce. A substantial increase in scientific output would also change how that work is organised and distributed, as earlier shifts in the scale of science have done. This paper develops a thought experiment around Collaborative Debating Models (CDMs), topic-focused environments where researchers work with AI and one another to pursue questions and maintain an evolving account of their field. Individual contributions would remain attributable as ongoing debate and further analysis change the shared account. The paper considers how journals could evolve into these gathering places and how different forms of ownership would shape scientific agendas and the support for continuing work. CDMs could connect participants to remote laboratories and other research services to conduct new studies, with shared repositories making the resulting data available for further inquiry. The proposal links expanded scientific production to collective interpretation through continuing assessment and revision, while leaving room for disciplinary differences in how contributions are reviewed and recognised.

items.title: A VLT/CRIRES+ study of helium 1.083$μ$m absorption features towards the inner Orion Nebula
items.abstract: JWST NIRCam F115W observations towards the inner Orion Nebula revealed a diverse array of previously unknown dark features. The most likely cause was absorption or suppressed emission of the helium 1.083$μ$m triplet which lies in that filter. We have obtained VLT/CRIRES+ high-resolution spectrographic observations over a selection of different dark targets, confirming that the features are indeed explained by a reduction in the flux of the helium 1.083$μ$m triplet, a reduction that is fairly uniform across the line. The Orion Nebula is a blister HII region, with a dense, bright ionised layer on the far side from the observer near the Orion A molecular cloud and lower density gas elsewhere. Using a simple radiative transfer model, we show that dark features arise when emission from the dense layer is absorbed by intermediate density helium (e.g. in clumps, globules, or winds from objects like proplyds) on the near side of the dense layer.

items.title: First-principles calculations of far-wing absorption in He-broadened CO2 infrared spectra
items.abstract: We report theoretical predictions and modeling of the far-wing absorption of CO2 broadened by He over a wide temperature range (200-1000 K), which are relevant for exoplanet atmosphere studies. Accurate modeling of He-broadened CO2 absorption is essential for opacity calculations used to characterize the composition, structure, and climate of exoplanet atmospheres. In particular, the strong CO2 band at 4.3 mum has been clearly identified in the spectra of several exoplanets observed with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Requantized classical molecular dynamics simulations were first performed to predict absorption in the far wings of the 4.3 mum band of CO2. The resulting predictions show excellent agreement with available experimental data at room temperature. The theoretical predictions and measured data were then used to parameterize an impact energy-corrected sudden model, which allowed us to accurately reproduce the far-wing absorption of He-broadened CO2 in several infrared spectral regions over the (200-1000) K temperature range. Finally, for applications to exoplanet atmosphere opacity calculations, we derived temperature-dependent chi-factor corrections that account for the sub-Lorentzian behavior of the far wing of the major infrared bands of CO2.

items.title: PENGARUH PROGRAM MOTOR COGNITIVE COORDINATION TERHADAP PENINGKATAN KONSENTRASI: studi eksperimen pada siswa SD berbasis gelombang otak)
items.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji efektivitas penerapan Motor Cognitive Coordination (MCC) dalam meningkatkan konsentrasi siswa sekolah dasar, dengan menganalisis kontribusi gelombang otak beta. Latar belakangnya didasari oleh pentingnya integrasi fungsi motorik dan kognitif dalam pembelajaran. Metode yang digunakan adalah desain eksperimen pretest-posttest control group design dengan subjek siswa SD kelas 4-6, yang dibagi menjadi kelompok eksperimen (menerima program MCC) dan kelompok kontrol. Hasil analisis statistik menunjukkan adanya peningkatan signifikan pada tingkat konsentrasi siswa di kelompok eksperimen setelah perlakuan (p < 0,05), yang juga sejalan dengan kenaikan aktivitas gelombang otak beta pada kelompok yang sama. Uji korelasi menunjukkan hubungan positif yang kuat antara peningkatan gelombang otak beta dan peningkatan konsentrasi. Temuan ini menyimpulkan bahwa program MCC efektif dalam meningkatkan konsentrasi, yang terbukti dari kontribusi gelombang otak beta yang meningkat. Implikasi dari penelitian ini adalah MCC dapat menjadi pendekatan inovatif yang diintegrasikan ke dalam strategi pembelajaran untuk meningkatkan kemampuan kognitif, khususnya konsentrasi, pada siswa sekolah dasar. This study aims to assess the effectiveness of Motor Cognitive Coordination (MCC) implementation in improving the concentration of elementary school students, by analyzing the contribution of beta brain waves. The background is based on the importance of integrating motor and cognitive functions in learning. The method used is a pretest-posttest control group design with elementary school students in grades 4-6, who were divided into an experimental group (receiving the MCC program) and a control group. The results of the statistical analysis showed a significant increase in the level of concentration of students in the experimental group after treatment (p < 0.05), which is also in line with the increase in beta brain wave activity in the same group. The correlation test showed a strong positive relationship between the increase in beta brain waves and increased concentration. These findings conclude that the MCC program is effective in improving concentration, as evidenced by the increased contribution of beta brain waves. The implication of this study is that MCC can be an innovative approach integrated into learning strategies to improve cognitive abilities, especially concentration, in elementary school students.

items.title: Towards sustainable construction: A Roadmap for Aligning BES6001 with the UN SDGs
items.abstract: The architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector has grown significantly over recent decades, sparking ongoing debate about its environmental impact. While advancing sustainability is essential, the sector’s role in meeting housing needs, upgrading infrastructure, and restoring biodiversity remains critical to delivering safe and resilient communities. Responsible sourcing and green supply chains are increasingly recognised as key mechanisms for delivering sustainable construction. BES6001 is a certification standard for responsible sourcing, offering a structured and transparent framework for AEC organisations producing materials. However, its potential contribution to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remains insufficiently explored. This study examines the alignment between BES6001 and the SDGs, through the development of a conceptual roadmap. The roadmap was subject to expert review and identified strongest contributions to SDG-8 and SDG-12, although findings are based on preliminary validation (n=7). By analysing BES6001’s scoring criteria and principles, the roadmap illustrates how UK organisations may support the operationalisation of SDG commitments through BES6001 certification. Recommendations include revising BES6001 to strengthen SDG alignment and holistic review of SDG targets for developed regions where current goals may lack relevance. items.title: Diagnostic drivers of psychiatric inpatient bed use in Ireland 2013-2023: implications for service planning.
items.abstract: Objectives Psychiatric inpatient care is a high-resource component of mental health systems. Understanding the diagnoses driving inpatient care is essential for evidence-based service planning. This study describes psychiatric inpatient bed use in Ireland from 2013 to 2023 by diagnosis, sex, and age group. Methods National descriptive analyses using aggregated data from the National Psychiatric Inpatient Reporting System, covering acute inpatient admissions in Ireland. The outcome was total number of inpatient bed days, categorised by ICD-10 diagnostic group. Primary analyses focused on public services, with private services reported separately. We additionally report on child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS), adult services, and sex-stratified results. Results Between 2013 and 2023, there were k=3,993,628 public and k=1,879,877 private inpatient bed days. In public services, schizophrenia spectrum disorders accounted for 41.9% of bed days (k=1,673,529), more than twice as many as the next most prevalent diagnosis. Men accounted for 51.2% of acute public bed days. In private adult services, depressive disorders accounted for the largest proportion of bed days (28.5%, k=513,166). In public and private CAMHS, eating disorders accounted for the largest proportion of bed days (25.6%, k=46,850 and 24.4%, k=18,775), respectively. Conclusion This national analysis demonstrates that schizophrenia spectrum disorders represent, by far, the largest diagnostic group, accounting for 42% of public acute psychiatric inpatient beds days, highlighting the sustained, intensive service demands associated with these disorders. These data provide a clear empirical basis for future service planning, highlighting where targeted enhancements to community-based care could most effectively reduce the need for hospitalisation.

items.title: Involuntary Treatment in First-Episode Psychosis and Mania: A Retrospective Population-Based Cohort Study.
items.abstract: The study aimed to examine how involuntary status at first presentation affects 5-year trajectories of first-episode psychosis or first-episode mania (FEP/FEM). The authors conducted a population-based cohort study on FEP/FEM. Legal status at first episode was classified as involuntary or voluntary. Participants were followed up to 5 years to examine relapse, emergency department use, vocational status, and Social and Occupational Functioning Assessment Scale (SOFAS) scores. Relapse was compared by using log-rank tests; repeated-measures outcomes used mixed-effects models that adjusted for age and sex, with linear, logistic, or negative binomial regression as appropriate. The cohort included 200 individuals (voluntary, N=139; involuntary, N=61). The involuntary group was older than the voluntary group (p<0.001) and had greater illness severity (Clinical Global Impressions-Severity mean=5.5 vs. 5.1, p=0.002) at FEP/FEM. Time to relapse did not differ, nor did emergency department visits or psychiatric hospitalizations. Functioning improved at a similar rate in both groups; however, the involuntary group remained lower in functioning (SOFAS mean difference=-5.9, p=0.007) and had higher odds of being vocationally disengaged throughout follow-up (odds ratio=3.82, p=0.009). The authors found that involuntary treatment at FEP/FEM is common and is characterized by greater baseline illness severity. Involuntary status can serve as an entry point into care without excess long-term service utilization, and both groups showed similar rates of functional improvement. Persistently lower functioning and higher odds of vocational disengagement in the involuntary group support the need for targeted vocational interventions.

items.title: Life in the fast lane: early-successional species show four different strategies.
items.abstract: Background and aims Global land-use change and climate change are transforming tropical forests into regrowing secondary forests, where early-successional species play a crucial role by colonizing abandoned lands and paving the way for later-successional species. While often considered a homogeneous group with uniformly fast strategies, this study evaluates the diversity of early-successional strategies from Ghanaian tropical dry and wet forests. Methods We selected 30 early-successional species from Ghanaian dry and wet forests differing in leaf habit (deciduous vs. evergreen), and measured wood density and 12 morphological and physiological leaf traits related to drought adaptation and resource acquisition. Traits were compared between forest types and leaf habits using two-way ANOVA, and multivariate analyses identified trait associations and trade-offs. Key results Dry forest species were more drought-tolerant and had slower gas exchange rates than wet forest species, reflecting reduced water use under limited water availability. Multivariate trait analysis showed that early-successional species span a two-dimensional trait space with two main trade-offs: (1) drought tolerance (i.e. high absolute leaf turgor loss point and wood density) versus gas exchange, and (2) investment in leaf structural carbon versus nutrients. The two axes defined four strategies: species that (1) tolerate drought and have tough leaves ("tolerant-and-tough"), (2) tolerate drought and have nutrient-rich leaves ("tolerant-and-rich"), (3) grow rapidly and have tough leaves ("fast-and-tough"), and (4) grow rapidly and have nutrient-rich leaves ("fast-and-rich"). Conclusions Early-successional species followed four diverse strategies rather than converging on a single, fast-growing, acquisitive strategy. Their strategies also extended beyond the commonly described fast-slow gradient, with unexpected trait combinations reflecting the contrasting demands of rapid carbon gain and water conservation during early succession. Such variation may steer successional trajectories because different environmental conditions select for different early-successional strategies.
