items.title: Examining college sexual violence mandatory reporting policies and report outcomes: Evidence does not support a universal approach over alternative approaches.
items.abstract: Mandatory reporting policies for sexual violence in U.S. institutions of higher education (IHEs) require certain designated employees to report any potential sexual violence they learn about to IHE officials, even when the victim/survivor does not want to report. The most common policy approach is a Universal approach, in which all or nearly all employees are designated as mandatory reporters. However, some have adopted Alternative approaches (e.g., designating only select employees as mandatory reporters, considering survivor consent to the report). It is often assumed that Universal policies best facilitate beneficial outcomes, such as addressing cases of sexual violence and supporting survivors. Yet, these assumptions have not been supported with empirical evidence. This exploratory study examined if having a Universal approach (vs. an Alternative approach) was associated with the number of reports made to the Title IX office and key report outcomes following a mandated report. There were no formal hypotheses. This study used survey data collected from a national sample of Title IX practitioners in IHEs (N = 260). Title IX practitioners working at IHEs with a Universal policy received significantly more reports from mandatory reporters than those with an Alternative policy. However, there were no clear significant differences between policy approaches for other outcomes, including total reports, percentage of reports possibly actionable under Title IX policy, how frequently survivors responded to contact from the Title IX office, or how frequently survivors wanted or received a formal investigation process, accommodations, or resource referrals. There were few differences between policy approaches for important mandatory report outcomes, refuting assumptions that Universal mandatory reporting policies are associated with better outcomes than Alternative approaches. items.title: An intervention based on acceptance and commitment therapy for people experiencing work- or career-related difficulties: A randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: This randomized controlled trial assessed the effectiveness of a group intervention based on acceptance and commitment therapy designed for people facing work- or career-related difficulties (e.g., job loss, burnout). Participants were recruited with the assistance of community organizations providing career counseling services, and they were randomly assigned to either an intervention group (n = 82) or a waitlist group (n = 82). They completed questionnaires aimed at measuring process (i.e., psychological flexibility and inflexibility) and outcome variables (i.e., psychological well-being, psychological distress, meaning in life, and career engagement) on three occasions (baseline, postintervention, and follow-up). Participants took part in seven 2.5-hr sessions offered online during a 7-week period. Results of mixed-effects models on intention-to-treat data showed that the intervention led to an increase in psychological flexibility (d = .64), well-being (d = .32), and meaning in life (d = .42) and a decrease in psychological inflexibility (d = -.51) and distress (d = -.36). These effects were maintained at follow-up (17 weeks later), moderated by participants' initial levels of distress and precarity (for some outcomes). Indirect effect analyses showed that changes in psychological flexibility/inflexibility statistically accounted for these effects. The intervention had no significant effect on career engagement. Overall, this trial suggests that the intervention helped promote well-being and flourishing among people struggling with work- or career-related difficulties. items.title: Implementation of School-Based Traffic Light Labeling and Calorie Information Intervention to Reduce Sugary Drink Purchases Among Indonesian Adolescents.
items.abstract: Sugar-sweetened beverages consumption remains high among adolescents and requires effective interventions. This study evaluated the impact of traffic light labeling (TLL) displayed in the school canteens on beverage purchases among high school students. A 2-stage study consisted of a qualitative approach exploring preferred TLL designs and a quantitative quasi-experiment involving intervention and control schools. The intervention school displayed energy, sugar, and fat TLL on beverage menus for 2 months, preceded by an educational session, while the control school displayed a balanced nutrition poster. Beverage purchases were recorded at baseline, 1 month, and 2 months using an online self-administered questionnaire. At baseline, nutritional status and pocket money did not differ significantly between groups. Mean BMI-for-age z -scores were 0.03 ± 0.01 in the intervention school and 0.13 ± 0.01 in the control school. Repeated-measures analyses showed significant reductions in energy, sugar, and fat beverage purchases in the intervention group (all P < .05). Traffic light labeling combined with education may promote healthier beverage purchasing.

items.title: Seasonal Variation in Mood and Associated Patterns of Sleep, Activity, Circadian Rhythms and Light.
items.abstract: The mechanisms underlying seasonal mood variation are incompletely characterised. We tested whether wearable-measured sleep, activity, circadian and light exposure patterns are associated with seasonal mood variation in young Australians with emerging mood disorders. We analysed 733 observation periods from 422 participants (mean age 24.3 ± 5.5 years; 63% female) attending early-intervention clinics. Each observation included a clinical assessment paired with ≥5 valid days of wrist actigraphy. Season was modelled using sine-cosine functions of day-of-year. Sleep, activity and circadian features were reduced using joint and individual variation explained (JIVE). Light exposure features were reduced using principal component analysis (PCA) applied to light regularity, timing and exposure interval across 7 illuminance thresholds. Linear mixed-effects models tested seasonal effects on clinical outcomes; indirect associations for 12 candidate JIVE/PCA variables were estimated by cluster bootstrap. Depressive symptoms (β = -0.67, P = .023) and negative symptoms (β = -0.17, P = .041) peaked in winter, whereas manic symptoms peaked in autumn (β = 0.24, P = .019). Winter increases in negative symptoms were associated with an 'extended sleep with phase-delayed activity' profile (indirect β = -0.015, P < .002) and a 'constrained pattern of moderate-to-bright indoor light exposure' profile (indirect β = -0.038, P = .002), reflecting high day-to-day consistency with a narrow daily exposure window. The light association persisted after adjustment for time spent above the light threshold, which itself was not associated with symptoms. Winter increases in depressive symptoms were associated with lower overall physical activity levels (indirect β = -0.009, P = .040). No indirect associations were identified for manic symptoms. In this transdiagnostic youth sample, seasonal variation in mood was modest but was accompanied by differences in how personal light exposure was arranged across the day, not only in how much light was received and in daily activity patterns. These cross-sectional associations identify light patterning and activity rhythms as candidate modifiable targets for prospective and interventional research.

items.title: Multi-level factors influencing the implementation of Cambodia's National Policy on School Health: a qualitative case study.
items.abstract: Background Since the 2000 World Education Forum, international organizations have encouraged low- and middle-income countries to strengthen school health systems through national school health policies based on the Health Promoting School (HPS) concept. While these policies offer proven benefits, implementation remains challenging in many low- and middle-income settings. In Cambodia, despite the establishment of the National Policy on School Health (NPSH), implementation remains uneven and insufficient across administrative levels. While implementation factors have been identified at the national, provincial, and elementary school levels, evidence remains limited at the secondary school level. Therefore, the current study investigated the factors influencing NPSH implementation at the public secondary school level in Battambang province. Methods This qualitative case study assessed complementary information from 27 key informant interviews (KIIs) with stakeholders involved in policy implementation and 13 documents related to previous implementation efforts. Participants represented national policy, provincial, district, commune, and school perspectives. Content analysis combined deductive coding guided by Vince Whitman's wheel of factors influencing the implementation of policy and practice, with inductive coding of context-specific themes. Results Nine thematic domains were identified to influence NPSH implementation. Policy reform, policy implementation-adapted strategy, and champions and leaders at all levels were described primarily as enabling implementation. Dissemination gaps and limited understanding within the international and national guidelines domain, attention to external forces, and gender gap and mandated roles were described primarily as inhibitors. Dedicated time and resources, administrative and management support, and stakeholder ownership and participation contained both enabling and constraining processes. These categories describe reported implementation experience rather than measured effect or the relative importance of factors. Conclusions Participants described an interaction between a binding legal mandate and perceived local autonomy in the implementation of NPSH. Their accounts suggest that a clearer legal framework, support for local adaptation, leadership, and cross-sector participation may help implementation in this setting. This study did not establish causal effects or examine students' health and learning outcomes. Research across additional provinces, incorporating frontline staff, parents, students, and independent implementation data, is needed to assess the interpretations and their transferability.

items.title: Approximating Peak Prevalence in Multistage SIR Epidemics.
items.abstract: Estimating peak prevalence is a central problem in epidemic modeling because it determines the period of greatest infectious burden and is closely linked to health-care demand. In multistage SIR models, however, peak prevalence is generally less tractable than in the classical model with exponentially distributed infectious periods. Motivated by the use of weighted infectious-stage aggregates as surrogates for prevalence, we investigate the relationship between the prevalence peak and the maximum of a weighted stage functional in a deterministic SIR-like epidemic model with k identical infectious stages, which we call an SI(k)R model. We show that this relationship depends critically on how the stage-progression rate is scaled as the number of infectious stages increases. Under naive scaling, in which the progression rate remains fixed, the weighted peak is asymptotically equivalent to the prevalence peak and the commonly used factor-two approximation fails. Under Erlang scaling, which preserves the mean infectious period, the multistage model converges to a delay formulation in which prevalence and the weighted stage functional become unweighted and triangularly weighted moving averages of incidence. This limiting representation provides a theoretical basis for the factor-two approximation and identifies the regimes in which it is accurate. It also explains why this approximation deteriorates as epidemic waves become more sharply peaked. We derive analytical error bounds and develop curvature-based and parameter-based corrections that substantially improve accuracy. Numerical studies confirm these improvements across a broad range of epidemiological parameters. Overall, the results show when weighted-stage peaks can be used reliably as proxies for peak prevalence and how the resulting estimates can be refined when the standard approximation loses accuracy.

items.title: Genomic analysis of early case samples from the 2025 Marburg virus outbreak in Ethiopia.
items.abstract: In November 2025, Ethiopia reported its first outbreak of Marburg virus disease, with a case fatality rate of 64%. Here we report the analysis of seven near-complete Marburg virus genomes from seven early cases. The outbreak lineage belonged to the MARV.A.1 clade, which is closely related to genomes from historical human cases and bats. A high nucleotide identity across the seven genomes suggests human-to-human transmission after a zoonotic spillover event. These findings highlight the importance of genomic surveillance for outbreak detection, response and preparedness.

items.title: Local politicians' perspectives on mental health literacy in their political and social work environment.
items.abstract: BackgroundMental health literacy is important for local politicians working in socially demanding roles. Given the high prevalence of mental health problems and rising sick leave, they must engage with these issues in an informed and reflective way, particularly in elder care, a field characterised by public scrutiny, emotional strain, and frequent criticism.ObjectiveTo examine how local politicians responsible for elder care conceptualise mental health literacy and how they relate it to their own social work environment.MethodsThis qualitative content analysis study draws on 41 interviews with local politicians responsible for elder care across Sweden, representing a range of political parties, geographical contexts, and political roles.ResultsThe analysis resulted in two categories: Navigating mental health in a politicised work role, and Psychosocial pressures within a hostile political work environment The findings show that politicians work under demanding conditions characterised by high workload, public scrutiny, and the risk of threats and harassment from both citizens and political colleagues. Despite these challenges, the results reveal limited mental health literacy regarding their own psychosocial risks and work environment.ConclusionThis study highlights how the socially demanding work environment of local politicians shapes their understanding of mental health and contributes to psychosocial strain. The findings underscore the need for greater awareness, organisational support, and preventive measures to promote sustainable and healthy political work environments.

items.title: The role of platelet-rich plasma and stem cells in the management of osteoarthritis: Current evidence, clinical positioning, and translational challenges.
items.abstract: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapies are among the most widely used regenerative interventions for knee osteoarthritis (OA). Despite being driven by a broadly similar regenerative concept, important differences in biological characteristics, evidence availability, and regulatory requirements mean that they should not be regarded as broadly comparable therapies. At the same time, conflicting findings from clinical trials and evidence syntheses continue to shape interpretation and clinical decision-making. Substantial heterogeneity across products, treatment protocols, patient populations, and study designs has further complicated the evidence base. Yet as public enthusiasm and commercialization continue to accelerate, these uncertainties are often overshadowed by simplified narratives and therapeutic expectations. Amid this uncertainty, clinical interpretation should prioritise reliable evidence over expectation-driven narratives. In this rapidly evolving landscape, regenerative therapies should be considered through a cautious, evidence-based, and guideline-informed lens. Current evidence does not support routine, indiscriminate, or first-line use of regenerative injections in knee OA. PRP may be discussed as a selective option for carefully selected patients after inadequate response to established conservative treatments, but uncertainty about the magnitude and durability of benefit, together with caveats related to reporting limitations, spin, and costs, should be clearly communicated to support shared decision-making. MSC-based and other cell-based therapies remain less established and require further rigorous evaluation before broader clinical adoption.

items.title: Bacterial microbiota profiling of human-biting ticks in Yozgat Province, Türkiye.
items.abstract: In the present study, the bacterial microbiota of ticks infesting humans in Yozgat Province, Türkiye, was investigated. Ticks were collected from 54 patients who were presented to the Emergency Service of the Yozgat Bozok University Research and Training Hospital between March and November 2019. The following tick species were identified: Hyalomma marginatum, Rhipicephalus turanicus, Rhipicephalus bursa, Haemaphysalis parva, Dermacentor marginatus, and Hyalomma aegyptium. 16S rRNA libraries were prepared from tick DNA pools using a two-step PCR protocol targeting the V3-V4 region. In the second (indexing) PCR, dual Illumina indexes and adapters were added using the Nextera XT Index Kit. The resulting libraries were then sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq platform. A total of 3782 operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were identified; an average of 127,823 reads were obtained per sample, and an average of 31,561 reads were retained after taxonomic assignment. The OTUs were classified into 20 phyla, 41 classes, 94 orders, 168 families, 344 genera, and 452 putative species-level taxa. At the phylum level, Proteobacteria were predominant (averaging 63%), followed by Actinobacteriota and Bacteroidota (each approximately 10%) and Firmicutes (9%). At the class level, Alphaproteobacteria (average 37%) and Gammaproteobacteria (26%) exhibited the highest relative abundance, while at the order level, Rickettsiales (34%) and Francisellales (17%) were prominent. At the family and genus levels, the dominant taxa were identified as Rickettsiaceae (33%), Francisellaceae (17%), Rickettsia (33%), Francisella (17%), and Coxiella (7%), respectively. The most prevalent species included symbiotic bacteria such as Francisella sp. and Candidatus Midichloria mitochondrii. The Kruskal-Wallis test, conducted from phylum to genus level to evaluate taxonomic composition differences among tick species, revealed no statistically significant differences (p ≥ 0.05 for all comparisons). In alpha diversity analyses, no significant differences were found between tick species in terms of Shannon and Simpson indices (Shannon: H = 7.69; p = 0.26, Simpson: H = 8.07; p = 0.23). Similarly, no significant differences were observed between sex and developmental stages (Shannon: p = 0.86, Simpson: p = 0.73). The Chao1 and observed OTU values indicated higher richness trends, particularly in the Hyalomma marginatum and Hyalomma sp. pools. However, Spearman correlations between sample size and diversity indices were not significant (p > 0.05). These findings provide a baseline overview of the bacterial microbiota associated with human-biting ticks in Yozgat Province and may serve as a foundation for future studies employing higher-resolution methods to assess pathogen presence and public health risk.

items.title: Cardiothoracic Surgery Training Attrition (2014-2023): Predictors, Trends, and Delay-Adjusted Rates Across Traditional and Integrated Pathways.
items.abstract: Resident attrition disrupts training pipelines and threatens cardiothoracic (CT) surgical workforce sustainability. This study quantifies national attrition rates and identifies predictors using trainee data from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC), while accounting for reporting delays. We analyzed de-identified records of 1,476 CT surgery residents entering ACGME-accredited programs from 2014 to 2023. Attrition was defined as departure before expected completion. Rates were stratified by year, gender, citizenship, and training pathway: integrated (TS-I) versus traditional (TS). Multivariable logistic regression, LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost with nested cross-validation were used to identify predictors. A parametric nowcasting model corrected for administrative reporting lag. The overall attrition rate was 3.9% (57/1,476), significantly higher in the TS-I than the TS pathway (7.0% vs. 2.6%, p 36 group (aOR 6.05, 95% CI 1.87-19.62) compared with those ≤30 years. Gender and citizenship were not significant after adjustment. Model performance was consistent across methods (AUC 0.67-0.72). Delay-adjusted analyses corrected an apparent decline in recent cohorts, revealing a stable underlying rate with a 3-4-year reporting lag. Training pathways are the strongest predictor of CT resident attrition, with TS-I trainees at markedly higher risk. Correcting reporting delays is critical for accurate workforce planning. These findings support targeted retention interventions for at-risk trainees.

items.title: Supplementation with fortified balanced energy-protein during pregnancy and lactation and infant growth outcomes in southern Nepal: a community-based 2×2 factorial randomized trial.
items.abstract: Small-for-gestational age birth and infant linear growth faltering are prevalent in South Asia. The World Health Organization recommends balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplementation in pregnancy for undernourished populations, but evidence on the extension of supplementation through lactation to improve infant growth remains limited. To examine the effect of daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy and lactation on infant mean length-for-age z-score (LAZ) and secondary growth outcomes at 6 months of age. MINT (Maternal Infant Nutrition Trial) was a 2x2 factorial, household randomized, unblinded efficacy trial to assess a daily fortified BEP supplement during pregnancy and/or lactation compared to no supplement on birth and infant growth outcomes in Sarlahi, Nepal. A modified intention-to-treat analysis estimated the effects of supplementation on infant growth outcomes using linear and Poisson regression models. Models without and with adjustment for birth size were used to estimate the overall effect and the effect independent of birth size, respectively. Among 1,554 mothers and 1,568 infants randomized after delivery, there was no interaction between pregnancy and lactation supplementation on the primary infant growth outcome. Neither BEP supplementation during pregnancy nor lactation had an effect on mean infant LAZ at 6 months (unadjusted mean difference for pregnancy: 0.01 [95% CI: -0.10, 0.12]; for lactation -0.02 [95% CI: -0.13, 0.09]). Significant differences were not observed for any secondary outcomes: mean weight-for-length z-scores, weight-for-age z-scores, infant weight, length, head circumference, mid-upper arm circumference or prevalence of stunting, wasting, and underweight at 6-months or for a subset of infants at 12-months. Null effects persisted after adjustment for birth size. In rural Nepal, daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy or early lactation did not improve linear or ponderal growth of infants at 6- or 12-months. To reduce the burden of early infant growth faltering, alternative strategies should be considered. NCT03668977. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03668977?term=nct03668977&rank=1.

items.title: Developmental exposure to PBDE-47 induces sex- and organ-specific glucose uptake alterations linked to thyroid hormone disruption in rats: phenotypic parallels to early cardiorenal-metabolic crosstalk.
items.abstract: 2, 2', 4, 4'-Tetrabromodiphenyl ether (PBDE-47) is a ubiquitous persistent organic pollutant with developmental toxicity and thyroid-disrupting activity. Increasing evidence links PBDE-47 exposure to metabolic disorders, yet it remains unclear whether developmental PBDE-47 exposure disturbs glucose metabolism in multiple organs of offspring and how thyroid hormone (TH) changes relate to such effects. Using a rat model of perinatal PBDE-47 exposure, organ-specific glucose metabolism were assessed via positron emission tomography with the 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) tracer. Adult male offspring exhibited increased FDG uptake in the heart but decreased uptake in the brain and kidneys, whereas female offspring showed elevated uptake in the brain and kidneys and reduced cardiac FDG uptake. These changes were accompanied by sex-specific TH alterations, with increased T3 in males and decreased T3 and T4 in females. Correlation analyses revealed significant associations between TH levels and organ-specific FDG uptake. Intriguingly, these coordinated metabolic and endocrine disruptions exhibited early phenotypic parallels to features of the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework. Network toxicology identified 89 core targets, with PIK3CB, PIK3R1, PIK3R2, PLCG1, and PLCG2 as hub molecules enriched in apoptosis, endocrine signaling, insulin resistance, and central carbon metabolism pathways. Molecular docking suggested high-affinity binding of PBDE-47 to these targets, and gene set analysis further implicated PI3K/AKT, insulin receptor signaling, and the AGE-RAGE pathway. Collectively, this study suggests that perinatal PBDE-47 exposure elicits sex-specific multi-organ alterations in FDG uptake that correlate with TH disruption, providing a hypothesis-generating basis for developmental metabolic toxicity and highlighting phenotypic parallels to early cardiorenal-metabolic crosstalk.

items.title: Early-Life NO 2 Exposure and developmental coordination disorder in Preschool Children: A Cross-sectional Study.
items.abstract: Although air pollution is a potential neurotoxicant, evidence linking early-life nitrogen dioxide (NO2) exposure to motor development remains inconsistent, and large-scale studies are limited. This cross-sectional study investigated associations of prenatal and postnatal NO2 exposure with motor coordination performance and suspected developmental coordination disorder (DCD) risk among 105,280 children aged 3-5 years from Chinese National Cohort of Motor Development. Motor coordination was assessed using the Little DCD Questionnaire (LDCDQ). NO2 exposure was estimated using a high-resolution satellite-based random forest model. Linear mixed-effects models and generalized linear mixed models with a binomial distribution were applied to evaluate associations with LDCDQ scores and suspected DCD risk, respectively. Per interquartile range (IQR) increase in NO2 during the first trimester and from birth to 36 months, LDCDQ scores decreased by 0.20 (95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.08, -0.31) and 0.10 (95% CI: -0.02, -0.19), respectively. Odds ratios for suspected DCD were 1.07 (95% CI: 1.03, 1.11) for first-trimester exposure and 1.04 (95% CI: 1.004, 1.07) for birth-to-18-month exposure. Among three LDCDQ subdomains, general coordination showed the strongest association. Associations appeared to be stronger among boys. These findings suggest that early-life NO2 exposure may adversely affect motor coordination development of preschoolers, though the modest effect sizes were observed.

items.title: Early pregnancy exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and phthalates: linear and nonlinear associations with fetal growth in a Chinese birth cohort.
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that combined prenatal exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and phthalates (PAEs) may interfere with fetal development, yet relevant evidence based on fetal growth measures covering the transition phase from mid to late gestation remains limited. In this study, we enrolled 811 pregnant women from the Zunyi Birth Cohort and detected urinary metabolites of OH-PAHs and mPAEs in early pregnancy. Fetal growth measures including head circumference (HC), biparietal diameter (BPD), abdominal circumference (AC), femur length (FL), and placental thickness (PT) were collected at 14 to 27 weeks of gestation. Linear regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to explore linear and nonlinear relationships between exposure levels and fetal growth outcomes, and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) was further adopted to assess the combined effect of pollutant mixtures and screen core pollutants. RCS models revealed distinct linear and nonlinear exposure-response relationships for various pollutants. Supplementary RCS analyses using LOD-constrained truncated multiple imputation (truncated MI) indicated that overall exposure-outcome trends were largely consistent with the LOD/√2 substitution approach. Truncated MI was used to address measurement uncertainty within the low-exposure range. BKMR analyses found that the PAHs mixture was negatively associated with PT at the 75th percentile, with 1-OHPYR identified as the primary contributing component. For the combined PAH and PAE mixtures, MBP was positively associated with abdominal circumference z-scores (AC-z) at low concentrations, while MEP showed a negative association with AC-z at high concentrations.

items.title: Combined effects of LINE-1 DNA methylation and exposure to metals on renal cell carcinoma.
items.abstract: Exposure to heavy metals and trace elements is associated with renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Methylation of long interspersed nuclear element-1 (LINE-1), a surrogate marker of global DNA methylation, has also been linked to metal exposure and cancer-related outcomes; however, no studies have examined the combined effects of metal exposure and LINE-1 methylation on RCC. We evaluated the association between LINE-1 methylation and RCC and its pairwise combined effects with metals. We conducted a clinic-based case-control study of 204 incident RCC cases and 715 non-cancer controls, frequency-matched by age and sex. Cadmium and lead concentrations in red blood cells (RBC) and selenium concentrations in plasma were quantified, and LINE-1 methylation levels in blood leukocyte DNA were measured by pyrosequencing. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for associations of LINE-1 methylation and metal concentrations with RCC. Combined effects of each metal with LINE-1 methylation were assessed on an additive scale. LINE-1 methylation and RBC cadmium were positively associated with RCC, whereas plasma selenium was inversely associated with RCC. The odds of elevated LINE-1 methylation (highest tertile) were 5.79 times greater among RCC cases than controls (95%CI=3.48-9.61). The odds of both high RBC cadmium and high LINE-1 methylation were 16.45 times greater among RCC cases than controls (95%CI=8.12-33.30), and the OR-based interaction measures suggested a potential positive departure from additivity. The point estimates of additive interaction between low plasma selenium and high LINE-1 methylation were consistent with a positive departure from additivity, although the estimates were imprecise. Our study suggests a potential positive additive interaction between LINE-1 methylation and cadmium for RCC, whereas the findings for selenium require cautious interpretation. These findings support the consideration of epigenetic factors when evaluating associations between metals and RCC.

items.title: Exploring "equigenesis" in the association between the natural outdoor environment, mental health and death by suicide before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: a population-based cohort study of more than 2 million records in Northern Ireland.
items.abstract: Recent evidence suggests that the natural outdoor environment (NOE) may mitigate socioeconomic inequalities in mental health, but it remains unclear how such associations vary between the pandemic and the non-pandemic period. Therefore, this study focused on the association between NOE and inequalities in mental health before and during the pandemic. We used a population-based cohort of individuals in Northern Ireland (NI), including more than 2 million General Practice participants from 2017 to 2022. NOE was assessed using the proportion of blue space and green space within the administrative neighbourhoods, respectively. Mental health outcomes included death by suicide, mental health-related hospital admissions and prescriptions. We applied multilevel Cox proportional hazards and logistic regressions. Further, we stratified the analysis by area-level deprivation index. The analyses were performed for the pre-pandemic (2017-2019) and during the pandemic (2020-2022), respectively. People living in neighbourhoods with a higher proportion of NOE (e.g., 4th quintile of blue space) had lower odds of being in receipt of mental-health-related prescriptions (e.g., pre-pandemic: OR=0.835, 95% CI=0.796-0.874; intra-pandemic: OR=0.802, 95% CI=0.763-0.844) and a lower risk of dying by suicide (e.g., pre-pandemic: HR=0.634, 95% CI=0.451-0.890; intra-pandemic: HR=0.684, 95% CI=0.469-0.998). However, there is no evidence that NOE is related to a lower risk of having a mental health-related hospital admission (e.g., pre-pandemic: OR=1.053, 95% CI=0.794-1.396; intra-pandemic: OR=1.044, 95% CI=0.778-1.401). The association between NOE and mental health-related hospital admissions, as well as the association between NOE and prescriptions, was more pronounced in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighbourhoods, especially during the pandemic. However, such "equigenesis" was only observed for death by suicide before the pandemic. Therefore, NOE may mitigate socioeconomic inequalities in mental health, especially during the pandemic. Our findings demonstrate the importance of sufficient NOE to support better and more equal mental health and preparedness for future pandemics.

items.title: What Is PBL 4.0? Generative Epistemic Inquiry As A Framework For AI-Augmented Learning
items.abstract: Problem-Based Learning remains one of higher education’s most significant pedagogical contributions. Its core premise (that students learn more effectively, particularly for the application, transfer, and retention of knowledge, when actively engaging with problems than passively receiving information) is as valid as ever. What has changed is the environment: organisations restructuring around AI, professional roles shifting from execution to oversight, and civic life requiring disciplined reasoning in information environments that actively resist it. Many implementations of PBL, particularly at large scale, have not kept pace. Neither, in many cases, have the institutions responsible for it (optimising for procedural consistency, satisfaction scores, and completion rates) imperatives that solved real problems of equity and scalability, but that under certain conditions can create incentives that gradually erode exactly the challenge that makes education worth having. This document proposes a response and makes the case that the response is timely, practically feasible, and already taking shape in practice. What PBL 4.0 is. Generative Epistemic Inquiry adds a dimension that earlier PBL stages often did not reach: the collective interrogation of the assumptions and mechanisms underlying knowledge claims, rather than their application or reproduction. Students do not explain what theories say; they examine what those theories assume, and under what conditions they hold. The primary targets are epistemic agency and ontological reasoning. A practical classroom heuristic, Marginal Analytical Value (MAV), makes these concrete: a contribution earns its primary analytic credit if it advances collective reasoning beyond what any attentive reader could produce alone; with capable AI systems serving as a vivid contemporary illustration of where that baseline now sits. Clarifying, summarising, and connecting contributions retain their proper role; MAV simply names the upper bar against which deeper engagement is calibrated. This is a higher bar than most PBL currently sets, yet vital for the age of GenAI. Why the same competencies solve three problems at once. AI systems generate false positives and false negatives; detecting and acting on those errors requires domain-grounded, first-principles reasoning; not tool fluency. Meanwhile, AI is restructuring organisations in ways that remove the entry-level rungs through which junior employees have always developed practical judgment, raising the floor of what competence must look like on day one (this organisational forecast is actively debated; PBL 4.0’s argument does not depend on it materialising in the strongest form). And contemporary civic life requires citizens who can reason carefully in environments saturated with contested and manipulated information. These are not three separate problems. They are one convergence and the competencies PBL 4.0 develops (epistemic agency, argumentation, evidence evaluation, ontological reasoning) are precisely the ones that professional oversight, organisational survival, and civic participation all now require. In various fields and educational traditions, it has been mentioned that first-principles competencies are also the most durable investment in a fast-changing world: argumentation theory and the scientific method have remained functionally stable across centuries of technological upheaval, which is the opposite of the tool, or even specific theories, landscape. PBL 4.0 is not just a response to AI. It is a response to what AI reveals about competences higher education has long claimed to develop and has not always succeeded in developing under scale. How it works, and what makes it different. Eight integrated design principles together are designed to produce something that none of its parts contains separately. Strategic ambiguity (i.e., deliberately withheld resolution) requires students to determine what is actually at stake before solutions can be considered, introduced gradually through scaffolding and fading as capacity develops. The student-as-facilitator model rotates the responsibility for designing and leading sessions across the group: the preparation this demands is qualitatively different from anything participation alone produces. A learning contract at the start of each cycle establishes not just behavioural norms but a shared competency orientation (where each member is starting from, what the group needs to develop, and how the session design responds to that) making genuinely tailor-made learning environments possible rather than merely promised. Rotating Epistemic Observers make the group’s reasoning patterns visible in real time. AI is positioned as a preparation-phase analytical partner, engaged only after independent human analysis: the machine stress-tests, it does not originate. The assessment architecture addresses directly what most institutions avoid naming (namely that the current configuration of grade fear and evaluation asymmetry can produce a mutual performance of the relationship rather than the thing itself) and proposes structural alternatives rather than individual heroism. A layered competency-tracking system makes development visible from individual session to programme level, without adding administrative burden. The result is a learning environment that is adaptive, presence-based, and genuinely responsive to the specific group in the room; the things online formats and traditional lectures structurally cannot offer. How to adopt it. PBL 4.0 is a menu, not a mandate. Each element has independent value; a course that adopts three of them is already a materially different course. A course at PBL 2.5 or 3.7 is not failing; yet hopefully it is in motion and this framework gives guidelines for how to do so. However, while not required, full integration is designed to produce something emergent: a learning environment whose character becomes visible only from a distance, and which represents PBL’s most complete realisation of what it has always promised. The purpose. Every design choice in this document is ultimately made for the student in the room, and for the organizations and societies they will enter. The framework is therefore modular and architectural as these stakeholders vary in their needs. Overall, PBL 4.0 aims not to just credential students, but to develop them: into professionals who can reason from first principles when the theories and model fail, into people with a genuine internal locus of control rather than a performance orientation calibrated to the nearest evaluator, into thinkers robust enough to hold uncertainty without collapsing it prematurely and resilient enough to learn from failure rather than avoid it. The old ideal of the homo universalis (invoked here only for its core insight that depth across multiple fields produces a qualitatively different capacity to navigate genuinely novel territory — not for its historically narrow class, gender, and cultural framing) is not an historical luxury. In an age of rapid AI-driven change, the underlying competence it names (capabilities that are grounded rather than merely trained) is a personal, professional, and civic necessity. As such, a mastery orientation, adaptive reasoning, epistemic independence, and the kind of character that sustained intellectual difficulty actually builds: these are what PBL 4.0 is designed to develop. What this integrated framework is thus building toward are resilient, robust, and self-directed persons.

items.title: Effects of Grit and Major Satisfaction on Metacognition in Nursing Students
items.abstract: This study examined the relationships among grit, major satisfaction, and metacognition among nursing students and identified key factors influencing metacognition.A descriptive survey design was employed.Data were collected from nursing students enrolled at a university in a designated region and analyzed using SPSS/WIN 26.0.Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations, were utilized to analyze general characteristics and main study variables.Differences in key variables based on participants' general characteristics were examined using independent t-tests and one-way ANOVA, followed by Scheffé's test for post-hoc analysis.Pearson's correlation coefficients were used to evaluate relationships among grit, major satisfaction, and metacognition.Finally, multiple linear regression was conducted to identify the primary predictors of metacognition.The findings demonstrated significant positive correlations among grit, major satisfaction, and metacognition in nursing students.Specifically, higher levels of grit and major satisfaction were associated with enhanced metacognitive capacity.Personality traits, grit, and major satisfaction were also identified as significant factors influencing metacognition.The regression model accounted for 61.2% of the explanatory variance, indicating strong predictive power.The results suggest that to effectively enhance metacognitive abilities in nursing students, educational strategies must consider individual personality characteristics.Furthermore, tailored educational interventions and multifaceted extracurricular programs should be developed and implemented to reinforce grit-defined as passion and perseverance for long-term goals-and to elevate overall major satisfaction, ultimately fostering more self-directed and competent future healthcare professionals.

items.title: Critically about the descriptive category "Generation Z"
items.abstract: Cel pracy Wartość naukowa kategorii opisowych w badaniach determinuje jakość wyników. Zarządzanie, jako nauka stosowana, stoi przed wyzwaniem przekształcania popularnych słów, używanych w organizacjach, w rygorystyczne kategorie naukowe. Niniejsze badanie koncentruje się na kategorii „Pokolenie Z”, dążąc do zapewnienia trójstopniowej weryfikacji jej wartości w dziedzinie zarządzania zasobami ludzkimi. Materiał i metody Zastosowanie podejścia mieszanego, w badaniu integruje analizy jakościowe i ilościowe dostosowane do wymagań każdego podcelu badawczego. Kluczowym punktem odniesienia dla syntezy i interpretacji danych jest paradygmat relacyjny. Z niego wynikają również wskazówki dla wykorzystania wyników badania Wyniki Kategoria „Pokolenie Z” została oceniona pod kątem trafności, wiarygodności i użyteczności. Wyniki określają wartość naukową i pragmatyczną kategorii „Pokolenia Z”. Zidentyfikowano także jego, potwierdzone przez respondentów, cechy. Wnioski Ponadto badanie zakłada, że wartość tej kategorii zależy od procesu jej społecznej i naukowej konstrukcji. Zamiast postrzegać etykietę jako nietrafiony deskryptor demograficzny, można ją w zarządzaniu wykorzystać do wspierania spójności organizacyjnej. Ta zmiana perspektywy – przejście od popularnego deskryptora do narzędzia rozwoju zarządzania zasobami ludzkimi – stanowi oryginalny, oparty na dowodach wkład, który wypełnia lukę między dyskursem powszechnym a rygorem naukowym.

items.title: Gene tree conflict between genomic and functional partitions impacts phylogenetic inference in Zygophylloideae
items.abstract: Abstract The Zygophyllaceae subfamily Zygophylloideae includes seven genera and around 180 species distributed worldwide particularly in arid areas where they show adaptations to drought including C 4 and CAM photosynthesis. Phylogenetic relationships of Zygophylloideae have been analysed in several studies using Sanger sequenced markers, but none have been able to resolve all deeper relationships between genera in the subfamily. Here, we use ion semi-conductor sequencing of chloroplast and nuclear ribosomal regions to analyse these relationships and assess why they have proved so challenging to resolve. We sequenced 39 chloroplast genes and nuclear ribosomal 18S, 5.8S, and 26S genes and internal transcribed spacers (ITS) for key species of Zygophyllum sensu stricto, Roepera, Tetraena, Fagonia , Zygophyllum stapffii and monotypic Augea capensis ; and Tribulus of the subfamily Tribuloideae as outgroup. We aligned these with data from published chloroplast genomes followed by phylogenetic analyses using Maximum Likelihood and Bayesian approaches, summarising phylogenetic results separately for non-coding introns and intergenic spacers, and for genes that are, or are not, involved in photosynthesis. We combined the chloroplast data with sequences of three highly variable noncoding chloroplast regions used in previous studies of greater numbers of taxa, and similarly the nuclear ribosomal data with more densely sampled ITS sequences and assessed whether adding such data resulted in improved support for consistent topologies. We used a chloroplast sequence matrix to infer a dated phylogeny. Adding data did not always improve phylogenetic resolution which was apparently impacted by non-informative variation in chloroplast photosynthesis related genes as well as by conflicting chloroplast and nuclear signals. Chloroplast genes not related to photosynthesis provide robust support for a topology that is consistent with independent data and may therefore represent a useful species tree hypothesis. The cause of the gene tree conflicts remains unclear: potential explanations include functional constraints in photosynthesis related genes and introgressive hybridization and/or incomplete lineage sorting during an ancient rapid divergence. Further testing will require a broader sampling of lineages with different photosynthetic modes and multiple informative, independent, and selectively neutral gene trees.

items.title: Contribution of fine roots on carbon allocation patterns in Norwegian forests
items.abstract: Abstract. Boreal forests play a key role in the global carbon (C) cycle, with fine root production and turnover contributing to belowground C fluxes and inputs to soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. However, fine root biomass and production are difficult to quantify and introduce uncertainty in estimates of net primary production (NPP), limiting the assessment of C allocation patterns in boreal forests. The objective of the present study was to assess how different fine root modelling approaches influence estimates of NPP, gross primary production (GPP), carbon use efficiency (CUE), and belowground C allocation to fine roots in Norwegian boreal and nemo-boreal forests. Using Norway’s national forest resource map together with MODIS remote sensing data, we estimated fine root biomass and production using three approaches that differed in how foliage biomass was derived: two based on leaf area index (from MODIS or the forest resource map) and one based on allometric biomass equations. These approaches were combined with alternative fine-root turnover rates and foliage-to-fine-root biomass ratios. Mean NPP derived from the forest resource map ranged from 318 to 243 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ across young to mature forests. In Norway spruce and Scots pine forests, NPP increased during early stand development, peaked between 50 and 80 years, and declined with increasing age. Comparison against European MODIS NPP revealed that tree growth alone accounted for 16 % of MODIS NPP, while including fine root and understory NPP contributions increased total NPP by roughly 3–5 times, depending on the fine root estimation method. CUE ranged from 0.30 to 0.63, showing age-related declines and species-level variation, with the lowest values in mature Norway spruce forests. Our analysis sheds light on the role of fine root biomass and production in forest C budgeting and their influence on NPP, CUE, and belowground C allocation. Excluding fine roots creates a major gap in forest C analyses and we conclude that the choice of method for fine root estimation has a strong impact on regional NPP and its component fluxes. Estimates of forest CUE may guide management by identifying areas with low efficiency, where interventions may enhance C sequestration.

items.title: Water Quality Assessment of Sisauli Wetland of Morang District, Nepal
items.abstract: Wetlands provide essential ecosystem services, including biodiversity conservation, water purification, nutrient cycling, and hydrological regulation. Assessing their water quality is therefore important for understanding environmental conditions and informing conservation priorities. This study evaluated the post-monsoon water quality of Sisauli Wetland in Morang District, Nepal, using selected physicochemical parameters to characterize aquatic conditions and identify monitoring needs. Water samples were collected from five representative sites following standard sampling procedures. Temperature, pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), and dissolved oxygen (DO) were measured in situ, whereas the remaining physicochemical parameters were analyzed in the laboratory using standard methods. Recorded values included a temperature of 30.2 °C, pH of 8.5, TDS of 92.2 ppm, and DO of 9.64 mg/L. Total alkalinity was 92 mg/L, while nitrate, nitrite, ammonium, and iron concentrations were 6.8, 0.48, 0.02, and 0.26 mg/L, respectively. The results characterized the sampled water as well oxygenated, with low dissolved solids, alkaline conditions, and alkalinity indicating buffering capacity. Nevertheless, the reported nitrite concentration and localized alkaline conditions warrant periodic monitoring to determine their persistence and ecological significance. The measurements provide a baseline for understanding post-monsoon physicochemical conditions, while conclusions about overall ecological health remain limited by the parameters assessed and the seasonal scope of sampling. Continued assessment across seasons, supported by biological indicators, would strengthen the evaluation of wetland condition and potential environmental pressures. The study recommends regular monitoring of nutrients, pH, and DO, together with effective conservation measures, to detect changes in water quality and support the long-term ecological integrity of Sisauli Wetland.

items.title: Locally Available Beans as an Alternative Low-Cost Nutrient Source for Yanagi (Agrocybe aegerita) Mushroom Culture in the Philippines
items.abstract: Mushroom farming provides economic opportunities, but in the Philippines, the high cost of commercial culture media hinders its development. This study aimed to determine whether locally available beans could serve as a cheaper nutrient source for cultivating Agrocybe aegerita in Tabuk City. In this study, researchers measured the mycelial diameter of A. aegerita on five media: Water Agar (T−), Potato Dextrose Agar (T+), and black bean (T1), mung bean (T2), and white bean (T3) agar. A One-Way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD test was applied at the 5% significance level. The species was identified on the basis of its appearance, and the media were prepared by boiling the beans to obtain a broth. The results indicated that PDA (T+) gave the greatest mycelial diameter (49.63 ± 13.28 mm), followed by black bean (31.87 ± 0.517 mm), mung bean (29.09 ± 0.522 mm), and white bean (27.19 ± 0.522 mm) agars. All the legume-based media outperformed the negative control. Higher humidity also slightly inhibited mycelial growth. Although PDA remained the most effective, agars made from black, mung, and white beans are viable alternatives. The study suggests that further research should be carried out to improve methods of media preparation and to promote affordable mushroom production in rural and low-resource areas.

items.title: River Health Assessment of the Ganga River via Geomorphic Metrics: The Anthropocene Context
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Rivers, particularly large river systems, constitute one of the most fundamental life‐support systems that have sustained civilisations and are projected to be a critical determinant for the future sustenance of human civilisations. A river can be termed a healthy ecosystem only when all the flora and fauna are in and along the river, the cultivation in floodplains is healthy, and the river's form is in equilibrium. The Ganga River system in India is a large river system with high geodiversity and biodiversity, where about one‐third of India's population depends on the river directly or indirectly. This study focuses on the development of a Geomorphic River Health Index (gRHI) based on eight geomorphic attributes derived from geospatial data, including sinuosity, braid‐channel ratio, width/depth ratio, occupancy, floodplain development, bar density, bar complexity and stream power. The selected river health parameters were analysed using a multi‐criteria decision‐making technique, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), in a GIS framework. We adopted a five‐fold river health classification framework (i.e., near‐pristine, good, fair, poor and degraded) for the entire Ganga River system from Gomukh to Farakka. Our results, based on geospatial data and supported by field observations, indicate that most reaches of the Ganga River in the higher mountainous stretch are in ‘near pristine’ condition, while some in the lower reaches fall into the ‘good’ and ‘fair’ classes. In contrast, several reaches in the alluvial part show ‘poor’ river health, primarily associated with flow reduction and sediment accumulation leading to morphological degradation, which is well manifested in geomorphic indicators used for river health assessment in this study. The geomorphic framework presented in this study can serve as a good template to evaluate river health and link this to scenarios of habitat suitability, environmental flows and flood risk associated with large river systems.

items.title: Proposal for monitoring the Eastern Grey Squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis) in Poland
items.abstract: The report presents a nationwide, continuous monitoring program for the invasive eastern grey squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis) in Poland, aimed at early detection and prevention of its spread. Monitoring focuses on high-risk areas such as urban parks, deciduous forests near cities, protected areas and border regions. The program includes repeated surveys across seasons using camera traps, field observations, winter nest searches and citizen reports. Grey squirrels pose a serious threat to native fauna, particularly the red squirrel, through competition and disease transmission. Immediate removal of detected individuals, strict enforcement of legal bans, cross-border cooperation and public awareness are emphasized. Effective monitoring combined with rapid response offers a real opportunity to prevent the establishment of this invasive species in Poland.

items.title: Catching small fish in a big pond: optimizing fish environmental DNA detections
items.abstract: Biomonitoring of teleost fish using environmental DNA metabarcoding is frequently performed using the 12S ribosomal RNA marker gene, especially with the MiFish primer set. These primers have associated laboratory and bioinformatic processing challenges that can generate spurious, incomplete, or inaccurate results. Here, we address each challenge to minimize off-target amplification and maximize the accuracy of observed species richness and community composition of the target taxa (teleost fish). We first tested the effects of amplification and sequencing library preparation protocols. We next tested infrequently used parameters in the common bioinformatic software program DADA2 using both environmental samples and mock communities with known composition. Our results support removing known off-target amplicons prior to sequencing and demonstrate that certain parameter settings can maximize the number of fish amplicon sequence variants generated bioinformatically. Furthermore, while changes in OMEGA_A and pooling parameters may yield additional amplicon sequence variants and previously undetected taxa, these amplicon sequence variants generally do not improve biodiversity estimates and are more likely to have associated uncertainty in taxonomic annotations. Based on our results, we recommend the following approaches using the MiFish 12S marker for marine biomonitoring: 1) Incorporate amplicon size selection prior to sequencing, 2) Consider increasing OMEGA_A and investing in manual curation of results.

items.title: Invasive rats and threatened lizards on islands: a DNA metabarcoding approach to assess dietary spectra and trophic interactions on the Aeolian archipelago
items.abstract: Abstract Island ecosystems often host endemics that are highly vulnerable to invasive species. In the Mediterranean biodiversity hotspot, the Endangered Aeolian wall lizard Podarcis raffonei is undergoing severe population decline. Its largest remaining population, on Vulcano Island, dropped by c. 60% from 2017 to 2022. A newly identified threat is the invasive black rat Rattus rattus , recently recorded at high densities in the area. Using DNA metabarcoding of faecal samples, we investigated potential trophic interactions between rats and lizards on Vulcano and provided a detailed characterization of the lizard’s diet across three populations. Podarcis raffonei primarily consumed arthropods (65.7%), particularly Hymenoptera, Hemiptera and Lepidoptera, but also a significant proportion of plant matter (34.3%) including Asterales, Fabales and Poales. Rats exhibited a similarly broad diet; they showed a limited dietary overlap with lizards for animal resources but a high dietary overlap for plant resources. No lizard DNA was found in rat faeces. These findings suggest that trophic competition, rather than direct predation, may be a key driver of the lizard’s decline. This study highlights the power of DNA metabarcoding to reveal cryptic ecological interactions and provides crucial insights for urgent conservation measures, including rat control and habitat management under the LIFE EOLIZARD project.

items.title: Responsible Management Education and Its Potential as an Epistemic Object of Change
items.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether and how RME can be performed as an epistemic object to broaden business schools’ education on climate change. The research builds on a qualitative case study involving 10 Finnish business schools. The analysis reveals that RME is performed as both an epistemic object and a boundary object, with different implications for its embeddedness within institutions. Our findings show how accreditations have introduced RME as a boundary object enforcing performativity around sustainability themes yet enabling disciplines to maintain their distinct or limited roles. At the same time, RME is met with both resistance and compliance, depending on how well the object fits with disciplinary boundaries and career trajectories. Lastly, as an epistemic object, RME encourages co‐reflexivity, which is essential for climate‐proofing business schools. We discuss the possibilities of a hybrid orientation of RME as both a boundary object and an epistemic object for enforcing climate‐orientation in management education.

items.title: Climate change impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem-based adaptation mechanisms in Azerbaijan
items.abstract: Climate change is altering ecosystems, species distributions and the services that support human well-being, while habitat loss and unsustainable resource use intensify ecological vulnerability. This narrative review examines the major pathways through which warming, hydrological change and extreme events affect biodiversity and identifies adaptation mechanisms relevant to Azerbaijan. The paper synthesizes authoritative global assessments, peer-reviewed literature and selected national policy documents, with emphasis on forests, mountain ecosystems, freshwater habitats, agricultural landscapes and nature-based solutions. The reviewed evidence links climate stress to habitat modification, range shifts, altered seasonal processes, water scarcity and increasing pressure on ecosystem services, although local impacts depend on land use, exposure and species-specific sensitivity. Ecosystem-based adaptation offers opportunities through habitat restoration, ecological connectivity, water and soil conservation, sustainable forestry and biodiversity-sensitive land management. These measures require careful ecological design because poorly located tree planting or other single-purpose interventions may create trade-offs for water resources and native species. For Azerbaijan, integrating biodiversity monitoring into climate planning, aligning adaptation investments with watershed-scale risk, and involving local communities are practical priorities. The review concludes that protecting ecological function is both a conservation objective and an economic resilience strategy. Its contribution is a context-specific policy synthesis rather than a new quantitative assessment of climate impacts.

items.title: Changing waters: from waterscape to landscape and back again
items.abstract: Across Sweden, around 2,400 lake-lowering and drainage projects since the early nineteenth century converted wetlands and lakes into fields, fixing a particular vision of progress into ditches, land deeds, and sediment. This article reviews 82 archival, scientific, and policy sources to ask what was done, why, and when, and to trace how these interventions continue to shape contemporary restoration politics. Lake drainage modifications started gaining interest in the 1830s and peaked around 1870–1930, enabled by ideals of patriotic ‘improvement’, expanding credit, and the 1879 Drainage Act. The resulting hydro-social legacies, long-lasting impacts on water systems and related social arrangements, such as subsiding peat, altered runoff pathways, and internal stores of various metals and compounds, complicate future plans to refill old lake basins and rewet peatlands for climate and biodiversity goals. Evidence from Swedish rewetting experiments indicates that restored peatlands can experience transient increases in total phosphorus and total mercury in outflow waters, while recently rewetted sites may remain net carbon sources during the first years after intervention. Restoration is conceptualised as a negotiated, case-specific intervention in which targeted projects, long-term monitoring, and shared governance confront historical debts rather than rely on expectations of a return to pristine nature.

items.title: Intestinal and Urinary Helminthiases: Prevalence, Polyparasitism and Associated Factors among Schoolchildren in the Sahelian and Sudanian Zones of Chad
items.abstract: ABSTRACTIntroduction. Polyparasitism involving intestinal helminths and schistosomes is common among schoolchildren in sub-Saharan Africa, but its structure and determinants remain poorly documented in Chad. This study aimed to describe helminth species richness, infection intensity, infracommunity structure, and factors associated with polyparasitism among schoolchildren in the Sahelian and Sudanian zones of Chad. Methods. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in 19 rural public schools between September 2021 and February 2022. Stool samples were examined using a single Kato–Katz smear read twice, and urine samples were examined after centrifugation. Factors associated with polyparasitism were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Results. Of the 1,443 pupils enrolled, 1,408 provided both stool and urine samples. Nine helminth taxa were identified. The prevalence of intestinal helminths was 35.87% (505/1,408), while the prevalence of Schistosoma haematobium was 45.46% (656/1,443). Heavy-intensity infections affected 41.6% (273/656) of S. haematobium carriers and 42.1% (83/197) of S. mansoni carriers. Polyparasitism affected 23.08% (325/1,408) of pupils and comprised 28 infracommunity types. Polyparasitism was less likely in the Sahelian zone than in the Sudanian zone (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42–0.74) and more likely among pupils aged 15–18 years than among those aged 10–14 years (aOR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.03–2.06). Conclusion. Chadian schoolchildren harbour a diverse helminth fauna, with frequent polyparasitism and heavy schistosome infections. An integrated control strategy combining praziquantel and albendazole, health education, and improved sanitation is needed.RÉSUMÉ Introduction. Le polyparasitisme à helminthes intestinaux et à schistosomes est fréquent chez les écoliers d’Afrique subsaharienne, mais reste mal documenté au Tchad. Cette étude décrit la richesse spécifique, l’intensité des infestations, les infracommunautés et les facteurs associés au polyparasitisme chez les écoliers des zones sahélienne et soudanienne. Méthodes. Une enquête transversale a été menée dans 19 écoles publiques rurales entre septembre 2021 et février 2022. Les selles (un frottis de Kato–Katz lu deux fois) et les urines (centrifugation) ont été examinées. Les facteurs associés au polyparasitisme ont été étudiés par régression logistique multivariée. Résultats. Sur 1 443 élèves inclus, 1 408 ont fourni des selles et des urines. Neuf taxons d’helminthes ont été identifiés. La prévalence était de 35,87 % (505/1 408) pour les helminthes intestinaux et de 45,46 % (656/1 443) pour Schistosoma haematobium. Les infestations intenses touchaient 41,6 % (273/656) des porteurs de S. haematobium et 42,1 % (83/197) de ceux de S. mansoni. Le polyparasitisme (23,08 % ; 325/1 408) comprenait 28 types d’infracommunautés. Il était moins fréquent en zone sahélienne qu’en zone soudanienne (OR ajusté [ORa] : 0,56 ; IC à 95 % : 0,42–0,74) et plus fréquent chez les élèves de 15–18 ans que chez ceux de 10–14 ans (ORa : 1,45 ; IC à 95 % : 1,03–2,06). Conclusion. Les écoliers tchadiens présentent une faune helminthique diversifiée, un polyparasitisme fréquent et des infections schistosomiennes souvent intenses. Une lutte intégrée associant praziquantel et albendazole, éducation sanitaire et assainissement est nécessaire.

items.title: Development of Wildlife Identification System Based on Local Alignment Algorithm
items.abstract: Wildlife crimes seriously threaten biodiversity and public health security. Identifying the species of wild animals and their products involved in such cases is the key to handling them. This study aimed to establish a wildlife DNA identification system based on a local alignment algorithm, thereby providing reliable technical support for public security organizations with high-precision and high-efficiency species identification techniques. The system adopted the Smith–Waterman local alignment algorithm, recognized the local similarity of DNA sequences with dynamic programming, and solved the problem of heavy reliance on complete sequences when using traditional global alignment. The parameters were optimized in combination with the Basic Local Alignment Search Tool, and matrix calculation was accelerated with C-Extensions for Python, thus significantly enhancing the processing efficiency for large-scale data. The database was based on self-dedicated identification data from the College of Criminal Science and Technology, Nanjing Police University. Experts reviewed the data, and the accuracy and safety of data were ensured to avoid the risk of species classification errors in open-source databases. The system innovatively integrated the Streamlit framework to develop the visualization platform and user-friendly interface. The grassroots police officers obtained species-matching results and the related species information by inputting DNA sequences, thereby facilitating case handling. The system provides an efficient technical tool for combating wildlife crimes and maintaining biodiversity, with significant practical value and immense promotion potential.

items.title: Social imaginaries on wildfires, burning practices, and fire management in two Colombian national newspapers: tensions between risk, illegality, and ecological function
items.abstract: Introduction This article analyzes the construction of social imaginaries about the application of fire in two Colombian national newspapers, El Tiempo and El Espectador , based on three key concepts understood as distinct discursive categories: fire use and management, burning practices, and wildfires. Methodology A mixed-methods approach is adopted, combining artificial intelligence tools with qualitative analysis. The quantitative phase employs a BETO model to classify the evaluative framing of fire, while the qualitative phase utilizes a discursive analysis. The corpus consists of 504 items published in El Tiempo and El Espectador between 2020 and 2025. Results The findings show that, in the coverage of both newspapers, the application of fire is primarily represented as a problematic practice, associated with risk, illegality, and destruction. This trend is quantified by the predominance of negative valuations within the corpus. Based on the automatic classification of text fragments, 71% present a negative valuation, compared to 29% neutral. Specifically, “burning practices” concentrate 87.5% negative valuations and 12.5% neutral, while “wildfires” record 68% negative and 32% neutral, with no positive valuations identified in the manually annotated sample. In contrast, “fire use and management” has marginal visibility in the corpus, with only 24 news items; their manual classification as complete news items, reported separately because of its different unit and procedure, shows that 15 (62%) were positive and 9 (38%) negative, despite the potential of this concept to recognize ecological and territorial functions. Discussion These findings suggest that terminological distribution may contribute to consolidating interpretive frameworks that reduce the complexity of the phenomenon. Consequently, the analyzed coverage tends to leave the ecological and cultural dimensions of fire in the background, which may limit the legitimacy of integrated management approaches in environmental governance.

items.title: Addressing environmental problems and the role of environmental policy in achieving sustainable development in Azerbaijan
items.abstract: In the modern era, ensuring sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with environmental safety and social welfare. Intensive use of natural resources, climate change, pollution of water and land resources, increase in waste, air pollution, and reduction of biodiversity are among the main factors affecting the long-term sustainability of economic development. The purpose of the study is to evaluate current environmental problems in Azerbaijan from the perspective of sustainable development principles, determine their impact on economic and social development, and substantiate directions for improving environmental policy. The study used a systematic and comparative approach, analysis of statistical data, and methods of scientific-theoretical generalization. The analysis utilized environmental statistical data from the State Statistical Committee of the Republic of Azerbaijan, state programs, and international documents. Existing statistical data show that both positive changes and problems requiring resolution exist in the fields of waste management, use of natural resources, and ensuring environmental safety. Based on the results of the study, the main directions determined for solving environmental problems include efficient use of resources, expansion of waste recycling, development of digital monitoring systems, application of green technologies, and strengthening the institutional capacities of environmental management.

items.title: Using ecosystem science to achieve ecological nutrient management
items.abstract: The reliance on inorganic fertilizers, along with the simplification of cropping systems and agricultural landscapes, fueled tremendous increases in yield while generating severe consequences for the biosphere, human health, and biodiversity. There is a critical need to address these issues and transition to a more sustainable approach to soil management and food production. Ecosystem ecology provides a flexible systems approach for understanding the complex and dynamic interactions among organisms, their environment, and agricultural management, which ultimately govern biogeochemical cycling and soil-mediated ecosystem services. This chapter reviews concepts from ecosystem ecology and related disciplines that form the foundation of ecological nutrient management (ENM), including how communities of plants and soil organisms govern soil organic matter dynamics and nutrient cycling. It presents the foundational principles of ENM and discusses key management practices that extend these principles into desirable improvements in agroecosystems, emphasizing how ecosystem science can be leveraged to implement ENM effectively.

items.title: Recent Progress on Limonoids: The Potential, Challenges, and Insights of Chemistry and Biology
items.abstract: Limonoids are an important class of highly oxygenated triterpenoids containing a distinctive 4,4,8-trimethyl-17-furanylsteroid skeleton. To date, over 2700 members, including azadirachtin, toosendanin, limonin, obacunone, nomilin, harrisonin, nimbolide, gedunin, salannin, nimbin, khayanolide, xylocarpin, swietenine, rocaglamide, trichilin, vilasinin, etc., have been isolated from citrus fruits and the plants of the Rutaceae and Meliaceae families. They play a significant role in the discovery of novel drug and pesticide candidates owing to their wide range of biological activities, such as protective, anti-inflammatory, anti-cancer, antimicrobial, and insecticidal properties. Therefore, their potential, challenges, and insights into the chemistry and biology of triterpenoid-type limonoids have recently garnered much attention. The focus of this review is not only to summarize the isolation, total synthesis, and structural modifications of limonoid-type natural products as potential therapeutic and pesticidal agents, but also to highlight the underlying mechanisms of their pharmacological effects from 2017 to 2025. Noteworthily, perspectives were given on the limonoid-type compounds as leads for further development of novel drugs and agrochemicals, and their applications in the future. Hopefully, this review can serve as a comprehensive reference for future research on limonoids and their derivatives in the pharmaceutical and agricultural fields.

items.title: Major pests of fruit and berry crops in the western region of Azerbaijan and environmentally safe control methods
items.abstract: In recent years, clearly observable global climate change in Azerbaijan, as in various geographical regions of the world, together with the expansion of intensive fruit orchards, has become one of the major factors contributing to the spread of diverse pest organisms, reduced crop productivity, and deterioration in the quality of agricultural products. In this context, studying pests of fruit and berry crops, determining their distribution patterns, and implementing environmentally safe control methods represent important components of modern plant protection. The aim of this study was to identify the most widespread pests affecting major fruit and berry crops cultivated in the Western region of Azerbaijan, particularly in the Ganja-Dashkasan and Gazakh-Tovuz economic regions, to assess their biological characteristics, distribution patterns, and harmful effects on plants, and to substantiate environmentally safe pest management and control measures. The study focused on major pests associated with apple, pear, plum, sour cherry, sweet cherry, apricot, peach, grape, strawberry, raspberry, and blackberry crops. The biological characteristics, feeding behavior, distribution, and damage caused by important pest species such as Aphis pomi, Cydia pomonella, Grapholita funebrana, Panonychus ulmi, and Metcalfa pruinosa were assessed based on literature data and field observations. Particular attention was given to the application of biological products, entomophages, pheromone traps, agronomic practices, plant-based preparations, and integrated pest management systems, which can contribute to reducing the intensive use of chemical pesticides.
