items.title: Widening educational inequalities for young people attending child and adolescent mental health services: a longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Background A 'mortality gap' is well-documented in individuals with severe mental illness but an 'education gap' emerges much earlier in life, with major long-term consequences. While educational attainment has improved in most high-income countries in recent decades, it is unknown whether these improvements have narrowed the education gap for young people who attend child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS). Methods This nationwide, longitudinal cohort study used linked administrative data from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage (SAIL) databank for a large cohort of individuals in Wales born between 1992 and 2003 and followed to 2019. We compared performance on the General Certificate of Secondary Education (GCSE) exams, taken at age 16, between young people with and without prior CAMHS contact. We divided the population into two sequential birth cohorts (1992-1997 vs 1998-2003) and tested whether the association between CAMHS contact and failure to achieve key GCSE thresholds changed over time. Results In the total population, the proportion of young people failing to achieve the basic GCSE level one threshold fell from 6.9% in the older (1992-1997) cohort to 3.7% in the younger (1998-2003) cohort. Young people who attended CAMHS, however, were significantly more likely to fail to achieve level one GCSEs in both cohorts (aOR = 4.28, 95% CI = 4.08, 4.48). Critically, this gap widened over time for GCSE Level-1 attainment, both for CAMHS outpatients (interaction aOR = 1.30, 95% CI = 1.20, 1.40) and CAMHS inpatients (interaction aOR = 1.80, 95% CI = 1.47, 2.19). Conclusions Despite overall improvements in educational attainment in the general population, there is a growing gap in educational attainment between young people accessing CAMHS and their peers. The failure to attain basic qualifications may lead to lifelong socioeconomic disadvantage. Research on how to effectively address the educational needs of young people attending CAMHS is an urgent economic and public health issue.

items.title: The impact of interventions combining nutrition and physical exercise on frailty in old age: A systematic literature review and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM).
items.abstract: BackgroundFrailty is common in older adults and associated with inadequate nutrition, reduced physical function, and increased vulnerability. While physical exercise benefits frailty outcomes, evidence on combined nutrition and exercise interventions remains unclear.AimTo systematically review evidence on the impact of interventions combining nutrition and physical exercise on frailty status among community-dwelling frail older adults (≥65 years).MethodsThe review followed the Cochrane Handbook, Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis guidelines. Searches were conducted in PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus. Randomised controlled trials explicitly defining frailty were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened and assessed methodology using RoB 2.0. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Due to heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis without meta-analysis was performed.SummaryOf 2447 records identified, 10 publications met the inclusion criteria. Two trials directly assessed frailty reversal and reported improvements favouring structured exercise, with one showing additional benefit when combined with a nutritional supplement. Odds of frailty reversal ranged from two- to fivefold. Additional studies reported modest improvements in mobility disability risk, lean body mass, and functional performance. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to high, limited by small samples and heterogeneity.Although some studies reported favourable effects of combined nutrition and exercise interventions, the available evidence is insufficient to determine whether nutrition adds benefits beyond exercise alone. Structured exercise consistently benefited frailty-related outcomes. However, due to few studies and substantial heterogeneity, firm conclusions cannot be drawn. Further standardised trials are needed to clarify the role of nutritional components within combined nutrition-exercise interventions in frailty management.

items.title: Content Adaptations and Usability Improvements in a Brazilian Digital Mental Health Platform: Lessons Learned from Iterative User-Centered Research.
items.abstract: Introduction: Digital mental health interventions are especially relevant in low- and middle-income countries, where access to face-to-face care is limited. However, many platforms insufficiently incorporate user experience, reducing engagement and effectiveness, particularly among vulnerable populations. Methods: This study adopted an exploratory mixed-methods approach conducted across four sequential phases to improve a Brazilian digital mental health platform focused on anxiety and stress management. Data were collected from four sources: focus groups with 36 community leaders from a low-income urban area; surveys with 36 highly educated users; think-aloud usability interviews with 10 participants; and an online survey with 102 young adults. Qualitative and quantitative data were integrated to identify design and content gaps. Results: Participants consistently reported the need for culturally resonant language, shorter and more dynamic videos, greater diversity among presenters, and improved visual design and accessibility. These findings guided platform adaptations, including revised audiovisual formats, updated language and imagery, and enhanced accessibility features. The results reinforce the importance of user-centered and culturally sensitive design in digital mental health tools, particularly in socially diverse contexts. Conclusion: Findings suggest that user-centered adaptation processes can help improve the usability and cultural relevance of digital mental health interventions.

items.title: Resource waves across snowpacks and alpine vegetation extend seasonal resource availability in alpine ecosystems.
items.abstract: Alpine ecosystems are energy-limited and highly seasonal. Consumers in the alpine zone must track rapidly shifting windows of prey availability during the short growing season. Prolonged snowmelt creates a mosaic of persistent snowfields, scrubs and alpine tundra. In addition to vegetation-dwelling arthropods, wind-transported arthropods deposited on snowpacks, known as arthropod fallout, provide an allochthonous subsidy from lower elevations to alpine environments. Asynchronous arthropod phenology across alpine vegetation and snowpack may create resource waves and prolong food availability for alpine consumers. However, no multi-mountain studies have jointly quantified the phenology of vegetation-dwelling arthropods and arthropod fallout. We examined whether phenological asynchrony between arthropod fallout on snowpacks and vegetation-dwelling arthropods creates sequential resource peaks that extend food availability for alpine consumers. Across three mountains in the Japanese Alps (Tateyama, Norikura and Kisokoma) along broad climatic gradients, we sampled arthropods over 2 years at half-monthly intervals from late May to early August on alpine snowpacks and in alpine vegetation, including Japanese stone pine scrub and alpine tundra. Seasonal changes in arthropod biomass were estimated using taxon-specific length-mass regressions. Community structures of arthropods were analysed using non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS). Seasonal changes in abundance and biomass of arthropods on vegetation and snowpacks were examined using generalised linear mixed-effects models (GLMMs). Aphids dominated on snowpacks, whereas Diptera were most abundant in vegetation. Arthropod abundance peaked sequentially across habitats, occurring early on snowpacks, mid-season in Japanese stone pine scrub and late in alpine tundra. Biomass was high early on snowpacks but increased later in vegetation, with the increase occurring earlier in scrub than in alpine tundra. Our findings suggest that arthropod fallout and vegetation-dwelling arthropods provide food resources for alpine consumers during different periods of the growing season. These sequential peaks in arthropod abundance and biomass create resource waves that extend seasonal food availability for consumers. Warming and earlier snowmelt may disrupt these resource waves through taxon-specific responses to changing temperature and snow conditions. Conserving the snow-scrub-tundra mosaic and its temporal complementarity should therefore be a priority for sustaining alpine biodiversity under rapid climate change.

items.title: Zero-valent iron powder- and sponge iron-biochar composites drive enhanced nitrate conversion in autotrophic nitrate reduction by distinct electron delivery strategies.
items.abstract: Iron-mediated autotrophic denitrification is promising for low-carbon wastewater treatment because it requires little external carbon and avoids secondary pollution. Current studies show that enhanced electron transfer between iron and carbon may improve its nitrogen removal efficiency, while the intermediate processes and mechanisms of electron-transfer mechanisms remain poorly elucidated. Therefore, in this study iron powder (IP) and sponge iron (SI) were combined with conductive biochar to construct iron-carbon autotrophic denitrification systems. And we compared the system's denitrification performance, iron corrosion characteristics, and microbial responses. Results revealed that both iron sources enhanced nitrate reduction. However, IP was associated with more pronounced accumulation of NH 4 + and NO 2 - , whereas SI produced fewer intermediate metabolites. Corrosion of the iron substrates produced conductive Fe 3 O 4 , which bonded with organic matter coating the biochar surface, creating an "iron oxide-biochar-biofilm" conductive network thereby enhancing the potential for extracellular electron transfer within the system. The two systems showed different microbial responses. The IP system developed a community dominated by Thiobacillus, and genes associated with the dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) were significantly enriched, indicating a strong tendency toward DNRA in the system. In contrast, the SI system supports diverse and synergistic microbial networks; the simultaneous enrichment of denitrification genes and electron transport genes promotes the relatively complete conversion of nitrogen into gaseous nitrogen for removal. This study provides a mechanistic basis for the design and operational optimization of iron-based autotrophic denitrification materials for low C/N wastewater.

items.title: Biochar-immobilised phosphate-solubilising bacteria enhance soil available phosphorus by affecting phosphorus fraction transformation and phosphorus-acquiring microbiota.
items.abstract: Phosphate-solubilising bacteria (PSB) play an important role in phosphorus (P) transformation and plant P uptake. However, their effectiveness is often limited by environmental instability and soil poor survival. Biochar has been proposed as a suitable carrier for microbial immobilisation; however, the effects of biochar-immobilised PSB on soil P fractions and the microbial mechanisms underlying P transformation remain unclear. In this study, we developed a biochar-immobilised PSB using Klebsiella sp. N107 and assessed its effects on soil P availability, P fraction transformation, and microbial processes regulating P cycling. A pot experiment was conducted: no fertilisation, conventional fertilisation (NPK), NPK + pristine biochar (NPKB), NPK + PSB (NPKP), and NPK + biochar-immobilised PSB (NPKBP). Soil properties, P fractions, organic acids, enzyme activities, and metagenomic characteristics were analysed. Compared with NPKB and NPKP, NPKBP enhanced plant P uptake and soil available P. It also increased labile P fractions, organic acid concentrations, and the activities of P acquiring enzymes. Genes associated with P transport (pit, ugpB, ugpQ, and ugpE), polyphosphate degradation (ppk1 and ppk2), organic P mineralisation (phoA and phoD), and inorganic P solubilisation (gcd, ppa, and ppx) were upregulated. P acquiring taxa, including Sphingomonas, Gaiella, and Bradyrhizobium, were enriched and contributed functionally to P cycling. Overall, biochar-immobilised PSB improved soil P availability by promoting P fraction transformation and restructuring microbial communities involved in P cycling. Soil pH, organic acids, and available nitrogen were identified as key drivers of these processes, highlighting the potential of biochar-immobilised PSB to improve soil P utilisation and management.

items.title: Shotgun Metagenomic Profiling of Phlebotomus papatasi (Diptera: Psychodidae, Phlebotomine) in Zoonotic Cutaneous Leishmaniasis Endemic Foci of Iraq: Microbiota, Resistome, and Virulome.
items.abstract: This study aims to develop a regional baseline for future individual-level and comparative studies of microbial ecology and symbiont-based vector control. Phlebotomus papatasi is a major vector of Leishmania major and an important component of the transmission cycle of zoonotic cutaneous leishmaniasis (ZCL) in Iraq, although the internal microbial communities of this vector are poorly characterised in the region. In this study, shotgun metagenomic sequencing was employed to investigate the microbial communities of a pooled sample of 129 blood-fed female Ph. papatasi collected from ZCL-endemic foci in Nineveh Governorate, Iraq, from 2024 to 2025. Approximately 32.9 million raw reads were obtained from sequencing, with the quality-filtered, host-removed, and low-diversity-filtered reads analysed for taxonomic and functional profiles. The data revealed a complex microbial community inside blood-fed Ph. papatasi dominated by bacteria. Moreover, several species of Proteobacteria in blood-fed Ph. papatasi were detected, which accounted for 98.32% of the classified reads, with Enterobacter cloacae as the most common species (74.34% of classified reads). Strains associated with Wolbachia were also detected (approximately 8.96% of classified reads). The microbial data further revealed the presence of genes associated with antimicrobial resistance including oqxA/oqxB-associated efflux and AmpC-type β-lactamase families, and virulence factors associated with motility, iron acquisition, and secretion systems. Nevertheless, the data represented the distribution of sequencing reads within the pooled sample (single sample), rather than the prevalence or average abundance among individual sand flies.

items.title: Tissue-specific transcriptional reprogramming in the fat body is associated with long-term immune protection in Galleria mellonella after immune priming with Bacillus species.
items.abstract: Background Immune priming in insects is well-documented, but its persistence across larval development and the tissue-specific mechanisms remain poorly understood. Whether closely related bacteria differ in inducing durable memory and whether protection correlates with transcriptional reprogramming in specific organs is unclear. Methods First-instar Galleria mellonella larvae were orally primed with inactivated Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. galleriae (Bt), B. cereus (Bc), or B. subtilis (Bs) and challenged at fourth-instar with virulent Bt subsp. galleriae. Survival was recorded for 7 days, and phenoloxidase activity was measured in hemolymph 24 h post-challenge. In parallel, fourth-instar larvae received the same cells; at 12 h, transcription of 10 immune genes was analyzed in hemocytes, fat body, and midgut, and lysozyme-like activity was measured in the midgut at 24 h. Results Immune priming was species-specific: Bt conferred strong homologous protection against Bt subps. Galleriae (82% survival), Bc moderate cross-protection (60%), Bs none (27%). Protection correlated specifically with Toll pathway activation and AMP induction in the fat body, whereas Bs triggered strong hemocyte responses yet failed to activate the fat body or restore PO activity. Conclusion Oral priming in G. mellonella is species-specific and organ-compartmentalized. Effective long-term protection requires transcriptional reprogramming in the fat body, whereas hemocyte-restricted activation is insufficient - revealing that immune memory is organized at the organ level rather than systemically. These findings link tissue-specific responses to protective efficacy.

items.title: PBDE-to-OPE Substitution in Urban Greenspace Soils: OPE-Dominated Burdens and Endpoint-Specific Risk Priorities.
items.abstract: The phaseout of polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) and expanded use of organophosphate esters (OPEs) have reshaped flame-retardant contamination, yet how legacy PBDEs and emerging OPEs coexist in urban soils, and how this coexistence reshapes risk priorities, remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 230 surface soil samples from 49 greenspace sites in Shenzhen, China, for 12 PBDEs and 14 OPEs and evaluated their occurrence, sources and risks. Median ΣOPEs (233 ng/g dry weight, dw) was 22-fold higher than median ΣPBDEs (10.6 ng/g dw), indicating strong OPE dominance in present-day soil burdens. OPE distributions were positively correlated with human activity indicators, whereas PBDEs were more closely associated with soil properties, particularly organic matter. Despite the concentration dominance of OPEs, risk priorities differed by endpoint. OPEs dominated ecological risk and contributed 99.8% of total carcinogenic risk, whereas residual PBDEs contributed 66.9% of total noncarcinogenic hazard despite accounting for only 4.2% of total concentration. Source-resolved analysis further showed that the mass-dominant Alkyl-OPE-rich source was not the dominant contributor to health risk: noncarcinogenic hazard was driven mainly by a legacy PBDE source, whereas carcinogenic risk was dominated by a TDCIPP-rich foam-related factor. Although estimated human health risks remained within commonly used risk threshold, these results show that PBDE-to-OPE substitution can produce endpoint-specific risk priorities, highlighting the need for source-resolved and toxicity-weighted assessment to prioritize contaminants and sources when managing legacy and emerging contaminants in urban soils.

items.title: Plastic Film Mulching Affects Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons Contamination in Farmland Soils across Mainland China: Nationwide Comparison.
items.abstract: The application of plastic mulch films is widespread in contemporary agriculture, and China alone consumes more than any other country. However, the contamination and sources of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), which exhibit carcinogenic, teratogenic, and mutagenic toxicity, remain unclear in farmlands with and without mulching nationwide in mainland China, as does the influence of plastic mulch films on PAH accumulation. Topsoil samples were simultaneously obtained in this study from mulched and non-mulched farmlands across mainland China to systematically compare the contamination characteristics of PAHs and to analyze the influence of plastic mulching. The results demonstrate that mulched farmland had significantly lower PAH levels than non-mulched farmland (p 0.05). PAHs in mulched farmland were predominantly derived from field-scale agricultural sources and nearby traffic emissions, whereas those in non-mulched farmland were characterized by regional-scale atmospheric mixed inputs. North China exhibited the highest proportions (exceeding 70%) of both mulched and non-mulched farmlands posing potential cancer risks to humans, whereas Northwest China showed the lowest proportions (below 20%). Influenced by plastic mulching, the abundances of film-microplastics and fiber-microplastics were significantly positively correlated with PAH concentrations in mulched farmland (p < 0.05) and could serve as indicators of PAH contamination in mulched farmland, but showed no significant correlation in non-mulched farmland. This study provides evidence for differentiated pollution prevention and control strategies in mulched versus non-mulched farmland systems.

items.title: Lead-Aggravated Duodenal Barrier Injury Accompanied by Fecal Microbiota Alterations in 5xFAD Mice.
items.abstract: Lead (Pb) is a persistent environmental toxicant, yet its effects on intestinal homeostasis in the 5xFAD background remain poorly characterized. Six-month-old 5xFAD mice were exposed to 200 μg/L Pb in drinking water for 8 weeks, with age-matched wild-type and unexposed 5xFAD mice serving as reference groups. We integrated duodenal metal profiling, mucosal architecture assessment, proteomic analysis, and fecal 16S rRNA sequencing to characterize the Pb-associated intestinal responses. Pb exposure increased duodenal Pb burden and reduced Ca, Cu, and Mg concentrations relative to unexposed 5xFAD mice. These elemental changes were accompanied by more pronounced villus shortening, crypt deepening, a lower villus height-to-crypt depth ratio, and loss of AB-PAS-positive goblet cells, suggesting impaired mucosal architecture and mucus-associated protection. Duodenal proteomic screening identified Pb-associated patterns involving epithelial junction organization, cell adhesion, calcium signaling, mineral absorption, complement activation, and mucosal immune pathways. In parallel, Pb-exposed 5xFAD mice showed lower fecal microbial richness and diversity than the unexposed 5xFAD mice, together with reduced abundances of Lachnospiraceae-related commensals and compositional shifts involving taxa associated with inflammatory or barrier-stress responses. Chronic Pb exposure in 5xFAD mice was associated with concurrent changes in duodenal metal homeostasis, mucosal structure, pathway-level proteomic profiles, and distal fecal microbial ecology. The duodenal findings highlight the proximal small intestine as a relevant peripheral site of Pb toxicity.

items.title: Seasonal habitat dynamics and anthropogenic exposure of loggerhead turtles at a global scale.
items.abstract: Loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) are highly migratory marine reptiles whose seasonal habitat shifts can alter their exposure to fisheries, vessel traffic, and plastic pollution. We combined global occurrence records with seasonal environmental predictors to build species distribution models (SDMs), mapped potential habitats for four seasons, and overlaid these habitats with fishing, shipping, and floating-plastic layers. We then compared cumulative exposure with the global marine protection network to identify conservation gaps. Potential habitats varied strongly among seasons and were associated mainly with sea surface temperature, mixed layer depth, and distance from shore. Fisheries exposure was concentrated in nearshore and continental shelf waters, shipping exposure followed major traffic corridors, and plastic pollution produced broader areal exposure. Multiple-pressure hotspots occurred consistently in the Mediterranean Sea, the northwestern Pacific, and the northwestern Atlantic. Existing marine protection covered only 11.2%-13.7% of cumulative exposure across seasons, indicating that the majority of cumulative exposure occurred outside the current marine protection network. These results show that seasonal habitat dynamics can substantially reshape anthropogenic exposure for a wide-ranging marine vertebrate. Integrating seasonal SDMs with pressure-specific exposure layers can help prioritize dynamic ocean management and transboundary conservation for loggerhead turtles.

items.title: Ecosystem restructuring of subtidal oyster reefs responding to a dredged material disposal disturbance revealed by ecological network analysis.
items.abstract: Understanding how coastal ecosystems reorganize after abrupt anthropogenic disturbances is fundamental for predicting ecosystem resilience and informing adaptive management strategies. Here, we examined the temporal reorganization of an oyster reef ecosystem responding to an unexpected dredged material dumping event using a before-after assessment framework. Four annual Ecopath models (2017-2020) were constructed to characterize temporal variations in ecosystem structure, energy pathways, trophic organization, and functional resilience. Ecosystem-level indicators displayed strong temporal fluctuations (p 2020 > 2019 > 2018. Following extensive mortality of oysters and macroalgae, the ecosystem experienced substantial functional reorganization in 2018, characterized by reduced ascendency/development capacity ratio and connectance index, together with increased system omnivory and total primary production/total respiration ratio (p < 0.001). These shifts suggested enhanced trophic flexibility accompanied by reduced ecosystem maturity. Following the disturbance, Finn's cycling index, Finn's mean path length, and the detritivory/herbivory ratio increased and reached their maximum values in 2019, indicating enhanced detritus-based energy pathway. Keystone functional groups gradually shifted from fish-dominated regulation toward invertebrate-mediated control, while oysters consistently remained among the dominant functional groups. Redundancy/ascendency index analysis revealed that top predators played important roles in maintaining ecosystem stability under disturbance, whereas zooplankton functioned as key mediators of trophic connectivity. Collectively, these results demonstrated that ecosystem stability depends on higher functional diversity, trophic connectivity, and ecological redundancy. Maintaining ecosystem engineers and preserving diverse energy pathways may therefore represent essential strategies for sustaining ecosystem resilience and long-term ecological stability.

items.title: Chemical Ecology and Management of Imported Fire Ants.
items.abstract: Imported fire ants ( Solenopsis invicta and S. richteri ) are invasive pests that were introduced into the United States via Mobile, Alabama, in the early twentieth century. As these species spread, interbreeding led to the emergence of hybrid populations. Their rapid expansion and ecological dominance prompted extensive control efforts, including chemical eradication campaigns and biologically informed strategies. Today, fire ants infest over 140 million hectares across the southern United States, affecting public health, agriculture, and ecosystems. Despite decades of research, many fire ant semiochemicals remain unidentified because of the ants' complex social behavior and because multicomponent chemical signals occur in trace amounts and are difficult to isolate, especially those involved in aerial mating. Additionally, components often lack activity unless presented in specific combinations. These challenges limit traditional bioassay-guided structure elucidation. This review summarizes advances in fire ant chemical ecology, highlights persistent knowledge gaps, and proposes innovative strategies to accelerate pheromone discovery and improve management.

items.title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon.
items.abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO 2 or CH 4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Here, we simulated both dammed and non-dammed scenarios for 5346 global reservoir dams to assess their impact on carbon emissions from retained OC. The results show that reservoir-only approaches overestimate dam-induced carbon emissions by neglecting baseline emissions under no-dam conditions. After baseline correction, dams increase carbon emissions by an average of 21.5% in CO 2 -equivalent (CO 2 -eq), which represents only 18.6% of the emissions estimated using the conventional reservoir-based accounting approach. XGBoost identified reservoir depth and hydraulic residence time as the primary controls on dam-induced carbon emissions.

items.title: Cultural norms of exogamy and mobility shape genetic evolution of Central African hunter-gatherers.
items.abstract: Through a hunting and gathering lifestyle, humans have managed to thrive across all terrestrial ecosystems. A key adaptive feature enabling this ecological success is the ability of hunter-gatherer societies to maintain high levels of genetic diversity despite ecological and demographic shocks, but the mechanisms underlying this resilience are poorly understood. Here, we integrate genomic, demographic, mobility, and ethnographic data from two Central African hunter-gatherer populations to show that genetic diversity emerges from interacting effects of population size, mobility, and cultural norms governing marriage. We first demonstrate direct selection against background homozygosity: Even modest increases in runs of homozygosity, in the near absence of close-kin marriages, are associated with reduced reproductive success. Despite regional differences in effective population size, clustering of relatives, sedentism, and exogamy rules, overall levels of homozygosity are similarly low in both populations. These shared genetic outcomes are achieved through distinct strategies: In one region, strict exogamy combined with high lifetime mobility limits local relatedness, whereas in the other, more relaxed exogamy norms are offset by increased male mate-search distances that reduce offspring homozygosity. Together, our results show that human populations flexibly adjust mobility and social norms to demographic constraints to preserve genetic diversity and avoid fitness costs, revealing culture as a central component of human adaptation.

items.title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons.
items.abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing "impact trajectories"). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

items.title: Dissolved organic matter uptake balances carbon budgets of Red Sea bivalves and ascidians.
items.abstract: Benthic suspension feeders have long been thought to depend solely on particulate organic matter (POM) for their nutritional needs. Our research, conducted in the Gulf of Aqaba (Red Sea), shows that the available concentration of planktonic carbon in the reef water is too low to meet the metabolic demands (measured through in situ oxygen uptake) of common bivalves ( Spondylus sp. and Chama pacifica ) and ascidians ( Polycarpa mytiligera and Halocynthia spinosa ). In situ measurements confirmed a concentration-dependent uptake of bulk dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and protein-like dissolved organic compounds (fDOM, analyzed via spectrofluorometry) by Spondylus sp. and P. mytiligera , suggesting that DOC uptake may balance their carbon budgets. Stable isotope (δ 13 C) mixing models indicate that reef-derived DOC (mean δ 13 C = -18.4 ± 0.7‰) emerges as the primary carbon source for bivalves (57% of their body composition), far surpassing contributions from particulate sources (26% from POC > 100 µm and 14% from POC < 100 µm). While ascidians still rely primarily on POM (60 to 71%), DOC plays an essential role as a supplementary food source (23 to 29%). These results challenge the prevailing assumption that POM is the exclusive food source for these organisms. Given the widespread presence of bivalves and ascidians in benthic habitats, our findings highlight their ability to bypass the microbial loop and directly utilize dissolved organic compounds, prompting a reevaluation of current benthic carbon budgets.

items.title: Microbiome plasticity during the early life-stage of the angelshark (Squatina squatina) in Las Teresitas (Canary Islands).
items.abstract: Shark microbiome studies offer acute insights into host health, immunity, and ecological interactions, yet remain poorly studied compared to other marine vertebrates. Shark-associated microbial communities, despite being species-specific, are influenced by environmental conditions and feeding ecology. In this study, we aimed to characterize shifts in the microbiome of the Critically Endangered angelshark (Squatina squatina) during the early stages of development and to assess how environmental factors contribute to the shaping of a specific microbiota. Samples from thirty-nine juvenile angelsharks were collected from Las Teresitas nursery area in the Canary Islands over one year. Skin, oral and cloacal microbiomes were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. The sizes of individuals ranged between 24 and 42 cm in length. The shark microbiome was clearly distinct from the surrounding environment, indicating a unique composition from early life stages. Dominant bacteria present in the shark microbiomes included Vibrionaceae (up to 96%), Pseudoalteromonas (up to 63%), Rhodobacteraceae (up to 57%) and Alteromonadaceae (up to 20%). Seawater had a greater influence than sediment on the external skin microbiome, especially in younger individuals. This was not expected due to the burial behaviour of the species. Notably, the abundance of Pseudoalteromonadaceae (assessed by qPCR) was positively correlated with shark growth but was independent of the skin mucus. This suggests a protective role of this phylotype in younger individuals and may help in the adaptation to habitat conditions. This is the first comprehensive microbiome study in angelsharks, highlighting the importance of environmental preservation for microbial integrity and juvenile fitness.

items.title: Modern Himalayan marmot faeces analyses: Implications for palaeodietary, palaeoecological, and palaeoclimate analysis.
items.abstract: Pollen and nutrient analyses of the faeces of the Himalayan marmot (Marmota himalayana) were made to understand its preferred dietary plants and ecology. Pollen preserved in the faeces accurately reflected its diet as a mixed feeder including Artemisia, Caryophyllaceae, Asteroideae, and Ephedra, characteristic plants of the Alpine steppe vegetation under a cold and arid climate in the higher Himalaya. Pollen ratio values between Artemisia/Chenopodiaceae, Artemisia/Cyperaceae, and Artemisia/Ephedra are identified from the Pensilla Pass and Rimkhim regions, as useful tools that characterize the Alpine steppe vegetation and climate in the higher Himalaya. Principal Component Analysis of the pollen taxa indicated only a slight difference in the relative abundance between the two localities sampled, Pensila Pass and Rimkhim areas. Coprophilous fungal spores, Sporormiella and Saccobolus, were abundant and considered useful for understanding the interrelationship between vegetation and the marmot's preferred habitat. Fifteen nutritional elements were recorded, and the high concentration of carbon, nitrogen, calcium, silicon, and, phosphorous is considered significant with a direct dietary relationship with the preferred plants consumed. This study provides a modern analogue and a baseline for coprolite and palaeoecological analyses in marmot inhabited regions and to observe the species future response to vegetation and climate change resulting shifts in altitude in the higher Himalaya.

items.title: Salmonid science on the move: Twenty years of research through the lens of early career researchers
items.abstract: Salmonids are among the most studied fish species worldwide, owing to their wide geographic distribution, diversity of life-history strategies, ecological and socioeconomic importance, and vulnerability to global change. In this review, we take advantage of two decades of the International Workshop of PhDs and Post-doctoral Fellows on Anadromous Salmonids (NoWPaS) conference series to track the evolution of salmonid science through the lens of early-career researchers (ECRs). From all abstracts presented at NoWPaS meetings between 2005 and 2025, we extracted structured qualitative and quantitative information to characterize major trends and shifts in the field. Our results show a strong research bias toward Atlantic salmon and brown trout, concentrated in Europe and Atlantic Canada, and a persistent mismatch between the life stages and habitats studied. In particular, the marine phase remains understudied in comparison to fresh and coastal waters. Over the study period, salmonid research shifted markedly from hydro-geomorphological and habitat-based approaches toward genetic and genomic methods, alongside the rise of advanced telemetry methods for reconstructing individual life histories. Research orientation, measured as a gradient from fundamental to applied research, was on average intermediate but varied among countries and disciplines, with the UK and Norway showing shifts to more applied research, as well as the discipline of Ecology becoming more applied. Additionally, we identified a significant increase in Climate change and Aquaculture as research drivers, with some drivers well-represented in some species (e.g., Hydropower and dams for landlocked Atlantic salmon and Climate change for Arctic char). These trends should be interpreted in context of the composition of the NoWPaS network: participation is primarily ECRs in the Northern Hemisphere, with research from Asia, South America, and western North America largely absent from this synthesis. Despite this lens, our analysis identifies clear knowledge gaps, particularly around marine life stages and species other than Atlantic salmon and brown trout, and highlights opportunities for broadening taxonomic, geographic, and life-history coverage in future salmonid research. We also present a roadmap, identifying combinations of life stages, disciplines and taxa which have been under-represented and constitute potential knowledge gaps, while also flagging those combinations that have already been well studied. Overall, we advocate for a continued shift toward integrative and holistic approaches, bridging distinct research disciplines, to better understand, manage, and conserve salmonids under increasingly uncertain future environmental conditions.

items.title: Multicellularity and virulence in the budding yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae
items.abstract: In the real world, microbes must cope with environmental fluctuations, compete for scarce resources, and avoid predation. One adaptation to survive this tangled web is the formation of multicellular aggregates, such as biofilms, which are known to be associated with pathogenicity. Despite the importance of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae to biomedical research, little is known about the natural variation in its multicellular, biofilm-related traits. We investigated five multicellular phenotypes in a diverse, worldwide panel of ~1000 isolates. We found that all traits varied significantly and ~2/3 of the isolates expressed at least one multicellular trait. Both recent ecology and evolutionary history explained some of this variation, with clinical isolates exhibiting increased levels of three biofilm-related traits. When tested against wax moth larvae, hyper-multicellular isolates tended to be more virulent than non-multicellular isolates. Genome-wide association analysis on each trait suggested a genetic architecture of many small effect loci, compatible with polygenic adaptation. Only four genes, SLN1 , ECM5 , MLP2 , and ECM9 , were shared among the traits; deletion of MLP2 and ECM9 verified their association with multicellularity. Our results show that this yeast expresses far more multicellularity than previously appreciated and suggest that the aggregative phenotypes are likely evolving independently.

items.title: Durophagous adaptations in a new crocodyliform from the Santonian of Hungary and a systematic reassessment of European Cretaceous atoposaurids
items.abstract: Atoposauridae comprises a group of diminutive, semiterrestrial, brevirostrine neosuchian crocodyliforms that represents a characteristic component of European Jurassic-Cretaceous tetrapod faunas. Although frequently evaluated within the context of crown-group Crocodylia origins, their highly contested phylogenetic relationships continue to obscure their precise role in crocodylomorph evolutionary history. Particular ambiguity surrounds the monophyly of the genus Theriosuchus - with some hypotheses inferring long-term persistence of the lineage in Mesozoic Europe, whereas others interpreting select Cretaceous species as representatives of separate, even non-atoposaurid clades (e.g. Sabresuchus spp). We describe a new, stratigraphically intermediate taxon from the Santonian of Hungary based on isolated cranial elements, consistently placed as the sister taxon of Sabresuchus (Theriosuchus) sympiestodon from the Maastrichtian of Romania by our comprehensive set of phylogenetic analyses using three separate datasets. Sabresuchus tribodon sp. nov. is either recovered within Atoposauridae (global datasets) or Paralligatoridae (ingroup analysis) and can be distinguished from all other representatives of these groups by a specialized morphology consisting of massive, thick-enameled bulbous posterior maxillary teeth ornamented with apicobasal ridges, an extremely short rostrum with a reduced number of maxillary and dentary teeth, and the significantly upturned dorsal margin of the posterior dentary and surangular. Comparable anatomical adaptations are present in ecomorphologically convergent extinct crocodyliforms whose inferred feeding ecology included durophagy. However, this complete suite of characters has not been previously documented in either atoposaurids or paralligatorids. Our systematic reassessment results in an up-to-date taxonomy of Cretaceous European atoposaurids and tentatively confirms the polyphyly of Theriosuchus, though more definitive conclusions require combining individual, differently focused datasets. We reinterpret Aprosuchus ghirai from the Maastrichtian of Romania as a junior synonym of Sabresuchus sympiestodon and the putative European notosuchian Ogresuchus furatus from the Maastrichtian of Spain as an indeterminate atoposaurid.

items.title: A 47% decline in wind speed shapes phenology and selection on mismatching in Tree Swallows across a quarter century
items.abstract: Studies of the effects of climate change on birds typically focus on how temperature affects the average timing of breeding, often neglecting other climate variables such as wind or precipitation and their ultimate effects on reproductive success. Here, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of Tree Swallow (Tachycineta bicolor) breeding ecology in southeastern Wisconsin, USA, over a 26 year period (1997-2023). During this period there was no significant change in mean annual laying date or air temperature. Wind speed was the only weather variable that changed, slowing by 47% during the laying and hatching periods. This decline in wind speed increased food availability (Nematoceran flies), leading to larger clutches, heavier nestlings, and greater fledging success over time. It also allowed later-nesting birds to advance their laying dates. In contrast, earlier-laying birds did not advance their laying date. A changepoint analysis revealed consistently lower food availability and colder temperatures at the end of April than in early May when laying starts. This change in breeding conditions has not shifted during the study and likely acts as a constraint against earlier breeding. Over the years, the distribution of laying dates has been compressed against this early-season wall, which has resulted in a dramatic decrease in the variance of laying dates, but relatively little change in the population mean. Slowing wind speed has also relaxed selection against individuals that mistime egg laying relative to peak food abundance (i.e., phenological mismatching). Mismatching exerted relatively weak effects on reproductive success, which was driven mainly by food and weather conditions early in the season, prior to and during laying. This pattern contrasts with other Tree Swallow populations in which reproductive success is primarily influenced by temperature, particularly cold snaps, later in the season during the nestling period. Our study demonstrates that more comprehensive analyses of the effects of climate change are needed because temperature, food and wind speed can interact to produce different effects at the beginning and end of the breeding season, and this can reshape long-term trends in phenology and selection, even before eggs are laid.

items.title: Considering more complex covariate responses improves predictive performance in dynamic occupancy models
items.abstract: Finding: the right level of model complexity is a key challenge in most contexts, including ecology where data are often messy and underlying patterns complex. Dynamic occupancy models (DOMs) are increasingly used for modelling species distributions. DOMs have advantages over traditional species distribution models because their hierarchical structure allows them to explicitly model changes in occupancy over time while accounting for imperfect detection. The modelled processes (initial occupancy, colonisation, extinction, and detection) can be described as a function of covariates to account for heterogeneity in occupancy and detection dynamics. While this model structure is more complex than most alternative distribution models, in practice users of DOMs tend to fit simple linear responses to covariates with only infrequent use of non-linear responses or interactions. However, where data suffices and where ecologically justified, permitting more complex relationships between covariates and species occurrence may yield greater predictive power. Here, we assess how the complexity of covariate relationships affects the predictive performance of DOMs fit to Swiss breeding bird data. We find that models allowing quadratics and interactions tend to provide superior performance in predicting future occurrence, and that some covariates are only informative predictors when represented using non-linear relationships or interactions. Relying solely on linear relationships alone is not only inconsistent with ecological theory, but also potentially costly for predictive ability. To improve predictive power and the utility of these models for identifying important habitat and species at risk of declines, users of dynamic occupancy models should carefully consider not only their choice of candidate covariates, but also the functional forms of covariate relationships.

items.title: Drivers of variation in nocturnal insect prey mass and quality
items.abstract: Abstract Global declines in aerial insectivores highlight the need to understand their foraging landscape. Aerial predators face unique biomechanical and aerodynamic constraints; therefore, prey profitability must be evaluated through the combined lens of nutritional value and handling costs. To address this gap, we evaluated the body mass and lipid content of nocturnal insects to determine how intrinsic (i.e. taxonomy and adult feeding strategy) and extrinsic traits (i.e. larval developmental habitat) traits of the sampled insect groups influence profitability of this group of prey. Our results demonstrate that prey quality is driven by three factors. First, taxonomy influenced nutritional profiles. Relative to their body mass, mayfly’s lipid content scaled hypo-allometrically whereas the other sampled taxa scaled isometrically. Second, intrinsic feeding strategies predicted energy stores of insects. Larval-feeders had higher body mass and lipid content than life-time-feeders. Third, developmental habitat influenced total body mass but not proportional lipid content. Terrestrial insects were heavier than aquatic-emergent insects, yet total lipid content did not differ between terrestrial and aquatic-emergent insects. While these traits define potential energetic payload for insectivores, actual profitability is strictly bounded by the handling capacity of foraging predators, particularly with regards to gape limitations. Energy-dense prey are only ecologically valuable within an optimal size range for size-selective predators. By quantifying multiple drivers of prey quality, our study provides a nuanced view of the nocturnal prey landscape, demonstrating that the nutritional ecology of aerial predators is highly context-dependent on the composition of the prey community.

items.title: mTOR and Extracellular Vesicles: Linking Chemical Stress to Ecological Communication.
items.abstract: Environmental stress, including that exerted by exposure to toxic chemicals, can shift cellular priorities from growth towards maintenance and communication. These changes in cellular resource allocation are coordinated by integrative molecular hubs such as the mechanistic Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) pathway. It regulates both the autophagy, which supports maintenance, and the release of extracellular vesicles (EVs), which mediate intercellular communication. This review discusses these interconnected processes and argues that environmental contaminants may influence not only intracellular signaling but also the molecular information exchanged among cells and potentially among organisms. EV-focused studies, performed at the intersection of chemical ecology, molecular biology, and ecotoxicology, can advance mechanistic understanding and open new opportunities for non-invasive environmental biomonitoring.

items.title: Beggars can't be choosers: Competitive dominance and size-dependent resource investment jointly constrain partner associations in a multispecies mutualism.
items.abstract: Competition theory predicts that dominant species should gain preferential access to more valuable resources, whereas optimal foraging theory predicts that organisms should invest more heavily in higher-value resources. Together, these theories predict that dominant species should exhibit stronger value-dependent investment than subordinate species, consistent with the adage that 'beggars can't be choosers'. In mutualisms, where partners differ greatly in the rewards they provide, it remains unknown how competitive hierarchies influence associations with partners that vary in value. We tested whether competitive dominance and value-dependent investment jointly determine partner associations in an ant-aphid mutualism, focusing on resource quantity as a key axis of value. We measured ant responses to variation in resource quantity using experimental sugar baits and repeated censuses of wild aphid colonies spanning a range of sizes. The dominant ant preferentially recruited to larger baits and tended the largest aphid colonies, whereas subordinate ants increased recruitment with bait size only when the dominant ant was excluded. Aphid colony size also influenced behavioural investment in tending: the dominant ant showed strong increases in tending initiation, continuation and forager allocation with colony size, while subordinate ant taxa responded more weakly. Together, these results demonstrate that aphid colonies function as a graded resource whose size shapes competition among ants, leading dominant taxa to monopolize larger aphid colonies while constraining subordinate taxa to smaller ones. More broadly, these findings show that partner associations emerge from the interaction between competitive dominance and value-dependent investment, integrating classical competition and optimal foraging theories to explain partner associations in a multispecies mutualism.

explanation.extraction_note: Passages are quotations or excerpts of the author-supplied abstract; not independently verified.
